events.title: Olney Stands Up for Democracy

address_lines: Park in the Walgreen's parking lot and follow the sound of the music!

events.description:
We stand with our neighbors for democracy, for justice, and for an economy that works for all of us, not just billionaires. We stand for science, the rule of law, a working government, kindness and common decency.

We stand on the streets so people who are fearful know they are not alone. We protest to remind ourselves that this is not normal. This is not what generations of Americans have fought and died for; we stand in the streets to honor their legacy.

We oppose fascism, tyranny, the lawless cruelty of ICE, the epic corruption, the reckless attacks on science, the idiotic tariffs, and we call out the spineless elected officials who are bending their knees to a clown who thinks only of himself.

Our protests give courage to everyone else who takes a stand. We won't back down to a clown. And when that clown goes down, we will mourn all that we have lost, and then we will rebuild on a firmer foundation. Together.

Come for your own reasons, bring your own signs or borrow one. Bring your own light or borrow one. Bring your own sounds, or dance to the protest playlist we have.

It's going to be dark and cold at 5:00, so dress warmly and maybe bring a booklight to illuminate your protest sign. To keep us all safe, we will cancel if the temperatures are below freezing, or when it rains, sleets, or snows. This is a marathon.

**Join us in going door-to-door to talk to voters in the Central Valley, in the Modesto area (California's 13th Congressional District, "CA-13").** In 2024 Adam Gray flipped this House seat by only 187 votes. Let's talk to voters now to hold CA-13 in 2026, as we take back the House majority!

Just bring your smartphone or tablet and a charger, a water bottle, sunscreen, hat, comfortable shoes, and a smile. Arrive at 9:30 am to pick up supplies, get assigned turf (addresses), and quick training. Then we will head out to knock on doors, for issue canvassing and voter registration.

Read more about how Adam Gray always puts the Central Valley first - https://gray.house.gov/

If you haven’t heard of it, Swing Left is a national network that helps people find high impact ways to support Democratic candidates. We focus on the most flippable races as an important step towards ensuring the progressive change needed to create a more inclusive and equitable government and society.

_By signing up for this event you are giving permission to be added to the Swing Left Peninsula email list. Our emails share timely, impactful actions (letter parties, phone banks, canvasses, voter registrations, and more) for strategic, toss-up races that will help us win back the House and other important races._

_Every email we send includes an unsubscribe link. If you don't want to be on our list, we want you to unsubscribe! (Please don't mark this email as spam, or we will have trouble reaching the people who DO want to hear from us.) You won't be resubscribed by us._

events.title: Overpass Visibility Brigade Action: Hwy 13 Oakland
events.description:
Start your week off getting in "Some Good Trouble"! Join us for an overpass visibility event in Oakland over Hwy-13 @Joaquin Miller/Lincoln Mountain/Monterey.

We’ll use huge letters to spell out an inspiring message for passing cars during the morning commute and wave to cars honking in support. Bring your signs as we will also be on the four corners waving to drivers as they pass by.

Message TBD in response to current events.

Here's what you need to know:

- Street parking is available on Mountain Blvd. and Joaquin Miller. Parking on Woodminster is available but meters start at 8:00 a.m. 

- It can be cool and windy on the overpass.

- Photos and video of this event may be shared publicly. If you'd rather not appear in photos/video, please tell the organizer (Jenny). 

- ** If police or counter-protesters visit the event: Rather than engage with them yourself, please let the organizer (Jenny) speak with them. If you're comfortable doing so, take video of the interaction from a safe distance. **  

- We use whistles on the overpass to signal "help" or "heads up." To avoid confusion, we do not use whistles as protest noisemakers. 

- Take care not to drop anything through the fence onto the roadway. Hold pompoms, signs, flags, etc inside -- not through -- the fencing.

- Be aware of traffic on the overpass. The intersection is very busy, with school traffic in both directions, and there are limited crosswalks. For safety, always cross in the crosswalk and do not jaywalk.

- Note that flying a drone over the freeway (i.e., to take photos/video) is not permitted. 

- Overpass visibility is a practice of nonviolent civil resistance. By participating in IEBOVB actions, you are indicating that you will refrain from violence.

To help plan overpass events/messages and learn how to get involved in other resistance projects, ** join Indivisible East Bay's Slack **  (https://join.slack.com/t/indivisibleeb/shared_invite/zt-3a7m0uwys-imIj1Pe5ySPuhpbtl0Eyow), where you'll find an #overpass_visibility_brigade channel. 

Thanks for taking the time to speak up for justice.
We look forward to being visible with you!

Whether you care about cuts to Medicare, attacks on science, or the cruelty of our current immigration system—choose an issue, make a sign (just cardboard and marker is fine), and meet us in O’Fallon on Saturdays!

Why protest? (1) Protests are effective - We saw their effectiveness in Serbia in 2000, Ukraine in 2014, S. Korea in 2024, etc. (2) Protests change the narrative, bring-in new people, foster community, and spread courage. (3) Protests cause MAGA loyalists to defect and refuse to comply. events.title: Compost Hub Support: Palmer Park
events.description:
At our Compost Hubs, food scraps collected from the community are transformed into nutrient-rich compost, and we need your help to make it happen! As a Compost Hub Support Volunteer, you’ll gain hands-on experience working alongside our knowledgeable Compost Managers. Get ready to leave feeling accomplished, a little sweaty, and brimming with new compost knowledge. 

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
Roll up your sleeves and dive into a variety of engaging activities; whether it’s managing a three-bin system, tending to a compost pile, sifting finished compost, or exploring a mix of everything. There’s something for everyone, from beginners to seasoned pros! Plus, our Compost Hubs are situated in LA County’s most cherished green spaces: community gardens, urban farms, and beautiful parks. Join passionate community composters, learn to turn food scraps into rich compost, and connect with the local food system. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You will be working outdoors! Shade levels vary by site.
* Activity level can be adjusted to your comfort and abilities—just communicate with your Compost Manager.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome!
* This site has bathrooms
* If you sign up, we ask that you show up! We rely on volunteers, like you, to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.
* Access to water, but please bring a filled water bottle. 

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under the age of 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 

VOLUNTEER WAIVER: Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. Access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver

CODE OF CONDUCT: All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

events.description:

The Spartanburg County Democratic Party is building a "Civic Watch" team to attend key local meetings, take notes for the party and the public, and sign up to speak during public comment when timely issues come up.

The Spartanburg County Legislative Delegation is made up of state House and Senate members representing Spartanburg County. They meet periodically throughout the year to address local legislative matters that require General Assembly action.

By attending these meetings as a volunteer observer, you'll help ensure our community stays informed about decisions being made by our state legislators on local issues. Whether you choose to speak during public comment, take notes, or simply be a presence in the room, your participation matters.

No prior experience is necessary—just a willingness to show up and pay attention to what's happening in your community.

events.title: PPT & T4APA! Research Committee
events.description:
The Research Committee is the brain of PPT’s policy work, hosting weekly working meetings to conduct data and policy research in support of our campaigns. During these meetings, attendees analyze data, investigate policies active in other cities, and assemble reports that recommend action that can improve our transit system. [Check out the Research Committee’s past work](https://www.pittsburghforpublictransit.org/research-and-resources/) to see the types of projects you might collaborate on as part of the Research Committee.

Right now we have a few concurrent projects, namely:

- Identifying a ridership growth goal for Pittsburgh Regional Transit that matches the ridership growth in other similar transit systems, with recommendations for ways that they can meet that goal.

-Evaluating the Busline Refresh Draft 2.0 and publishing our research and feedback.

- Identifying the root causes of the drop in Pittsburgh Regional Transit service reliability to raise up solutions that work for transit riders and workers.

-Publishing a white paper about what local tax or referenda options should be available Pennsylvania municipalities in order to raise revenue for transit.

Since 2025, the Research Committee has been a joint space for members of Pittsburghers for Public Transit and supporters of [Transit for All PA!](https://www.transitforallpa.org/), the statewide transit campaign that we lead. Supporters of both organizations are welcome at these meetings, and we may work on projects relevant to Allegheny County or elsewhere in Pennsylvania.

### You might be a good fit for the Research Committee if...
- You have a knack for crunching numbers
- You consider yourself a policy wonk
- You love chasing research topics down a rabbit hole
- You have an academic or professional background in data, research or planning (although none is required to join the committee!)

**Note:** Research committee meetings often involve working closely with documents, on Google Docs or sourced from the internet. Please keep this in mind if that might pose an accessibility challenge for you.
events.accessibility_notes: ASL and Spanish interpretation is available on request, but must be booked in advance. events.title: Trump Regime Takedown Saturdays
events.description:
Keep democracy alive every Saturday by showing up, taking a stand, and sticking together for the long haul. Standing together is better than standing alone. Let’s get together and call out the Trump/MAGA regime as a community. Plus, it’s fun! Think of it as our democracy corner—a place for you to voice your opinion, hang out with like-minded fellow protesters, and experience a cathartic moment together.

What you can do:
----------------

*   If you’ve got signs, flags, cardboard cutouts, or any protest visuals you want to make, bring ’em! We also have spare signs to lend.
    
*   If you have whistles, drums, cowbells, or other noisemakers, bring ’em!
    
*   Musicians are welcome and encouraged. Sing the song of democracy!
    
*   Many of our regular protesters are part of local activist groups who are happy to chat with anyone who wants to pair their indignation with direct action beyond street protest.
    
*   Grab a flyer or zine with information on how to resist day-to-day.
    
We've turned this into the liveliest, loudest weekly protest in the city and we welcome you to join us! Bring your friends or feel free to show up by yourself. Note: We expect attendees to comply with traffic laws and stay safe since it’s a busy intersection.

This weekly event is hosted by Indivisible SF and 50501 SF (organizers of the San Francisco No Kings March), and a committed group of active protest regulars who have been showing up to this corner on a weekly basis since February 2025.

_A core principle behind all Indivisible and 50501 events is a commitment to nonviolent action. events.title: Every Saturday Pullman Rally for Sanity #Indivisible #NoKings #HandsOff #MoveOn #50501

location.venue: On the sidewalk in front of Neill Public Library North Grand Avenue & Northeast Olsen Street, Pullman, WA 99163

events.description:
This is a local Indivisible event!

Hello, people who care about democracy! My name is Syd and I call myself the reluctant activist, because I'd really rather be home resting, crocheting and managing my health issues but I'm instead forced to fight fascism in America. Someone said that the best way to not feel hopeless is to get up and do something. I'll be the one with the flower pin in my hat and the loud voice. 

With the rapid assaults on our rights, the government cuts designed to hurt the poor and vulnerable, endlessly funding genocide and starting wars, I feel it's important that we protest this insanity. Since May of 2025 we have held a rally every Saturday. We meet from 12-2 on the sidewalk in front of the Neill Public Library. It's at the intersection of N Grand and Olson NE across from the Cougar Plaza.

We won't give up our rights to peacefully protest. We need to remind this administration that it's the people who have the power, it's supposed to be Congress that writes laws and declares war, that protest is legal but human trafficking is not. This Big Beautiful Killer Bill is the opposite of what our government should do for the people. Republicans are choosing to let people go hungry, lose insurance and frankly, die. Not to balance the budget, they're doing it to reward the wealthiest.

I know these are scary times and I appreciate your bravery. I have rallied here multiple times and usually the worst pushback is a few harsh words from a moving vehicle (that I can't hear). I simply reply with "I love you!" as loudly as I am able. It's fun and it prevents any hate from sticking to us. Mostly we get a lot of honking and waving. I find it invigorating, especially when we are surrounded by a lot of other rally-goers. I'm not downplaying the new steps towards full fascism this administration has taken and I don't want you to. Please take the necessary steps to protect yourself and your identity if you feel the need.

It's important that our protest remain on the sidewalk, stay at least 18" from the curb for your safety and to not block the traffic or crosswalks so we don't give the police a reason to arrest anyone. If someone tries to instigate trouble don't confront them and remain peaceful. Yell for me. If you have a whistle, blow it. Keep back and stay safe. Record video if you are able, so that authorities will be able to ID the agitator. 

Again, I expect no problem at our little events, I expect colorful, creative signs, lots of bubbles, sidewalk chalk and numbers of like-minded people who care about our country.  Get your feelings out on your signs, enjoy the marker fumes and chalk dust or use one of our many signs. Bring water. It's thirsty work.

If you have any questions contact me on the Rally4Sanity Facebook page 
p.s. Despite what Tr*mp and Fox News say, I have never received a paycheck for rallying against his theft of power, but I have noted his history of projection. Has he paid people to rally for him?

events.description:
Add Your Name: Tell Congress Pass H.R. 14 — John Lewis Voting Rights Act

## H.R. 14 — John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act (PASS)

### TAKE ACTION NOW: Restore Voting Rights. Defend Democracy.

Democracy is not real if eligible voters can be blocked, targeted, or erased from the process. We are demanding Congress pass the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act and restore strong federal protections against voter suppression and discrimination.

---

### Legislation  
**H.R. 14 — John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act of 2025**  
https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/14

---

### What’s at risk  
Across the country, communities are facing:  
- discriminatory election rule changes  
- voter roll purges  
- manipulated district maps  
- targeted barriers that make voting harder, not easier  

And when voting access is weakened, our communities lose power over the decisions that shape our lives—schools, healthcare, safety, housing, and economic opportunity.

---

### Why this fight matters  
Voter suppression doesn’t always look like violence. Sometimes it looks like “policy.”  
Sometimes it looks like “procedure.”  
But the outcome is the same: **people locked out of democracy.**

---

### What we demand  
Congress must **PASS H.R. 14** and restore modern voting rights protections.

---

### The Advocacy League position  
✅ **SUPPORT / PASS**

---

events.title: Add Your Name: Tell Congress Stop the SAVE Act
events.description:
# Add Your Name: Tell the Senate STOP H.R. 22 (SAVE Act) — Protect Voting Rights

## TAKE ACTION NOW: Stop the SAVE Act. Protect Voter Access.

The SAVE Act **(H.R. 22)** is a voter suppression scheme disguised as “election security.” This bill would create new barriers to voter registration and threatens to block eligible voters from participating in federal elections through paperwork requirements and restrictive processes.

This is not how democracy is protected. This is how democracy is restricted.

---

## LEGISLATION
**H.R. 22 — SAVE Act (Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act)**  
https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/22

---

## WHAT’S AT RISK
H.R. 22 would require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections — adding new obstacles that will predictably hit hardest for:
- low-income voters  
- seniors  
- voters with name changes  
- voters who don’t have easy access to original documents  
- communities already targeted by voter suppression tactics  

This bill would make voting harder, not safer — and that is unacceptable.

---

## WHY THIS FIGHT MATTERS
Voter suppression doesn’t always look like intimidation at the polls.  
Sometimes it looks like “paperwork.”  
Sometimes it looks like “rules.”  
Sometimes it looks like “compliance.”  

But the outcome is the same: **eligible voters blocked from the ballot box.**

We refuse to let the freedom to vote become something only the privileged can easily access.

---

## WHAT WE DEMAND
The U.S. Senate must **REJECT H.R. 22 (SAVE Act)** and stop voter suppression.

---

## THE ADVOCACY LEAGUE POSITION
❌ **OPPOSE / STOP**

---

## TAKE ACTION NOW
**Add your name. Share this petition.**  
Tell the Senate: **STOP H.R. 22 (SAVE Act). Protect voter access. Protect democracy.**

(español abajo)

Join us for a prayer vigil as we shine a light on the names of all victims of ICE and DHS brutality under the current administration.

**Saturday, Dec 12th | 4:30 pm (prayer starts at 5:00 pm)**
**Munn Park, Lakeland**

All spiritual expressions are welcome, and you do not need to be religious to attend.

Are you feeling overwhelmed watching events unfold in our country? The erosion of democratic norms, immigration enforcement concerns, data privacy issues, threats to healthcare and Social Security, voting rights — it can feel like too much.

**But you don't have to just watch. You can act.**

---

## One Call Can Make a Difference

Calling your elected representatives is one of the most effective things a constituent can do. Members of Congress and Senators pay attention to constituent calls — it's a direct signal that voters are engaged and watching.

Maybe you've been meaning to call but weren't sure what to say. **We've solved that problem.**

---

## Join Us Every Monday on Zoom

Every Monday, we host a free 30-minute virtual training session where we do it **together**. We provide everything you need:

- 📞 **Phone numbers** for your representatives
- 📝 **Ready-to-use scripts** so you always know what to say
- 🎓 **Training and support** for first-timers and regulars alike

---

## Register Today

When you register, please include your cell number so we can send you a text reminder on the day of each session. **Your information stays private — we never share attendee data.**

Thirty minutes. Real impact. Millions of voices rising together.

**We're in this together — and we hope to see you Monday.**

---

*Ready to make your voice heard? Register now.*

If you include your phone number in your Mobilize registration, you will receive at text reminder regarding the event.

events.description:
At our Compost Hubs, food scraps collected from the community are transformed into nutrient-rich compost, and we need your help to make it happen! As a Compost Hub Support Volunteer, you’ll gain hands-on experience working alongside our knowledgeable Compost Managers. Get ready to leave feeling accomplished, a little sweaty, and brimming with new compost knowledge. 

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
Roll up your sleeves and dive into a variety of engaging activities, whether it’s managing a three-bin system, tending to a compost pile, sifting finished compost, or exploring a mix of everything. There’s something for everyone, from beginners to seasoned pros! Plus, our Compost Hubs are situated in LA County’s most cherished green spaces: community gardens, urban farms, and beautiful parks. Join passionate community composters, learn to turn food scraps into rich compost, and connect with the local food system. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You will be working outdoors! Shade levels vary by site.
* Activity level can be adjusted to your comfort and abilities—just communicate with your Compost Manager.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome!
* This site has public restrooms
* If you sign up, we ask that you show up! We rely on volunteers, like you, to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under the age of 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 

VOLUNTEER WAIVER: Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. You can access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver 

CODE OF CONDUCT: All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

Please register! When you register with Mobilize, and you complete the quick after event survey, you are counted in the total attending!  Please share information about this event with friends, family and neighbors!  We are stronger . . . together!

This is always a peaceful non-violent demonstration. Please observe these safety rules:

•	Do not block vehicles, bikes or pedestrians- always leave room for others to use the sidewalks!

•	Do not stand in bicycle lanes, traffic lanes, or the medians. 

•	Tread carefully around newly planted landscaping near the highway.

•	Do not block traffic entrances to businesses.

•	Do not block or repeatedly occupy the crosswalks and watch carefully for turning vehicles. Frequent use of crosswalks slows traffic and annoys the people we're trying to reach.

We request that attendees:
•	Please review this message and learn de-escalation skills at this [LINK](https://docs.google.com/document/d/17-y2xSNg-S3W6lCm3JyhAzdcgqLrit2aHsojAEmRO4I/edit?tab=t.0)

events.title: Saturday Stand Up
events.description:
Every Saturday, we stand on the curb and show our signs, count friendly beeps from passing cars and trucks.  And chat and get caught up with each other.  We have had about a dozen people lately, though we expect to have more this particular Saturday because of the problems in Minnesota.  The community to have a safe space to share our opinions.  

Our protest activity is lawful and safe.  The police know we are here because of my weekly emails to the liaison patrol officer.  We use the buddy system, so we are not out here alone.  We stay on the sidewalk.  We do not block the sidewalk.  We obey traffic rules.  We do not go on private property.  We do not do any violence or graffiti.  We remain aware of our surroundings and talk about what we see.  If someone approaches us to explain why we are stupid and wrong, we take one step away, turn partway toward them, and let them talk.  We do not respond, or if we feel compelled to respond, we say something neutral like “Have a nice day.”  Remaining excessively cheerful de-escalates many situations.  If something is escalating uncomfortably, some of us video, and some call 911.  And we help each other remember the rules.

events.title: ICTX Unload & Unwind
events.description:
"Unload & Unwind" is a low-pressure, conversational space for community members and local candidates to connect as real people. No stiff podiums, no formal debate clocks, and no rehearsed stump speeches.

We’re inviting local candidates to join our circle, share what’s on their minds, and honestly vent about the grueling campaign trail if they need to. For community members, it’s a rare chance to get to know the folks on your ballot outside of a high-stress town hall environment.
Come for the community, stay for the real talk, and leave the political pressure at the door.

### What to expect:

- **A Casual Circle:** A relaxed, roundtable-style layout where everyone is on the same level.
- **Real Conversations:** Time for candidates to unwind and share their perspectives, followed by casual, open-ended mixing and mingling.
- **A Safe Space:** This is a supportive environment focused on empathy, civic connection, and humanizing the people who step up to run for office.

Come as you are. Cameras on or off, pajamas or your evening gown, whatever helps you recharge. Let’s clear out the noise so we can stay in the fight for the long haul.

events.description:
When you sign up for this event, you’ll receive an email from **welcome@newletter.socialists.us** domain titled *“Instructions for the Upcoming SDA Zoom.”*

Please open it as soon as it arrives and acknowledge it. If you don’t see the email right away, be sure to check your spam folder.

Acknowledging this message is important — without it, you won’t be able to fully participate in our activities, since most of our coordination happens by email.

If you’re looking for the event at 7:30 PM **Pacific** Time, here’s the link: https://www.mobilize.us/socialists/event/893260

# Who are we?

We are a faction within the Democratic Party, and we consider ourselves both **Democrats** and **Socialists**.

**This group is not a space for discussing leaving the Democratic Party**. If that is your goal or perspective, this organization is probably not the right fit for you. 

We are active members of our local Democratic Clubs, and this space is dedicated to learning how to navigate and work effectively within the Democratic Party.

The agenda for the meeting is available here: https://socialists.us/direct/list/agenda?ZoomAgenda.

events.title: Know Your Rights with Law Enforcement on Campus
events.description:
Last year, universities and colleges begun signing agreements with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), granting campus police the authority to conduct immigration enforcement. Now, 11 out of the 12 Florida Public Universities have signed this agreement, along with 7 colleges, and more stating their intent to sign on.

This collaboration raises critical concerns for immigrant students, faculty, and staff, who may face increased surveillance, questioning, and even detainment on campus.

There has also been heavy policing around students exercising their first amendment right. Due to this, all students should attend ensure they know their rights.

This "Know Your Rights on Campus" training is designed to empower students, educators, and community members with the knowledge and tools to protect themselves and others.

Participants will learn: 
- Understanding the legal agreements between universities & ICE. 
- Your constitutional & legal rights regardless of status. 
- How to respond if approached by officers. 
- Where to find Emergency plans, legal resources, and how to support peers facing enforcement actions. 
- How to push back against harmful agreements and demand an end to university-ICE collaboration.

Knowledge is power. Knowing your rights helps protect your community and resist unjust enforcement on campus.

events.title: Stand Up To End Cost, Corruption and Chaos

She has remained steadfast in her support for the current administration’s egregious and harmful policies and actions. 

We now face a slide toward authoritarianism, a threat to life as we know it. But we are not powerless. As Americans, we still have our voices and our vote. Mid-terms are coming and we have a chance to vote Ann Wagner out of office, shifting the majority in Congress and saving our democracy. Now, more than ever, we must come together and say "no" to the harmful policies that Wagner has supported. 

This weekly protest began in early 2025. Until recently, it was known as the “Where’s Ann” event. We continue to meet weekly, regardless of the weather. We stand in solidarity as we send the message that Ann must be voted out. Bring your signs reflecting your own concerns or borrow ours. Now that the primary election is over, signs in support of specific candidates are appropriate. Indivisible St. Louis is endorsing Fred Wellman for U.S. Congress. This event is for everyone, regardless of where you live. Join us on Sundays, from 1-3 pm, at the corner of Manchester & Weidman. Help us Flip The Seats!

events.title: WIN PA8 from NYC - Ground Truth Deep Listening Canvass w/ Target Majority NYC
events.description:
Join Target Majority NYC (a local Indivisible & Swing Left Group) for a Ground Truth canvass in must-FLIP PA-08. A short carpool just 90 mins from NYC.  

NOTE: Please share your phone, or you will need to be proactive about getting yourself into a carpool using the instructions we send with your confirmation email from mobilize.
----

We are knocking every door and identifying persuadable voters who Dems normally don't contact, in order to elect Paige Cognetti in a true toss-up race in a Trump '24 district where she's recently demonstrated a 1-point lead.

To help Democrats rebuild trust, win tough races, and flip the House, Swing Left has launched an [innovative new program](https://ourgroundtruth.org) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- Knock on **every door** in the neighborhood, not just the voters campaigns usually talk to

- Have real conversations that **listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, identifying net new voters for the Democratic Party and candidates  

- Add these new voters' partisanship scores, likelihood to vote, and contact info directly into the Democrats' voter database so they will follow up with persuadable folks

- Gather insights to share with campaigns, so they can be responsive to people’s needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach

Don’t worry if it’s your first time—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we’re started early and will continue every year:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground. Likewise, we'll continue this important work through 2027 ahead of 2028. (And beyond.)

- *How we’ll go big:* knocking every door, not just the ones the voter database tells us to, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ internal conflicts around voting and around party affiliation, getting to the “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

**A core principle behind all Target Majority events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.**

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: Cease and Desist: Trademark & Activism
events.description:
A lawyer claiming to represent Democrats Abroad has sent us a cease-and-desist letter, which raises serious questions about the line between activism and trademark law.

https://socialists.us/docs/letters/2026-02-24-ParisDemAbroad-CeaseAndDesist.pdf

One of our members was previously sued by the Campbell Corporation for using its trademark in political speech. Now we are facing a similar situation.

Is this attempt by a Democrat living outside the United States an effort to intimidate Socialists who are Democrats abroad, and effectively block our Socialist candidate from receiving the 21 votes at the Democratic National Convention?

Should we push back against these entities and raise this issue at the next law or rules meeting? We could argue that Democrats Abroad, through this non-democratic behavior, is engaging in intimidation and should therefore forfeit its 21 votes.

This discussion is not only about how to respond to the cease-and-desist letter, but also about launching a broader conversation on the use of trademarks in political speech and the ownership of creative labor.

For reference: https://www.morganlewis.com/pubs/2025/11/campbells-stipulated-order-reinforces-trademark-protection-in-political-speech

events.title: Inspire America To Vote
events.description:
Voter engagement in America is at a critical crossroads. Today, nearly 100 million citizens who are eligible to vote are not participating in our democracy. That is nearly half of all eligible voters sitting on the sidelines, their voices unheard in shaping the future of our country. This represents not just lost opportunities, but a deep challenge for the health of our democracy. Many of these citizens feel disconnected, frustrated, or overwhelmed by the voting process, while others may simply not realize the power their participation holds. Whatever the reason, the result is the same: millions of Americans are not contributing to decisions that affect their communities, their families, and the nation as a whole.

The goal of Inspire America To Vote is to address this challenge head-on. We believe that voter engagement is not just about encouraging people to cast a ballot—it is about fostering meaningful conversations that can inspire, educate, and empower those who have not yet taken that step. To do this effectively, we must equip ourselves with the tools, strategies, and confidence to engage in productive dialogue with non-voting citizens. It requires understanding their concerns, breaking down barriers, and showing them that their participation matters.

This event is designed to help you become a more effective advocate for civic engagement. We will explore how to connect with people in ways that are respectful, motivating, and action-oriented. By learning to communicate the importance of voting and inspiring those around us, we can transform apathy into action and ensure that more voices are represented in our democracy. Every conversation counts, and together we can help close the gap between eligible citizens and active voters, strengthening the foundation of our democratic process for generations to come.

This is our moment to step up, engage, and inspire. The work we do here will ripple across communities, turning potential into participation, and apathy into action.

Inspire America To Vote will feature a diverse lineup of guest speakers and motivational leaders provided by [Keynote Speaker](https://keynotespeakers.info/) and [Motivational Speaker](https://motivationalspeakerz.com/) who bring years of experience in civic engagement, community organizing, and voter advocacy. These speakers have worked directly with communities across the country, helping non-voters understand the power of their voice and how they can make a meaningful impact through participation. Their insights will provide attendees with real-world strategies for engaging citizens who have historically been disengaged from the voting process. Each speaker brings a unique perspective, from grassroots organizers who have successfully mobilized local neighborhoods, to national experts who have shaped voter outreach campaigns on a larger scale.

Motivational speakers will also play a central role in the event, inspiring attendees to take action in their own communities. These speakers understand the psychological barriers that prevent people from voting—apathy, distrust, confusion—and they will share practical techniques for addressing these challenges with empathy and effectiveness. Through stories of personal experience, case studies, and actionable advice, attendees will leave with a renewed sense of purpose and the confidence to motivate others to participate in democracy.

The sessions will focus not only on theory but on applied best practices. Speakers will break down successful outreach methods, from leveraging social networks and community relationships to using persuasive communication techniques that resonate with individuals across diverse demographics. Attendees will gain hands-on knowledge in facilitating conversations about civic responsibility, addressing objections, and encouraging first-time voters to engage with the process.

In addition to formal presentations, the event will include interactive workshops and Q&A sessions, allowing attendees to directly learn from experts and explore how to tailor strategies to their own communities. These opportunities for dialogue will ensure that participants leave equipped with both the knowledge and practical tools needed to implement voter engagement initiatives effectively.

By combining motivational inspiration with concrete expertise, Inspire America To Vote will provide a comprehensive learning experience. Attendees will not only be energized by the speakers’ passion but will also walk away with clear, actionable steps they can take immediately to reach non-voting citizens. This event is designed to create a ripple effect—arming committed individuals with the skills, strategies, and motivation necessary to strengthen voter participation and ensure that every eligible citizen understands the power and importance of their voice in shaping the future of our country.

events.title: Calling All Resistance Knitters/Crocheters - Melt the Ice Hat Knit-In
events.description:
In the 1940s, Norwegians quietly defied Nazi occupation by knitting and wearing red, pointed hats with tassels. A simple garment became an act of protest.

More recently, knitters in Minnesota revived this tradition during a surge of ICE activity—using red hats as a visible sign of solidarity and resistance.

We carry that work forward here. Proceeds from the sale of our patterns and finished hats and bandanas are donated to CASA de Maryland, supporting immigrant communities through advocacy and assistance.

Join us as we knit, crochet, sew and craft in solidarity. We will keep gathering—as long as there is a need to resist.

🧶 **Resistance Knit-In (Ongoing)**  
📅 **When:** Sundays (ongoing)  
⏰ **Time:** 2–4 pm  
📍 **Where:** The Shops at Kenilworth – Common Area  

**How:** Supplies if you have them for the Melt the Ice Hat, Pin or Baltimore Bandana and/or the Blue Wave Hat . Knit and crochet patterns can be found on Ravelry. Beginners welcome, and supplies may be available to share.

Get ready to leave feeling accomplished, a little sweaty, and brimming with new compost knowledge. 

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
Roll up your sleeves and dive into a variety of engaging activities; whether it’s managing a three-bin system, tending to a compost pile, sifting finished compost, or exploring a mix of everything. There’s something for everyone, from beginners to seasoned pros! Plus, our Compost Hubs are situated in LA County’s most cherished green spaces: community gardens, urban farms, and beautiful parks. Join passionate community composters, learn to turn food scraps into rich compost, and connect with the local food system. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You will be working outdoors! Shade levels vary by site.
* Activity level can be adjusted to your comfort and abilities; just communicate with your Compost Manager.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome!
* This site has public restrooms
* If you sign up, we ask that you show up! We rely on volunteers, like you, to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under the age of 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 

VOLUNTEER WAIVER: Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. Access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver

CODE OF CONDUCT: All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

events.description:
Join your neighbors each week at the intersection of Baltimore Pike & Route 320 (southeast corner of Springfield Mall property) as we stand up for constitutional government and the rule of law.

Many in our community are concerned about actions by the Trump administration that they believe undermine congressional authority, democratic norms, and long-standing constitutional principles. We gather to peacefully affirm that the United States is a republic governed by laws - not by any one individual.

**When & where**
We meet weekly at the intersection of Baltimore Pike & Route 320. We remain on public sidewalks and do not block traffic.  Please bring signs or flags if you’d like.

**Our values**
This is a peaceful, nonviolent event. We ask all participants to engage respectfully, avoid confrontation, help de-escalate any tensions, and follow all local laws and safety guidance.
	
Everyone who supports constitutional democracy and peaceful civic engagement is welcome.

**Transportation**
We encourage public transportation to the intersection via bus or trolley.  If you drive, please do not use the Mall's parking lot. There is plentiful free parking on nearby residential streets such as Sheffield Drive (one block northeast) or Cedar, Walnut, and Ogden Avenues (two blocks south).

events.description:
QPP is an action-oriented community for queers and allies joined together in solidarity, providing mutual aid-based survival work — rooted in principles of racial justice, gender justice, disability justice, economic justice and class justice — and creating a place of true belonging and community.

🌈

Here are our group norms:

Respect Worth/Dignity: We respect the worth and dignity of others and that guides our interactions with everyone in the group.

Intent: We assume others are acting with good intent. If someone says or does something insensitive or hurtful, we help them learn.

Accountability: We know that we can all make mistakes, and we endeavor to act with grace to acknowledge them and repair any damage done.

Embrace Growth Mindset: We strive to see mistakes or conflicts as opportunities to learn and grow.

Intergenerational Respect: We acknowledge that, while the lived experiences of group members of various ages will differ, we will give everyone's thoughts and actions due consideration. No one is too young or too old to contribute or to have great ideas.

Confidentiality: We agree that stories stay and learning leaves. We can apply what we learn from others in the group, we cannot share their stories.

Step Forward/Step Back: We strive to promote equitable participation in the group using the "step forward/step back" framework. If you frequently speak up in conversations, consider stepping back to make room for other voices. If you typically remain quiet in conversations, consider stepping forward to make your voice heard.

Leadership Rotates: We do not have a hierarchical structure. Working groups (including leadership!) are all made up of volunteers, and involvement in them is not set in stone. If you want to be involved in a working group, please let someone in that group know. (Planning consists of volunteers.) Choose how you best think you can contribute, and let someone know.

## The Power of Talking with Voters
With 8 years of experience on the frontline of innovation, Swing Blue Alliance is your go-to for taking effective action in the upcoming midterm elections.  

### Don't miss our featured presentations! 

- Join us on the ground with Lisa Pedulla, SBA, NH Lead, in purple NH for an update on how conversations at the door are moving the needle - with both Democrats AND Republicans!
- With Election Day just around the corner, see how special attention is being paid to critical competitive races.  Hear about calling opportunities from the SBA phone bank team that are available across Maine, Pennsylvania, and North Carolina – to ensure every voter turns out to flip Congress, defeat Susan Collins, and flip the Pennsylvania State Senate.

- Swing Blue Alliance co-lead Susan Labandibar will share findings from the AI Visibility Project, and what the project has learned about improving the accuracy and completeness of candidate information online.

We’ll also share concrete ways to put your time and energy to work before Election Day. The Frontline Update runs from 10:00–10:30 AM ET.

This is a focused, 30-minute meeting designed to deliver high-impact updates quickly and clearly, followed by optional time for Q&A.

---


## Frontline Update 
**Where grassroots volunteers get informed, inspired, and mobilized**

The Frontline Update is Swing Blue Alliance’s monthly virtual gathering for volunteers across the country who are ready to turn urgency into action.

Each month, we bring you inside the work that’s shaping the next elections — and the future beyond them.

### What You’ll Get

**The Latest on Key Races**  
Hear directly from campaign leaders, partner organizations, and Swing Blue Alliance team leads about the most critical state and local races on the horizon. From state Supreme Courts to House of Delegate races to emerging battlegrounds, you’ll learn what’s at stake — and why it matters now.

**Campaign Spotlights**  
We regularly highlight election campaigns where early volunteer engagement can make a decisive difference. You’ll meet candidates, organizers, and grassroots partners building power in places that are too often overlooked.

**Clear, Immediate Actions**  
We don’t just talk about strategy — we plug you in. Whether it’s canvassing, phone banking, postcarding, fundraising, protest organizing, or message testing, you’ll leave every meeting with concrete ways to take action.

**The Bigger Strategy**  
The Frontline Update connects the dots between today’s volunteer opportunities and our long-term strategy to defend democracy, protect voting rights, and build durable Democratic power.

### Who It’s For

- New volunteers looking for a place to start  
- Experienced organizers ready for their next assignment  
- Grassroots leaders who want to stay aligned and informed  
- Anyone who believes democracy is worth fighting for  

Whether you can give an hour a week or lead a team, this is where you find your place in the fight.

---

**Join the next Frontline Update and be part of what comes next.**

events.title: Together We Sing
events.description:
Join us each Thursday evening 6:00-7:00

With all that is going on in our world, human beings are challenged to the core, and our nervous systems are in overdrive. There is so much fear, anger, and ranting about what people are against and what others are doing that is ruining our lives. Against-energy is exhausting! I'm weary from the pounding of toxic negativity. I am for Peace on Earth and Goodwill to ALL! I want to know what you are for. From the deepest place of integrity, human dignity, and decency, what are you for? We cannot think, feel, or act from our deepest selves when our nervous systems are ragged with hyper-stimulation. I want to create a place for people to gather as a community with the common desire to feel welcome, safe, and to nourish our nervous systems.

I am a singer, singing coach, and rhythm circle facilitator. I envision gathering in a circle as friends, with the common ground of being human, and singing in a way that soothes our nervous systems and lifts our spirits.

You don't need to have a "great" voice or read music. I will teach you simple and beautiful songs. When we sing together, our breathing regulates, and the vibration created in our singing works together to shift the nervous system out of fight-flight-freeze into rest, digest, and coherence (the quality of forming a unified whole)... community!

I weave a spirit of play, rhythm, and movement into my teaching.

Interesting fact: Play is as vital to survival as food and water. The Science of Play, by Stuart Brown

 

Cullie Treichler

events.title: States Win Yolo Virtual Phonebank!
events.description:
Join States Win Yolo every Monday at 2pm PT to elect Democrats in majority making State Legislature districts!

Meet our candidates: **Mai Xiong,** **Stephanie Simacek,** **Michelle Kang,** and **April Cook!**

Reelecting **Mai Xiong** to Michigan's State House District 13 is essential to building a Democratic trifecta in Michigan in 2026.

**Stephanie Simacek** is running for re-election in Arizona State House, District 2! LD 2 is one of the most competitive and consequential battlegrounds in Arizona, making Stephanie’s reelection critical to maintaining and expanding Democratic power in 2026. 

We'll also be making calls for **Michelle Kang** to pick up a new Democratic seat in Georgia House District 99. Michelle Kang is a small business owner, first-generation immigrant, and community leader. She came within 621 votes of flipping the district in 2024, and she's running to finish the job this year. 

**April Cook** is looking to flip North Carolina State Senate District 34! She has spent her career making healthcare accessible for NC residents. Now, she wants to chip away at the Republican supermajority in the State Senate to protect healthcare, reproductive rights, and public education.  

**Why phonebank:** The data proves it: phonebanking is THE BEST volunteering option for remote voter contact. We identify supporters and let them know why their vote matters, speak with undecided voters, and recruit local volunteers. Every call helps us clean our lists, which makes for a faster, more efficient phonebank!

**Come one, come all:** No experience necessary. Each Zoom phonebank includes training and check-ins for first-timers (experienced callers can jump right in). Our veteran phonebank leaders will help you get comfortable, increase your effectiveness, and make sure you have a great experience.

events.description:
At our Compost Hubs, food scraps collected from the community are transformed into nutrient-rich compost, and we need your help to make it happen! There’s something for everyone, from beginners to seasoned pros! Plus, our Compost Hubs are situated in LA County’s most cherished green spaces: community gardens, urban farms, and beautiful parks. Join passionate community composters, learn to turn food scraps into rich compost, and connect with the local food system.

events.title: 6th Ave Bridge Bannering Over I-5
events.description:
There is street parking, but a lot of it is metered; Linda will have quarters with her on the bridge in case you need some.  There aren't meters on the bridge itself so try to nab a spot there first. 

We provide large physical messaging in the real world to connect with and activate voters to demonstrate that resistance is possible. Bring a sign for cars on the bridge or just wave to the cars passing below. You can also bring a flag, chair, bubbles, music, or anything else you want in order to have a good time!

Rules and Protocols

1. We avoid doing anything that could either harm ourselves or anyone else. This includes stepping into traffic, holding a sign where it could fall onto cars below, climbing fencing, etc.

2. We must not block pedestrian and bike traffic, so please keep the middle of the overpass and/or sidewalk clear to allow them to pass.

3. We supply the messages, you supply the waves. However, you are welcome to also display your own poster boards. Just avoid any messaging that would be rated above a PG-13.

4. We don’t litter. If we find litter, we pick it up and throw it away.

5. We don’t use stickers or anything that leaves a permanent mark on the overpass. However, chalk is okay and even encouraged.

6. If someone from the ‘opposition’ comes up to talk with us, do not engage with them. Best to just ignore them. One member will be designated to handle them and video record any aggressive interaction so that you can go right on waving.

7. We take lots of pictures and videos during our action for circulation on social media. If you prefer not to be included, please let us know and/or consider wearing a mask.

8. Should law enforcement pay us a visit, only the designated point person from the group should address them.

9. Ignore the middle fingers and negativity coming from some of the cars below. For every one of those confused folks, you are providing hope to another 100 people!

10. The Visibility Brigade is a non-violent, informal volunteer group in which we all participate with an understanding that our own actions are our personal responsibility and we accept our own personal liability. You participate with this understanding.

Feel free to reach out to VisibilityBrigadeSanDiego@gmail.com with any questions.

events.description:
Learn how decentralized finance (DeFi) works and explore how crypto rewards can be used to build a long-term Bitcoin and Ethereum portfolio.

Join RuneHold for a beginner-friendly virtual workshop exploring DeFi, blockchain governance, and practical cryptocurrency portfolio strategies.

Through real-world examples from RuneHold's daily Bitcoin and Ethereum accumulation process, participants will learn how decentralized financial systems operate and how governance rewards can fit into a broader digital asset strategy.

What you'll learn:

• DeFi fundamentals: Understand decentralized finance, blockchain networks, and how digital assets interact.

• Governance and rewards: Explore how systems such as Aquarius, AQUA, and ICE enable participation in decentralized governance and reward mechanisms.

• From rewards to Bitcoin and Ethereum: See how DeFi rewards can be converted into BTC and ETH through a structured accumulation approach.

• Long-term portfolio strategy: Learn about diversification, risk management, and the importance of consistency when navigating cryptocurrency markets.

• Real-world examples: Examine how RuneHold documents and evaluates its ongoing DeFi strategy.

Who should attend?

This workshop is designed for beginners, cryptocurrency enthusiasts, and anyone interested in understanding DeFi beyond buying and holding digital assets.

No prior DeFi experience is required.

Register to reserve your place.

This workshop is for educational purposes only and does not provide personalized financial or investment advice. Cryptocurrency and DeFi activities involve substantial risks, including potential loss of funds.

Local school boards play a critical role in shaping the future of our schools. Decisions about funding, curriculum, and policy directly impact students, families, and communities. 

Families for Strong Public Schools is expanding its School Board Monitoring Program statewide and is looking for engaged community members to help promote transparency, accountability, and student-centered decision-making. 

This program empowers volunteers to attend school board meetings, observe discussions, and submit brief monthly reports on key issues, including: 
-Budget allocations and funding priorities 
-Curriculum and instructional policies 
-Community engagement and transparency 

We need advocates who are willing to show up, pay attention, and help ensure decisions are made in the best interest of students and families. 

Why Get Involved? 

By participating, you can: 
-Speak up for students and families 
-Monitor whether funding and curriculum decisions meet the needs of all students Support transparency, equity, and strong public education 

Your voice matters. 

When communities show up, school boards listen. Together, we can help ensure local decisions reflect the values and priorities of the people they serve. Let’s build a stronger future for our students right here in Clay County—one meeting at a time.

events.title: Phone Bank for Gina for Texas
events.description:
Join us for weekly Virtual Phone Banks on Monday and Wednesday nights from 6pm to 8pm, hosted by the Fair Shot PAC as we work to elect Gina Hinojosa for Governor AND competitive State House campaigns across Texas. It’s up to us to make sure that when Gina is elected, she has State Representatives who want to work with her to fight for working class Texans! 

In response to popular demand, we are expanding our volunteer phone bank to another night to increase volunteer opportunities. Please help spread the word by inviting your friends.

Log on from a computer at home, and use your cell phone to call voters to tell them about Gina's labor endorsed, people-powered campaign for a Texas that works for working people, not billionaires. 

You will need a computer and cell phone for this process. Headphones and/or a quiet space where you can put your phone on speaker are strongly encouraged but not required. 

A full training will be provided ahead of each phonebank. The zoom link will be available upon RSVP! 

Fair Shot PAC is a state PAC working to elect pro-labor and pro-union candidates who will fight to give Texas workers a fair shot inside the Capitol in Austin.

events.title: Woodburn Has the Most Detentions Per Capita in Oregon. Join Woodburn Indivisible!
events.description:
We're just a group of neighbors who couldn't look away while our neighbors are being disappeared. 

Woodburn has the most detentions per capita in the entire state of Oregon. Over 100 souls have been disappeared.

In a place where most of us are at-risk of detention, it falls to the rest of us to look out for our neighbors.

Join our little, dedicated family of Woodburn and North Marion County neighbors determined to help our communities cope with the damage caused by ICE.

Don't have much time? We have impactful actions that will take a minimum of your time but yield powerful results.

Not a joiner? Neither are we but we just couldn't sit back and do nothing while the world around us crumbles. Join us anyway.

We welcome newcomers and are totally open to new and creative ideas. We are a new chapter that really needs all hands on deck. We are a warm, friendly group with a tight focus on problem-solving.

Email WoodburnIndivisible@Yahoo.com with any questions. A friendly human will patiently answer your questions and tell you our meeting times and locations. Join us!

events.title: Virtual Phone Bank for Marcy Kaptur!
events.description:
Come join Team Kaptur as we make phone calls to help re-elect Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur! 

We know this is going to be another really tough cycle. This is one of only four Democrat-held toss-up seats in the entire country. The race for this R+5 district is a toss-up because Marcy outperforms typical democrats, but we need to talk to as many voters as possible before they decide who they will vote for.

This race will help decide the House majority, and we want you to join us in this campaign to win in November.

We will begin the phone bank with simple training where you will learn how to make the calls and what our goals are for the day. Whether you are a seasoned volunteer leader or you are brand new and participating for the first time, we are happy to have you join the team.

events.description:
Join Us: A Feast for All
Inspired by the timeless wisdom that "the rich and the poor meet together; the Lord is the Maker of them all," we invite you to an event celebrating community, compassion, and shared humanity.
We believe in opening our hands and our hearts, especially to those who are often overlooked. Just as we are called to "invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind" to our feasts, and to "open your mouth for the mute, for the rights of all who are destitute," this gathering is a testament to our commitment to judge righteously and defend the rights of the poor and needy.
This isn't just about charity; it's about building a world where no one's heart is hardened, and no hand is shut against a brother or sister in need. We remember the words, "He has distributed freely; he has given to the poor; his righteousness endures forever."
Come, let's share a meal, share stories, and share our collective hope for a more inclusive future. Because if a brother or sister is poorly clothed and lacking in daily food, simply saying, “Go in peace, be warmed and filled,” isn't enough. It’s time to act, together.?

events.title: Messaging Storm - Weekly Calls to Congress
events.description:
## Messaging Storm
 
### November 4, 2026

**A coordinated call to our Elected Officials**

U.S. Capitol Switchboard

(202) 224-3121

### Background

** Protect our Elections**

The Trump administration has been falsely sowing seeds of election fraud for nearly a decade. They have grabbed 2020 election information from Georgia, demanded voter rolls from numerous states, tried to ban mail-in voting, threatened to send federal agents to polling places, and preemptively sued states like Alaska and California to cast doubt on the legitimacy of the elections in those states. Voter fraud is statistically very low, and yet the Trump administration is still perpetuating lies that the 2020 election was stolen from him, that non-citizens voting sways elections towards democrats, and the only way democrats win is by cheating. All these claims are unfounded. We need Congress and our State Officials to protect our elections from these false claims.      

### Call Script

 **adapted from [5calls.org](https://5calls.org/issue/state-voter-records-election-interference/)**

**_Please be vigilant in your state and make adjustments based on current events. Be prepared to mobilize if needed._**

Hi, my name is [NAME] and I’m a constituent from [CITY/STATE].

I’m calling to express my concerns about the Trump administration’s ongoing interference with our election systems. I ask that [REP/SEN/GOV] defend the integrity of our elections not only in our state but to defend every state’s constitutional authority to run their election without Federal interference. 

Thank you for your time and consideration.

**Leave full address if leaving a voicemail so your opinion is tallied.**

events.description:
Overpass Visibility Actions Every Week!

Join us to remind people that democracy is on the line. Meet up on local Lancaster, PA, overpasses. Overpass messages change each week based on current events AND the enduring themes we need to remember.

The current regime is a menace, throwing kerosene on every fire. Cruel detention and deportation continues, the MAGA budget cuts critical supports for medical care and nutrition just to give huge tax breaks to those who have enough. Extremists in government are trying to avoid accountability by gutting voting rights and rigging voting districts. And the corruption and cronyism threatens all of us. It can seem like so much; it can seem hopeless. And yet, our neighbors need to know we RESIST this. That we are standing up, and we are the majority. We always need to encourage nonviolence in that effort.

Each week we stand up for vocal, peaceful, resistance. This message is a mantra of hope and determination that we can hold and share with each other in even our darkest moments. The message should be seen and heard EVERYWHERE–join us! 

Indivisibles and friends will gather on local Lancaster overpasses. Location details will be sent after registration. At each location there is sufficient parking. Indivisible LT will provide letters for the slogan to hold and flags. Feel free to bring your own signs as well. We recommend using LARGE letters, keeping it civil, and brief.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

There is a private room indoors for us to socialize, and when weather allows, we may choose to gather outdoors in the courtyard. Either location provides an environment where we can gather, unwind and enjoy, all while getting to know each other as Indivisible members.

Special discounted happy hour pricing is available until only 5 p.m., although we generally stay until 6.

This is a happy hour for citizens concerned about what the current regime is doing to our country. It’s a safe space to come together and to speak freely about what is going on in national, state and local politics.

Who can come? This is for everyone, from the politically curious to the terminally plugged-in, to have real conversations with your neighbors and maybe to hatch some plans. As this is a casual neighborhood meetup, come as you are.

There will be information about ways to get involved in your community both to understand and to resist the growing authoritarianism we see happening at a national level and how it affects us here.

Join Southern Resistance Coalition and Indivisible Southern Action Network for a peaceful protest every Saturday from 12-2 pm in front of the Oak Ridge Library.

- Bring a friend! The more the merrier.
- Bring a sign, or borrow one of our extras.
- You’re welcome to bring a chair.
- Stay the whole time or stop and show support as long as you’re able.
- Please stay out of the street at all times & only cross at crosswalks.

We believe the power of the people is stronger than the people in power, and that we are stronger together.

One way we build our strength is with our weekly Defending Democracy protests. Beyond just exercising our First Amendment rights every week we also use that time to share info, make connections, learn and educate others, collect and distribute food and local resources, and show solidarity with groups who don’t feel safe coming out to protest.

By focusing on keeping our neighbors safe, fed, connected, and informed, we can build the foundation of care and resilience vital for sustained resistance and thriving as a community. We take care of each other, we stand together.

Hope to see you Saturday!

events.title: Justice 4 All Thursdays
events.description:
Justice 4 All Thursdays and Greater Assabet Indivisible Network (GAIN) invite you to stand in solidarity with immigrants and resistance to ICE and their cruel and lawless detention of our neighbors Thursdays from 11am-1pm. Regardless of any other political views you may hold, please join us in non-violent protest to demand Justice for all.

We are unaffiliated, but very much aligned, with other groups that demonstrate in Burlington. Our goal is to add to the total number of hours that citizens stand in non-violent opposition to the deplorable detainment conditions at this location. If you have been to Bearing Witness on Wednesdays, we would love to have you at Justice 4 All Thursdays.

Location: 
ICE Enforcement & Removal Operations Office
1000 District Avenue Burlington MA 01803

Schedule:
11:00-11:30 Welcome; music; announcements
11:30-12:30 Stand with signs along District Ave
12:30-1:00 Optional short march down to Mall Rd.

What happens at this ICE office?
ICE personnel depart from District Ave. in unmarked vans with tinted windows on missions to abduct immigrants across New England. Immigrants may also show up at the office for appointments. The facility on District Ave was never intended to be a detention center, yet immigration lawyers and media interviews reveal that people are being housed here in conditions that have been called “abysmal” and “unsanitary.”

What to expect at Justice 4 All?
We are committed to nonviolence, and we stand peacefully with signs outside the facility. We do not block the entrance, we do not physically approach ICE agents as they walk to/from the parking lot, and we do not block traffic on District Ave.

communities’ in our Villages, Cities, States, Countries, and the World, “We

events.description:
Join the Cabarrus County Senior Democrats in person in Concord for our monthly meeting every third Thursday (except July) from 6 to 7:30 pm. Doors open at 5:30 pm and Zoom begins at 6.

Zoom link and agenda is provided to registered guests upon sign up; shortly after you submit the sign up form, you will receive a Mobilize confirmation email. Please keep this.

We have amazing speakers and our six upcoming guests for our October meeting are our County Commissioner candidates; newcomer with quite a following from both sides, Daniel Redding; former Senior Democrat of the Year, our own Ingrid Nurse; and Indivisible leader and CCSD member, Phil Henry, whose terrific slogan is: Old Guy-New Voice!

Also joining us are our awesome School Board candidates including incumbent Pam Escobar; Mishell Williams running for the second time after a close race which faced interference by Cabarrus GOP’s nepotism and shenanigans! Courtney Steinberg, member of CCDP and former treasurer of the party is also vying for one of the three open seats on the board.

Last month we hosted Congressional District 8 Candidate, Colby Watson. Also, the House District 82 candidate, Chris Bishopp, and April Cook for Senate 34 joined us, plus our resident elections guru, Martin Ericson, explained what we need to know for this November 3 and why voting early is your best bet.
If you missed this meeting, links to the videos of their talks will be in our special election Oct/Nov issue of our newsletter.

Voting CCSD members must be registered Democrats age 50 and up, but we welcome all like- minded neighbors to listen, learn and connect.

Our focus for the 2026 midterms is to build our ranks through outreach and sharing our institutional memory with others including people new to our area and younger activists because Experience plus Energy Equals Power! 

Never forget, we were the ones who marched for civil rights, integrated public schools, built Medicare, protested a war, formed unions, fought for women’s rights, protected our planet and so much more! We won’t allow this administration to erase all we have achieved!
 
Let’s share our motto: We Have a Moral Authority That No One Else Can Claim!

Annual contribution is $20, $5 of which goes to the NC Senior Democrats which makes you a state member, too. To join or to contribute any amount, [click here](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/donation-form/become-a-member--2026) and make a single or recurring contribution.

Congress has the power to fix our broken immigration system by protecting Dreamers and asylum seekers, improving application processing, investing in smarter border security, reducing detention, and addressing the root causes that force people to flee.

Can you take one minute to send a message to your members of Congress and urge them to champion immigration reform rooted in dignity, safety, and justice?

events.title: Pass the Women's Health Protection Act and Protect Abortion
events.description:
Since the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade, millions of women, girls, trans people, and nonbinary people have been denied the freedom to make decisions about their own bodies, families, and futures. Abortion bans are forcing survivors to give birth, worsening maternal health outcomes, pushing people deeper into poverty, and causing massive economic harm.

Congress has the power to act. Please take one minute to send a letter urging your members of Congress to co-sponsor and support the Women’s Health Protection Act and defend reproductive freedom for all.

events.title: Tell your member of Congress to co-sponsor and support the Freedom to Vote Act and the John Lewis Vo
events.description:
For too long, wealthy special interests, voter suppressors, and partisan power grabs have weakened our democracy and made it harder for everyday people, especially Black and Brown communities, senior citizens, people with disabilities, low-income communities, and disenfranchised people, to have an equal voice.

Congress can help protect voting rights, stop election sabotage, reduce the power of big money, and restore key protections of the Voting Rights Act by passing the Freedom to Vote Act and the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act.

Please take one minute to send a letter urging your members of Congress to co-sponsor and support these critical democracy protection bills.

events.title: Protect Free Speech from Government Suppression
events.description:
The First Amendment protects our right to speak, dissent, organize, protest, and learn without fear of government retaliation. When any administration targets immigrants, students, journalists, universities, or everyday people for their views, it threatens the foundation of our democracy.

Please take one minute to send a message urging your members of Congress to defend free speech, protect dissent, and stop government suppression of our constitutional rights.

events.title: Tell Congress: Stop the Medical Debt Crisis
events.description:
No one in America should die, delay care, or go bankrupt because they cannot afford to see a doctor. Yet millions of people are still trapped by high costs, medical debt, denied care, and restrictive insurance networks.

Congress has the power to change that by passing Medicare for All and guaranteeing health care as a right, not a privilege.

Please take one minute to send a message urging your senators and representatives to co-sponsor and support the Medicare for All Act.

events.title: Tell Congress: Expand the Supreme Court, create term limits, and institute a code of ethics.

The Supreme Court has enormous power over our voting rights, civil rights, reproductive freedom, climate protections, and democracy. When lifetime appointments, ethics concerns, and political extremism weaken public trust, Congress has a responsibility to act.

Please take one minute to send a message urging your member of Congress to support Supreme Court reform, including expanding the Court, creating term limits, and establishing a binding code of ethics to protect equal justice and the rule of law.

events.title: Tell Congress: Protect the Vote. Defend the People’s Voice.
events.description:
The freedom to vote is the foundation of democracy. It is how we choose leaders, shape our future, and hold power accountable to the people.

But that freedom is under attack. Across the country, politicians and extremists are working to spread distrust in elections, intimidate election workers, restrict access to the ballot, and weaken the systems that allow every eligible voter to have a voice.

We cannot wait until the next election to defend our rights. The time to protect our vote, our election workers, and our democracy is now.

We are calling on lawmakers at every level of government to champion laws that protect voting rights, defend election officials and volunteers, stop voter suppression, strengthen election security, and fully fund fair, accessible elections.

Our vote is our voice. Our voice is our power. And democracy only works when every eligible voter can participate freely, safely, and equally.

Please take one minute to send a letter to lawmakers and urge them to protect the freedom to vote.

events.title: Christina for Congress Phone Bank!
events.description:
Join Team Christina for Congress for one of our recurring phone banks!

Thursday, September 24th in the first day people can vote!  That day through Election Day, voters can go to their clerk's office and request an absentee ballot, and absentees will start arriving in mailboxes shortly thereafter. Voters can fill out their ballot and turn it in on the spot.  November 3rd is Election Day, but vast numbers will have already voted by then. 

That means we need to be talking with people encouraging them to vote early and helping them to realize Christina is their candidate for Congress.

Before running for Congress, Christina spent 10 years as an SVU prosecutor. That job is about showing up for people in the middle of the worst thing that's ever happened to them and making sure the system actually works for them. That's exactly who we need fighting for us in Congress to lower costs and end corruption.

events.title: Health Care Is a Human Right, Not a Luxury
events.description:
In the wealthiest nation on Earth, health care should never be a luxury reserved for those who can afford it. No one should be forced to choose between seeing a doctor, paying rent, buying groceries, or taking on medical debt just to survive. Yet every year, people in America suffer, delay care, go bankrupt, and die because our health care system puts profit before people.

Congress must act. We are calling on every member of Congress to co-sponsor and pass the Medicare for All Act so every person in the United States is guaranteed the care they need, when they need it. Medicare for All would save lives, lower costs, protect families from medical debt, and give people the freedom to choose their doctor without being trapped by restrictive networks or outrageous bills.

Health care is a human right. Send a message to Congress to build a healthcare system that puts people, dignity, and life ahead of corporate greed.
