events.title: Guarantee freedom for all and pass the Equality Act
events.description:
No one should be denied the basic right to live safely, openly, and equally.

Across the country, LGBTQIA+ people are facing escalating attacks from extremist politicians, state legislatures, and organizations determined to roll back civil rights. Congress has the power and responsibility to stop this discrimination.

The Equality Act would provide clear federal protections against discrimination and affirm that LGBTQIA+ rights are civil rights. This is about freedom, dignity, safety, and the promise that every person deserves equal protection under the law.

None of us are truly safe until everyone is safe.

Take action to urge Congress to pass the Equality Act and protect freedom for all.

events.title: We deserve to live in a community free of gun violence
events.description:
Everyone deserves to live in a community where they are safe from gun violence. We honor every life stolen, every family shattered, and every loved one left grieving by turning our pain into people-powered action.

Everyone who is eligible should be allowed to own a gun. However, our state and federal laws need to be updated to better define eligibility:

Require background checks on all gun sales and ammunition sales

Have a red flag law

Prevent domestic abusers from accessing guns

Ban assault weapons

Limit magazine capacity

Require concealed carry permits

Restrict open carry

Ban firearms in libraries, schools, and hospitals

Have a waiting period

Allow victims of gun violence to have their day in court and that gun manufacturers, sellers, and interest groups are not shielded from liability when acting with negligence and disregard for public safety.

Take action to support: We deserve a community free of gun violence

events.title: (Mon/Tue) Protest for Justice and Food Drive @ Burlington ICE Detention Center
events.description:
# Standout for Justice: Burlington ICE Detention Center

**Join us to stand in solidarity with those detained and to alert the community to the I.C.E. facility in Burlington.**

The conditions reported inside are inhumane: no due process, no mattresses, no showers, and minimal food. Your presence makes a tangible difference—immigrants have reported that seeing supporters outside transforms their spirit from fear to hope and confidence.

### **Event Details**
*   **Time:** 10:00 AM – 12:30 PM
*   **Location:** Meet on the green at **1000 District Ave, Burlington**.
*   **The Action:** We gather at 10:00 AM outside the facility to show direct support to those inside. Bring fod which will be distributed to immigrants leaving the facility.  
*   **The March:** Once we have enough participants, we will move as a group to **Burlington Mall Road** to raise public awareness of this facility. 

> **Important Note:** Please arrive at the 1000 District Ave location at the start. We move to the Mall Road as a group based on turnout; arriving early ensures you find the team and can participate in the march.

### **What to Bring**
*   **Food for the immigrants:** Shared items for those being released.
*   **Protection:** Sunscreen, a hat, and appropriate gear depending on the weather.
*   **Footwear:** Comfortable shoes for standing and walking.
*   **Signs:** We provide a small number of signs, but feel free to bring your own! **Note:** If you are bringing several signs, you can drop them off at 1000 District Ave first before parking.

### **Parking & Transportation**
**Please Read:** Parking at 1000 District Ave is strictly for customers; vehicles identified as belonging to protesters **will be towed**. 

*   **Safe parking and public transportation options will be provided via email once you register for the event.**

address_lines: LOOK FOR JAN'S YELLOW JEEP in the parking lot

events.description:
FOUR SILENT MARCHES. ONE MESSAGE is part of Good Trouble Indivisible’s ongoing regional Public Awareness Event Series across West Michigan.


GOOD TROUBLE INDIVISIBLE'S
           
                               — FOUR SILENT MARCHES. ONE MESSAGE. —

Good Trouble Indivisible will coordinate FOUR silent protest marches through downtown. PLEASE REGISTER.

We provide all signs. Please dress in black.

OUR PUBLIC AWARENESS SIGNS ILLUMINATE THE ADMINISTRATION'S

👉 CONSTITUTIONAL VIOLATIONS

👉 VOTER SUPPRESSION

👉 INDICATORS OF FASCISM

👉 ICE ATROCITIES

📍LOOK for Jan’s yellow Jeep close to the Town Hall in downtown @ 11:30 AM. The Marches will start promptly, so don't be late.
                                          

                                                    SCHEDULE:
⏰ 11:30 AM sign-in & sign pickup (We provide signs). Signs are not available once the lineup begins.

⏰ 11:45 AM LINEUP & Instructions You must be present for Lineup and Instructions to march.

⏰ March begins promptly at Noon

⏰ Event Concludes Around 2:00 PM

👉 Water and Protein Bars are provided by Good Trouble Indivisible
Participants will march silently in coordinated single-file formation through downtown in black clothing, carrying themed protest signs while accompanied only by the steady heartbeat drum.
Participants march silently and directly in line with the person in front of them, at a slow pace, emulating a funeral procession (death of our democracy). We do not acknowledge passersby. We look straight ahead and are expressionless. Our Safety team will lead and flank participants, ensuring safety and providing safe street crossings.
At designated points throughout the march, the formation stops, turns toward the storefronts and restaurants, and raises signs in silent witness before continuing forward.

No chanting.

No screaming.

No chaos.

Just silent, disciplined civic resistance.

This visual, disciplined style of protest has drawn attention across Michigan and around the US, from both viewers and groups interested in replicating Good Trouble Indivisible's model in their own communities. We continue to mentor groups to help them add this 4-March silent protest to their event schedule. Together, we are building a Civic Resistance Ecosystem as we create public awareness with our unique brand of silent marches.

WHAT TO WEAR: Participants wear black clothing.

IMPORTANT NOTES:

• This is a silent march.

• Please remain respectful of pedestrians and local businesses.

• Signs will be provided.

• Water & Protein Snacks will be provided.

• Comfortable walking shoes recommended.

Together we remain visible, peaceful, disciplined, and impossible to ignore.

Good Trouble Indivisible hosts marches at highly visible downtown public places throughout West Michigan and mentors Michigan groups and groups across the country to perform these marches to create public awareness.

We the people means ALL OF US.

events.title: Food Scraps Collection: Montrose Farmers' Market
events.description:
As a volunteer, you’ll be right in the action, collecting food scraps from market-goers—the first step in a crucial process that turns waste into nutrient-rich compost. These scraps, gathered at local markets, are then processed at nearby green parks or gardens. Throughout your shift, you'll be guided by an experienced LA Compost staff member, who will act as your Compost Manager, offering insights and helping you share the benefits of composting with the public. The best part is that during your volunteer shift, you can take some time to shop at the market. Join us and be part of the composting movement that's transforming LA—one food scrap at a time!

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
As a volunteer, you’ll play a hands-on role in guiding market-goers through composting, ensuring their food scraps are clean of stickers, compostable, and ready to be turned into nutrient-rich compost. You’ll monitor for contamination, assist with tracking data, and serve as a friendly, welcoming host to our composting community. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You'll be stationed at the LA Compost booth under a pop-up canopy within the farmers' market. There will also be seating available.
* You may be asked to assist with moving filled bins of material weighing 60+ pounds. We always offer team lifts; you will never be asked to lift bins if you prefer not to.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome. 
* Bathrooms are accessible at the Coffee Bean close by. 
* If you sign up, please show up! We rely on volunteers like you to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 
VOLUNTEER WAIVER: Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. Access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver

CODE OF CONDUCT: All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

You are invited to show your support for these messages and to encourage the public to do the same. Your presence is a powerful message! events.title: Compost Hub Support: Augustus Hawkins
events.description:
At our Compost Hubs, food scraps collected from the community are transformed into nutrient-rich compost, and we need your help to make it happen! As a Compost Hub Support Volunteer, you’ll gain hands-on experience working alongside our knowledgeable Compost Managers. Get ready to leave feeling accomplished, a little sweaty, and brimming with new compost knowledge. 

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
Roll up your sleeves and dive into a variety of engaging activities, whether it’s managing a three-bin system, tending to a compost pile, sifting finished compost, or exploring a mix of everything. There’s something for everyone, from beginners to seasoned pros! Plus, our Compost Hubs are situated in LA County’s most cherished green spaces: community gardens, urban farms, and beautiful parks. Join passionate community composters, learn to turn food scraps into rich compost, and connect with the local food system. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You will be working outdoors! Shade levels vary by site.
* Activity level can be adjusted to your comfort and abilities; just communicate with your Compost Manager.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome!
* This location has bathrooms available
* If you sign up, we ask that you show up! We rely on volunteers, like you, to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under the age of 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 

VOLUNTEER WAIVER 
Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. You can access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver 

CODE OF CONDUCT
All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

events.title: Constitutional Observer Training
events.description:
## _Do you know what to do if you see ICE in your community?_

**This 1-hour basic class will show you what to do if you happen to see immigration enforcement activity.** It’s like taking CPR training: you hope you’ll never need it, but it’s good to know what to do in case of an emergency.

**Topics include:**

* The role and responsibilities of a Constitutional Observer
* Key constitutional rights relevant to observation and documentation
* How to use the V.I.D.E.O. framework for clear, consistent reporting
* How to identify immigration agents
* Best practices for personal safety and non-interference

This training was developed by Indivisible Eastside, Seattle Indivisible and West Seattle Indivisible, with support from ACLU-WA and WAISN.

**You can sign up and bring a friend with you to this training!** Just indicate the total number of people that you will be bringing in the "Are you signing up a group?" field when registering.

Join Indivisible San Mateo for conversation and conviviality and a no-host lunch at the The Terraces food court at Hillsdale Mall in San Mateo on Saturdays, from 11:30 to 12:45 p.m.

Look for us at the northwest table with a sign posted on the wall by the table so you can see us.

The lunch is open to everyone connected with Indivisible San Mateo and will take place prior to our weekly Saturday street protests from 1 to 2:30 p.m., around the corner on El Camino at East 31st Avenue. On the street, we'll be enjoying not only the very popular music of The Freedom Strummers but also the company of pro-democracy friends and the cacophonous sounds of solidarity from the passing honking horns.

The Terrace Dining area is on the second floor at the north end of the Mall, accessible by escalator and elevator. Our table is across from the elevator in front of the big windows in the northwest corner of the food court.

There's ample parking at the Mall, lots of seating and lots of lunch options for those dining at one of the places in the food court. The restaurants include Sarku Japan; Tacos E. Grullens; Hakata Kuro Obi Ramen; and Panda Express, among others. Shake Shack is downstairs and there's a Starbucks nearby.

Reservations are not necessary and all are welcome, whether for lunch or dessert or just fellowship for members of Indivisible San Mateo. All are encouraged to be part of the rally afterward on El Camino around the corner.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Ground Truth Weekly Campaign Call
events.description:
### Join Ground Truth volunteers and volunteer leaders from across the country for our weekly campaign update call.

Every week, we'll come together to hear what we're learning from conversations with voters, celebrate your achievements, share conversation best practices, and get the latest updates on Ground Truth's strategy and goals.

Whether you're signed up to knock on your first door or led dozens of canvasses already, this call is your opportunity to connect with fellow action takers, learn from organizers across the country, and see how your efforts fit into our larger mission to build Democratic power through deep listening voter conversations.

**Each call includes:**

- Campaign progress report outs and program news
- Volunteer and team recognition
- Stories and lessons from voter conversations in the field
- Tips to strengthen your Ground Truth conversation skills
- Upcoming volunteer opportunities and ways to get involved

Ground Truth is built on listening, learning, and growing together. Join us each week to stay connected, sharpen your organizing skills, and help shape the future of this campaign.

Gather: Every Wednesday - 8:30 AM (so we are in place before court convenes)
Court starts: around 9:00 AM
Court ends: between 10:30 and 11:00 AM

Why this matters:
ICE has stepped up enforcement in Robertson County. Families are being separated. Neighbors who have lived here for years are being pulled into deportation proceedings. Our presence at the courthouse, peaceful, visible, and consistent, does three things:

  * It tells the individuals walking in that they are seen and supported.
  * It tells their families that this community has their back.
  * It reminds local officials that Robertson County is watching.

You do not need to stay the whole time. Even 20 minutes of presence in the morning matters. Bring water, comfortable shoes, and a sign if you have one. If you do not have a sign, come anyway. We often have extra signs. New folks are always welcome and you will find a community of people who care.

Our campaign is about more than knocking doors - it’s about building relationships, strengthening our community, and showing what’s possible when we show up for each other. Whether it’s your first time or you’ve been with us from the start, your voice and your time truly matter.

ScamBusters is proud to offer a free (virtual) class to educate you:

## _Do you know what to do if you see ICE in your community?_

**This 1-hour basic class will show you what to do if you happen to see immigration enforcement activity.** It’s like taking CPR training: you hope you’ll never need it, but it’s good to know what to do in case of an emergency.

**Topics include:**

* The role and responsibilities of a Constitutional Observer
* Key constitutional rights relevant to observation and documentation
* How to use the V.I.D.E.O. framework for clear, consistent reporting
* How to identify immigration agents
* Best practices for personal safety and non-interference

This training was developed by Indivisible Eastside, Seattle Indivisible and West Seattle Indivisible, with support from ACLU-WA and WAISN.

Learn how decentralized finance (DeFi) works and explore how crypto rewards can be used to build a long-term Bitcoin and Ethereum portfolio.

Join RuneHold for a beginner-friendly virtual workshop exploring DeFi, blockchain governance, and practical cryptocurrency portfolio strategies.

Through real-world examples from RuneHold's daily Bitcoin and Ethereum accumulation process, participants will learn how decentralized financial systems operate and how governance rewards can fit into a broader digital asset strategy.

What you'll learn:

• DeFi fundamentals: Understand decentralized finance, blockchain networks, and how digital assets interact.

• Governance and rewards: Explore how systems such as Aquarius, AQUA, and ICE enable participation in decentralized governance and reward mechanisms.

• From rewards to Bitcoin and Ethereum: See how DeFi rewards can be converted into BTC and ETH through a structured accumulation approach.

• Long-term portfolio strategy: Learn about diversification, risk management, and the importance of consistency when navigating cryptocurrency markets.

• Real-world examples: Examine how RuneHold documents and evaluates its ongoing DeFi strategy.

Who should attend?

This workshop is designed for beginners, cryptocurrency enthusiasts, and anyone interested in understanding DeFi beyond buying and holding digital assets.

No prior DeFi experience is required.

Register to reserve your place.

This workshop is for educational purposes only and does not provide personalized financial or investment advice. Cryptocurrency and DeFi activities involve substantial risks, including potential loss of funds.

events.title: Tucson Shutdown Committee, Sun., 9/13 and weekly thereafter
events.description:
Tucson Shutdown

Please join Shutdown Trump Committee meeting, by Zoom, weekly on Sundays. The Steering Committee meets from 7-730 pm each week, followed by the General Meeting, from 7:30-8:30 pm. All are welcome to observe the Steering Committee meeting, but only the Steering Committee members (active Working Committee heads and sponsoring organizational reps) participate and vote.  You will be given the zoom link after you sign up. This meeting is for anyone who wants to volunteer.

Trump has threatened to cancel the mid-term elections. This would be a crucial step in completing his authoritarian takeover. The only thing that has been shown to reliably stop such a takeover is large-scale, non-violent noncooperation. An historic coalition came together in St. Louis in late May to call for exactly such a shutdown–if he does try to cancel the election. MayDayStrong.org has 600 labor unions and community groups as members.  Seven representatives from Tucson organizations went to St. Louis, including Democracy Unites Us, Party for Socialism and Liberation, Tucson Democratic Socialists of American and the local African-heritage ministerial alliance. Nine cities representing 30% of the economy have already committed to disrupt their economies for two weeks in case he does try to cancel the elections, so called “Tier 1” cities. Some of us in Tucson seek to make us a “Tier 2” city, to support the national Shutdown by disrupting our local economy as much as possible, at or above the scale of January 30th, for as long as we can. 

Please join us as individuals or representing a group.

* Defending democracy and the rule of law
* Encouraging voting

This approach keeps signs aligned with RhRR’s purpose, while preserving personal expression and emotional authenticity.

🇺🇳 Flags, banners, and even inflatable costumes are welcome. Some blow lots of bubbles. While our mission is serious, humor and camaraderie matter.

Over the last year, RhRR expanded from a handful of participants to multiple locations across the Valley, reaching thousands of pedestrians and motorists each week. 🗳️ As we approach the midterm elections, our united mission is to safeguard free and fair elections and promote civic participation, particularly in local and primary races where every vote carries weight. When tensions surface, we withdraw, stay composed, and look out for one another. This discipline keeps our rallies inviting and helps newcomers feel secure joining us.

events.title: MCDP HQ Office Staff Volunteers
events.description:
We're Opening Our Doors — And We Need You Inside Them!

Madison County Democrats is establishing a community hub and party headquarters — a place where neighbors can come to get information, get involved, and get connected to the resources and candidates that matter to this county.

And we need volunteers to make it run.

We're looking for friendly, committed Madison County Democrats to staff the office in 2-hour shifts with a partner — someone to greet visitors, answer questions, and represent the best of what this party stands for. No experience necessary. Just a willingness to show up and talk to your neighbors.

This is democracy at its most local. A front door. A friendly face. A place where anyone in Madison County can walk in and feel welcome.
What volunteering looks like:

-2-hour shifts, scheduled in advance

-Two volunteers per shift 

-Simple tasks — greeting visitors, sharing information, directing people to resources

If you've been looking for a way to get more involved this election season, this is it. The simplest and most powerful thing we can do is open our doors and be present for our community!

events.title: Arkansas Society of Freethinkers - Pint Nite / Humanist Happy Hour
events.description:
A casual, come-as-you-are gathering for freethinkers, skeptics, humanists, and anyone who enjoys good conversation over a drink or a meal. No agenda, no program — just an easy evening to meet people in your community who share a commitment to reason, compassion, and living ethically without reliance on the supernatural.
What to expect
Show up, grab a seat, and talk about whatever's on your mind — current events, books, life, the big questions and the small ones. Your host will be there to welcome you, introduce you around, and answer questions about the Arkansas Society of Freethinkers and the American Humanist Association if you have them.
First time? You're especially welcome.
A lot of people find Humanist Happy Hour an easier first step than a lecture or formal meeting. You don't need to identify as a humanist (or anything in particular) to come — just bring curiosity and an open mind.
About drinks
Alcohol is optional and never expected. The venue has non-alcoholic options and food, so come however you come.
Finding us
We meet on the third Monday of each month at 7 PM at the Flying Saucer in downtown Little Rock. Street parking is free but limited after 6 PM on President Clinton Ave. Additional street parking is free and usually available off President Clinton Ave, but may require walking a block or two. Paid lots and garages are also available in the area, including the library garage located in the same building as the Flying Saucer.
Hope to see you there.

Join us as knock doors for Alderperson Jessie Fuentes, we are ready to fight for a safer and more equitable 26th Ward. Working families deserve a city that works for them - good jobs, safe streets, a home they can afford, and a real voice in decisions that affect their lives. Working families deserve a city that works for them - good jobs, safe streets, a home they can afford, and a real voice in decisions that affect their lives. 

From our Alder:

I’m Alderperson Jessie Fuentes, and I’m running for Re-election to deliver for working families by focusing on three promises:

Build affordable housing now — fast-tracked, mixed-income developments with strong tenant protections, community land trusts, and funding for deeply affordable units so parents and seniors can stay in the neighborhoods they love.

Deliver real safety through investment — expand proven violence-prevention programs, fund crisis-response teams for mental-health and substance calls, fix lighting and sidewalks, and invest in youth jobs and after-school programs so our streets are safer and our kids have opportunities.

Practice co-governance — make decision-making local: participatory budgeting that directs resources to neighborhood priorities, empowered community advisory committees, transparent city contracting, and regular, multilingual neighborhood events so families shape the policies that affect them.

I will also fight for living-wage job pipelines, affordable housing, reliable transit, and support for small businesses so families can do more than survive. Join our campaign to turn these promises into results. Sign, volunteer, or donate today to keep building a stronger, safer, and fairer community for working families.

events.title: Alleghany County Tuesdays Canvassing for Change
events.description:
Come meet your neighbors in the county. We will be canvassing Tuesdays from 2-4:30 knocking on doors of Dem friendly targets to talk about their concerns and to encourage everyone to vote! Tuesdays will focus on the 65+ age group of people who don’t vote consistently. Our goal is to create relationships with them, to educate about all of our candidates up and down the ballot, the election times, places, and voter ID requirements, and to give them resources that day that they can refer to later. 

If you have never canvassed, it is a wonderful way to get out and meet people and to hear what people’s concerns are. We go out in teams of two using a phone app that guides you from house to house, gives you a script, and allows you to enter feedback from the people you speak with. Canvassing isn’t scary. We are not talking to ruby red Republicans. 

This election is vitally important to our democracy. We need people like you to help us get Democrats elected. Come join us!

events.title: [Yolo County] Self-Directed Door Knocking — Eric Jones for Congress (CA-4)
events.description:
Knock doors on your own schedule, anywhere in the Yolo County portion of CA-4.

Self-directed canvassing means you pick the day, get your turf, and go. There's no launch event to show up to and no meeting spot. We'll get you set up beforehand.

BEFORE YOUR FIRST SHIFT

Your County Captain is Mel Halem. She'll reach out after you sign up to get you literature and a turf assignment.

We also run a volunteer Slack with a channel for every county in the district. You'll get the invite when you sign up.

New to canvassing? Come to a virtual training first. Thursdays at 6:00 PM and Sundays at 3:00 PM, 45 minutes. You'll leave knowing how to talk to voters, how to use the app, and what to do at the door. Sign up here:


ericjones.us/trainingsignup


WHEN TO GO OUT

You can knock between 9:00 AM and 9:00 PM. The hours that actually work:

Weekdays — 4:00 to 8:00 PM

Weekends — 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM

People are home and willing to talk then. Go earlier and you're mostly knocking on empty houses.

WHAT A SHIFT LOOKS LIKE

Aim for 50 doors. Twenty-five is the floor, and most turf lets you hit that in an hour or two. Move quickly — we have a lot of doors between now and November 3.

Sign up for whatever days you can. Come back as often as you want.

events.title: [Virtual] Phone Banking — Eric Jones for Congress (CA-4)
events.description:
Join us to phonebank for Eric Jones! Eric is running against a long term blue dog Democrat, who relies on a ton of corporate cash from PG&E, large insurance companies who refuse wildfire claims and Big Pharma. Meanwhile the cost of living keeps rising as these major companies continue to bankroll incumbent politicians. 

Eric is fighting to change that. Eric Jones wants to ban Congressional stock trading and foster economic opportunity to revitalize the American Dream. 

HOW IT WORKS

Sign up for any weekday shift, 5:00 to 7:00 PM. Join the Zoom link you'll get after you sign up. We'll spend the first few minutes on training and getting you set up, then you'll start dialing.

Stay for the full two hours or drop off when you need to. Take as many shifts as you want.

WHAT YOU NEED

A computer and a quiet spot. Headphones help. That's it — the calling happens through your browser, so you don't need to use your own phone number.

NEW TO THIS?

Or just show up to a shift. We train at the top of every one.

WHY IT MATTERS

The incumbent was elected nearly 30 years ago. The only way voters hear there's a choice —  and a true difference between the candidates —  in this race is if someone tells them. That's the whole job.

Sign up for whatever nights you can.

Join Common Cause New Mexico for our monthly **Democracy Action Hour**, a space for volunteers, supporters, and community members to get updates, take action, and help build a stronger democracy in New Mexico.

- Opportunities to get involved locally through Community Action Teams

events.title: Good Trouble Anti-Racism Workshop Series Session 4: The Iceberg Is Right Here

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Session 4: The Iceberg Is Right Here
Connecting history to our community today, how the past continues to shape the present right where we live.

The essence of the Good Trouble Anti-Racism Workshop Series 
(hereafter referred to as GTAR Workshop Series) is encapsulated in a quote from Congressman John Lewis: "Not the civil rights we inherited-but the civil rights we are building." 

GTAR Workshop Series is created and led by Sondra Light-Holt - a Black woman, a community health provider and advocate, a lifelong resident of Sandusky Ohio, and an active member with the NAACP. She is a board member of Serving Our Seniors and brings 25 years of experience in the field of healthcare to this Series.

THE GTAR Workshop Series is anti-racism education through the lens of healthcare, allowing us to more fully understand one another across racial lines, thus strengthening and expanding our community. Racism is America's wound. This series provides information regarding the harms of racism in housing, healthcare, education, and the justice system. Each session equips participants with factual knowledge, historical context, and civic language to recognize and respond to systemic racism in their own lives. 

The Series intentionally encourages people of all races to open up, share their experiences, ask hard questions and be heard without judgment. We'll learn, expand and strengthen our community, and take action by working together to heal our wounds, thus mitigating future damage. Medical racism runs throughout this series as a core thread, because community health is inseparable from community justice. 

Solidarity is practiced in real time, not just discussed in theory. Attendees are encouraged to share experiences of being targeted by racism, or being encouraged to behave in a racist way. Additionally, discussion is open to talking about positive experiences of friendship or power-sharing partnerships across racial lines. This model allows participants to acknowledge what has occurred in the past and make choices about how to build their future. 

Each session contains 2 parts: the Education portion of each Workshop provides relevant information to absorb; the Training portion builds solidarity across races. 

Topics: 
Session 1-How We Got Here-The Blueprint of American Racism (8/13) 
Session 2-The Iceberg-Seeing What You Were Taught Not to See (9/10) 
Session 3-It's Personal-Lived Experience, Privilege & the Stories We Tell Ourselves (10/8) 
Session 4-The Iceberg Is Right Here-Our Community Today (11/12) 
Session 5-What Do We Do Now-The Call to Action (12/10)

events.description:
IEP Circles WV is a parent-led community where families of exceptional learners come together to find support, build knowledge, and create change. If you're navigating an IEP, 504 Plan, evaluations, school communication, or accessing services, these gatherings are designed to help you feel informed, connected, and supported.

Each meeting brings caregivers together with experienced advocates, education attorneys, and community partners who provide practical guidance, answer questions, and facilitate meaningful discussions. You'll have opportunities to share experiences, learn from other families, discover helpful resources, and build lasting relationships with people who understand the challenges you face.

Beyond individual support, IEP Circles helps families understand the larger issues affecting special education. We'll explore how school funding, staffing shortages, IDEA funding, and state and federal policy decisions impact the services available to students. By connecting personal experiences to these broader challenges, families can better understand why obstacles exist and how they can work alongside educators and other parents to improve public education.

For those interested in taking the next step, IEP Circles also offers opportunities to develop advocacy skills through workshops on legislative advocacy, storytelling, public speaking, community organizing, and civic engagement. Whether you simply want support or hope to help shape the future of special education in West Virginia, you'll find a welcoming community where your experiences are valued and your voice matters.

Together, we can strengthen support for our children, build stronger communities, and advocate for a public education system that works for every student.

events.title: Election Defenders Weekly Hangout
events.description:
Election Defenders is a weekly organizing call to learn, plan and promote resistance to authoritarian interference in our democratic elections.

We act in service of democracy and in line with lawful, nonviolent civil resistance against authoritarians.

The meeting will be hosted on Zoom every Saturday at 11:00 AM CT and will bring interested parties together to build the skills and community needed to amplify resistance voices across the country.

Why It Matters

Free and fair elections are a basic pillar of healthy democracies, and our elections are under attack by the Trump regime.

Trump and his enablers are trying many tactics: disenfranchising legitimate voters, blocking mail delivery of ballots, calling for armed intimidation at polling locations, making false or unsubstantiated claims about voting fraud, etc.

Election Defenders will support activists who wish to use lawful, nonviolent civil resistance to protect our democracy.

When: 

Every Saturday at 11:00 AM CT (9am PT, 12pm ET)

Format: Weekly group call via Zoom

Duration: 60 minutes

Focus areas: 

Understanding the entire election process and its vulnerabilities, utilizing training and information opportunities, supporting and growing the resistance, coordinating election protection efforts.

events.title: SALEM & VIRTUAL - Share Your Comments at a Universal Health Plan Governance Board Meeting
events.description:
The State of Oregon's Universal Health Plan Governance Board (UHPGB) is developing our state's transition plan to a universal healthcare system. They recently voted to delay the delivery of their plan to the Oregon Legislature until December 2026. 

Learn more about the Board here: https://www.hcao.org/uhpgb

They have set aside time in their monthly meetings to hear from YOU about what you need in a new system. Share your perspective with the Governance Board in the form of Public Comment.

TALK TO THE PEOPLE MAKING THE PLAN! 

You must register in advance to reserve your time for public comments by emailing uhpgb.info@dcbs.oregon.gov. Or, if attending a meeting in person, you may sign-up 15 minutes before the meeting begins.

The Board meets on the 3rd Thursday of the month, both remotely and in-person at 350 Winter St. NE, Salem OR 97301. Often meetings are in Basement Conference Room F: please check meeting information for room changes. 

Upcoming meeting dates:
August 20th, September 17th, October 15th, November 19th, December 17th.

Meeting times and materials are posted here:
https://www.oregon.gov/uhpgb/board-meetings/Pages/2026-meetings.aspx


The UHPGB mission: "We’re creating a strong, workable plan so everyone in Oregon can get the high-quality, equitable health care they deserve. This new system will be simpler, more affordable, and more sustainable — cutting costs for families and businesses while building a healthier, more stable future for our state."

Health Care for All Oregon has seen in real time that public comments has changed the work of the Board, and the framework of the plan. Your input can make a difference in this work.

Interested in attending and speaking virtually? To speak you must inform UHPGB Staff 24 hours in advance to reserve your spot, by emailing uhpgb.info@dcbs.oregon.gov.

events.title: Block by Block - Phone Bank with SURJ! (Let’s block MAGA & send progressive champions to Congress!)
events.description:
## Candidate Schedule:

- **Ossoff for GA Senate** - 10/27, 11/1, 11/3
- **Jackson for ME Senate** - 10/25
- **Colom for MS Senate** - 10/15, 10/22, 10/31
- **MI- US  Congress (Lawrence)  US Senate ( El-Sayed)** - 10/18, 11/2
- **Pearson for TN Congressional District 9** - 10/29, 10/31
- **Villegas for CA Congressional District 22** - 10/20

## Come phone bank with SURJ!

We are now in a decisive phase of the fight against authoritarianism, the threat is real and the stakes are high. And people are fighting back. Millions have protested, and we've watched powerful organizing coming out of Minneapolis, Chicago, and other cities that have borne the brunt of ICE's assaults on our communities. Mass anger exists, but mass organization does not yet exist at the scale needed to win. Movements become real when they reach millions: organized, trained, and acting together.

The stage for the midterm elections is set, and the stakes for our movement and democracy couldn't be higher.  

**Join SURJ in doing our part to help flip the House and Senate and block MAGA while sending a crop of true movement champions to Congress.**

**These races include:**
**SENATE:**

 - **Michigan Senate** *(Build Race - Movement Champion)* - **Abdul El-Sayed**, who is born and raised in Michigan, studied to be a doctor but then realized he wanted to dedicate his career to building government systems that actually work for Michiganders. He has secured free glasses for kids who need the,, removed lead from Detroit’s elementary schools, taken on Michigan's biggest polluters and made Narcan universally accessible. He has also spearheaded a program to eventually cancel up to $700 million in medical debt for 300,000 Michiganders over 2 years. He is a true fighter and is ready to take that to DC on behalf of the whole state!
- **Maine Senate** *(Build Race - Movement Champion Race)* - **Troy Jackson**, who is a logger from Allagash, a lifelong fighter for workers' rights, and former Maine Senate President who is running to put power back in the hands of working people and unseat Susan Collins.  
- **Georgia Senate** *(Block MAGA Race)* - **Jon Ossoff**, who is an incumbent democratic Senator for the state of Georgia. He was born and raised in Atlanta. He is focused on exposing and stopping governmental corruption all while being one of the few US Senators whose campaign refuses corporate PAC money. 
- **Mississippi Senate** *(Block the Right Race)* - **Scott Colom**, who is a District Attorney for the 16th judicial district of Mississippi. As DA, he has pursued policies like avoiding incarceration for non-violent offenses, was the first District Attorney in Mississippi to offer restorative justice for victims, and is currently on the Advisory Board of the VERA Institute for Justice, a partner that SURJ has worked with over the years. 
 
**HOUSE:**

- **Michigan Congressional District 7** *(Build Race - Movement Champion)* - **Will Lawrence**, who is an organizer and coalition-builder with experience speaking truth to power and getting results at the local, state and federal level. Born and raised in Mid-Michigan, Will has fought tirelessly to protect people’s rights to housing (co-founder of the Rents Is Too Damn High Coalition), bring good, green jobs to the district (as a co-founder of Sunrise Movement) and to ward off data center greed. 
- **Tennessee Congressional District 9** *(Build Race - Movement Champion)* - **Justin Pearson**, who is an organizer, born and raised in Southwest Memphis, Tennessee. He grew up in a working class family and has been advocating for his community since the age of 15, fighting for better education for his classmates. He has since formed Memphis Community Against the Pipeline (MCAP) to fight billion dollar oil companies that would have polluted over a million people’s drinking water, fought alongside workers for better wages and taken on the xAI data center for their illegal pollution.
- **California Congressional District 22** *(Build Race- Movement Champion)* - **Randy Villegas**, who is a 30-year old son of immigrants and activist for immigrant rights in his area. He is an elected school board trustee in Visalia, CA and political science professor who is running to represent California’s 22nd congressional district, representing Bakersfield and portions of the central valley.
- **North Carolina Congressional District 11** *(Block the Right Race)* - **Jamie Ager**, who is a fourth generation Western NC farmer. Running on making healthcare accessible, lowering costs, stopping government waste and corruption, and getting necessary relief to Hurricane Helene survivors.

**New**
**North Carolina Statewide** *Build Race- Movement Champion*- **Anita Earls** is an associate NC Justice running for re-election. On the NC Supreme Court, Earls has championed healthcare access, education, and protecting the right to vote. Earls is a critical line of defense to protect and re-institute fair maps for NC voters.

    
Come as you are! No experience needed! Full training & lots of support included!
      
***

## Logistics:

-   These phone banks are online on the Zoom platform. Log into the call on Zoom on your computer and bring your phone to make the calls (if you only have one device, still come!).
-   We have a robust training on the call to give you all the information you need -- a script, technical support, and coaching throughout.
-   Returners can start early.
-   You will receive an email with orientation materials ahead of time.
-   ***Please note the time zone for call time.***
    
***

## Feeling Unsure?

-   **Our model works** - learn from the best! Our phonebanks have one of the highest rates of success in the country. No matter whether you're brand new caller or a seasoned organizer, if you join our banks, you can trust that you are putting your effort into a method that works. And you'll get to learn powerful organizing skills from seasoned leaders!
-   Our conversations are based on **open-ended questions** and **deep listening.  You do not need to be an expert** on the issues or a candidate - our phone banks are successful because we deeply connect with voters and make them feel heard.
-   Want to hear what a phonebank is like? Check out [this video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U3w4tNKPTY8) interviewing SURJ phonebankers.
    
***
## Context:

As Trump and republicans defund the social safety net and peddle more racist lies, millions of people are increasingly feeling the effects of the billionaire agenda. We know this fight is on multiple fronts, and **this fall we have an opportunity to harness the energy of the streets and rising resentment towards November’s elections** – to not only wrest power from MAGA, but to **put candidates in office who are willing to stand up to Trump and fight for working class people. BOTH the House AND Senate are in play for Democrats to take back control and this year we aim to put progressive working class champions in a position to WIN.**

For the last six years, SURJ’s phone banking program has grown to be one of the strongest in the country, reaching millions of working class people with our vision of finding our shared interest in standing alongside people of color and rejecting white supremacy. This year is an opportunity to deliver strategic blows to the MAGA agenda and throw down a gauntlet to force the Democratic Party to reckon with true progressive, working class fighters.

To do this, **protecting or flipping key Senate seats in North Carolina, Georgia, Maine and Mississippi** and **flipping critical house seats in Michigan 7, Tennessee 9 and California 22.**

These races will affect millions of working class people this year. Riding the high from many wins for progressive champions throughout primary season, we are well positioned to send some of these same folks to the halls of Congress. We will continue to build power to stop MAGA, by **supporting unapologetically progressive working class champions, while showing up in key races to block MAGA and showing up in solidarity alongside Black racial justice leaders in the south** who are fighting back and beginning the long-build back from the gutting of the VRA. Alongside our partners across the country, this is the time for our movements to offer a bold vision and bring our people into it.

***

## About SURJ:

[Showing Up for Racial Justice](https://surj.org/) (SURJ) is the largest organization in the country that explicitly organizes white communities for justice. Instead of choosing racism, silence, or complicity, we help white communities choose justice. We have thousands of national members and 150+ chapters across the US and Canada.

events.title: 14th Annual National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence
events.description:
Each year since 2013, the Newtown Action Alliance Foundation (NAAF), the charitable arm of the Newtown Action Alliance (NAA), and numerous partners in the gun violence prevention community have sponsored the National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence on or near the anniversary of the Sandy Hook shooting tragedy. These multidenominational events, held in Washington, D.C., at the National Cathedral and St. Mark’s Episcopal Church, bring together survivors of gun violence, victims’ family members, concerned citizens, faith leaders, lawmakers, leaders of gun violence prevention organizations, and activists from across the nation. 

The 14th Annual National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence will be held on Wednesday, December 9, 2026 from 7-9:00pm ET at St Marks Episcopal Church on Capitol Hill, Washington, D.C. 

December 14, 2026 is the 14-year mark of the Sandy Hook tragedy. By this December, more than 1.4 million Americans will be killed or injured by guns since the Sandy Hook shooting tragedy. We urge you to join the gun violence prevention community in our collective effort to continue to shine a light on the devastating epidemic of gun violence in our nation until these gun deaths and injuries are reduced. 

The victims, survivors and the families impacted by gun violence are often forgotten. We have lost our #FreedomToLive. Therefore, the Newtown Action Alliance Foundation and the Newtown Action Alliance, in partnership with 160+ organizations  will host the annual national vigil service of mourning and loving remembrance for all who have fallen victim to the ongoing epidemic of gun violence in America. 

Our goal is simple. The gun violence prevention movement will unite to support the families and communities impacted by gun violence, educate, continue to raise awareness, and keep this critical issue front and center throughout our nation. events.title: Knock on doors with Ground Truth in Belmont County, Ohio!
events.description:
Show solidarity with fellow progressive activists in rural Ohio! On July 18th, two Ground Truth canvassers in Belmont County, OH, were surrounded by 4 police cars. They were ordered to cease and desist from canvassing or face arrest for “Soliciting and Creating a Public Nuisance.” Of course, political canvassing door to door is constitutionally protected free speech. No permit or fee can be required, and it is definitely not grounds for arrest. One of the canvassers who was stopped was a Latino naturalized citizen, and racial profiling appeared to play a part.

We’re working with local candidates and activists, the ACLU, the County, the City, and the Police Department to make sure every area officer understands our rights and protect them. We remain focused on deep canvassing in Eastern Ohio and listening to our neighbors’ concerns. We are determined to strengthen voter participation through exercising our constitutional civil rights. We do not seek to escalate this situation. We are building mutual trust and respect with our neighbors.

WHAT YOU CAN DO TO HELP: The best thing you can do to help is to sign up for deep canvassing shifts with us in Belmont County, OH! We need folks now more than ever to stand in solidarity with us! 

Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust and win back power in the Midterms and beyond. We’re launching an [innovative new program](https://ourgroundtruth.org) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- Knock on **every door** in the neighborhood, not just the same voters campaigns usually talk to.

- Have real conversations that **listen deeply** to voters’ concerns.

- Gather rich insights for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we’re starting early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* knocking every door, not just the ones the voter database tells us to, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: Post Election Review
events.description:
Minnesota takes election security seriously. Before the Election, we have the Public Accuracy Test. During the election, election judges ensure that the processes in the polling places follow the law. After the election, we have the Post Election Review. 

**[Minnesota Statutes 206.89](https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/206.89)** states that after every state general election, Minnesota counties perform a post-election review of election results returned by the optical scan ballot counters used in the state.  The review is a hand count of the ballots for each eligible election (U.S. President, U.S. Senator, U.S. Representative, and Governor) in the selected precincts compared with the results from the voting system used in those precincts.

The post-election review is carried out by the County Canvassing Board, made up of the County Auditor (in St. Louis County, Nancy Nilsen), the Court Administrator of the District Court (Kim Vizena), the mayor/chair of the town board of the largest municipality in the County(Roger Reinert), and two County Commissioners (Patrick Boyle and Ken Musolf). 

Come witness this historic process. Our elections are precious. Maybe in prior years we could let this operate in the background. 2026 is different. 

Note: the starting time, 9 am is set, the ending time depends on how long it takes to review the selected precincts.

Jump Jam is back on Saturday, on November 7th (rain date from October 10th), and we'd love to have you on the team!

Hosted at the Subaru of Spartanburg Bike Park, Jump Jam is PAL's annual bike park fundraiser featuring kids' bike races, amateur and professional dirt jump competitions, food trucks, vendors, and family activities. Every dollar raised helps support the maintenance and improvement of the bike park while introducing more children and families to cycling and outdoor recreation.

It takes an incredible team of volunteers to make the day possible! Whether you're helping set up before the event, checking in kids for the races, assisting along the course, or helping us pack everything up at the end of the day, your time makes a real difference.

Three volunteer shifts are available throughout the day, and every volunteer will receive a PAL T-shirt. No previous experience is necessary - just bring comfortable clothes, closed-toe shoes, and a willingness to jump in and help!

10:00 AM - 1:00 PM | Set Up

Help transform the bike park for Jump Jam! Volunteers will assist with setting up tents, tables, banners, signs, inflatables, race course signage, vendor areas, and other event equipment before participants arrive.

1:00 PM - 4:00 PM | Kids Ride & Check-In

Help make the Kids Ride a success by checking in participants, distributing race T-shirts, lining kids up by age group, holding age group signs, directing riders along the course, and handing out finisher medals.

4:00 PM - 6:30 PM | Crowd Voting & Breakdown

Walk through the crowd with QR codes so attendees can vote for the Best Style competition, then stay after the awards ceremony to help the PAL team break down the event, pack equipment, and clean up the park.

Thank you for helping PAL create another unforgettable Jump Jam. We couldn't do it without you!

Packed Classrooms: Composite state rankings consistently place Arizona public education near the bottom (48th to 51st). While state averages mask the crisis, actual core classrooms (Math, English, Science) regularly pack 30–35+ students into a single room with low teacher retention and bottom-tier funding.

Corporate Loophole: Arizona is now one of the least affordable states to live in, yet under state law (A.R.S. § 43-1111), over 80% of corporate filers pay only the $50 minimum state tax floor (JLBC data), leaving working families to carry the load.

We have the power to change this.

Tempe Rising Indivisible is organizing "Flip Flops on the Ground" Lit Drop shifts to get crucial campaign information into the hands of voters across key neighborhoods.

🎯 Our Target Districts

👟 How You Can Help
Walkers: Come get your steps in! Whether you have 1 hour, 2 hours, or 3 hours, every neighborhood covered matters.

Drivers Needed: Prefer driving over walking? We urgently need drivers to transport lit drop teams and cover larger routes!

We provide all materials, turf maps, and a brief launch overview before you head out. Bring water, comfortable shoes, and a friend!

events.title: Proactive Behavior Screening for Stronger Student Success
events.description:
**Proactive Behavior Screening for Stronger Student Success**

Join Firelight Books for an informative presentation introducing the Nichols Behavior Checklist (NBC), an innovative universal behavior screening and intervention tool designed to help schools identify behavioral and emotional concerns early—before they become barriers to student success.

The NBC is an Internet-based, individualized screening instrument for students in 1–12 that is quick, user-friendly, cost effective, and highly informative. In approximately 10 minutes per student, the NBC provides individualized behavioral screening reports with practical recommendations to support intervention planning and behavior management.

This presentation will demonstrate how the NBC helps educators, intervention teams, counselors, administrators, and clinicians:

* Identify areas of behavioral and emotional concern
* Improve student behavior through early intervention
* Support positive school functioning and interpersonal relationships
* Strengthen data-driven decision making
* Monitor trends at the district, campus, classroom, or individual student level
* Provide meaningful documentation for intervention planning

Attendees will learn how the NBC can be used as both a proactive screening instrument and an effective intervention support tool to help improve student outcomes, classroom climate, and overall school success.

The Nichols Behavior Checklist provides schools with practical behavioral insight—turning data into positive action for students.
www.firelightbooks.com

events.description:
**Summary**

The Family and Politics workshop teaches participants how to preserve family bonds while staying true to their values and political beliefs. Although the focus is on family relationships, you can use these strategies with any loved one. You’ll have some fun in this workshop – it won’t be all serious. After all, we all come from quirky families.

**Goals**

- Insight into why family differences over politics are uniquely challenging
- Recognition of common roles that family members play in political conversations
- Strategies and skills for handling family political differences in a constructive way

**Who Can Attend**

The Family and Politics workshop is open to everyone who struggles over political differences with a loved one.

**What to Expect**

You will learn about the family dynamics of political differences, apply them to your family, and learn and practice effective communication skills with difficult family members.

events.title: Intro to Community Organizing: Growing to Win
events.description:
How do we win? How do we advance our goals for social change? We get organized! Community organizing is people power in action. It's about uniting around a shared goal to make a difference together. Anyone can be an organizer. You don’t need a degree or years of experience—just a passion for change and a willingness to listen and learn.

_Billionaires are already organized, and we can be too!_

In this training opportunity, facilitator Brian Eaton will lead participants in an exploration of Structure Based Organizing, a century-old technique for building power and creating durable solutions to issues that matter to a community.

Participants in this one-hour workshop will learn:

- How Structure Based Organizing works—its key principles and techniques

- How Structured Organizing Conversations act as the foundation of successful campaigns

- How Structure Based Organizing can enable us to build local power into a mass movement

**Note: Enrollment limited to 15 participants.**

events.title: Food Scraps Collection: NoHo Farmers' Market
events.description:
As a volunteer, you’ll be right in the action, collecting food scraps from market-goers—the first step in a crucial process that turns waste into nutrient-rich compost. These scraps, gathered at local markets, are then processed at nearby green parks or gardens. Throughout your shift, you'll be guided by an experienced LA Compost staff member, who will act as your Compost Manager, offering insights and helping you share the benefits of composting with the public. The best part is that during your volunteer shift, you can take some time to shop at the market. Join us and be part of the composting movement that's transforming LA—one food scrap at a time!

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:

As a volunteer, you’ll play a hands-on role in guiding market-goers through composting, ensuring their food scraps are clean of stickers, compostable, and ready to be turned into nutrient-rich compost. You’ll monitor for contamination, assist with tracking data, and serve as a friendly, welcoming host to our composting community. 

#### MORE INFO: 

* You'll be stationed at the LA Compost booth under a pop-up canopy within the farmers' market. There will also be seating available.
* You may be asked to assist with moving filled bins of material weighing 60+ pounds. We always offer team lifts; you will never be asked to lift bins if you prefer not to.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome!
* Bathrooms are available
* If you sign up, please show up! We rely on volunteers like you to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 
VOLUNTEER WAIVER: Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. Access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver

CODE OF CONDUCT: All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

events.title: New Member Orientation! (Fall Series)
events.description:
As a member-led youth movement, MOVE Texas Members are at the heart of our mission to transform democracy in Texas and beyond. **Born out of the student organizing movement in San Antonio in 2013,** MOVE Texas was founded by young people who saw a gap in civic engagement and decided to take action. What started as a small group of student leaders registering their peers to vote has since grown into a statewide movement of young people that trains, mobilizes, and empowers a new generation of progressive community organizers.

## Who are MOVE Texas Members?

MOVE Texas members are the backbone of the organization, reflecting the energy and diversity of young Texans leading the charge for a more just and equitable future for all Texans across race, class, and place.  As a youth movement, MOVE Texas members are under 35, and are either:


- **Students:** The original foundation of MOVE Texas, young leaders organizing on campuses across the state, running voter registration drives, educating their peers, and leading local issue-based campaigns.

- **Community Members:** Young Texans who are inspired by MOVE Texas’ mission and actively work to build power in their neighborhoods, from hosting events to advocating for direct local and statewide policy change.

## MOVE Texas members receive:

- Access to MOVE trainings, programs, and resources,

- Voting power for statewide and local campaigns,

- Exclusive invitations to MOVE statewide events,

- Connection to a network of peers organizing across the state,

- Exclusive members merch.


MOVE Texas membership is open to anyone who believes in the power of young people to lead and shape the future AND our present.

# The LGBTQ+ Summit During the New Jersey League of Municipalities is BACK this November!

Join us and the Garden State's new LGBTQ+ business association, the Unity Chamber of Commerce, at the Hard Rock Hotel & Casino in Atlantic City on Tuesday, Nov. 17, for the return of this special event.⁠

The LGBTQ+ Summit During the New Jersey League of Municipalities is powered by PSEG.
⁠
### Special Guests
#### Honorable Julien X. Neals
*United States District Judge, District of New Jersey*

Since 2021, Judge Neals has served as a US District Judge of the US District Court for the District of New Jersey. Before that, he served as County Counsel and Acting County Administrator for Hackensack, and the Business Administrator for the City of Newark. He is a staunch ally for LGBTQ+ equality.

#### Assemblywoman Luanne Peterpaul
*NJ Legislative District 11*

In 2023, Luanne Peterpaul became the first openly lesbian woman elected to serve in the New Jersey Legislature. While representing NJ's 11th Legislative District, she was the primary Assembly sponsor for a bill to expand access to HIV medication and a primary sponsor of the recently signed into law bill to shield reproductive and transgender healthcare.

#### Bernie Wagenblast
*Transportation Journalist and Voice Actor • Summit Emcee*

Bernie Wagenblast is a transportation journalist and voice actor. She's best known for being a voice millions hear daily on transit systems, including the NYC subway, the AirTrain at Newark Liberty International Airport and PATCO in South Jersey and Philadelphia. Since her transition in early 2023, she's become a highly visible advocate for trans folks. 

Attendees will receive a free lunch.

Every Saturday at 1:00 PM | Coolidge Corner

Join members of three Brookline pro-democracy groups — indivisible Activist Evenings, Brookline Pax, and Speak Out, Seniors! — for our weekly rally at Coolidge Corner.

We gather to raise our voices and our signs in defense of democracy, justice, and decency — and to stand united against the abuses of the Trump administration and the forces that threaten our rights and freedoms.

We stand for:

• Immigrant rights, human rights, and racial justice

• Free speech, the Constitution, and the rule of law

• Access to health and healthcare for all

• Protection of our planet and the future we leave to the next generation

We choose empathy over cruelty, peace over violence, and hope over fear.

Our rallies are peaceful, spirited, and uplifting — a chance to connect, recharge, and stand up for what matters. Bring your friends, your voice, and your sign (or borrow one of ours!).

All are welcome!  The rally is multi-generational and family-friendly; those using walkers or other mobility devices may use them to sit to participate.

In the event of inclement weather, we’ll each use our best judgment about whether to attend. We hope you’ll do the same! 

Please join us, one rally at a time.  We’ll continue for as long as it takes.

events.title: ARC Book Club: 'The Warmth of Other Suns' by Isabel Wilkerson
events.description:
Welcome to ARC’s (Antiracist Conversations) 12-week Virtual Read-Around Book Club.

 We will read Isabel Wilkerson’s book, The Warmth of Other Suns, which tells the epic story of America's Great Migration.

Our book club uses a unique format called a “Virtual Read-Around.”
No reading ahead is required: we will meet every Tuesday from September 8 through December 15, 2026, to read and experience Isabel Wilkerson’s The Warmth of Other Suns live as a group.

The book club will be facilitated by Jan, Pat, and Ms. Evelyn.

Together on live video, we will open each session with greetings and an icebreaker, and then we will read the book out loud.

There will be no verbal discussion during our weekly live meetings.

Important Note: Space is limited to 20 participants.  Registering for all book club meetings at once is the best plan. 

If you register and determine that you are unable to attend, please cancel your Mobilize registration so we can open your spot to someone else.

Weekly Meeting Schedule
We will meet every Tuesday for 90 minutes from September 8 through December 15, 2026. Find your local time zone below:

Pacific Time (PT): 8:00 AM – 9:30 AM
Mountain Time (MT): 9:00 AM – 10:30 AM
Central Time (CT): 10:00 AM – 11:30 AM
Eastern Time (ET): 11:00 AM – 12:30 PM


Meeting Timeline Breakdown
Every session follows this exact 90-minute structure (listed in Central Time):

10:00 AM – 10:10 AM: Open Zoom room, greetings, icebreaker, and tech check.

10:10 AM – 11:25 AM: Read out loud together as a group for 75 minutes.

11:25 AM – 11:30 AM: Wrap up and log off.

Reading and Journal Steps
We will cover about 30 to 35 pages together each week. 
 Confirm your attendance for the series by September 2, 2026. 

We’ll email additional information after you’ve confirmed your participation. 

Catching Up: If we do not finish the designated pages during our live read-around, please finish those specific pages on your own before the next Tuesday session.


Write Notes: After completing the weekly block, spend 10 to 15 minutes writing in a private journal while your thoughts are completely fresh.


Final Gathering: We will meet on Tuesday, December 15, at our usual session time for a final virtual gathering to share ideas from our journals and have a full verbal discussion.

See you on Tuesday, September 8, 2026.

With much appreciation,
The ARC Team

events.title: Dem Days Of Action
events.description:
# Nobody Is Coming to Putnam County to Do This for Us.

Five days. Two to three hours each. Doors and phones at Gobin Church — and no experience necessary.

*Sign up at the bottom of this page. ↓*

---

## There is no cavalry.

There's no army of paid staff driving in from Indianapolis. No national organization has Putnam County on their list. Nobody is coming.

The people who elect our candidates this year are the people who already live here. That's the whole plan. That's it.

So we're asking you for five days.

---


## Here's exactly what happens when you show up.

**1. Come to Gobin Church.**
Pick one day or come to all five. Wear comfortable shoes either way.

**2. Get assigned and trained.**
Tell us on the form whether you'd rather knock doors or make calls — we'll do everything we can to put you where you want to be. Then you're trained on site. You will not be handed a clipboard and pointed at a neighborhood.

**3. Work two to three hours.**
Then go home knowing you did the thing that actually decides elections.

---


**You get to tell us which one you want.**  If you have no preference, say that too — we'll put you wherever the need is biggest that day.

### 🚪 Door Knocking

**What to bring:** Comfortable walking shoes and your cell phone. That's it.

**You will never knock alone.** Every single door knocker is paired with a partner — no exceptions. If you come by yourself, we'll pair you with someone. If you come with a friend or your spouse, you can walk together.

**What to expect:** You'll be trained on site and given your route and instructions before you head out.

**Experience required:** None.

### 📞 Phone Banking

**What to bring:** At minimum, a phone and headphones. Ideally a phone, headphones, and a laptop or tablet so you can read the script from a screen.

**What to expect:** Full training before you make a single call. The script is written for you.

**Experience required:** None.

---


## Five Days of Action

All at Gobin Church. Two to three hours each.

| Date | Time | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Saturday, September 5** | 10:00 am | Kickoff |
| **Tuesday, September 22** | 6:00 pm | Evening shift |
| **Tuesday, October 6** | 5:30 pm | Early voting begins |
| **Saturday, October 24** | 10:00 am | Final Saturday |
| **Monday, November 2** | 5:00 pm | Election Eve |

*Keep scrolling to claim your days. ↓*

---

## This is the main work.

Not yard signs. Not social media posts. Not opinions at the coffee shop.

Knocking doors and making phone calls is how our candidates get elected. Real conversations, neighbor to neighbor, are what move people to the polls — and there is no substitute for them. Every serious campaign in America knows this. Most people never find out, because most people never show up.

Two to three hours, five times, is roughly ten to fifteen hours between now and Election Day. That is the difference between winning and wondering.

We need as many volunteers as we can possibly get across all five days for this to work.

---

## IN CASE YOU'RE HESITATING

**"I've never done this before."**
Good. Most people on these teams haven't. We train everyone, every day, before anyone talks to a single voter.

**"I'm not comfortable knocking on doors."**
Then take a phone. The form asks which team you'd prefer, and both teams matter equally.

**"I don't want to knock doors by myself."**
You won't. Every door knocker is paired with a partner, every time. Nobody walks a route alone.

**"I can only make one day."**
Take one day. One volunteer for one shift is worth more than a hundred people who meant to.

**"I already vote."**
Voting is the minimum. This is the part where you actually build something.

---

events.title: Volunteer Phone Banking - Virtual
events.description:
Every vote matters, and we’re on a mission to make that a reality. That's why ACLU of Michigan volunteers will be calling voters whose ballots need to be cured to ensure their vote can be counted.
 
In Michigan, voters who vote via Absentee Ballot must sign their ballot envelope before their vote is counted. If there are any issues with the signature, the voter’s city or township clerk will notify the voter with instructions on how to fix, or “cure”, the signature issue. (Often, the voter forgot to sign the back of their Absentee Ballot.)
 
Studies have shown that voters are more likely to follow up on their clerk's notice if they receive a call from friendly volunteers, so join us to make sure that every vote counts!
 
No experience is required; we will provide the training. You will just need: 1) a computer or tablet, 2) a cell phone, and 3) a steady internet or Wi-Fi connection.

events.title: Orlando Food Show: March 6th, 2027
events.description:
The 2027 SEPC Food Show Produce Rescue will occur on March 6th at the Orlando World Center Marriott in Orlando, FL.

Volunteers will glean fresh fruits and vegetables from the SEPC Southern Exposure Food Show.  All produce will be donated to those who struggle with food insecurity in Florida.  

This large indoor event requires bending, lifting, packing boxes, and working with others!  We are looking for up to 100 volunteers to help!  We will have two shifts available. 

The morning shift will begin around 8:30 am, and the second shift will begin at 6 pm.  The more volunteers we have the quicker we will finish, and the fresh food will be off to those in need!

### Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

#### 1. What is the SEPC Food Show?

- This is an annual event hosted by the Southeast Produce Council (SEPC),  which is a large trade show connecting growers, distributors, retailers, and foodservice professionals to showcase new produce, technology, and trends in the fresh fruit and vegetable industry, featuring education, networking, and exhibits. 

SoSA is the food recovery recipient of the showcased food. Following the events, with the help of our volunteers, we pack everything up to be sent to various food storage and distribution agencies.  

#### 2. Who can attend? Are community service hours available?

- All are welcome—no prior experience needed! Perfect for families, small groups, or anyone looking to serve or receive community service hours. (Kids under 18 must be with an adult.) Please bring any community service paperwork to be signed at day of event.

#### 3. Can I take food if I would like to try it?

-  No. Contractually all food is sent to food banks and agencies that will distribute to people in need. If you know someone in need or are in need yourself, please let one of the SoSA Crew staff know that would like to take back. Food that is deemed "inedible" is available for volunteers to take as animal feed after all pounds are accounted for.

#### 4. What do I wear?

- Wear comfortable clothing that you can bend, lift and walk in. Closed-toed shoes are mandatory.

#### 5. Where does the food go?

- All the produce goes directly to local food banks and community partners feeding those in need.

#### 6. How can I stay in the loop?

- For event updates via email, sign up at: https://endhunger.org/get-involved/volunteer/

#### 7. Other FAQs :

- NO smoking, NO pets
Please note- Please bring your own water. There will be restrooms. 

📢 Questions? 
Contact:
Megan McEwen 
📞 (863)224-0403
📧 fl-glean@endhunger.org
