events.title: Freedom Fridays
events.description:
Join us on Fridays at NOON at the Williamsburg James City County Courthouse, located at 5201 Monticello Avenue, Williamsburg, with your signs, a cold beverage, and a chair, if needed. Bring a sign that represents the theme you are most passionate about.

COMMUNITY NORMS: Please read before attending one of our events. One of our main objectives is to host PEACEFUL, RESPECTFUL and SAFE EVENTS. Remember, when attending a Williamsburg JCC Indivisible event, your actions represent our group, and you are expected to conform to the Community Norms. Safety is a top priority for our attendees. Please remain out of the median, per instructions from the police. Being in the median puts us at risk and potentially drivers as well. Do not block the right-of-way for others. If someone is on the sidewalk, please step back and let them pass. If an Urgent Situation arises, we will raise a straight arm with our Hand in a Fist to ask for Silence. PLEASE DO THE SAME TO QUIET THE CROWD. This way we can quickly relay an important message to all. We wish to remind everyone that we do not react to those drivers who make it clear they do not support us by aggravating them through screaming obscenities or making certain hand gestures. We do not want to enrage them and potentially make everyone, including other drivers, less safe. It is easier to wave at everyone and say, “Have a nice day.”
PLEASE DO NOT BLOW WHISTLES UNLESS ICE IS PRESENT. The purpose of the whistles is to alert the public to be vigilant. Otherwise, blowing them can falsely alert the crowd to a danger that does not exist! At our events, please do not hold signs or otherwise promote other events that Williamsburg JCC Indivisible is not hosting. You may be placing a potential legal liability onto our group that we are NOT willing to accept. Please do not engage in DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOURS! If you are asked to stop engaging in activities which are disrupting an event to the point people are complaining to the hosts that they are experiencing physical or emotional trauma, it is expected that you will be respectful of others and follow our Community Norms and stop those behaviours. Loud noises, such as, but not limited to, COWBELLS, horns, etc., are usually deployed by counter-protesters to disrupt an event, not by attendees participating in an event. If you refuse to disengage from such thoughtless behaviours, do not ruin the event for everyone else - please be kind and leave! As with our previous events, the same rules apply. We will not engage with counter-protesters. If an issue arises, please notify one of the event organizers, who will be wearing Williamsburg JCC Indivisible T-shirt. We will not engage in any acts of violence or violation of any applicable laws or engage in civil disobedience. All actions will be peaceful. Everyone participating in this event will be required to behave lawfully to ensure the safety of event participants and will seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. We will obey the orders of authorized event marshals and law enforcement authorities. Event organizers will not be responsible for any injury or damage if any were to occur during this event. Each individual is responsible for the consequences of their actions and attends at their own risk. We will park in the Courthouse parking lot without blocking access lanes and will remove any trash that is left. We are committed to maintaining public health measures to practice safe protesting during these times. Please wear a mask and socially distance if that makes you more comfortable - weigh your own risk in attending. Follow all local safety guidelines at minimum, and any safety instructions from hosts that exceed local law.

location.venue: Donovan Hines Foundation of Exuberance Co

events.description:
2026 #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence

Beginning Wednesday, December 9, 2026 until the end of December, we will come together across the nation to host the #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence.

These local events will be anchored by the 14th Annual National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C.—held near the 14-year mark of the Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting tragedy, when a 20-year-old gunman armed with an AR-15 hunted and murdered 20 first graders and six educators.

Across the country, vigils (as simple as lighting candles) and gatherings will honor lives stolen by gun violence, uplift survivors, raise awareness, and demand urgent action from our leaders to finally end this epidemic. From schools and workplaces to houses of worship, neighborhoods, grocery stores, homes, nightclubs, streets, and even our democracy itself—gun violence impacts every aspect of American life.

The theme of this year’s campaign is #FreedomToLive—the simple, powerful idea that every person deserves to live free from the daily threat of gunfire. Together, survivors, families, advocates, and allies will raise our voices to ensure that FREEDOM means the right of every person to live, learn, work, worship, speak, vote, and gather without the daily fear of gun violence.

We stand in solidarity with over 1.4 million Americans who have been shot since Sandy Hook, with every community devastated by gun violence for decades. We will send a clear message to our local, state, and federal lawmakers, raise awareness, and help build the movement for common-sense solutions.

Let’s #HonorWithAction together. Let’s demand freedom from gun violence.

We're recruiting volunteers to serve as Election Protection Poll Watchers throughout Yuma County. This is an important, nonpartisan role that helps ensure voters can access the ballot free from intimidation or unnecessary barriers.

Whether you can volunteer for a few hours or a full shift, your participation makes a difference.

events.title: Anytime Virtual Phone Banking: Clyde for Congress
events.description:
Phone Bank for Clyde on Your Own Schedule

We know your schedule is busy, so we have made it easier than ever to make a difference on your own time. Sign up to make calls for the Clyde Jones for Congress campaign whenever it fits into your day—whether that is for 15 minutes between errands or two hours on a Sunday afternoon.

Phone banking is the fastest way to scale our grassroots outreach and talk directly with voters across Alabama's 1st Congressional District about lowering healthcare costs, fighting for working families, and bringing accountability back to Washington. With our flexible phone banking system, you can pull up a list and start dialing whenever you have free time.

How it Works:

Sign Up: Register here to receive instant access to our virtual phone bank hub. Your confirmation email will include details for how to start making calls right away from wherever you are. 

Start Dialing: Log in from any computer, tablet, or smartphone. 

Log the Data: Simply select the outcome of your call on the screen, follow the script to chat with the voter, and click to move to the next neighbor!

What You Need:

A laptop, desktop, or tablet with internet access.

A quiet, comfortable place to make calls.

Your unique login link (sent immediately upon RSVP).

Every call moves us one step closer to victory. Secure your access today and start dialing when it works best for you! For technical support or questions along the way, our organizing team is just an email or text away.

events.description:
Wisconsin is a critical battleground in the fight to roll back Donald Trump's extreme, authoritarian agenda. 

How?  By putting Democrats in control of the Wisconsin state offices, including governor, that can block voter suppression and gerrymandering efforts. But we'll only succeed if we're working together. We'd love you to come knock doors in Wisconsin with us.

### Meeting Location in Highland Park, address provided upon sign-up


Volunteers will meet at meet at the Highland Park Target parking lot (2099 Skokie Valley Rd, Highland Park, IL 60035) before carpooling to the Milwaukee area to knock doors.


### Please download MiniVAN


If you haven’t canvassed before (or if you have and you want to review) you will find it helpful to download the MiniVAN User guide and application in advance of your canvass (links below).


MiniVAN is the application we use to keep track of what happens during the canvass. It tells you what doors to knock, who you’ll be speaking to, provides the script for you to use, etc.


If this is your first time using MiniVAN, you'll receive an in-person training on-site during the canvass training!

events.title: Literature & Ladle Society Sorting Soup’s (Book Club’s) Sunday: Burnout @9am & This is the Plan @4pm
events.description:
#### Literature & Ladle Society Sorting Soup’s (Book Club’s) Sunday: Burnout @9am & This is the Plan @4pm -ZOOM

#### _This fall, The Ladle & Literature Society—also known as the Sorting Soup Book Club—this weekend 9/20 has  two (2) Book Clubs.. 9am and 4pm.

_We’ll gather around books that take both the personal toll of organizing and the practical work of winning seriously.

#### Let us know you will be attending either the 9am by RSVPing here -> https://mobilize.us/s/30D6NR

#### Sunday @ 9 am ..Burnout: The Secret to Unlocking the Stress Cycle

*Burnout: The Secret to Unlocking the Stress Cycle* by Emily and Amelia Nagoski explores why stress lingers in our bodies long after the immediate crisis has passed, and how we can interrupt the cycle through rest, connection, movement, boundaries, and joy. Organizers are regularly asked to absorb urgency, outrage, grief, and other people’s needs; without ways to process that load, exhaustion becomes a predictable political outcome. 

This discussion is for anyone who wants to build a practice of care sturdy enough to support the long haul—because a movement cannot afford to treat its people as disposable.

It is an antidote to doomscrolling and magical thinking: organized people change what looks inevitable by showing up, making a plan, and bringing others with them. 

#### Join the 4pm CDT we have  *This Is the Plan: How to End America’s Meltdown & Save Democracy* by Ben Wikler, turns toward the collective work of democratic renewal. Drawing from his organizing and political experience in Wisconsin, Wikler lays out a practical argument for building durable power, expanding participation, and addressing the systems that undermine democracy—not simply focusing on a single candidate or election. \\ NOTE NOV 1ST 4PM THIS IS THE PLAN IS CANCELED THIS WEEK ONLY …

sponsor.name: Organizing to Fight Oligarchy / We The Fighters

events.description:
### The election is around the corner. Let’s turn our anxiety into action!

We the Fighters is a group of everyday people who have decided to step up. In the face of injustice, we choose to act together over despairing alone. And we’re inviting you to join us.

We’ll be calling voters in our district to talk about our representative’s vote for the “Big Beautiful Bill,” what it has meant for our lives, and our chance to hold them accountable this November.

**We use an approach called deep canvassing:** asking meaningful questions, sharing personal stories, and making space for people to talk about what matters to them. We believe those connections are how we build the power to change things.

### Never done anything like this? You’re exactly who we need.
You don’t need political experience or all the answers. Bring yourself, a willingness to listen, and the belief that everyday people deserve better.

events.title: Honesty Coalition 2026 LGBTQ+ Youth & Parents Listening Session
events.description:
This session is for students and their parents. We'll have two rooms in the Zoom—so parents and students can speak freely with their peers!

The Belonging for Every Student Listening Campaign is a statewide effort to better understand how recent anti-LGBTQ+ laws are shaping the experiences of students, educators, and families across Ohio.

Over the past few years, laws like House Bill 8 have required all 611 school districts in Ohio to adopt new policies. While these policies are public record, what remains unclear is how they are being put into practice and how they are impacting real people in school communities.

This autumn, we are listening. We want to know: How are districts implementing these policies? Are schools going beyond what the law requires? How are LGBTQ+ students and families being affected? What changes are educators experiencing in their classrooms, materials, and ability to support students?

By gathering stories, insights, and data from across the state, this campaign will help build a clearer picture of what’s happening on the ground. These findings will directly inform advocacy strategies for the 2026–2027 school year, ensuring that efforts to support safe, inclusive, and equitable schools are rooted in the lived experiences of Ohio communities.

Please share with young Ohioans who have something to say about the experiences of LQBTQ+ students in our schools in the 2026-2027 school year.

events.title: Poll Greeting for Windsor Hills on Election Day

location.venue: Bent Mtn Community Center, Back Creek Elementary, Christ the King Prebyterian, Oak Grove Elementary, Hidden Valley High, Brambleton Center, Hidden Valley Middle

events.description:
We need your help to cover the polls in Roanoke County! Sign up to be a smiling poll greeter where you can welcome voters to the polls and hand out sample ballots with the names of Democratic candidates and information on 3 proposed state constitution amendments.

Voters who cast their votes for Democratic candidates want to see themselves represented! You can be the Democratic poll greeter that lifts our voters up and make them feel validated and proud to be a Democrat!

Poll-greeting is a simple activity. As voters come to the polls, simply ask if they would like a sample ballot. If so, then hand them one and point out that there is also information on the sample ballot about the proposed state constitutional amendments which they will also be voting on. It is that easy! As voter leave the polls, thank them for coming out and voting.

Feel free to bring a friend or come alone!

Once you sign up a Roanoke County Democratic Committee representative will contact you to assign one of the following polling locations; Bent Mountain Community Center, Back Creek Elementary School, Christ the King Presbyterian Church, Oak Grove Elementary School, Hidden Valley High School, The Brambleton Center, Hidden Valley Middle School.

events.title: The People's Tea
events.description:
## **Special Announcement** 

On Wednesday, November 4th, we'll hold a special session to hear stories from folks on the ground, make sense of what this election tells us about our landscape, and name what comes next. 

Because **our work doesn't end on Election Day**: we'll share the concrete ways we'll keep organizing to keep each other safe and protect our democracy in the months and years ahead.

We'll have Spanish translation available for this call. 

**Anuncio Especial**
El miércoles 4 de noviembre, realizaremos una sesión especial para escuchar historias de la gente en el terreno, entender lo que esta elección nos dice sobre nuestro panorama, y definir lo que viene después.

Porque nuestro trabajo no termina el Día de las Elecciones: compartiremos las maneras concretas en que seguiremos organizándonos para protegernos mutuamente y defender nuestra democracia en los meses y años por venir.

Habrá interpretación en español disponible durante esta llamada.

### More information: 
**The People's Tea** is a biweekly power hour where we’ll discuss what’s going on, what it means, and what we can do. 

At the People’s Tea, we will slow down, process the news, and make sense of what’s happening. We’re building a space where we can stay informed without losing our humanity (and sanity), and move from feeling overwhelmed and isolated toward understanding, connection, and collective action. 

We will meet every other **Wednesday at 8 PM Eastern / 7 PM Central / 6 PM Mountain / 5 PM Pacific.** There’s only one requirement to join. This will be a judgment-free space where we will show compassion and curiosity. We simply expect you to be respectful and non-judgmental. There are no expectations to have all the answers, know the “right” things, or even know where to begin. 

**Come learn, listen, and connect.**

events.title: Vienna/Fairfax VA Bridge Brigade - Weekly Wed. PM Rush Hour - Pop Up Nov 2

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
We are the Vienna/Fairfax chapter of over 400 Visibility Brigades around the country. As a group of volunteers, we will display large messages on the bridge at Vaden Drive over I-66 on a regular basis, starting Wednesday, September 16, to encourage early voting and other pro-democracy actions.   

We will provide large signs facing I-66 traffic on the bridge.  Please do not post other signs (or stickers or anything permanent) on the bridge.  You do not need to bring anything other than your energy.  But if you want to bring hand-held signs, please display those for the traffic driving over the bridge on Vaden Drive.  

Other notes: 
- There are two garages backing onto Vaden Drive; one on the Vienna side of the highway and one on the Fairfax side.  You need a credit card or metro card to exit the garages; weekday parking is $4.95.   Neighborhood parking is very limited.
- Bring water, hat, snacks, folding chairs, and sunscreen as needed for your own comfort.  Please take any litter home with you.
- Please be cautious if you cross Vaden Drive for the other side of the bridge.
- There is a public restroom in the Metro station.
- Check your email in case there is a last minute change. The event may be altered due to rain or extreme temperatures.
- We will do one Thurs in Oct (the 22nd) because early voting at the Jim Scott Rec Center on Vaden Drive starts there Oct 22 and runs to 7 PM.
- Most drivers react positively to our messaging.  If you receive a negative reaction, please remain positive (or at least neutral) to avoid escalating the situation.
- We must not block pedestrians getting across the bridge, so please leave room on the back end of the bridge sidewalks for pedestrians.
- No weapons of any kind and no violence. 
- If you wish to bring friends or family members with you, they are welcome. Please familiarize them with our rules and safety tips.

Our mission is to bring visibility to specific issues we're facing under the Trump regime, encourage action, and foster a sense of community for those that feel disheartened by the state of our nation. Join us and help us fight fascism!

Learn more about the Visibility Brigade at www.visibilitybrigade.com

events.title: Virtual Phone Bank for Karen Bass for Mayor!
events.description:
Join us every Tuesday and Thursday evening for a virtual phone bank where we’ll call Los Angeles voters to talk about why this election matters for them, their community and our collective future.

No experience needed!  You can join from anywhere (even outside of LA), as long as you’ve got a computer, internet connection and a headset or earbuds. You’ll get a quick training, a call script, and a list of numbers to work through. It’s a high-impact way to help: every conversation moves a real voter closer to the polls in support of Karen Bass.

What to expect:

	•	Weekly shifts, Tuesday and Thursday evenings
	•	Brief training and script walkthrough at the start of each shift
	•	Calls made through our online dialer, no special equipment beyond your computer and headset
	•	Campaign staff or skilled volunteers on hand the whole time to answer questions
	•	Join from anywhere: home, dorm, couch, wherever you’ve got wifi

What you need:

	•	A computer with internet access
	•	A headset (for clear calls and to keep your hands free)
	•	That’s it. We’ll teach you the rest

Every shift gets us closer to the votes we need. Sign up for a Tuesday or Thursday slot now, we’ll send the Zoom passcode and call tool access before your shift starts.

Questions? Feel free to reach out to us at saskia@karenbass.com or volunteer@karenbass.com

Quick note - for safety reasons, you are not allowed to make calls from your car while driving.

This event is modeled on the Signs of Fascism protests but is all about encouraging people to register and vote. Here's what to expect:

- The protest will last about an hour 
- Please dress colorfully (perhaps in red, white, and blue!) and wear comfortable shoes.
- We will stand spaced 10-15 feet apart by the side of the road, and each person will hold one sign.
- Our signs are in English on one side and in Spanish on the other side, so we will periodically switch languages all at the same time.
- This is not a somber protest the way Signs of Fascism is! When possible, we will have music. Feel free to bring a flag to wave, and to dance!

We will need a minimum of 15 people to have the most impact. We have 20 signs, so we can have up to 20 sign holders - but we will need a few additional folks to record, keep an eye out for any hazards or disruptions, and keep the sign-holders coordinated.

events.description:

Every other Thursday, we come together to learn what’s on the ballot, understand the issues **impacting our communities**, and explore practical ways each of us can be the difference.

These sessions help us live out the three **StayAwake** Commitments:

- **Dinner Table Conversations** — learning how to talk with family and friends about what matters most.

- **Voter Registration & Education** — helping others check their registration status, apply for absentee ballots, and get fully election ready.

- **Petition Campaigns** — adding your name to efforts that hold politicians accountable and protect the rights of Black people at home and across the nation.

events.title: Butte Door Knocking
events.description:
Nothing beats talking to a voter on their doorstep about Sam! Join Sam's Crew for a day of knocking doors around Butte. We'll meet at our campaign office at the Carpenter's Union Hall, where we'll train you on how to knock doors for Sam and you'll get a chance to practice before you head out.

We'll have a list of doors for you to knock, the script for your conversations, and a handy reference sheet on Sam's background and platform that you can carry with you. After everybody has knocked doors for a couple hours, we'll reconvene to debrief how it all went with some cold refreshments!

You do not need to have knocked a single door before this event - this is for beginners and experts alike! Talking in person with voters is one of the most effective and rewarding ways to spread the word about Sam, and we'll make sure you have the skills and tools to feel confident to get out there!

events.title: Georgia GOTV Phone Bank
events.description:
GA Ossoff Weekly Phone Bank — Every Thursday

Join us as we call Georgia voters to help them return their mail ballots and make a final plan to vote ahead of the November 3 general election.

Every week, we're reaching voters across Georgia to make sure they're ready to participate in one of the most competitive Senate races in the country. These are high-stakes elections, and turnout will decide the outcome—we're making sure no voter is left behind.

We'll help voters who have already requested mail ballots complete and return them on time, understand key deadlines, and make a clear, confident plan to vote, whether by mail, early in person, or on Election Day. We'll also send follow-up texts with early voting, polling location, and absentee ballot tracking information to those planning to vote early or on Election Day.

Volunteers will have real conversations with voters and help turn intention into action—making sure ballots are returned and votes are counted.

📞 Weekly phone bank: Thursdays at 12p.m. PT / 3p.m. ET (every week through Election Day)
🔥 No experience needed—training, scripts, and support provided.

This is how we win close races, by making sure every vote counts.
Your call could be the reason someone follows through. Sign up now and help power turnout in Georgia!

events.title: Intro to Abolitionist Feminisms Series: Intro to Abolitionist Feminisms Panel
events.description:
Hear from organizers and advocates in a conversation about abolitionist feminism, transformative justice, incarceration, and what it means to build movements rooted in collective liberation. This panel will connect the ideas explored throughout the series to the work happening in our communities today.
Panelists include Florida NOW members Sana Hafeez and Amaria Smith, as well as Miss Mei with Decrim305 and Hugo with Success Stories, the program featured in the film we are screening, The Feminist on Cell Block Y.
Stay after the panel for a brief Q&A chat. The panel will be recorded and uploaded to YouTube.

events.title: Florida NOW Anti-Racism Book Club Discussion: Abolition. Feminism. Now.
events.description:
Join the Florida NOW Anti-Racism Book Club for a discussion of Abolition. Feminism. Now. by Angela Y. Davis, Gina Dent, Erica R. Meiners, and Beth E. Richie.

n this groundbreaking book, four leading abolitionist feminist thinkers and organizers explore the history and present-day practice of abolition, drawing connections between struggles against prisons, policing, racism, gender-based violence, and economic injustice. The authors examine abolition not simply as an effort to dismantle systems of punishment, but as a project of building the social, political, and economic conditions that allow communities to thrive.

The book brings together decades of feminist organizing, scholarship, and movement-building to ask what it means to imagine a world beyond punishment, and how we begin creating that world now.

Join us for a conversation about the book’s central ideas, the movements and histories it explores, and what abolitionist feminism can teach us about building a more just and liberatory future.

Monday, December 21st, at 6:30 PM on Zoom

All are welcome, whether you’ve finished the book, are still reading, or are joining the conversation to learn more.

The Park Church, 208 West Gray St. Elmira, NY -- Beecher Hall

events.title: DCCC Rural Action Cohort Phonebanks
events.description:
The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee's (DCCC) National Rural Engagement program is welcoming volunteers for our Rural Action Cohort for the 2025-2026 election cycle!

What is the Rural Action Cohort?

The DCCC Rural Action Cohort is a newly created initiative built of and by rural folks and will be doing rural-specific, virtual, direct voter contact to rural voters across our battleground districts with each session offering participants exposure and connections with leading national and statewide rural organizations across the country to help build the different toolboxes, infrastructure, and efforts of our cohort in our own communities.

It is a virtual opportunity for like-minded rural volunteers and committed leaders to build a community specifically for mobilizing our networks and taking regular action to take back the House with a coalition that reflects our communities.

We know that we must both build lasting infrastructure and do direct action and outreach to meet this moment and build lasting change for our folks on the ground. We hope this to be a starting point that can be scaled in cycles to come.

The virtual cohort will be active leading up to the Election with activation including phonebanks, text banks, and Days of Action targeting key House districts that are part of our path to victory while the emphasis is placed on being OF rural folk, BY rural folk, and FOR rural folk!

events.title: Volunteer as a Nonpartisan Election Challenger in MI!

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Sign up here for an **in-person challenger shift** at an early voting site or Election Day polling place! **Requirements: challengers must be registered to vote in MI and can't be a candidate on the ballot or poll worker during this election**
 
As our eyes and ears on the ground, nonpartisan challengers are stationed at polling places, early voting sites, and absentee counting boards across Michigan to monitor the election process. Challengers have the right to challenge the actions of poll workers if the challenger believes that the poll worker is not following the law. Our pro-voter challengers make sure eligible voters can cast their ballots, free from interference and voter intimidation.  

Before your shift, you must complete our virtual, on-demand training. The training will be available starting in October. After you complete the training, we will send you your challenger credential and official shift assignment via email.

events.title: Phonebank for Trina Swanson!
events.description:
Trina has built this campaign on listening to Minnesotans and making sure every community has a voice. Now, we need your help reaching voters across the district. 

Join us to call voters across the district and share Trina’s vision for opportunity at home! Together, we can make sure voters across northern and central Minnesota hear Trina's message and build the momentum we need to win in November! 

In the first 10 minutes of your shift, we'll provide a short tutorial on our calling system on a google meet. Please note that you will not be expected to make calls directly from your phone number.

If you are interested in making calls but none of the listed shifts work for your schedule: please reach out to jtaylor@crossroadscampaigns.com. We can find another time!

events.title: Weekly Doorknocking with No Hate in WA State in Whatcom

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
What to expect

New to canvassing? That’s completely okay! No experience is required, and we’ll start every shift with a short training so everyone feels prepared before heading to the doors.

We’ll meet together at the Community First Whatcom office, go over the basics of the conversation, show everyone how to record who they spoke with at the door, and get paired up before heading out to canvass in the community.

For your first shift, you can shadow an experienced canvasser so you can hear how they talk with folks at the door and get comfortable before jumping into conversations yourself.

Most of the shift will be spent walking through a neighborhood and having short conversations with voters. You do not need to memorize a script or be an expert. We’ll provide the information, materials, and support you need.

Please bring:

A fully charged smartphone
Comfortable walking shoes
Weather-appropriate clothing
Water and anything else you may need while walking

Additional details, resources, talking points, MiniVAN instructions, and arrival information will be sent after signup so you have everything you need to feel prepared for your shift.

Why door knocking matters

Most of us have had an election where the ballot showed up and we realized we hadn’t researched everything on it yet, or where voting almost slipped our minds altogether. One of the most effective ways to help people participate is simply reaching them before their ballot arrives, having a one-on-one conversation, and making sure they know what is on the ballot and why it matters.

Those conversations can make a real difference. Here in Whatcom County, the 2026 primary for the 42nd Legislative District Senate race came down to just four votes between two candidates.

If knocking on doors sounds intimidating, know that canvassing is typically a really positive experience. We’ll be reaching out to voters who regularly participate in elections and having short, friendly conversations with people in our community. You’ll also be out there alongside other volunteers, not doing it alone.

events.title: Knock Doors to Get Out the Vote for Iowa Democrats in Fort Dodge!
events.description:
Election day is fast approaching, and we’re hitting the pavement and knocking on doors for Rob Sand and Iowa Democrats up and down the ticket. Talking to voters face to face is the best way to have an impact on this election and turn out voters to vote early! 

Rob is visiting every corner of the state to share his vision of an Iowa that isn’t Redder or Bluer, but Better and Truer with voters, and so are we! Whether you’re a long-time volunteer or stepping up to help for the first time, we’ve got you covered.

Before knocking doors, we will make sure everyone gets trained on how to talk to voters, how to record canvassing data, and canvassing best practices. Then, we’ll hit the pavement.

Election Day will be here before we know it! We have times every day through November 3rd, and we need your help!  Find more events here: https://www.mobilize.us/iowaforward/

We can't wait to see you!

events.title: 2026 #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence
events.description:
2026 #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence

Beginning Wednesday, December 9, 2026 until the end of December, we will come together across the nation to host the #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence.

These local events will be anchored by the 14th Annual National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C.—held near the 14-year mark of the Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting tragedy, when a 20-year-old gunman armed with an AR-15 hunted and murdered 20 first graders and six educators.

Across the country, vigils (as simple as lighting candles) and gatherings will honor lives stolen by gun violence, uplift survivors, raise awareness, and demand urgent action from our leaders to finally end this epidemic. From schools and workplaces to houses of worship, neighborhoods, grocery stores, homes, nightclubs, streets, and even our democracy itself—gun violence impacts every aspect of American life.

The theme of this year’s campaign is #FreedomToLive—the simple, powerful idea that every person deserves to live free from the daily threat of gunfire. Together, survivors, families, advocates, and allies will raise our voices to ensure that FREEDOM means the right of every person to live, learn, work, worship, speak, vote, and gather without the daily fear of gun violence.

We stand in solidarity with over 1.4 million Americans who have been shot since Sandy Hook, with every community devastated by gun violence for decades. We will send a clear message to our local, state, and federal lawmakers, raise awareness, and help build the movement for common-sense solutions.

Let’s #HonorWithAction together. Let’s demand freedom from gun violence.

Bring signs and your friends. Sign Messages Recommended: End Gun Violence, March For Our Lives, Stand With Victims, Stop Domestic Abuse

events.title: Volunteer at the Polls on Election Day
events.description:
Help us cover every polling location on Election Day! Volunteers are needed to help pass out the Official Democratic Slate outside the polls on November 3rd.

Passing out the blue slate at the polls on Election Day is the single most impactful thing you can do to help elect Democrats up and down the ballot. Our judges do not have partisan affiliation on the ballot, and passing the blue slate helps ensure that Democrats know who to vote for.

The polls are open from 6:30 am - 7:30 pm. Are you able to cover a polling location all day? If you can, sign up for all 4 shifts.

Only able to help a part of the day? Sign up for the shift(s) that work best for you.

After you sign up, you will be contacted by a volunteer or staffer from HCDP to schedule you for a specific polling location. The outreach will not be immediate. Please include your phone number when you RSVP so we can call you. We ask that you be as flexible as possible with the location so we can cover as many of our polls as possible.

Note: If you are a precinct executive, you do not need to sign up here. Instead, reach out to your Ward or District Chair, or if you don't have their contact information, email HCDP's Executive Director Zophia Pittman at zophia@hamiltoncountydems.org.

events.title: Election Protection for Beginners, Procrastinators, and People Seeking Community (EVI)
events.description:
Do you think everyone should be able to exercise their right to vote? Are you concerned about both what might go wrong with the election but also about your personal ability to do something about it? Whether you don’t know the difference between a ballot box and a voting center, whether you know what you should do but fear you might never get around to doing it, or you just want to pair your activism with hanging out with other like-minded people, please join our Fall Online Election Protection Group (sponsored by East Valley Indivisibles, but anyone is of course welcome)!

The beginning of each meeting will feature a presentation of timely Election Protection concepts and actions that will be recorded, followed by a closed (not recorded) conversation by attendees about their questions, concerns, and strategies.

Everyone who registers will receive a link to the presentation recording as well as action items and key takeaways for the week. Whether you can join live or just want to receive the updates, please register and invite your friends!

All meetings will be held on Tuesdays at 5pm Pacific EXCEPT the week of the mid-term election, when we meet on Monday, November 2nd. We will also have one planned post-election meeting on Tuesday, November 10th to celebrate our work and discuss next steps. We will continue this group until results are certified and winners are seated.

events.description:
What we're doing:
Every conversation matters, even the ones that happen one phone call at a time. We're gathering on Tuesdays and Thursdays in-person, or Wednesdays virtually, to call Democratic and unaffiliated voters across NC-01 to listen to what's on their minds and earn their support for Congressman Don Davis.

Why it matters:
This district has shifted again; What was once rated R+3 has been redrawn to R+5. That's a real challenge, but it also means this race is winnable, and it will come down to who shows up and has the best conversations, whether at the door or on the phone.

We're not just asking for votes. We're listening first to what voters and their families care about, what's worrying them, and what they need from their next Representative. Then we're asking for their support, and making sure every single one of them knows: early voting runs October 15th–31st, and Election Day is November 3rd.

Why your help is essential:
You don't need a car, comfortable shoes, or even to leave your couch: just your voice and a little time. Phone banking lets us reach voters who might never answer the door, and every call you make is one more NC-01 neighbor who hears directly from our campaign instead of an ad.

The ask:
Join us virtually to make calls using our auto-dialer. Use the script as your guide, listen more than you talk, and invite voters to make a plan to vote early or on Election Day. 
No experience necessary, we'll train you, and our team will be with you the whole time.

What you'll receive:
Auto-dialer access
Call script
Zoom link for live training and support during your shift

events.title: Educating Texas: Text Bank for Pro-Education Candidates
events.description:
Every Monday  | 6:00 - 7:30 P.M. | Virtual 

Join us Monday nights as we combine learning with action. Educators will be virtually text banking for pro-public education candidates while building our collective political power.

Each session in our Educating Texas series digs into a different public education topic affecting our students, educators, and staff; connecting what we learn directly to the work of turning out voters who will fight for our schools. 

This is political education in action. Join us in text banking for candidates who will show up for public education and higher education. 

Bring a working cell phone and your energy to change Texas!

Schedule: 
 

October 26 

•	The last week of early voting. Help us remind voters to go to the polls! 

November 2 

•	The night before Election Day. We need all hands on deck to do a final Get Out The Vote push.

events.title: IA: Calls for Clean Water
events.description:
This year, Food & Water Watch fought the Iowa legislature to restore our statewide water monitoring program, and sued the EPA to protect Iowa’s drinking water. **Now, Food & Water Action is calling our neighbors, asking people how they’ve been impacted by the crisis, and building the movement to fight for what Iowans deserve.**

Join our Community Calls for Clean Water to take action!

Together, we'll spread the call to action about what we can do to keep our water safe and send a clear message to elected officials: _stop putting billionaires ahead of working families._ These virtual phone banks will be hosted on Zoom and kick off with a community check-in, plus training for first-time callers! We'll debrief at the end to share lessons learned and talk about what's next. 

Please note: you will need a phone AND a computer, laptop, or tablet to participate! Please contact an organizer if you don't have access to these devices, and we will do our best to accommodate. 

**No experience is required; beginners are welcome!** Calls will not be made using your phone number.

events.title: Tax the Billionaires: Phone Bank for YES on Prop 40
events.description:
Join YES on Prop 40 as we call voters to win a billionaire tax this November!

California is one of the wealthiest places in the world, but working people are being asked to pay the price for devastating healthcare cuts so billionaires can get more tax breaks.

Prop 40 is our chance to change that. It makes billionaires pay their fair share so California doesn't lose healthcare funding and essential services. 

At this phone bank, we'll talk to voters about why California needs to tax billionaires to keep hospitals and ERs open, protect healthcare for California families, and fund food assistance and K-14 education.

No previous campaign experience is necessary. We'll give you everything you need to take action.

Together, we're building a grassroots movement to mobilize one million Californians and win YES on Prop 40.

Tax billionaires. Save lives. Vote YES on Prop 40.

events.title: Blue Water Indivisible Saturday Pop-ups
events.description:
Now that our evenings are getting darker earlier we are returning to our Saturday mid-morning pop events at the corner of Sanborn Street and Pine Grove Avenue.  With the mid-terms around the corner, please consider lots of get-out-the-vote messages and only the occassional candidate message. 

Pease watch our Facebook page for additional sign ideas. We rather like  'Hate isn't Patriotic," and "Your Vote is Your Super Power." What's caught your eye that resonated with you?

This a local Indivisible event!

We will meet from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. every Saturday, beginning Saturday, Sept. 12, 2026. Please pay close attention to the weather and dress accordingly. We will have handwarmers available for those who might need them. Parking is available across Pine Grove Avenue along the service drive, at the Sanborn tennis courts and baseball field and along Sanborn east of the baseball field. 

Please join us to help get out the vote!!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: 威善高 Scott Wiener 電話拉票活動! Chinese Phone Bank!

sponsor.name: Team Wiener: Supporting Scott Wiener for Congress

events.description:
歡迎參加我們每週之電話拉票活動,支持威善高 (Scott Wiener) 競選國會!

每逢星期三及星期四下午1:00至4:00,來自選區之義工一同致電選民、分享威善高政綱，並協助我們競選團隊。

毋須任何經驗。活動開始前我們將提供簡短培訓，過程中亦會全程提供支援。無論閣下是初次參與電話拉票，抑或經驗豐富之義工，我們誠意歡迎閣下加入。

電話拉票是我們接觸選民之重要方式之一。

閣下需要準備:
- 一部手提電話
- 一顆願意協助威善高當選之熱誠!

即刻報名，與我們一同建立這場由人民力量推動的競選團隊。

Join us for our Weekly Chinese Phone Bank for Scott Wiener for Congress!

Every Wednesday from 1:00–4:00 PM, volunteers from across the district come together to call voters and share why Scott Wiener is the right leader for Congress.

No experience is required. We’ll provide a quick training at the beginning of the phone bank and support throughout the event. Whether you're a first-time caller or a seasoned volunteer, we’d love to have you join us.

Phone banking is one of the most important ways we connect with voters!


What you need:
- A cellphone
- Enthusiasm to help elect Scott Wiener!

Sign up and help us build the people-powered campaign that will win this race.

events.title: Knock Doors for Abdul, Jocelyn & Michigan Democrats in Marquette
events.description:
Join One Team Michigan to Get Out The Vote & talk with voters in your community!

This fall, Michigan picks a new U.S. Senator, a new Governor, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.

Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.

Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.

Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

Join One Team Michigan to Get Out The Vote & talk with voters in your community!

This fall, Michigan picks a new U.S. Senator, a new Governor, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.

Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.

Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.

Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

events.title: Untested, Unsafe, Unacceptable – Write to Your Members of Congress NOW!
events.description:
Dear friends,  

I am one of the millions of Americans who rely on mail in voting. But now, the government is trying to rush through a dangerous, untested USPS rule that could disenfranchise millions of voters who rely on mail in voting. Our Votes Are in Danger!

Here’s what’s happening: 

•USPS built a brand new ballot screening system in just 3 months (normally takes over a year)

•It was given less than 1 week of testing

•A “zero failure” policy means: one barcode error = thousands of ballots rejected

•The Trump administration has appealed to the Supreme Court to allow this rule to take effect before the midterm elections

📢 "Untested, Unsafe, Unacceptable" – That's Our Message

We are saying NO to:

❌ UNTESTED – A system built in 3 months with less than 1 week of testing

❌ UNSAFE – One barcode error could reject thousands of ballots

❌ UNACCEPTABLE – Our votes are NOT your experiment

We need to make our voices heard – NOW.

📝 Your Action: Write to Your Members of Congress

Step 1: Find your members of Congress

•	Find your U.S. Representative:  
https://www.house.gov/representatives/find-your-representative

•	Find your U.S. Senators:
 https://www.senate.gov/senators/senators-contact.htm

Step 2: Use this template (copy and paste)

Subject: UNTESTED. UNSAFE. UNACCEPTABLE. – Protect Mail-In Voting Now

Dear [Senator/Representative Last Name],

I am a constituent from [City, State], and I urge you to take immediate action to protect mail in voting.

The new USPS ballot system is:

❌ UNTESTED – A system built in 3 months with less than 1 week of testing

❌ UNSAFE – One barcode error could reject thousands of ballots

❌ UNACCEPTABLE – Our votes are NOT your experiment

Over 250 current and former members of Congress have already urged the Supreme Court to block this executive order.Please join them.  

I ask you to:  

1.Support Senator Blumenthal’s investigation

2.Co sponsor legislation to protect mail in voting rights

3.Call on USPS to pause and independently test this system

Please act now. Our votes depend on it.

Sincerely,  
[Your Full Name]  
[Your Address]  

Step 3: Send it!  

•Use your members’ official website contact forms (fastest)

•Or email/call their offices directly

events.title: Phone bank for Kelly
events.description:
Kelly needs your help so that she can help everyone in Northeast Indiana and win! Sign up and you can phone bank from home to help elect Kelly!

If you want to make calls with a Google Voice:

For Android and iPhone:

Sign up for Google Voice & get your number
Important: Google Voice doesn’t offer 1–800 numbers. 
Make sure that your phone is on and can get texts. To check, we’ll text you a code.
1.	Download the Google Voice app.
2.	Open the Voice app  .
3.	Sign in to your account.
4.	Review the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy    tap Continue.
5.	To pick your Google Voice number, tap Search.
•	You can search by city or area code. If numbers aren’t available, try a nearby city or area code.
6.	Next to the number you want, tap Select. 
7.	Follow the instructions.

This fall, Michigan picks a new U.S. Senator, a new Governor, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.

Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.

Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.

Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

events.title: Wave Signs - Win Votes!
events.description:
Wave Signs. Build Momentum. Win Votes!
Join fellow volunteers for a fun, high-energy sign-waving event in various locations in Spokane County! 

We'll gather at a busy intersection during the morning and evening commute to wave campaign signs, greet passing drivers, and show our community that our campaign is strong. 

Exact locations will be sent prior to the shift.

Sign waving is one of the easiest and most effective ways to build name recognition before the primary. Every smile, wave, honk, and thumbs-up helps spread enthusiasm and reminds voters that Election Day is approaching.

No experience is necessary—we'll provide the signs and everything you need. Just bring your energy, and help us make a big impact in a short amount of time!
events.accessibility_notes: We will be standing on busy street corners, likely on sidewalks.

events.title: Phone Bank for Lauren Jewett
events.description:
Join us for a virtual phone bank session to support Lauren Jewett's campaign for Louisiana's 1st Congressional District! Lauren is a special education teacher, community leader, and the only Democrat running for Congress against House Majority Leader Steve Scalise.

Team Lauren is working hard to reach as many voters as possible before the election and we need you help to hit our goal. Every conversation can make a difference. 

No experience necessary. You can make calls to voters across the district from the comfort of your own home. 

Let’s make some calls and win this together!

events.title: Get Out the Vote the VA Dems!

This event is VIRTUAL - you can join from ANYWHERE. Training will be provided! Sign up for 2 or more times and invite your friends!

events.title: Lakeville Democratic Town Committee Monthly Meeting
events.description: This is the monthly meeting for the Lakeville Democratic Town Committee. The meeting is open to all community members in Lakeville and the greater Plymouth and Bristol County area. We welcome not only Democrats but also Unaffiliated voters and Republicans to get greater community consensus.

events.title: Florida Student Power Youth Climate Coalition
events.description: We are a coalition of young people fighting for climate justice, rooted in our communities, committed to action, and building a better future together. At this meeting, we’ll connect with fellow youth organizers, give updates on our local and statewide climate campaigns, and plan our next steps around events, actions, policy, and advocacy. There will be space to share ideas, build leadership, and support one another as we organize for bold, intersectional climate solutions.

events.title: Pass Sample Ballots during Early Voting!
events.description:
Friends! Please join us as we greet voters outside Early Voting at the Wilmette Park District Community Recreation Center!

Voters look to us for recommendations in down-ballot races! Join and/or bring a friend!

Please volunteer for one or more 2-hour shifts to distribute sample ballots, which help inform voters of democratic candidates in all down-ballot races.  We are looking for at least 2 people per shift.

events.title: Team Folk Weekend Doorknock

We are so excited to have you on our team and for volunteering to turn out the vote for Anders - thank you & see you soon!

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Join us for our next Choice Voting Volunteer Action Meeting as we prepare for the next phase of our campaign to bring more representative elections to San Diego.

We'll share campaign updates, introduce our new Volunteer Manager, relaunch our volunteer committees, and discuss upcoming opportunities to get involved. Whether you're a longtime volunteer or attending for the first time, this meeting is designed to help you find meaningful ways to contribute based on your interests, skills, and availability.

We'll also be recruiting volunteers to host Neighborhood Conversations (house parties), expand our volunteer network, and support community outreach efforts across the city.

This is more than an update—it's an opportunity to help shape the future of the campaign. Come ready to connect, get involved, and take action.

Together, we're building the movement for Choice Voting—one conversation, one volunteer, and one neighborhood at a time.

events.title: The Pioneer Project
events.description:
The Pioneer Project is a two-part program where participants will be trained in the fundamentals of legislative advocacy and then supported as they practice what they learned in a real-world policy campaign. The program begins with 8 remote trainings over the course of 4 weeks (skipping over the week of Thanksgiving) that will equip our trainees with the skills to design a policy, propose it to their lawmakers, and pull the right levers to get it passed into law. After completing the trainings, participants can choose to join us in our mission of jumpstarting a nationwide transition to clean energy by launching a policy campaign of their own. 

Our curriculum covers the process of legislative advocacy from start to finish, and is based on the lived experience of youth and environmental advocates over the years. Legislative advocacy is a skill that allows everyday people to weigh into and lead political decisions in their community. Right now, politicians mainly hear from corporations and paid lobbyists when making their decisions and creating policy. Legislative advocacy opens the door for anyone to enter that conversation and make political change. 

The second and most exciting phase of the program is our clean energy policy campaigns, led by past participants in the states where a clean energy transition is needed the most. After completing all the trainings, participants can choose to launch their own statewide policy campaign or join an ongoing campaign using our clean energy policy framework. Throughout these campaigns, participants will apply everything they've learned from the trainings in real life, strengthening their knowledge with experience. Policy campaign teams will be provided with continuous support from Pioneer Energy through coaching, templates, and other resources. 

Everyone and anyone is welcome to join the Pioneer Project, but we believe this program will be especially helpful to grassroots groups looking to add another tactic to their toolbox, young activists learning how to build their own power, and people interested in a future in public policy.

PROGRAM DETAILS: The training phase spans 4 weeks, skipping over the week of Thanksgiving. Trainings are Monday and Wednesday at 6 PM est, and run for an hour or less. Finally, these trainings are free, remote, and open to all!

TRAINING TOPICS
November 16th: Welcome to Pioneer Energy
November 18th: Engineering a Policy
November 30th: Preparing for the Project
December 2nd: Researching your Legislature
December 7th: Lobby Meetings
December 9th: Bill Drafting and Sponsorship
December 14th: Supporting the Bill
December 16th: Advocacy and the Home Stretch

events.title: Protest ICE Deportations the AROCC Detention Center at Mesa Gateway Airport

address_lines: East Southern Avenue & South Stapley Drive

events.description:
## 🛫 ICE & AROCC: Stop ICE operations at Mesa Gateway Airport!

For eight months, [Mesa Valley Indivisible](https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/) members and a coalition of groups around the country have been working relentlessly to end Avelo Airlines’ involvement in the unlawful and inhumane deportation of primarily non‑violent immigrants via Mesa Gateway Airport. As a result, Avelo Airlines ended their contract with ICE in January 2026! 

Although Avelo Airlines has left our Mesa Gateway Airport, ICE deportation missions still happen every day and the Arizona Removal Operations Coordination Center (AROCC) continues to operate.

When local lawmakers recently conducted a surprise visit to the Arizona Removal Operations Coordination Center here at Mesa Gateway, they were sickened by what they found. Despite being a transit hub meant for 12-hour stays, people were being held for weeks, packed like sardines on bare concrete floors with no beds or showers. While the administration continues to claim these are short-term facilities, the reality has proven to be gut-wrenching medical neglect and overcrowding.

#### 📢 Join us on Saturday, December 19th to challenge the illegal, inhumane, and unconstitutional ICE removal operations!

    
--------------------------------------

## 🔑 Key Concerns Driving the Protest:

- We have compiled public records, congressional oversight letters, and local reporting into one place. 
- Please read our complete [Mesa Valley Indivisible AROCC and ICE Air Deportations Fact Sheet](https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/ice-deportationsarocc) to understand the full scope of our key concerns and see how you can take action.

--------------------------------------

  - Keep an eye out for emails from Mesa Valley Indivisible and check your spam/junk folder if you do not see them!
  - [Mesa Valley Indivisible](https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/) prioritizes strategic visibility to ensure our message reaches the widest possible audience. To keep our movement growing, we protest at high-traffic areas where Mesa residents are most likely to see us and join the cause.

events.title: Potluck and White Elephant Get Together
events.description:
LET’S CELEBRATE! 
Let’s get together, share some food, swap some questionable gifts, and talk about how much fun we had along the way! 
POTLUCK
Bring your favorite dish to share for a late lunch. Homemade, store-bought, famous family recipe, mystery casserole.
WHITE ELEPHANT FUN
Bring a wrapped gift valued at $25 or less. Don’t put your name on it. Just add it anonymously to the gift pile.
Then the fun begins!

Everyone draws a number. In numerical order, each person gets to choose a wrapped gift OR steal a gift someone else has already opened.

 THE STEAL RULE
A gift can be stolen up to four times. After the fourth steal, that gift is officially LOCKED IN and cannot be stolen again.

Come hungry. Bring a gift. Prepare to defend your treasure.
And, most importantly, come ready to celebrate with friends!

At the gathering we are also collecting for the Children’s  Holiday Toy Drive, brought to you by The ZIPPER JUNCTION Project™, The goal is to ensure that children in need, residing in Wayne and Pike Counties, are served by this local community effort.

events.description:
Join the Madison NorthEast Dems to Get Out the Vote for the Midterm Elections! This will be our last big push to knock on every door to motivate our neighbors to cast their votes for our Democratic candidates.

The NED Team Needs You!

Our candidate slate for the state is great!
•	Governor – David Crowley 
•	Lt. Governor – Sarah Godlewski
•	Attorney General – Josh Kaul
•	Secretary of State – JoCasta Zamarripa
•	Treasurer – Yee Leng Xiong

We will also be canvassing to GOTV for our state assembly candidates, Dina Nina Martinez-Rutherford and Andrew Hysell and our Congressman Mark Pocan.

Have you heard?! There are 3 constitutional amendments on our ballot this November. We're voting NO on every one of these.

- Prohibit Government Discrimination or Preferential Treatment
Ballot language: Prohibits state government from discriminating against, or granting preferential treatment to, any person based on race, sex, color, ethnicity, or national origin in public employment, education, contracting, or administration. 

Context: Wisconsin already prohibits discrimination under state and federal law; the amendment also bars “preferential treatment” programs aimed at equity. 

- Prohibit Partial Veto to Increase Tax or Fee
Ballot language: Bars the governor from using the partial veto power to create or increase any tax or fee.

Context: When Republican State Legislatures have passed budgets eliminating the funding of programs that serve the people, a Democratic Governor has been able to use this power to ensure the program is funded. 

- Prohibit Government Closure of Places of Worship During Emergencies
Ballot language: Bars the government from closing gatherings at places of worship during declared emergencies, including public health emergencies.

Context: Covid was very serious before the vaccines were widely available.  Superspreader events led to illness and death outside the circle of the attendees.  

---
 The NED team offers new canvasser training at the start of every shift. We will try to pair up new canvassers with more experienced ones as folks are available. We provide all the materials you need to canvass; literature, a list of voters, a script to follow, a bottle of water, and a snack. You just need to bring your smartphone. We'll be using the MiniVAN App to collect the voter responses and guide you through your turf. Please download the MiniVAN Touch or MiniVAN 9 App by NPG VAN and create and Action ID before coming to the canvass. Training on how to use MiniVAN is included in the new canvasser training. 

 Don't want to canvass, but you still want to help? Sign up for a shift and tell the NED team member who reaches out to confirm that you want to help in another way, such as making phone calls for volunteers, delivering yard signs, or assisting with canvass launches. There is a place for you on the NED team. 

 This year is our first opportunity in 16 years to win a trifecta of Democratic government in Wisconsin. We can win the State Assembly, Senate, and Governor's seat this November. With a Democratic trifecta, progressive priorities can become law. Lower taxes, higher wages, funded public schools, affordable health care, environmental protections, the overturning of Act 10, and more can be in our future by wining these November elections. You need to be a part of this effort.

 Join NED to Get.Out.The.VOTE!!!

You’re invited to join us for a screening of 'No Country for Mothers', a film sparking honest conversations about modern motherhood and building a movement demanding better support for families. This isn’t just about watching a film. It’s about coming together to talk openly about the realities of motherhood, family life, and the systems that shape them. Whether you’re a parent, an ally, or simply someone who cares about the future of families and communities, there’s a place for you in this conversation.

After the screening, we’ll have a moderated discussion where we can share experiences, ask hard questions, and explore what it means to build a movement for better support for families. We’ll then gather for a reception and continue the conversation together.

We’d love for you to join us and help spread the word to parents, non parents, and allies in Riverdale and beyond.

events.description:
Join State Rep. Natalie Price for a virtual phonebank to support Dr. Theresa Brooks for State Senate! 

We'll be reaching out to voters across Senate District 9 to talk about the issues that matter most to Michigan families - lowering costs, fixing our broken healthcare system, investing in public education, protecting our lakes and water, and delivering real experience for our communities. 

Whether you're a seasoned volunteer or phonebanking for the first time, every call matters as this is one of the most competitive state senate races in Michigan, and we need your help to FLIP this seat and DEFEND our Democratic Majority. 

------------------
Dr. Brooks is a current Troy City Councilwoman and a practicing physician where she is focused on delivering results and bringing investments and infrastructure back to the people of the district. As a physician, she knows her patients are having to make impossible choices such as between their prescriptions and their groceries. 

The district includes: Rochester, Rochester Hills, Troy, Utica, parts of Sterling Heights and Shelby Township

events.title: 2026 Election Day Poll Greeting w/ Granville Dems
events.description:
Join us for a shift - or three! - of poll greeting at one or more of the 15 polling places in Granville County on election day! This is a great opportunity to engage with voters and provide key information about our candidates and the issues that matter most to Granville County.

Poll greeters will help create a welcoming atmosphere for voters, answer basic questions, and distribute blue sample ballots and candidate literature.

What You’ll Do:

Greet voters with a friendly smile as they arrive to vote early. Hand out sample ballots and candidate literature, talk briefly about issues such as clean water, healthcare access, and public education. Help ensure that voters feel comfortable and empowered to cast their ballots.

Why It Matters:

Your presence at the polls helps build community, increases visibility for our Democratic candidates, and encourages voter turnout. Every conversation can make a difference in this important election. Together, we can turn out more voters and make our voices heard!

No experience necessary – just wear a Democratic shirt, or a blue shirt if you can. Please sign up for at least three shifts to help us ensure a successful election season.

Check this link for a list of our polling locations to find the one nearest you! https://www.granvillecounty.org/DocumentCenter/View/1431/Current-Precinct-List-PDF

RSVP today and make a direct impact on your community!

events.title: Intro to Community Organizing: Growing to Win (MV)
events.description:
How do we win? How do we advance our goals for social change? We get organized! Community organizing is people power in action. It's about uniting around a shared goal to make a difference together. Anyone can be an organizer. You don’t need a degree or years of experience—just a passion for change and a willingness to listen and learn.

_Billionaires are already organized, and we can be too!_

In this training opportunity, facilitator Brian Eaton will lead participants in an exploration of Structure Based Organizing, a century-old technique for building power and creating durable solutions to issues that matter to a community.

Participants in this one-hour workshop will learn:

- How Structure Based Organizing works—its key principles and techniques

- How Structured Organizing Conversations act as the foundation of successful campaigns

- How Structure Based Organizing can enable us to build local power into a mass movement

**Note: Enrollment limited to 8 participants.**

events.title: Voter Protection Calls with Mass Dems Organizing Hub
events.description:
Join us to help ensure that likely Democratic voters in states such as Georgia, Iowa, Michigan, Nevada, North Carolina and Ohio are able to cast their ballots this fall and have their votes counted!

In each shift, we will do phone banking to support current voter protection priorities for the Democratic Party in one of these key states. Our calls may include recruiting volunteers to serve as poll observers, helping voters who have been marked inactive or have other registration issues to update their registration, or helping voters whose ballots have been rejected to fix the issue, known as ballot curing.

ON NOVEMBER 1, we will work on ballot curing in Nevada, meaning calling voters whose ballots have already been received but were rejected due to a technicality and letting them know so they can address the issue and get their vote counted!

We will meet on zoom and provide training, a script, and contact information for targeted voters through the OpenVPB system. No experience or background knowledge required. 

It can be helpful to use Google Voice for these calls. We will explain further in the training, but you may want to prepare by signing up for a free account at http://voice.google.com if you don’t already have one.

Hosted by the Massachusetts Democratic Party’s Campaign Services Subcommittee in partnership with VoPro Pros, a national volunteer organization focused on voter protection. Open to volunteers anywhere.

In the week after Election Day, many voters in North Carolina will need to take one more step to make their vote count. They may need to complete a form; they may need to bring their ID or a proof of address to their County Board of Elections.

events.title: The Black Table: YDNC Black Caucus FIRST Annual Friendsgiving
events.description:
Pull up a chair and join the YDNC Black Caucus for our first annual Friendsgiving! The Black Table: An evening of community, connection, and joy. We will begin with our Black Caucus General Meeting and end with a Friendsgiving celebration.

 6:00–6:30 PM | BLACK CAUCUS GENERAL MEETING

We’ll kick off the evening with a brief Black Caucus meeting where we’ll:

- Share updates and upcoming initiatives
- Discuss our goals and priorities moving forward
- Talk about ways members can get involved
- Give members an opportunity to share ideas and connect

After the meeting, we’ll officially transition into our Friendsgiving celebration!

6:30 PM | THE BLACK TABLE: FRIENDSGIVING

Once the meeting wraps, it’s time to eat, fellowship, and celebrate!

We’re asking everyone who is able to bring a dish to share. Whether it’s your favorite family recipe, a holiday classic, a dessert, a side, or something completely your own, bring a little something to add to the table! This is a potluck-style celebration, so the more dishes, the better. 

WHAT TO EXPECT

🍽️ Friendsgiving Dinner
Bring a dish, grab a plate, and enjoy good food with good people.

🥂 Drinks & Mocktails
Enjoy an evening of drinks, conversation, and fellowship. We will have wristbands for anybody 21+

🎶 Music & Black Joy
Relax, socialize, laugh, and enjoy the evening with your Black Caucus family.

🤝🏾 Community & Connection
Build relationships with Black young professionals, organizers, leaders, creatives, and changemakers from across North Carolina.

WHO SHOULD ATTEND?

This event is open to Black Caucus members, prospective members, and Black young adults interested in connecting with the community. You do not have to be politically active to attend. Whether you’re an organizer, professional, student, creative, community member, or simply looking for a space to connect with other Black young adults, there’s a seat at our table for you.

👗 DRESS CODE

Friendsgiving Chic | Elevated Casual

Come cute, comfortable, and ready to fellowship!

WHY “THE BLACK TABLE”?

The table is where we gather.
Where we break bread.
Where we share stories.
Where relationships are built.

Come for the meeting.
Stay for the fellowship.
Bring a dish. Bring a friend. Bring your good energy.

There’s always room at the table. 🖤

events.title: The First Five Years: Nashville Early Childhood Convening

location.venue: American Baptist College- Lewis & Scruggs Hall

events.description:
## Birth to five isn’t a phase. It’s the blueprint.

The first five years shape everything that follows. Our children deserve a community that treats them that way.

Join us — parents, providers, educators, leaders — as we start building a coalition for Davidson County’s youngest residents.

This isn’t a meeting about our kids. It’s a room built by the people raising them. That coalition carries the work forward: setting its own priorities, doing its own research, and advocating for the investment this community’s youngest residents deserve.

### What This Convening Does

- **Builds the line from kitchen table to policy table**, which helps residents connect lived economic pressure to local systems and public investment while understanding how to plug in after the election

- **Sets community-defined priorities** around family affordability, carried forward into TEA's economic justice work with community voice at the forefront

- **Activate and equip residents and trusted messengers with toolkits to GOTV** because while we know that voting alone won't fix the problem, we acknowledge that it is a power-building tool in our toolbox

## The gaps are real. So is our power to close them. Let's put our feet on the street and our boots on the ground.

events.title: Weekly Text Banking
events.description:
**Text Bank for Hands Off Colorado — Weekly Shift**

Join us for a flexible, remote text banking shift in support of Hands Off Colorado! No experience necessary — everything you need is provided.

**How it works:**

*Every Monday, you'll receive an email with a link to that week's active campaign
*Commit to logging in for at least 1 hour sometime during the week — work whenever fits your schedule
*Scripts are pre-written, and responses to common questions are already prepared for you
*Just click the link, log in, and start sending texts to reach community members

**Why it matters:**
Hands Off Colorado is standing up for trans and immigrant communities across the state. Text banking is an effective ways to have real, personal conversations at scale — every text helps build support and mobilize people to act.

**What you need:**
*A computer or smartphone with internet access
*No prior experience required — the platform walks you through everything
*About 1 hour of your time, any time during the week

Need help? Join office hours every Monday from 12 - 1p on Zoom here: https://us06web.zoom.us/j/85091758479

Sign up below and we'll send you the details each Monday to get started!

Join One Team Michigan to talk with voters in your community about the issues that matter most!


This fall, Michigan picks a new Governor, a new U.S. Senator, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.


Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.


Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.


Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

Voting is our right and our responsibility and the only way we have to resist the authoritarian takeover led by DJT with GOP support.

We will be standing out (and sitting in folding chairs) on a section of Route 9 between Brookline Ave and Brookline Place 4 days a week to encourage people to vote and to vote early. We will be there for regular 30 minute shifts in support of voting and early voting between now and Election Day.  

Mondays and Wednesdays 8:00-8:30pm 
Tuesdays and Thursdays 5:00–5:30pm

We will gather with signs and American flags on the sidewalk along the section of Route9/Washington St. between Brookline Ave. and Brookline Place.  Depending on the number of people we might be on one or both sides of the street.

events.title: Hands Off Beverly Weekly Standout
events.description:
HANDS OFF BEVERLY believes that Trump and his authoritarian policies pose a serious threat to America. We stand firmly for democracy, the U.S. Constitution, civil liberties, and equal rights for all. These values are what truly make our nation strong—and we refuse to let them be taken away. We resist with determination, creativity, and community. 

Through joyful, peaceful, and musical protests, we raise our voices, inspire others to stand up, support one another, and remind people that they are not alone. The majority of Americans believe in democracy, justice, and freedom.
