events.title: PA Labor 2026 - Pennsylvania Alliance for Retired Americans Senior-to-Senior Weekdays Phone Bank
events.description:
Do you care whether Social Security will continue to pay full benefits? Do you care that your prescription drug prices are increasing? Do you care that your local hospital may close, because of Republican cuts to Medicaid?

If you care about these issues, then join the Pennsylvania Alliance for Retired Americans (PARA) and the Pennsylvania AFL-CIO in helping to flip the US House of Representatives this fall. Join our phone banks calling senior voters in Pennsylvania districts where we can elect pro-senior, pro-worker, pro-retirement security candidates to Congress. The next Congress will decide whether Social Security is fully funded or whether every senior receives a benefit cut. The midterm elections are crucial for deciding whether seniors in this country can retire with dignity. Join PARA in the fight to protect and expand Social Security and Medicare by phone banking for pro-senior candidates with us.

Before making calls, PARA will provide all phone bank participants with a brief training on our phone banking system and a script to use when calling constituents. No phone banking experience is necessary to join us! All you need is a phone and a computer or tablet. Staff will be on hand to answer any questions and guide you through the process.

Admission is free, but please consider making a small donation during registration. Reserve your spot today to connect with fellow advocates for an unforgettable evening of art, discussion, and solidarity!

events.title: Standout to SUPPORT IMMIGRANTS- No Fear Street Theater - Saturdays 11am-1pm

sponsor.name: No Fear Street Theater in MA

address_lines: Intersection of Mall Road and District Ave.

events.description:
Speechifying, Shakespeare, & Sea Shanties! Every week, we stand on Burlington Mall Road with signs, costumes and flags. We come out to show support for our immigrant neighbors, express our shame at ICE, and build community in opposition to the cruel and unconstitutional actions of our government. We are there to tell the world that there is a ICE CONCENTRATION CAMP just two blocks away. 

We are not there merely to make propaganda against ICE. We are there to make propaganda against fear.

Every car that honks in support as they pass is in a small way joining the Resistance. Many who honk may be expressing themselves against ICE terror for the first time. This breaks the ice, and makes it easier for them to take the next steps. It helps them help others to overcome their fear. We are there to cause a ripple effect. To fight against the terror visited on immigrants, we need to fight against our own internalized terror. We have nothing to fear. We are America, fighting back. If you REGISTER by FRIDAY, you will be notified of cancellations by email. All events held rain or shine & only cancel for large storms or high winds. We recommend dressing comfortably for the weather and bring a water bottle. Bring your sign in support of Immigrants or you are most welcome to use one of the ones we have on hand. 

This is a creative, participatory protest. If you support immigrants and their constitutional rights, join us!

https://www.nofearstreettheater.com/

events.title: Carrollton AREA Democrats - Nico Nights with Neighbors

location.venue: Nico's Cocina - Event Room (to right of restaurant)

events.description:
WELCOME to our once a month (third Wednesday) meeting of the Carrollton AREA Democrats Club.  Our focus is to get to know our Neighbors - to meet like-minded folks for fellowship, education, solidarity and purpose.  Learn how WE can shape our plans as we seek to SAVE OUR COUNTRY AND DEMOCRACY!  

Our November 18th meeting is a continuation of our mission to understand and get to know our neighbors better as we take a timely look at our "Mosaic of Carrollton" - people living in our community and how we can be Allies to Each Other. 

This month we have invited Madison Noelle McNair (she/her) to present "Disability & Democracy: Inclusion As A Core Value."  We will be discussing accessibility, inclusion, accommodations, activism, disability history, and how disability is intersectional with all causes.

Presenter's Bio:
Madison is 29, she was born & raised in the Dallas area, she has been disabled her entire life and is passionate about accessibility. She began her journey by volunteering starting at 5 years old, and started more dedicated advocacy at 18 years old. She has been honored to work with many non-profit and advocacy groups across Dallas including Sunrise Movement Dallas and Sunrise Movement Tarrant, Dallas For Change, La Colectiva NTX, El Movimiento, Viva Colectiva, Vecinos Unidos DFW, New Disabled South, Dallas Area Transit Alliance, and she feels extremely lucky to have worked for many more in addition to these. Madison is currently a part of the Class of 2026 and Cohort 7 of the LBJ Women’s Campaign School at UT Austin, on the Patient-Family Advisory Council (PFAC) at Parkland, and the Paratransit & Accessibility Advisory Group (PAAG) with DART.

Instagram: @monoqueenmadi 

We are looking forward to presenting additional educational topics at future meetings for all of us to learn about, understand, and appreciate our commonality. 

As always - we will give time to any candidates that are stopping by to introduce themselves and speak for a few minutes at the end of our meetings.

PLEASE NOTE - for those who can arrive early - about 5pm - you may participate in #CRAFTIVISM. If you arrive at 5PM or later - we will be creating "At Risk" packets to be distributed in our community for those who may be targeted by ICE. In addition - we have created "Whistle kits" for Allies.

THE MEETING WILL BEGIN A LITTLE BEFORE 7PM.

We are a Grass Roots Group dedicated to preserving our American way of Life that honors the Individual with Diversity, Equality and Dignity. Learn about ways you can participate in ACTIVISM.  Learn how you may participate in our HIVES (Precinct) project.  We are Creating FUN Caring Communities - and Winning Elections!  And we are building on our momentum from 2025 thanks to your growing enthusiasm! 

Let us help you find ways that you may use your skills, talents and strengths to participate in our fight to take back our country thru activism, demonstrations, precinct building, voter registration and much more.  

Our Goal is to be a source of Information to all Carrollton AREA Democrats so they may make informed and wise decisions at the voting booth. 

We now have a Web Site: https://www.carrolltondemocrats.com/. This will provide our Carrollton Democrats the resources they need whether they live in Denton or Dallas County.  

JOIN US every 3rd Wednesday of the Month:
Nico Nights with the Neighbors - Nico's Cocina (6:30 to 8:30). 

3065 N. Josey Lane, Carrollton, TX 75007

We meet in the EVENT ROOM to the right of the restaurant. 

Please sign up on Mobilize so we may prepare enough materials for everyone. 

If you wish to be placed on our email list, (only 3-4 a month) please SIGN UP on CarrolltonDemocrats.com.  And we'll be able to introduce you to your neighbors in your precinct.   

Again - we are happy you have found us - look forward to meeting you!

events.title: FINAL STRETCH - Road To Black November Phonebank with Us
events.description:
Join the Road to Black November Phone Bank and help us increase Black voter participation across Jefferson County!

You will call residents to share accurate, nonpartisan voter information and help them prepare for the November 3 election. Before the October 19 registration deadline, we will encourage residents to check their voter status, register to vote or update their information. After the deadline, our calls will focus on helping residents find their polling place, make a voting plan and identify any assistance they may need.

During your shift, you will:

Receive training and a phone-banking script.
Call Jefferson County residents from an approved list.
Direct residents to www.RoadToBlackNovember.com.
Help residents find the information they need to prepare for Election Day.
Record responses so our team can provide appropriate follow-up.

Thousands of residents may not discover a problem with their voter status until they arrive at the polls. A short telephone call now can help someone check their information while there is still time to act.

No experience is required. We will provide the training, script and support you need. All you need is a telephone, internet access and a willingness to help your community.

Every call matters. Every voter matters. Sign up for a shift and invite a friend or family member to phone bank with you!

Road to Black November is a nonpartisan voter-participation initiative. We do not support or oppose any candidate or political party.

### Welcome to #TeamMaryland.

events.title: Missouri State University ALL IN Party at the Polls: Voting is Easy as Pie
events.description:
To encourage voting and democratic engagement in a positive and festive atmosphere, Paws to the Polls will be joining us yo greatly enhance our usual tabling for Election Day. 

We have a table and tent near the door of the polling location on campus, and our presence has always been greatly appreciated. Normally we supply sample ballots, voter guides, general nonpartisan information, pens, and stickers and the opportunity to take a picture with our “First Time Voter” sign for those starting out their civic engagement path. 

Our fall theme this year is “Voting is as Easy as Pie.” We will serve pizza pies but also regular pie, hot chocolate, and cider. Join us for a fair-like atmosphere (like we do at the Voting Fair), with our table-top wheel and the opportunity to answer questions and win prizes, and photos with our mascot (The Bill of Schoolhouse Rock fame). 

All of the nonpartisan educational/informational aspects will also be included that we normally provide.
events.accessibility_notes: The Central Polling locations in Springfield are all accessible, with equipment accessible to mobility, visual, and hearing-impaired individuals.

events.title: Literature & Ladle Society Sorting Soup’s (Book Club’s) Sunday: Burnout @9am & This is the Plan @4pm
events.description:
#### Literature & Ladle Society Sorting Soup’s (Book Club’s) Sunday: Burnout @9am & This is the Plan @4pm -ZOOM

#### _This fall, The Ladle & Literature Society—also known as the Sorting Soup Book Club—this weekend 9/20 has  two (2) Book Clubs.. 9am and 4pm.

_We’ll gather around books that take both the personal toll of organizing and the practical work of winning seriously.

#### Let us know you will be attending either the 9am by RSVPing here -> https://mobilize.us/s/30D6NR

#### Sunday @ 9 am ..Burnout: The Secret to Unlocking the Stress Cycle

*Burnout: The Secret to Unlocking the Stress Cycle* by Emily and Amelia Nagoski explores why stress lingers in our bodies long after the immediate crisis has passed, and how we can interrupt the cycle through rest, connection, movement, boundaries, and joy. Organizers are regularly asked to absorb urgency, outrage, grief, and other people’s needs; without ways to process that load, exhaustion becomes a predictable political outcome. 

This discussion is for anyone who wants to build a practice of care sturdy enough to support the long haul—because a movement cannot afford to treat its people as disposable.

It is an antidote to doomscrolling and magical thinking: organized people change what looks inevitable by showing up, making a plan, and bringing others with them. 

#### Join the 4pm CDT we have  *This Is the Plan: How to End America’s Meltdown & Save Democracy* by Ben Wikler, turns toward the collective work of democratic renewal. Drawing from his organizing and political experience in Wisconsin, Wikler lays out a practical argument for building durable power, expanding participation, and addressing the systems that undermine democracy—not simply focusing on a single candidate or election. \\ NOTE NOV 1ST 4PM THIS IS THE PLAN IS CANCELED THIS WEEK ONLY … 

#### Join by Zoom .. The Literature & Ladle Society Sorting Soup’s (Book Club’s) Sunday sessions: Burnout - ZOOM at 9:00 a.m. & This is the Plan @4pm CST, -> https://bit.ly/NWSOFA-Zoom

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Since November 2020, the League of Women Voters of Michigan and their Pro-Democracy Partners have worked to be the public’s eyes and ears at Michigan’s county canvass of votes cast during an election. Each year they work together to ensure that trained volunteers observe County Board of Canvassers (BOC) meetings, across the state of Michigan, watching the process by which local results are reviewed and certified.

This consistent, nonpartisan observation promotes transparency and accountability, helps identify potential issues that could put timely certification at risk, and reassures Board of Canvassers members and election staff that the public is engaged in their work. Should observation uncover anything beyond the canvassers’ ministerial, nondiscretionary duties, LWVMI can elevate the issue to the Secretary of State’s office or an election attorney.

### Your Role As An Observer:
- Our BOC Observer are an important aspect of our volunteer election work! 
- Our observers not only serve to build trust in the community as well as between local government and the League, but they also help to ensure our elections are running as the laws intended. 
- Reporting from our observers helps us understand the health of our democratic systems, where issues are happening, and where things are running smoothly.  
- These insights are important to all of us working to support our democracy, and ultimately support our communities in ensuring their voices are heard! 

We hope you will join us, volunteer, and bring a friend to be a part of this election work!

PS: Shifts are subject to change, as county clerks work to finalize the details of the county canvass. If your shift is cancelled, you will be contacted by a representative from the League of Women Voters.

events.title: PR Committee Meeting - Democratic Party of Outagamie Co.
events.description:
Join the Democratic Party of Outagamie County’s Public Relations Committee to help us use tech to build the messages, visuals, outreach, and community connections that move local Democrats forward. We are an all-local, all-volunteer team within our county party, working to elect dems and further progressive values right here at home.

Volunteers with specialized skills often lead projects in their areas of expertise, but there’s room for learning and collaboration, too. You don’t need to know every tool already, we’re looking for people who are comfortable using technology, willing to learn, and ready to take ownership of tasks.

Whether you are a web developer, designer, photographer, chronically online, spreadsheet organizer, metrics-minded planner, email design wizard or simply someone who wants to pitch in when you can, there is a place for you on the PRC. Most volunteer roles are designed for a manageable 2–3 hours per week, and monthly project-based assignments are available for people who cannot take on an ongoing role.

At this meeting, we’ll:

- Welcome new and returning volunteers and make space for quick introductions
- Share updates on social media, email, events, and current PR projects
- Review open assignments and volunteer needs
- Match people with roles based on their interests, skills, and availability
- Discuss ways to support DPOC events, candidates, Outagamie Action Teams, and local community partners
- Gather ideas for future content, campaigns, and projects

We are currently especially looking for volunteers interested in:

- Social media static & Carousel content design, videos, and engagement
- Copywriting, editing, proofreading
- Graphic design, Canva templates, print materials, and email design
- Photography, short-form video, and video editing
- Website updates and event information
- Project coordination, deadline tracking, and intake support
- Press releases, talking points, media relations, and rapid-response writing
- Event promotion, flyer distribution, and volunteer coordination

No prior committee experience is required, just be comfortable working between your phone and laptop, learning new software as needed, and communicating digitally to a modern audience. We can provide tools, templates, direction, and a supportive team, bring your skills, curiosity, and ideas. If you are not ready for a standing role, you can also join our Project Volunteer pool and opt into one-off assignments that fit your schedule.

The PR Committee is where we turn good work into clear, local, people-centered communication. Help us make sure Outagamie County voters know what Democrats are doing, where they can get involved, and why every election matters.

Please RSVP so we can welcome you, share meeting materials, and help connect you with the right opportunities.

events.title: MFT & Moms First Present: No Country for Mothers | Live with Reshma Saujani

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
One night. One film. The founder of Moms First, in the room, in Denver.

RSVP: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/mft-moms-first-present-no-country-for-mothers-live-with-reshma-saujani-tickets-2002174965218

Only valid tickets purchased through Eventbrite will be admitted to this event.

We need to talk about something bigger than the next dance floor. The culture wars have divided us — this is how we come back together.

MFT is proud to partner with Moms First to bring their film No Country for Mothers to Apollo Hall, Denver — with founder Reshma Saujani joining us live.

No Country for Mothers explores the culture wars surrounding American motherhood and why both the "girl boss" and "trad wife" labels ultimately distract us from the real issue: the lack of support for American families. Following activist Reshma Saujani, the film charts a growing national movement to reunite moms across divisions and win the kind of historic support families actually need.

Since its June 2026 NYC premiere, the film has reached 1,000+ community screenings nationwide and holds the record for the most producers ever credited on one feature. On November 9, it's Denver's turn, with a live, intimate Q&A led by the film's Executive Producer and Moms First Founder & CEO, Reshma, in person.

Moms First is fighting for the policy change mothers deserve — paid leave, real childcare, structural support. We've spent years building the other half of that fight: the community, joy, and permission to come first that prove what happens when moms feel seen, resourced, and supported — we take on the world.

The night:

- Cocktail hour, charcuterie & cash bar
- Full screening of No Country for Mothers
- Live Q&A with Reshma Saujani
- Apollo Hall, Denver — Monday, November 9, doors 5pm
- $45 (+ fees) per ticket · 10% of proceeds go directly to Moms First
- Dress code: glam, elevated cocktail — wear something that makes you feel powerful. Can't swing it? No sweat, just bring the vibe.

Endless gratitude to Apollo Hall for donating their beautiful space and believing in this mission as much as we do — this night wouldn't be possible without them.

This isn't for a side. It's for every mother who's tired of being asked to pick one.

RSVP: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/mft-moms-first-present-no-country-for-mothers-live-with-reshma-saujani-tickets-2002174965218

Only valid tickets purchased from Eventbrite will be admitted to this event.

Guests can park in the garage, including designated accessible parking spaces, and take the elevator to the third floor, where an accessible walkway/ramp leads directly into Apollo Hall. events.title: GOTV Towson
events.description:
### Welcome to #TeamMaryland. 

We’re so excited you’re interested in knocking on doors to re-elect Governor Wes Moore and to elect Democrats up and down the ballot!

**First time volunteering?** No worries. Each canvass shift starts with a training with an organizer who will be there to help you out. We’ll send you out with a buddy so you can knock on doors together. 

**Are you a pro canvasser?** GREAT! Join us at our office to pick up some lit and a packet and we’ll get you out on the doors! 

### What you’ll need. 
**Before you knock on doors with us, you’ll need some things.**
1. A smartphone so you can download the MiniVAN Touch app, the Democratic Party’s canvassing app. Download it on [iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547) or [android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&gl=US).
2. A full water bottle! We’ll have water but always best to come prepared
3. Weather-appropriate clothes and good walking shoes!

**Who are you bringing along?** The more folks we have on the doors, the more voters we will be able to bring. So forward this event to a friend or two...or three? Or share it on social media using the hashtag  **#TeamMaryland.**

events.description:
# Join United for a New Economy Action in person or online to make calls, meet new friends and Get Out the Vote!!

This November, voters across Colorado have the opportunity to push back against greedy corporations and billionaires and prioritize a tax system that works for real people. That's why we'll be making calls to voters about **Prop NN and Amendment 87.** These measures represent a one-in-a-generation opportunity to build a better future for our communities- so let’s Get Out the Vote and win on November 3! Whether you’re a community leader, policy pro, or simply someone who believes in the power of fully-funded communities, we want you there.

Come meet fellow volunteers, speak with directly impacted voters and make sure EVERYONE has what they need to vote this November. 

No phone bank experience necessary, just a sunny disposition and a desire to help the people around you impact their community by voting!

### Don’t Forget!
Bring a fully charged phone and, if possible, a laptop computer. Snacks, drinks, and fun times will be waiting for you at the canvass site!

events.title: GOTV Windsor Mill
events.description:
### Welcome to #TeamMaryland. 

We’re so excited you’re interested in knocking on doors to re-elect Governor Wes Moore and to elect Democrats up and down the ballot!

#### On October 31st at 12pm, we have Governor Moore, Congressman Johnny O and Councilman Julian Jones joining for the canvass launch.


**First time volunteering?** No worries. Each canvass shift starts with a training with an organizer who will be there to help you out. We’ll send you out with a buddy so you can knock on doors together. 

**Are you a pro canvasser?** GREAT! Join us at our office to pick up some lit and a packet and we’ll get you out on the doors! 

### What you’ll need. 
**Before you knock on doors with us, you’ll need some things.**
1. A smartphone so you can download the MiniVAN Touch app, the Democratic Party’s canvassing app. Download it on [iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547) or [android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&gl=US).
2. A full water bottle! We’ll have water but always best to come prepared
3. Weather-appropriate clothes and good walking shoes!

**Who are you bringing along?** The more folks we have on the doors, the more voters we will be able to bring. So forward this event to a friend or two...or three? Or share it on social media using the hashtag  **#TeamMaryland.**

Join us for our monthly in-person meeting.

The first *Tuesday** of every month, True Northers meet in-person in Copley Square. Sign up to receive the location address.

### For November 10th:   

> These have been a lot of weeks — full of action, uncertainty, hope, grief, and everything in between. So we’re setting aside some time to just be together.
>

>

> 
> *Please join us — we’d love to see you.*

events.title: UTSA Main Campus  - Voter Mobilization Event

address_lines: Paseo Principal in front of the McKinney Humanities Building (MH)

events.description:
Are you serious about turning the tide in Texas? Are you tired of sitting on the sidelines and ready to make a difference?

## Sign up here to join us in registering eligible UTSA students to VOTE!
___
All volunteers are welcome! 

*HOWEVER*, to *register voters* at this event, you **MUST** be a certified Volunteer Deputy Registrar (**VDR**) in at least **Bexar County**.

If you're interested in becoming a Volunteer Deputy Registrar, you can take our [VDR Training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908495/).

### How to prepare:

If this is your first time volunteering with Powered by People, please sign up for our quick [**New Volunteer Zoom Training**](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)!
This will help you get up to speed with how we run events and how to use REACH.

Then, review our [**REACH Guide**](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1hgXy1A-xYafd4donvC18mGerT05S2yXICe5TLCX2hSE/edit?tab=t.0) as it has helpful information on using REACH in the field.

___
### Where we'll be:

**PARKING:** The [Ximenez Avenue Parking Garage](https://maps.app.goo.gl/jr3Hj1x6TXXNzkiZ7) is the best place for visitors to park. Don't forget to **pay downstairs** *before you leave*!

**MEETING LOCATION:** 
**Paseo Principal** outside the [McKinney Humanities Building](https://maps.app.goo.gl/13EmJf72WLmBKpmq7), near the Sombrilla Plaza.
___
### What to bring:
Please bring your **fully charged phone** with REACH installed, water, and comfortable shoes.

If you are a *Volunteer Deputy Registrar*, please bring your **VDR number** for Bexar County (and any nearby counties where you have VDR reciprocity). 

Clipboards, pens, voter registration forms, and other materials will be provided at the event, but feel free to bring your own just in case.

events.title: Phone Bank for Mary Ann Perkins (virtually on your own time)
events.description:
Help elect Mary Ann Perkins to the Missouri House by reaching voters across House District 100! This is a virtual, self-paced phone bank, so you can make calls from wherever you are and whenever works for your schedule.

No experience is necessary—we’ll provide everything you need to get started, including calling instructions and a script. Every conversation helps us build support, identify voters, and connect Mary Ann with the community.

How it works:

Sign up to phone bank on your own time
Make calls virtually from your phone or computer
Use our provided script and calling platform
Record your results and help the campaign reach more voters

Whether you have 20 minutes or a few hours, every call makes a difference. Thank you for helping us build a campaign powered by people!

events.title: Poll Greet with Team Perkins
events.description:
Help us get out the vote for Mary Ann Perkins for Missouri House District 100 on Election Day!

Join our team at a local polling location to greet voters, show your support, and help make sure Mary Ann’s campaign has a strong presence on Election Day. Poll greeters are an important part of our GOTV effort and help create a welcoming, positive experience for voters.

What you’ll do:

Greet voters as they arrive at the polling place
Hold campaign signage and represent the campaign
Encourage voters to support Mary Ann Perkins
Help answer basic campaign questions and direct voters to campaign resources
Check in with the campaign throughout your shift

No prior campaign experience is necessary. We’ll provide the materials and information you need.

Election Day is Tuesday, November 3. Sign up for a shift (or two) and help us finish strong!

events.title: Service At The Soup Kitchen With The Campbell County Democrats
events.description:
At the Campbell County Democratic Party, our motto is "Here For Good." That means we are here to serve our community and make it just a little bit better through our hands-on acts of service, showing up for our neighbors when it matters most.

We invite all community members, volunteers, and local Democrats to join us as we volunteer our time and energy at The Soup Kitchen on the second Monday of each month. Whether you are helping prepare meals, serving food, or assisting with cleanup, your presence makes a direct, meaningful difference for families and individuals in our area.

Come put our values into action alongside fellow community members who care deeply about lifting one another up.

What to Expect & How to Prepare

Tasks: Volunteers may help with food prep, serving guests, kitchen organization, and clean-up duties.

What to Wear: Please wear comfortable, casual clothing and closed-toe shoes. Aprons and hair restraints will be provided on-site if needed.

All Are Welcome: You don't need any prior volunteering experience, just a compassionate heart and a willingness to lend a hand!

Note: Please RSVP in advance so we can coordinate our volunteer count with the soup kitchen coordinators. We look forward to serving alongside you!

events.title: Chalk On The Sidewalk
events.description:
The election is over when all rightfully elected candidates are sworn into office.  Until then we need to use our voices to keep the midterm election front and center, in every way we can.  So we’ll spread the word with chalk!

We can provide short messages or bring your own on this subject. Our visually expressive messages will be written in a prominent location. 
We’ll email attendees the exact meetup location on Friday. It’s not the general intersection listed here.

(We’ll have just a few knee pads to lend out if you don’t bring something You’ll be fine without one though!)

*Desert Democracy stands firmly in alignment with Indivisible’s commitment to non-violence as a foundational principle of civic engagement and community organizing. We believe that meaningful change is built through peaceful action, respectful dialogue, and collective resilience.*

events.title: NC Ballot Cure
events.description:
Join us to knock doors of likely Democratic voters whose ballots were rejected. We'll be there to give them the information they need to get their votes counted!

These folks are committed to making their voices heard in this election, so these conversations are about proving guidance and encouragement to motivated voters.

This activity is best for experienced canvassers who are familiar with MiniVAN and have several hours to devote to this effort over the next few days. Volunteers must have transportation. 

**Cure Chase Canvass Schedule**

1. Attend a virtual canvass launch by Zoom. 
2. Canvass your turf (multiple passes may be required.)
3. Check in with your volunteer coordinator.

You'll only need to attend the training one time.

events.description:

Please sign up to receive details, updates, and reminders about sign-waving events. Training and materials will be available on-site. 

On Monday, we'll be meeting at Cottage Hill & Azalea at the old CVS location. 

 Let's Get Out The Vote, Mobile!
events.accessibility_notes: If you have a yard sign, please bring it.

events.title: Phonebank in Palm Springs (or on Zoom!)
events.description:
Every number we dial and voter we speak to brings us one step closer to flipping this seat! And Marni herself will kick this one off with us!

(Ignore the graphic above)  Join us in-person in Palm Springs or from the comfort of your own home on Zoom for a Monday phone bank! Hop on the dialer and chat with voters all over the district about Marni!

New to phonebanking! No worries! We'll train you, and be there to answer questions the whole time.

We hope to see you there! 

(ignore the graphic, Monday's event is 3 pm!)

events.title: Virtual Phone Bank: Reach New Texas Voters!
events.description:
### Help new Texas voters get the information they need.

We’re calling Texans who lean Democratic but don’t vote often, or haven’t voted before, to find out where they stand. When we find a supporter, we’ll text them resources to help them and their friends and family make a plan to vote: where to go, when, and how. The calls are quick, and everything you need is on one screen.

**No experience needed!** Whether you’re a first-time volunteer or a seasoned phone banker, you can make a real impact from the comfort of your own home. We’ll provide training at the start of each shift and support you every step of the way!

events.title: No Kings Vote Early GOTV Sign Waving w/Sammamish Stands Up
events.description:
Join the Sammamish Stands Up GOTV Sign Waving to remind Sammamish voters to turn in their ballots!

Bring your signs encouraging early voting - costumes and noise makers welcome, too!

Bring a GOTV sign to wave, a costume, and your energy!

Sign suggestions: Dropbox at City Hall - Ballot Boxes Open Now - The People Decide Our Elections - Voting Early Is How We Use Our Power - Early Voting is Election Protection - Use Your Power a the Ballot Box - When More People Vote, Democracy Wins

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

events.title: No Kings Vote Early - GOTV Banners Over Issaquah
events.description:
Join us at 4:30pm on the I-90 Exit 15 Pedestrian Overpass as we raise our banner to encourage voters to VOTE EARLY!

Stand alongside our banner or bring your own sign to wave towards the surface street side of the overpass. 

Sign suggestions: 
The People Decide Our Elections - Voting Early Is How We Use Our Power
- Early Voting is Election Protection - Use Your Power a the Ballot Box - When More People Vote, Democracy Wins

With heavy traffic both on the freeway and on the surface streets this is a high impact event.
Parking available near the I-Hop or Lake Sammamish Park with a Discovery Pass.

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

Safety is always our utmost concern and we are always looking for more safety team members. If you are interested in finding out more about joining, email us at indivisiblewa8@gmail.com

events.title: Flip the Future: Phone Banking with Barnwell County

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
One team. One South Carolina. Working together towards victory.

Help us Flip the Future statewide in South Carolina by reminding South Carolinians that polls are open and it’s time to Get Out the Vote! Every voter we talk to increases the likelihood of them voting and brings us one step closer to winning.

This action is the party’s number one priority for volunteers through Election Day.

This phone bank is VIRTUAL and includes training on how to use our phone banking website and how to talk to voters. You need a phone with internet connection. A laptop/tablet and headset/headphones are strongly recommended but not required. Once you have the link to your phone bank you can call at any time.

Invite your friends and call voters together!

Note: Shift times to the right are only suggestions. You can log in any time from 10 am to 8:00 pm and call for as long as you want! Once you’ve logged in for one shift and received the link to the phone bank, you can call any time you want – no need to sign in for another shift (unless you want a reminder)!

Be sure to get the word out to fellow Hill staffers and take part in flipping the House!

events.title: Knock Doors for Climate Champions in Cedar Rapids!
events.description:
Door Knocking for Climate Champions in Cedar Rapids! We’re hitting the pavement and knocking on doors for Iowa Democrats up and down the ticket. Talking to voters face to face is the best way to have an impact on this election. What better way to make a difference this election than talking to your friends and neighbors!

Before knocking doors, we will make sure everyone gets trained on how to talk to voters, how to record canvassing data, and canvassing best practices. Then, we’ll hit the pavement.

events.title: Planned Parenthood Coffee Talk & Book Club
events.description:
Join Planned Parenthood of TN & North MS for a book club! The book chosen is only 160 pages, so it can fit into busy schedules! 

Read the book, then come chat about key topics such as:
- Gender Oppression
- Beauty 
- Objectification 
- Sexuality 
- What feminist philosophy can bring to our understanding of justice, work, & the environment

Come hang out & chat even if you don't get to read the book. This is an impact circle event, so it's meant to celebrate community & bring like minded people together.

events.title: GOTV Canvass for Carol Glanville for State Senate
events.description:
Join Michigan LCV as we knock doors to Get Out the Vote for climate champion Carol Glanville for Senate District 30!

We'll be talking with voters across the district and encouraging them to support Glanville on November 3. This is a great opportunity to have meaningful conversations with your neighbors and help elect leaders who will fight for clean energy, environmental protection, and strong communities.

No canvassing experience is necessary, training will be provided before we head out.

Please bring: • Comfortable walking shoes • A reusable water bottle • Weather-appropriate clothing • A charged phone

Together, we can help elect climate champions and make a difference in our communities. We hope to see you there!

events.title: Sweetwater Monthly Executive Committee Meeting!
events.description:
🌵 Sweetwater County Democrats Monthly Meeting

Third Thursday. 6 PM. Rotating towns, same crew. 💙

It’s our monthly Executive Committee meeting! Come hang out, catch up, and help keep the wheels turning for the Sweetwater County Democrats.

We’ll talk about what’s happening, what’s coming up, where we can lend a hand, and how we keep showing up for our community.

📍 Green River Library
🕕 6:00 PM
📅 October 15th, 3rd Thursday of the Month 


We’re keeping our monthly meetings moving around Sweetwater County so we can stay connected to folks across the county. That means we’ll see you in Green River in October, Rock Springs in November, Green River in December, and keep rotating from there.

📅 October 15 — Green River
📅 November 19 — Rock Springs
📅 December 17 — Green River

We’ll kick things off at 6 PM with a short meeting — usually just 10–20 minutes to cover the business we actually need to cover. Then? That’s when the good stuff happens.

Stick around to catch up with fellow Democrats, meet new folks, swap ideas, ask questions, or jump into a training or organizing project. Sometimes we’ll have a specific training planned; sometimes we’ll just figure out what our community needs that month.

No fancy credentials required. No secret handshake. Just show up, bring a friend, and help us build a county party that knows its neighbors and knows how to show up for them.

Come for the meeting. Stay for the friends. 💙

events.title: Knock Doors with the Dunn County Dems!
events.description:
Help the Dunn County Democrats ensure the Chippewa Valley gets a blue wave in 2026 and elects David Crowley! Wisconsin Democrats are fighting for a democratic trifecta: Dem Governor and Democratic majorities in the state senate and state assembly. We are going to fire DVO and elect Becca Cooke to Congress while we are at it!

We’re keeping our monthly meetings moving around Sweetwater County so we can stay connected to folks across the county. That means we’ll see you in Green River in October, Rock Springs in November, Green River in December, and keep rotating from there.

📅 October 15 — Green River
📅 November 19 — Rock Springs
📅 December 17 — Green River

We’ll kick things off at 6 PM with a short meeting — usually just 10–20 minutes to cover the business we actually need to cover. Then? That’s when the good stuff happens.

Stick around to catch up with fellow Democrats, meet new folks, swap ideas, ask questions, or jump into a training or organizing project. Sometimes we’ll have a specific training planned; sometimes we’ll just figure out what our community needs that month.

No fancy credentials required. No secret handshake. Just show up, bring a friend, and help us build a county party that knows its neighbors and knows how to show up for them.

Come for the meeting. Stay for the friends. 💙

events.title: Yes On 2! Meet Voters At the Polls in Wayne County!

sponsor.name: Michiganders for Money Out of Politics

events.description:
Join Michiganders for Money Out of Politics (MMOP) to meet voters at the polls before they go vote!

MMOP is a grassroots, nonpartisan campaign working to reduce corporate influence in Michigan politics and bring greater transparency to our elections. After collecting more than half a million signatures from Michiganders statewide, Proposal 2 is officially headed to voters on the November 3, 2026 ballot!

We'll talk to voters outside their polling places and encourage them to VOTE YES ON 2! Whether you're a seasoned volunteer or it's your first time talking to voters, we'll provide training and supplies to get you ready to make a difference!

events.title: Show Up for Leon County Public Schools

location.venue: Aquilina C. Howell Instructional Services Center

events.description:
Join Families for Strong Public Schools-Leon at Leon County School Board meetings to stay informed, connect with neighbors, and advocate for students, families, and educators.

School board decisions shape classroom resources, student services, policies, and opportunities for families to be heard. When community members attend, we can follow those decisions and help keep students at the center of the conversation.

Whether this is your first meeting or you’ve attended many, your presence matters. Come to listen, learn about issues affecting Leon County Schools, meet other public education advocates, and share what you learn with your community. You do not need to speak during the meeting to make a difference.

Regular meetings are scheduled for the second and fourth Tuesdays at 6:00 p.m. at the Aquilina C. Howell Instructional Services Center, 3955 W. Pensacola Street. 
Check the Leon County School Board meeting page for the date, agenda, and any location changes before attending. https://www.leonschools.net/school-board-home

Let’s show up together for strong, accountable public schools in Leon County.

events.title: Phonebank for Blake Gendebien (Daily Training)
events.description:
New to phonebanking for Blake's campaign? Join us every day at 5:00 p.m. [EST] for a virtual training session. 

This isn’t a phonebank where success means making the most calls. We’re focused on quality over quantity: taking time to listen and having meaningful conversations with voters about Blake is the priority. We’ll cover how to start a conversation, listen without judgment, and focus our efforts on the issues which matter most to North Country voters.

events.title: Jen Todd Phone Bank
events.description:
Jen Todd represents the future Illinois’ 15th District deserves: practical leadership, real community connection, and a commitment to working people. A second-generation nurse, mother, daughter of a veteran, and union member, Jen has spent her life serving others—not chasing political power. She is running to ensure that rural communities, working families, veterans, farmers, and everyday people have a representative in Washington who listens, shows up, and fights for the resources our district needs. Her priorities include lowering costs for families, protecting access to healthcare, supporting public education, defending fundamental freedoms, and strengthening family farms and rural communities. And we're calling our neighbours to tell them all about Jen!

Mary Miller has held this seat since 2021, but Illinois’ 15th District needs more than divisive politics and empty representation. Jen Todd is offering a different path: leadership rooted in service, integrity, and a belief that government should work for the people it represents. Jen has already built a people-powered campaign across the district, and she is ready to bring a stronger, more unified voice to Congress. Visit [jentodd2026.us](https://www.jentodd2026.us/) to learn more, get answers to your questions, sign up to volunteer, or make a donation to help elect Jen Todd and move IL-15 forward. 🦋🖇️🌊

events.title: Angie For FL: South Mandarin - Jacksonville Canvass
events.description:
Join Team Angie this week as we knock doors and talk with neighbors about building a stronger, more equitable Florida for everyone. Angie Nixon has always been a fearless advocate for working families and real community investment — and now we’re bringing that energy directly to voters.

Whether you’re a longtime volunteer or joining us for the first time, this is a great way to meet like-minded people, make a real impact, and help power a people-first campaign.

What to expect:

- Brief training before we head out
- Canvassing in solo or in pairs
- Campaign materials provided
- A fun, welcoming environment for both new and experienced volunteers

What to bring:

- Comfortable walking shoes
- Water bottle
- Fully charged phone
- Sunscreen/hat if needed
 -Your energy and enthusiasm!

Every conversation matters — come help us turn out voters and keep fighting for the future Florida deserves.

events.title: GOTV canvass in the Fresno area, CD22 | October 30, 31, November 1, 2, 3

location.venue: Volunteer travel to the Fresno area!

events.description:
**CD22 GOTV is here!** Let's build the grassroots power Democrats need to elect Randy Villegas in 2026 and to defend democracy long term. Join us in going door-to-door talking to voters.  **$100 stipend** a day available to offset the cost of gas and lodging.

 - Friday, October 30 | 12:30 pm to 4:30 pm

 - Saturday, October 31 | 9:00 am to 4:30 pm

 - Sunday, November 1 | 9:30 am to 6:00 pm

 - Monday, November 2 | 9:30 am to 6:00 pm

 - Tuesday, November 3 | 9:30 am to 6:00 pm

Once you've signed up, a Bay Area Coalition volunteer will contact you and help with carpools and/or housing options. They will also give you details about the meeting location and names of people running the event.

No experience is necessary. When you arrive at the staging location you will be trained and given all the supplies you need. We'll have clipboards, forms, pens, snacks and water. Bring your personal items like comfy shoes, sunscreen, a hat, and a smile. We will be using PDI and so a well-powered smartphone is necessary.

RSVP today and invite a friend to join us!

events.title: Knock doors in Wisconsin: Drive Directly
events.description:
**Drive directly** to Milwaukee, Wisconsin and knock some doors for Wisconsin Democrats!

We’re just weeks away from the crucial 2026 Midterm elections where we have a once in a generation shot at electing for substantial Democratic leadership. Together, we’ll defeat Donald Trump’s extremist agenda once and for all, but we’ll only succeed with your help. 

We'll see you in Milwaukee!

### Please download MiniVAN

If you haven’t canvassed before (or if you have and you want to review) you will find it helpful to download the MiniVAN User guide and application in advance of your canvass (links below).

MiniVAN is the application we use to keep track of what happens during the canvass. It tells you what doors to knock, who you’ll be speaking to, provides the script for you to use, etc.

If this is your first time using MiniVAN, you'll receive an in-person training on-site during the canvass training!

- [MiniVAN User guide](https://www.ngpvan.com/blog/canvassing-with-minivan/)
- [MiniVAN on Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&pli=1)
- [MiniVAN Touch on Apple Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547)
### Staging Location

Volunteers will meet at 8405 W Lisbon Ave, Milwaukee, Wisconsin. Please plan to arrive when the shift begins (give yourself plenty of time to drive up and grab a coffee!).

events.title: Wisconsin Voter Registration Calls with Rust Belt Rising
events.description:
Join Rust Belt Rising to help make sure that everyone is able to vote in this year's General Election!

Rust Belt Rising's innovative voter registration programs helped thousands of Great Lakes state residents register the last three cycles and will do so again this year.

Here's how it works: RBR partners at Civitech find targets of people who would likely vote our way but are unregistered at their current address as they compare commercial mail lists and voter files. They will mail these targets a pre-filled voter registration form with a motivational flyer and postage to their clerk. That's where we come in. In addition to our texting them, we need volunteers to call these targets to encourage them to complete the easy process of registering.

We would love for you to be part of a team that makes these calls to Wisconsin voters as part of our virtual voter registration chase! 

We'll teach you everything you know over Zoom and get you calling to remind voters to register because there is an election coming up!

events.title: Knock doors in Iowa: Drive Directly
events.description:
**Drive directly** to Dubuque and knock some doors for Lindsay James and other Democrats in Iowa's 2nd congressional District!

We all know that farmers are the beating heart of America, and yet Iowans are disproportionately affected by Trump's Tariffs. The good news is that we finally have the chance to fight back against Trump's MAGA agenda. How? By driving on out to Dubuque to talk to Iowans! Let's make a difference! We'll be waiting for you!

If you arrive early or want to stay longer, no sweat! The office is wide open and would love to have you for as long as you're available to help!

### Please download MiniVAN

If you haven’t canvassed before (or if you have and you want to review) you will find it helpful to download the MiniVAN User guide and application in advance of your canvass (links below).

MiniVAN is the application we use to keep track of what happens during the canvass. It tells you what doors to knock, who you’ll be speaking to, provides the script for you to use, etc.

If this is your first time using MiniVAN, you'll receive an in-person training on-site during the canvass training!

- [MiniVAN User guide](https://www.ngpvan.com/blog/canvassing-with-minivan/)
- [MiniVAN on Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&pli=1)
- [MiniVAN Touch on Apple Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547)
### Staging Location

Volunteers will meet in Iowa at 123 Main St, Dubuque 52001 Please plan to arrive when the shift begins (give yourself plenty of time to drive up and grab a coffee!).

events.title: Voter Protection calls to Cure Ballots
events.description:
Join VoPro Pros’ Cure-A-Palooza on Election Day and beyond to make sure Democratic votes aren’t left uncounted!  From now through the last curing deadline, we are calling likely Democratic voters to help them fix mistakes, known as curing, so their voted mail-in and absentee ballots count! Unless they take action, their votes will not count. Please join us for these important and impactful voter protection phone banks to help votes count!

We will meet on zoom for 2 hour phone banks and provide training, a script, and contact information for targeted voters. We’ll call using the OpenVPB system, where you’ll call on your own phone or Google Voice (or a web based calling app on your computer or phone). No experience, preparation or background knowledge is required. You'll make calls 
while being supported by our experienced staff on zoom.

Our Election Day Cure-a-Palooza will run all day from 10am-9pm ET.  Sign up for a convenient time slot and stay as long as you can. 

In each shift, we will do phone banking to support the most critical and current voter protection priorities in one of our key states: Georgia, Ohio, Iowa, Nevada and maybe more!

 Below is our projected schedule, but it may change on a dime, if we have an urgent, immediate priority. If you have questions, write to us at voterprotectionVPP@gmail.com

Note: Please arrive on time as we cannot accommodate late arrivals after the first five (5) minutes of the session.

11/2 - Ohio cure 5pm ET

11/2 - Nevada cure - 7pm ET

events.title: Rush-hour Resistance Rally @ 10th St & I-10 Pedestrian Bridge in DTPHX
events.description:
**Join us for our Tuesday afternonn rally on the 10th St pedestrian bridge over the I-10 freeway downtown Phoenix**

*Rush-hour Resistance Rallies happen every Monday–Friday during rush hour across the Phoenix metro area. Check out [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us) for the latest locations!*

Here are the particulars for this rally:

**📆 TUESDAY AFTERNOONS**

The rally starts at 4:30. You are free to show up anytime, but we recommend arriving a few minutes early to introduce yourself. We end promptly at 6:00 PM.

Starting 29 Sep 2026, running thru 27 Oct 2026... or longer, if we love it!

**🧑‍🤝‍🧑 GATHERING POINT**

We gather on the bridge. Look for the signs. Can't miss us!

**🪧 MESSAGING & FOCUS**

One of RhRR’s strengths is that people feel free to express themselves. Ideally, your signs would help articulate any of our three pillars:

* Defending democracy and the rule of law
* Encouraging voting
* Protecting neighbors and communities (e.g., immigrants, LGBTQIA+ people, workers, and veterans)
This approach keeps signs aligned with RhRR’s purpose, while preserving personal expression and emotional authenticity.

The primary goal of this event is to encourage voter participation, but participants are welcome to bring any sign they wish. We will provide and display the main voting-related signs facing both directions of traffic. 

Bringing your own sign? Two large bars span the bridge. To make sure your sign isn't blocked, make it horizontal and no more than about 24" tall.

Flags, banners, and even inflatable costumes are welcome. Some blow lots of bubbles. While our mission is serious, humor and camaraderie matter.

RhRRs are peaceful, public events. Most attendees don’t hide their faces, though some do; participate at your comfort level. Photos and videos are commonly shared on social media, but you can ask posters to remove accidental appearances.

**🅿️ RECOMMENDED PARKING**

Street parking is available along East Moreland Street throughout the surrounding neighborhood. There's also a parking lot at 10th St & Culver on the north side, but it may not be as "public" as we'd like. Stay vigilant!

**🚌 PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION**

Route 12

**📣 SPECIAL NOTES**

Because the event takes place on a pedestrian bridge over an active freeway, safety is our highest priority. Clear safety guidelines will be provided to ensure everyone's well-being on the bridge and prevent items from falling onto the roadway below. Safety notices will be posted at both bridge entrances, and all participants will receive safety information in advance of the event. 

Five weeks can make a difference! 

🥵 During hot weather, shade is limited. Bring water, sun protection, and consider a portable chair.

Thanks in advance for joining us. See you on the streets! ✊

**More about RhRR and why we do what we do every day of the week:**

📣 Rush Hour Resistance Rally began with a clear idea: neighbors, gathering peacefully and regularly on busy nearby streets, could remind our communities that democracy is essential and that silence is unacceptable. Over the last year, RhRR expanded from a handful of participants to multiple locations across the Valley, reaching thousands of pedestrians and motorists each week. This momentum is significant, as is the duty it brings.

🗳️ As we approach the midterm elections, our united mission is to safeguard free and fair elections and promote civic participation, particularly in local and primary races where every vote carries weight. Our weekly rallies are more than outlets for frustration; they are consistent, visible commitments that normalize voting and democratic engagement as neighborly expectations.

🕊️ RhRR is a peaceful, nonconfrontational movement. Our goal is to reach the broader community, not to confront those seeking conflict. When tensions surface, we withdraw, stay composed, and look out for one another. This discipline keeps our rallies inviting and helps newcomers feel secure joining us.

🫂 Most of all, RhRR is about people caring for one another while standing up for the future of our democracy. Every person who shows up, every sign held, and every conversation sparked on a street corner is part of something larger and deeply hopeful.

More info at [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us).

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
The Vote is Sacred tour is coming to Arizona and we’re stopping in Flagstaff on Election Day Tuesday, November 3! Arizona Faith Network, Interfaith Alliance, Faiths United to Save Democracy, Party at the Polls, and community partners invite you to come together with neighbors for an evening of free food, community, celebration, and nonpartisan voter information about the upcoming election.

There will also be an interfaith Prayer Vigil for Democracy, bringing together faith and community leaders for prayer and reflection for a peaceful election season, the safety of voters and election workers, and the strength of our democracy.

Sign up through the form managed by Arizona Faith Network as well to ensure your RSVP: https://form-usa.keela.co/bustour 

The Vote Is Sacred 2026 is Interfaith Alliance's nationwide effort to protect our democracy and empower people of faith to get out the vote in the midterm elections. At the heart of The Vote Is Sacred is a cross-country bus tour, launching October 6 in Omaha and running through Election Day: a month on the road in the communities where the freedom to vote is under the most pressure, with public gatherings that platform local clergy and faith communities, election protection trainings, voter registration and canvassing anchored at the bus, and vigils standing against fear and intimidation at the ballot box. We partner with local organizations at every stop.

Come share a meal, connect with your community, get the information you need for the upcoming election, and join us in celebrating the sacred importance of every voice and every vote.

All The Vote is Sacred events are free, nonpartisan, and open to everyone. People of all faiths and no faith are welcome.

events.title: Standing Strong Sign Vigil

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
HELP US RAISE AWARENESS!

In order to raise awareness and stand vigil, our group holds signs at places throughout Salem, where our neighbors were abducted by ICE. 

• Please register to RSVP and get address.

• Every Friday, rain or shine.

• Signs are handed out and locations are assigned at a meeting spot to be disclosed.

• Teams of two then set out for one hour of sign holding.

• Bring a friend or we’ll assign you a partner.

• After the hour is up, meet back at the original meeting spot to turn in signs and check in.

Our purpose is not only to raise awareness of our neighbors being taken from us, but to hold sacred space and honor those who have been abducted and for their families who are dealing with the trauma of their loss.

• We hold these signs for each and every person languishing in detention centers across the US.

• We hold these signs in defiance of the fascism and the hate.

• We hold these signs to use our white privilege, for those of us who have it, and be the best allies we can be.

More about why we do this:

ICE activity in Salem has resulted in many of our neighbors being abducted over the past 18 months. The exact number is difficult to obtain, as ICE does not share information, but the local Rapid Response Team and PIRC (Portland Immigration Rights Coalition) data supports the number as being over 100 since Trump took office.

• Across the state, ICE has abducted over 2,500 individuals, 700 in August of this year. • Across the nation, ICE is ramping up numbers; also in August, 51,000 people were taken. • Most of which have no criminal record.

• Abductees are being warehoused in over 200 privately owned detention centers in the US, where they are held for months, or years, in deplorable conditions.

• There are documented cases of rape, abuse, malnutrition, bad water and food, restricted access to medical care and lawyers.

• GEO Group and Core Civic; the corporations who own most of the detention centers, earn $150 - $175 per person per day.

• Both corporations earned over 2 billion dollars in total revenue in 2025, with net profits exceeding $200 million.

• Half of the total revenue comes from ICE contracts.

Want to help us raise awareness?

events.title: Wind Changers Women's Gathering
events.description:
Wind Changers Women’s Gathering 2026:  2 night camp out. 

The “Wind Changers” represents a shift—a movement toward healing, restoration, connection, and renewed purpose. The Wind Changers Women’s Gathering is an intentional and sacred space created to bring women together for collective prayer, healing, meaningful connection, and empowerment.

In a world that can often feel isolating and overwhelming, this gathering provides a sanctuary where women from all walks of life can come together to build one another up, lift each other’s spirits, support one another, find motivation, and inspire each other.

The gathering is intentionally structured to help women move from isolation to community, creating an environment where women feel seen, heard, supported, and valued. Through shared experiences and meaningful connection, women are reminded that they do not have to walk through life alone.

The Gathering Will Provide:
Collective Prayer & Reflection: Creating a grounded and spiritually supportive environment where women can pause, reflect, reconnect, and renew their spirits.

Talking Circles: Providing safe and welcoming spaces for women to share their stories, express their experiences, release burdens, and receive mutual support without judgment.
Empowerment & Motivation: Creating impactful moments that inspire women to recognize their strength, build one another up, pursue their purpose with confidence, and encourage one another beyond the gathering.

Community Connection: Creating opportunities for fellowship, relationship-building, and meaningful connection so that no woman leaves feeling alone. The goal is for every participant to leave knowing she has a community around her.

We believe that when women have safe spaces to heal, connect, and grow, the impact extends far beyond the gathering itself. Women return to their families, communities, and neighborhoods renewed, strengthened, and empowered to become pillars of strength, hope, and positive change. 

At its heart, Wind Changers is about creating a shift within women that creates a ripple of change throughout families and communities. When women are supported, restored, connected, and empowered, they are better equipped to carry that strength, hope, healing, and purpose into the communities they call home.

Together, we can create a space where women feel seen, heard, supported, valued, and empowered—and where healing and connection become the beginning of lasting change.

events.title: Sexual and Domestic Violence Awareness Workshop
events.description:
Sexual Violence and Domestic Violence Workshops are designed to help you build resilience, develop skills to keep you and your loved ones safe, and create bonds with those who have been through the same experiences as well as educating and informing the public for prevention. Survivors deserve active, accessible and affordable advocacy, support and the right to heal on their own terms.

This group is ran by peers and volunteers with a few experts coming to speak to us at certain times also. We started this group because we know we have a serious lack of education surrounding this and even sex education itself and in rural areas, we lack these resources and education even more. In a world where there is so much violence put on our children and ourselves as women, we must find and create spaces where we feel safe, comfortable, heard and overall have the support we all need.

Every last Tuesday of the month 5-6pm. The majority of our workshops will be at the Peebles Library in their meeting room. Depending on weather, we may have locations outdoors, at a park or hiking location for the woods or even the private 3rd space we created where our community aid garden is. Our lead, Taryn, will be there to greet you and get us started at each of these groups and workshops.
We are allies and accomplices here.

5-6pm Sexual and Domestic Violence Educational Workshops
6-7pm Women's Support Group

There are no age restrictions only to make this accessible. We don't want to make younger children or your children who may need this group to feel like they can't be apart of it just because of their age. If they have experienced hardship or need a safe space just like we do, we will not be turning them away. We do understand that this could potentially keep conversations from being too deep but if enough girls or younger women would like to attend, we can start a support group for our youth.

Our sexual and domestic violence workshops are to bring awareness to ourselves and our youth to help prevent further violence against children and women. Both of these groups will be for survivors as well as the general public, those who want to learn more to help with prevention and education around sexual violence and assault.

What to Expect:
Bonding, Venting and Relating
Mutual Support
Trauma-Informing to Foster Healing
Education on Women’s Health
Sexual Violence Awareness + Education Workshops
Skill Building
Sharing Resources
Safety and Confidentiality

Specific Workshop Examples:
What is Sexual Violence, What is and Can be Considered Sexual Violence, Consent 101, What is Grooming, What are Warning Signs, Women’s Health and Anatomy, Self-Defense and more. In hopes we keep our children and community safe.

We’re working towards bringing our villages back. We can't have a village without villagers.

We want to add to ensure it's known, when we say women, we are always including trans women as well as non-binary folks who may also need a support system. As soon as we find a better term to use for only women and non-binary folks, the name of this support group will change. We apologize to anyone who may feel left out or uncomfortable to the term Women's Support Group.

Coffee and snacks will be available. Possibly pizza or other foods for dinner. If you have allergies, please inform us. We hope to see you at one or the other or even both. It matters to our health to have support and we must create spaces that lead to prevention of violence against us.

events.title: Women’s Support Group
events.description:
Women's group is a support group to gather women who may have been through the same experiences, would like to share stories, resources and bond with others on a monthly basis. This group is ran by peers and volunteers with a few experts coming to speak to us at certain times also. We started this group because we personally know how it feels to be alone with no one to relate to or to talk to. In a world where there is so much violence put on our children and ourselves as women, we must find and create spaces where we feel safe, comfortable, heard and overall have the support we all need.

Every last Tuesday of the month 6-7pm. Most of our support groups and workshops will be at the Peebles Library in their meeting room. Depending on weather, we may have locations outdoors, at a park or hiking location or even the private 3rd space we created where our community aid garden is. Our lead, Taryn, will be there to greet you and get us started at each of these groups and workshops.
We are allies and accomplices here.

6-7pm Women's Support Group
5-6pm Sexual and Domestic Violence Educational Workshops

Survivors deserve active, accessible and affordable advocacy, support and the right to heal on their own terms. This group and the workshops are designed to help you build resilience, develop skills to keep you and your loved ones safe, and create bonds with those who have been through the same experiences as well as educating and informing the public for prevention.

There are no age restrictions only to make this accessible. We don't want to make younger children or your children who may need this group to feel like they can't be apart of it just because of their age. If they have experienced hardship or need a safe space just like we do, we will not be turning them away. We do understand that this could potentially keep conversations from being too deep but if enough girls or younger women would like to attend, we can start a support group for our youth.

Our sexual and domestic violence workshops are to bring awareness to ourselves and our youth to help prevent further violence against children and women. Both of these groups will be for survivors as well as the general public, those who want to learn more to help with prevention and education around Sexual Violence and Assault. For more information on these workshops, you can find that on the event pages of the Sexual Violence Awareness Workshops and on our community aid page too.

We want this group to be as accessible as we possibly can, that includes rides and childcare. If you have children, you can bring them to the first group or workshop you attend if you need to. A kid’s club will begin once we find more volunteers to help us make this successful as well and we will have them during these times. Once we find enough volunteers and go through background checks, we will talk more about this at the our group meetings or workshops and spread the word more. We’re working towards bringing our villages back. We can't have a village without villagers.

Coffee and snacks will be available too. We hope you join us. We all need someone or something. We’re here for you. No shame, no judgement, no exceptions.❤️‍🩹

We want to add to ensure it's known, when we say women, we are always including trans women as well as non-binary folks who may also need a support system. events.description:
### Join Food & Water Action this October to talk with our neighbors about Iowa's water crisis, and elect leaders willing to stand up to Big Ag.  

Iowa has _the fastest-rising cancer rates in the country._ We know this is linked to pollution from industrial agriculture that flows into our waterways. 

Join us to talk to our neighbors and share information about keeping our water safe, _starting with electing candidates like Chris Jones for Ag Secretary,_ who will hold polluters accountable and clean up Iowa's water! 

We will meet at _Chamberlain Park_ for a brief training session on how to have effective conversations.

Then, we will pair up and head out!

After everyone finishes their list/shift, we meet back up at Chamberlain Park and debrief!

**No prior experience canvassing is needed!**

We use the website OpenField to track our conversations, so please bring a fully charged phone. We'll spend some time during the training familiarizing ourselves with OpenField.

**Join us in getting out the vote to elect water champions in Des Moines!**

events.title: Wenonah's Book of the Year: Author Talk with Zephyr Teachout [Livable Future LIVE]
events.description:
**Join us for a virtual conversation between Food & Water Watch Founder & Executive Director Wenonah Hauter and Zephyr Teachout, author of _Anti-Monopoly: A Citizen’s Guide_.**

_Anti-Monopoly_ is being called a “movement-defining” book that dives deep into the battle between the forces of oligarchy and the rise of the anti-monopoly movement. Zephyr explains how anti-monopoly sentiment cuts across traditional political lines, gives real teeth to economic populism, and offers actionable ways to use people power to solve this problem together. 

Zephyr Teachout is an award-winning author, constitutional law professor, and nationally renowned democracy and anti-corruption activist. _The New York Times_ called her “the godmother of the current moment of dissatisfaction with establishment politics,” and she has inspired anti-monopoly legislation in states across the country. Her additional writings include the books _Corruption in America_ and _Break ’Em Up_ and articles featured in _The New York Times_, _The New York Review of Books_, _Foreign Affairs_, and _The Nation_. Zephyr serves as Board Chair for Food & Water Action and sits on the board of Food & Water Watch, helping guide strategies on clean water, safe food, and climate advocacy.

events.title: So You Want to Run for Office?
events.description:
Join the National Democratic Training Committee on Thursday, November 12th from 1-2 pm ET for a free virtual live training on **So You Want to Run for Office**. We're here to help, so join us to learn the following:

1\. Understand the steps necessary to run for office

2\. Explain best practices for choosing which office to run for

3\. Identify what kinds of support you'll need to run for office

4\. Prepare for sharing your decision to run with your support network

  

**This training is right for you if you're considering a run for elected office but haven't yet made the commitment to run or filed your candidacy.**

  

A recommended (not required) course to take in our Online Academy is [Getting Your Campaign Off the Ground](https://traindems.org/course-details/100/getting-your-campaign-off-the-ground).  
_Have accessibility questions? Reply to your registration email to confirm your requirements or request more information._

1\. Identify key responsibilities of Democratic precinct chairs

2\. Introduce tactics used by local leaders to grow and engage membership

3\. Review approaches for persuading first time candidates to run

  

**This training is right for you if you hold a leadership position in a Democratic club/committee or progressive organization that actively supports candidates seeking elected office.**

events.title: Recovering from a Lost Election
events.description:
Join the National Democratic Training Committee on Tuesday, November 17th from 1-2 pm ET for a free virtual live training on **Recovering from a Lost Election****.** We're here to help, so join us to learn the following:

1.  Discuss productive ways to reflect on and debrief your campaign experience
2.  Plan a timeline for post-Election Day supporter engagement and goals for continued organizing efforts
3.  Explore ways to have an ongoing positive impact on local Democratic organizing, including the decision to seek election again in the future 

  

**This training is right for you if you are a candidate with some degree of desire to stay involved in political organizing, even if your bid for election is unsuccessful.**

  

A recommended (not required) course to take in our Online Academy is [The Fundamentals of Field Tactics](https://traindems.org/course-details/67/the-fundamentals-of-field-tactics)

events.title: What is a Democratic Precinct Chair?

1.  Describe the structure and purpose of local Democratic Parties
2.  Review common positions people hold in local Democratic Parties
3.  Identify key responsibilities of Democratic precinct chairs

events.title: Social Bank Training with Stand Up America: Help Senate Candidates Reach Undecided Voters
events.description:
Bots and accounts run from overseas have been flooding our social media feeds with MAGA content for years. Volunteers like you can help fight back.

That’s where the Stand Up America Social Squad comes in. Our Social Banks work just like a phonebank, but instead of a call list, we give you a list of posts from pro-democracy candidates in key Senate races who need help right now getting their content in front of undecided voters. You can make a difference even if you don’t live in a Senate swing state. 

Here’s why it works: Every time you engage with a post on social media, the algorithm takes note and shows it to more people. Most of them will be strangers, and many will be voters who are still making up their minds.

Join us to learn about our new tool and see how you can help cut through the noise ahead of the November midterm elections.

**What to expect**

We'll start with a short training on what social banking is and how to do it well. During the training, we'll share the link to Prosocial, the tool we'll use, and walk you through it step by step. When you first log in, you'll pick which social media platforms you use (Facebook, Instagram, Threads, TikTok, Twitter/X, YouTube), and Prosocial will show you content to engage with for those platforms. We'll spend the rest of the hour social banking together.

**What you'll need**

Your phone or computer, and your social media accounts. No experience necessary.


Don't want to wait for a training? Sign up [here](https://www.mobilize.us/standupamerica/event/1072159/) to start social banking now.

events.title: Phone Banking (Longmont)
events.description:
Join us at UCC Longmont to help GET OUT THE VOTE by phone banking!

**What to expect:**

We'll be using an online dialer platform that connects you directly to voters — no need to dial numbers yourself. Once you're connected, you'll read from a simple, conversational script designed to help you have real conversations, not a robotic pitch. The script walks you through an introduction, a few key talking points about what's at stake, and a couple of questions to gauge where the person you're speaking with stands.

Before calls begin, a trained lead will walk everyone through: 
- How to log into the phone bank platform 
- How the dialer works (it does the dialing — you just talk!) 
- A walkthrough of the script and how to enter responses 
- Tips for handling common questions or pushback

**Why it matters:**
Every conversation helps us identify supporters, share accurate information, and build the coalition we need to protect trans and immigrant Coloradans. Phone banking is flexible, low-pressure, and a great option no matter your schedule or experience level.

**What you need:**

*Computer
*Headphones
*Enthusiasm for the cause!
