events.title: Save Democracy, Not the SAVE Act – Write to Your Members of Congress NOW!
events.description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Dear friends,

I am one of the millions of Americans who believes that voting is a fundamental right—not a privilege reserved for those who happen to have the right paperwork. But right now, Congress is trying to pass the SAVE America Act, a bill that would make it harder for eligible citizens to register and vote.

Our Votes Are in Danger!

Here's what's happening:

•	The SAVE America Act passed the House 218–213 on February 11, 2026

•	It requires documentary proof of citizenship—in person—to register to vote and photo ID to cast a ballot

•	Over 21 million eligible American citizens do not have proof of their citizenship readily available

•	It is an unfunded mandate that would cost states hundreds of millions of dollars with zero federal funding

•	The Senate has repeatedly failed to pass it, and even Republican leaders admit the votes aren't there

•	President Trump is now demanding that the Senate abolish the filibuster to force it through

📢 "Save Democracy, Not the SAVE Act" – That's Our Message

📝 Your Action: Write to Your Members of Congress

Step 1: Find Your Members of Congress

events.title: Group Portrait Fundraiser
events.description:
Join us in the DPOC office to get your group photo or a professional headshot ahead of holiday card season (candidates for Spring elections welcome too!)  

Our volunteer photographer Richard will offer 5-10 mins per group on his one backdrop to capture your shot, and send via email within a week following. Groups can be kids, families, households, chosen families, or whoever you like to smile next to: max 6 per slot. Minimum suggested donation is $50.00 to be paid day of in cash or via Act Blue QR code. 

RSVP to reserve a slot within a 30 min window or just drop by and wait for the next opening. Reservations will jump the line to be taken at their pre-reserved time. 

We suggest you coordinate outfits with your group, avoid graphic tees or busy patterns, and dress in a way that is comfortable and authentic to YOU! We also ask that you check your shoes for clean bottoms to keep our backdrop clean for the next group. 

If the preferred time slot is full please sign up for the next one, and feel free to pop in early in case things are moving quickly and you can go early. Note that time slots are a range and we aim to fit in as many groups as would like to participate. 

Though we love them a lot, for liability purposes no pets or animals permitted for photos in the office. 

Light snacks will be provided for after your photo time and volunteers available to chat about what we do as Dems in Outagamie County. No obligation to join or volunteer, but we'd be happy to answer your questions.

events.title: Get Out the Vote with Team KMR & the MI Dems in Saginaw!
events.description:
This race is close, and it's going to come down to turnout. Join us for Get Out The Vote canvassing for Kristen McDonald Rivet and Michigan Democrats up and down the ballot in Saginaw!

We'll be knocking on doors of confirmed Democratic supporters and occasional voters — people who are already on our side but need a reminder that Election Day is here. We'll help them lock in their plan to vote, whether that's their polling location, early voting, or mail-in ballot options, and make sure they know their whole Democratic ballot matters — from Kristen McDonald Rivet all the way down.

This kind of face-to-face contact works: GOTV canvassing boosts turnout by an average of 8.5%. In a race this tight, that's the margin of victory — not just for Kristen, but for Democrats across Michigan.

What to expect:

A quick training and walk list when you arrive
A partner or team lead if you're new to canvassing
Friendly conversations with people who already support our ticket

Bring: comfortable shoes, water, and your phone.

No experience necessary — just enthusiasm for getting Michigan Democrats to the polls. Sign up below and help us bring the whole ticket home!

events.title: Election Eve Canvass | Every Vote, Every Member
events.description:
Election Day is 24 hours away, and the races that matter most to working Nevadans will be decided by just a few thousand votes. This is your second to last change to join union brothers and sisters from far and wide for one last day of member-to-member canvassing.

We’re knocking on the doors of union households to make sure every member has a plan to vote, knows where their polling place is, and has returned their mail ballot – join us! 

You’ll get the chance to meet veteran union canvassers, first timers, and Nevada union leaders for a full day of celebrating our hard work and knocking out what we still need to accomplish together. We’ll make sure you feel fully prepared with a quick training, a walk list, and talking points before heading out. 

Wages, working conditions, and the right to organize are on the ballot. Let's finish strong.

Join us at the Operating Engineers Local 3 Union Hall.

events.title: Get Out the Vote with Team KMR & the MI Dems in Bay City!
events.description:
This race is close, and it's going to come down to turnout. Join us for Get Out The Vote canvassing for Kristen McDonald Rivet and Michigan Democrats up and down the ballot in Bay City!

We'll be knocking on doors of confirmed Democratic supporters and occasional voters — people who are already on our side but need a reminder that Election Day is here. We'll help them lock in their plan to vote, whether that's their polling location, early voting, or mail-in ballot options, and make sure they know their whole Democratic ballot matters — from Kristen McDonald Rivet all the way down.

This kind of face-to-face contact works: GOTV canvassing boosts turnout by an average of 8.5%. In a race this tight, that's the margin of victory — not just for Kristen, but for Democrats across Michigan.

What to expect:

A quick training and walk list when you arrive
A partner or team lead if you're new to canvassing
Friendly conversations with people who already support our ticket

Bring: comfortable shoes, water, and your phone.

No experience necessary — just enthusiasm for getting Michigan Democrats to the polls. Sign up below and help us bring the whole ticket home!

events.title: Union Made Victory | Election Day Canvass

Polls are open 7 AM to 7 PM, and every union vote counts. We need all hands on deck to knock on doors of members who haven't voted yet and help them get to the polls before the clock runs out.

Election Day canvassing is fast, focused, and it works. Our lists are updated with who has already voted, so every door you’ll knock is one that matters. Nevada allows same-day registration at the polls, and we’ll be making sure our members you talk to know it.

Let us know we can count on your help and RSVP to join us now!

events.title: PDA Oklahoma State Chapter Meeting
events.description:
Join us in person at New Covenant Christian Church or online via Zoom for the monthly meeting of Progressive Democrats of Oklahoma (PDOk), the Oklahoma state chapter of Progressive Democrats of America.

Monthly meetings include discussion of current and upcoming political issues and elections, alongside community efforts focused on voter education, civic engagement, and other ways of cultivating progressive values and action in Oklahoma.

Everyone interested in learning more or getting involved is welcome—whether you're a lifelong Democrat, new to progressive politics, or simply interested in what we're doing. We'd love to see you!

For more information, to receive the Zoom link, or to connect directly with current PDOk members, join our GroupMe at tinyurl.com/PDOkla.

Our mission:

We believe in change through action. Our local and state chapter members work every day to make Oklahoma a better place, with a focus on:

--voter registration drives,

--get out the vote efforts,

--volunteering for issue or candidate campaigns,

--phone banking for state, local, or national candidates,

--building communities,

--forming coalitions with other organizations, and more.

**While Progressive Democrats of Oklahoma is not affiliated with New Covenant Christian Church and is not a faith- or religion-based organization, we understand that some meeting locations may carry personal or religious associations for chapter members, regardless of their context. New Covenant Christian Church is an open and affirming church that welcomes people from all backgrounds into their building.

events.title: Facilitating The Learning Environment
events.description:
Facilitating the Learning Environment:

Participants will be able to design equitable physical learning spaces that support engagement and access; co-create norms, routines, and procedures that foster trust, safety, and belonging; and implement behavior responses that promote student growth, accountability, and skill development.

events.title: Engaging Every Learner
events.description:
Engaging Every Learner: 

Participants will be able to explain how diversity, equity, inclusion, and social-emotional learning shape instruction and engagement; apply current research that expands Jacob Kounin’s group-management principles; plan lessons and strategies that engage every learner; and reflect on their group-management strengths and growth areas to identify improvements.

events.title: Principles of Instruction
events.description:
Principles of Instruction: 

Participants will be able to explain the social context of learning and its instructional implications; analyze knowledge development within the Zone of Proximal Development; apply cognitive and metacognitive strategies that foster independent learning; and design high-quality lessons that expand access, engagement, and opportunities for all students to demonstrate mastery.

events.title: Feedback for Deeper Learning
events.description:
Feedback for Deeper Learning: 

Participants will be able to distinguish effective feedback from other classroom communication; gather student feedback to inform instruction, elevate student voice, and promote agency; provide timely, actionable feedback aligned with individual needs and learning goals; and use purposeful questioning and discussion to deepen learning and foster meaningful feedback exchanges.

events.title: Maximizing Learning Time:
events.description:
Maximizing Learning Time:

Participants will be able to identify the time constraints including allocated time, engaged time, and academic learning time; understand the relationship between required learning time and actual time spent learning; account for lost learning time; and learn strategies for maximizing learner engagement.

events.title: Culturally Responsive Pedagogy

location.venue: Alief ISD Center for Talent Development

events.description:
Culturally Responsive Pedagogy 

Teachers connect culture and cognition to build strength-focused lessons with high expectations for diverse learners. Aligns with T-TESS 1.3 Knowledge of Students, 3.3 Classroom Culture, and 2.4 Differentiation.

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
2026 #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence

Beginning Wednesday, December 9, 2026 until the end of December, we will come together across the nation to host the #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence.

These local events will be anchored by the 14th Annual National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C.—held near the 14-year mark of the Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting tragedy, when a 20-year-old gunman armed with an AR-15 hunted and murdered 20 first graders and six educators.

Across the country, vigils (as simple as lighting candles) and gatherings will honor lives stolen by gun violence, uplift survivors, raise awareness, and demand urgent action from our leaders to finally end this epidemic. From schools and workplaces to houses of worship, neighborhoods, grocery stores, homes, nightclubs, streets, and even our democracy itself—gun violence impacts every aspect of American life.

The theme of this year’s campaign is #FreedomToLive—the simple, powerful idea that every person deserves to live free from the daily threat of gunfire. Together, survivors, families, advocates, and allies will raise our voices to ensure that FREEDOM means the right of every person to live, learn, work, worship, speak, vote, and gather without the daily fear of gun violence.

We stand in solidarity with over 1.4 million Americans who have been shot since Sandy Hook, with every community devastated by gun violence for decades. We will send a clear message to our local, state, and federal lawmakers, raise awareness, and help build the movement for common-sense solutions.

Let’s #HonorWithAction together. Let’s demand freedom from gun violence.

events.title: No Country for Mothers: Film Screening on the Farm
events.description:
Join Mom Dog, Woven and Juniper Green at The Old School Farm for a screening of No Country For Mothers: a documentary that explores what motherhood really looks like in America today.

The film examines the culture wars surrounding motherhood and why labels like “girl boss” and “trad wife” ultimately distract from the bigger issue at play in our society: the lack of support for American families. The documentary traces a growing national movement to reunite moms across divisions and win historic support. 

The screening will be followed by an open discussion, led by Maddie Adams (Matrescence Coach and founder of Mom Dog), Whitney Gorbett (owner of Woven Events), and Molly Martin (owner of Juniper Green and The Old School Farm).

DETAILS:

This al fresco film screening includes open conversation, food from Nashville food trucks, and drinks from The Old School Farm bar. BYO lawn chairs or picnic blankets to create a space where you and your friends can enjoy the evening together. 

Guests are welcome to bring their own picnic dinner, but please note that outside alcohol is prohibited.   

5:00PM - Food, drinks and mingling at The Old School Farm
6:30PM - Film screening, followed by conversation

This night isn’t just about watching a film. 

It’s about being in community with other mothers, linking arms with our sisters to form stronger connections, and saying the things out loud that we’ve been carrying quietly — because maybe some of what we’ve been taught to carry privately was never meant to be carried alone.

Join us for this special evening:

Step 1) Sign up below to attend.

Step 2) Purchase your ticket here: https://www.mom-dog.com/all-events/ncfm

Step 3) Share this event with your friends and encourage them to attend, too!

events.title: WEBINAR: Reproductive Justice for Transgender, Gender Non-Conforming and Intersex People!
events.description:

Join us for a webinar to walk through the process and findings from this inquiry.

-Ask questions about reproductive justice and its importance to the TGI community
-Reflect on how the findings align with on the ground experience
-Receive access to materials created through this work

This work was conducted with funding from the California Department of Public Health and in partnership with Goodwin Simon Strategic Research, TransLatin@ Coalition, Unique Woman's Coalition, Invisible Men, and Gender Justice LA.

events.title: March for Our Democracy: The Fight Isn't Over

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
New York is making it clear: the fight for democracy doesn’t end on election day

No matter what post-election scenario we’ll face, we are preparing to take to the streets, because we know this fight doesn’t end on Election Day. It goes to certification, through the seating of congress and beyond.

We’re demanding that our leaders protect the electoral process, while building a muscle for more mass action. If we see attempts to undermine the vote here or anywhere else in the country, we want it to be clear: New York is prepared to take sustained nonviolent action.

What: March for Democracy
When: Saturday, November 7, 2026
Time: 12 PM
Location: Times Square

We’re not watching history happen—we’re making it.

A core principle behind all Hands Off NYC events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: Interfaith Prayer Meeting for Peace

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Interfaith Prayer Meeting for Peace is a collaboration of people of faith from various organizations. We grieve this administration’s assault on human dignity and life at home and abroad. We grieve ruthless corporate war profiteering. So we meet monthly in the shadow of the largest weapons manufacturer on the globe, and across the street from the largest luxury mall in the nation, to pray and bear witness that a better world is possible.

NOTE: Time of event is approximate and will be finalized by email!

As people of faith and conscience committed to peaceful, legal, prayerful presence, we agree to the following:

We agree to respect “that of God in every person” and refrain from hostile language and insults.

We agree to leave room for repentance in those with whom we disagree and to oppose violence, not people.

We agree to trust the Divine to bring about peace, shalom and wholeness in our world.

We agree to follow all legal instructions from law enforcement.

We agree to quickly cooperate with peacekeeper and Meeting facilitator directions that are for our safety.

As an interfaith gathering, we agree to exercise freedom of expression and respect the freedom of expression of others. If you have a prayer, reading, song, or other activity, it will represent your faith and conscience with integrity. If someone else’s sharing does not align with your faith and conscience, you are free to abstain from participating during that moment.

events.title: Kits of Care: Pack with Purpose! 🧡
events.description:
🧡 Kits of Care: Pack with Purpose!

You’ve been donating. Now let’s get packing! 🙌

Over the past two months, we’ve been collecting supplies for three types of kits to share with community members served by Partners for Our Communities (POC):

🍪 Christmas Cookie Jars filled with baking ingredients and a recipe for a homemade holiday treat.
💜 Period Kits with menstrual care essentials.
🎒 Unhoused Kits with personal care items for neighbors experiencing homelessness.

Donations are coming along beautifully, and now it’s time to bring everyone together for our first assembly event!

📅 Saturday, November 14 | 1–3 PM
📍 Countryside Church Unitarian Universalist (CCUU), Palatine

We’re looking for 50+ volunteers to help put together 150 Christmas Cookie Jars, 150 Period Kits, and 75 Unhoused Kits. That’s 375 kits packed with care in one afternoon!

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 This is a kid-friendly event! Bring your family or a friend. Kids and adults can decorate cards with cheerful messages, fill jars, and pack supplies. No experience needed. We’ll show you what to do! This is a great opportunity for teens to get volunteer hours!

🎁 There’s still time to donate! Check out the list of items we still need: [Kits of Care Flyers - 11/1/26](http://tinyurl.com/KitsOfCare1101)

Whether you’ve donated supplies or are joining us for the first time, we’d love to have you there. Come meet your neighbors, learn about Partners for Our Communities and the services they provide, and help care for others! 🧡

We will have a second packing day on Sat, Jan 23rd. Look for the Sign up in December.

Sponsored by Indivisible Barrington, Countryside Church Unitarian Universalist (CCUU), and Partners for Our Communities (POC).

events.title: PHONEBANKING ON ELECTION DAY!
events.description:
Help us make phone calls on Election Day to get out the vote! We'll be calling supporters in District 33 to urge them to return their mail-in ballot to a dropbox or get out to the polls TODAY for Dawn, Andrew, Chuck, and Heather! 

You have two choices - you can either make phone calls from the comfort of your own home and join a video call link where we'll train you and be available for questions, OR you can come out to Broadneck High School and do the calls with fellow volunteers under our phonebanking HQ tent. 

By Authority: Committee to Elect Dawn Gile, Meghann Boosinger, Treasurer; Friends of Andrew Pruski, Mariam Nasseri Pelletier, Treasurer; Chuck Cook for Anne Arundel County, Brian Kemmet, Treasurer; Citizens for Heather Bagnall, Luke Tudball, Treasurer.

events.title: Flagstaff Community Voting Celebration - Arizona Faith Network Party At The Polls!
events.description:
Join us for a nonpartisan celebration of the vote as the Vote Is Sacred Bus Tour makes three stops in Arizona!

Arizona Faith Network, Interfaith Alliance, Faiths United to Save Democracy, Party at the Polls, and community partners invite you to come together with neighbors for an evening of free food, community, celebration, and nonpartisan voter information about the upcoming election.

Each gathering will also include an interfaith Prayer Vigil for Democracy, bringing together faith and community leaders for prayer and reflection for a peaceful election season, the safety of voters and election workers, and the strength of our democracy.

These events are free, nonpartisan, and open to everyone. People of all faiths and no faith are welcome.

Come share a meal, connect with your community, get the information you need for the upcoming election, and join us in celebrating the sacred importance of every voice and every vote.

**Any food, entertainment, buttons, stickers, or any other free items at this event are available to voters and non-voters alike. This is a nonpartisan event.**

events.title: Plymouth: Election Day Stand-Out with Sen. Dylan Fernandes

location.venue: PCIS, West Elementary, Indian Brook Elem, South Elementary, South Middle School

events.description:
Join us for an Election Day stand-out at one of Plymouth’s five polling locations!

Sign up for a 2-hour shift that works for you. We’ll provide signs and any campaign materials you need. Sign up for more than one if you'd like!

Once you sign up, we'll ask you which polling place you prefer. We'll be sure to provide the exact location of each stand-out, so you'll know exactly where to go.

Please arrive a few minutes before your shift, and follow all instructions regarding the designated stand-out area. 

Massachusetts law prohibits campaigning within 150 feet of a polling location, so volunteers must remain outside the marked electioneering boundary.

Tuesday, November 3
Polls open: 7:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.

Even one shift makes a difference — thank you for helping us maintain a visible presence across Plymouth!

Mitchell Street Arts, 710 W Historic Mitchell St, Milwaukee WI 53204

However, we ask artists to consider sharing 20% of their sale proceeds with Indivisible MKE, as this is our annual fund raiser.

Please Include: 3 examples of your work (PDF). All media welcome, as long as it demonstrates your passion for justice. events.title: AZ-01 GOTV Text Bank
events.description:
AZ-01 Weekly Text Bank, Every Monday

Join us as we text Arizona voters to help them return their mail ballots and make a final plan to vote before the November 3 general election.

Every week we reach voters across Arizona so they're ready to take part in one of the most competitive House races in the country. These are high-stakes elections, and turnout will decide who wins. We're making sure no voter is left behind.

We'll text voters who usually skip midterm elections to remind them of key deadlines and help them make a clear, confident plan to vote: by mail, early in person, or on Election Day. We'll also send voters who plan to vote early or on Election Day the information they need, including early voting sites, polling locations, and how to track their mail ballot.

Volunteers will have real one-on-one conversations with voters by text, answer their questions, and help turn intention into action so ballots get returned and votes get counted.

💬 Weekly text bank: Mondays at 6 p.m. PT (every week through Election Day)
🔥 No experience needed. All you need is a laptop. We provide training, scripts, and support.

Close races are won by making sure every vote counts. Your text could be the reason someone follows through. Sign up now and help power turnout in Arizona!

events.title: November 9 Meeting of Bellaire/Braeswood and West U Area Dems with Jeremy Wallace
events.description:
Come join the Bellaire/Braeswood Democrats and the West University Area Democrats at the November 9, 2026 meeting with Jeremy Wallace of the Houston Chronicle.  Jeremy will analyze what just happened on November 3rd and what to expect will happen going forward because of the results.

Jeremy Wallace has covered politics and campaigns for more than 20 years. Before joining the Hearst Texas newspapers in 2017, he covered government and politics for the Tampa Bay Times, The Miami Herald and the Sarasota Herald-Tribune. Previously he covered Congress for the Boston Globe and Detroit Free-Press. Originally from San Antonio, he attended the University of North Texas and earned his bachelor’s degree from the University of Missouri.

Jeremy also authors the Texas Take with Jeremy Wallace newsletter, where he shares insights from inside the Capitol.  Work on the Texas Take has him frequently on CNN, PBS, BBC America, MSNBC and statewide NPR stations.

Social time: 6:30 - 7:00 pm. Business time: 7:00 - 8:00 pm
Location: West University Community Center at 6104 Auden St. 77005

events.title: Indivisible San Mateo:  Saturday lunch at Terrace Food Court at Hillsdale Mall
events.description:
Join Indivisible San Mateo for conversation and conviviality and a no-host lunch at the The Terraces food court at Hillsdale Mall in San Mateo on Saturdays, from 11:30 to 1:00 p.m.

Look for us on the second floor at the northwest table near the elevator and the restrooms near the big windows.

The lunch is open to everyone and will take place prior to our weekly Saturday street protests from 1 to 2:30 p.m., around the corner on El Camino at East 31st Avenue.

There's ample parking at the Mall, lots of seating and lots of lunch options for those dining at one of the places in the food court. The restaurants include Sarku Japan; Tacos E. Grullens; Hakata Kuro Obi Ramen; and Panda Express, among others. Shake Shack is downstairs and there are coffee shops nearby.

Reservations are not necessary and all are welcome, whether for lunch or dessert or just fellowship with like-minded people for democracy.  All are encouraged to be part of the rally afterward on El Camino around the corner.

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Great Scott Farms is graciously extending a field to harvest fresh produce for families in need. This is a great way to way to give back, enjoy the outdoors, and share in meaningful community service.

All are welcome! The more hands we have to help- the more produce we can recover! Produce is available for anyone in need. 

We are beginning many gleans at 11am due to private gleans that are scheduled on the same day. The private groups will only be gleaning for an hour so there should be plenty of produce left over to rescue. 

If you would like to be a receiving agency please reach out to the leading coordinator or Megan at (863) 224-0403. 

🌱 What to Bring:

✅ Closed-toe shoes (required)

✅ Comfortable clothing that can get messy

✅ Hat, sunscreen, and gloves (optional but helpful)

✅ A reusable water bottle to stay hydrated

📢 RSVP or Questions? 
Contact:
Megan McEwen
📞 (863) 224-0403
📧 fl-glean@endhunger.org

### Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

#### 1. What is gleaning?

- Gleaning is collecting leftover crops from farms that would otherwise go to waste. These fresh fruits and vegetables are then donated to food banks and hunger relief groups.

#### 2. Who can attend?

- All are welcome—no prior experience needed! Perfect for families, small groups, or anyone looking to serve. (Kids must be with an adult.)

#### 3. Are tools provided?
- Yes! We’ll supply any tools and bags you’ll need to glean.

#### 4. What if it rains?

- We’ll monitor the weather and let you know if anything changes. Safety first!

#### 5. Where does the food go?

- All the produce goes directly to local food banks and community partners feeding those in need. If you are an organization in need - reach out to the event coordinator to become a recipient. 

#### 6. How can I stay in the loop?

- For event updates, visit: https://www.mobilize.us/endhunger/

#### 7. Other FAQs :

- NO smoking, NO pets

events.title: Share Mark Pinsley's videos (Easy!)
events.description:
Democrats have not controlled the Pennsylvania Senate for three decades. Their path to flipping it likely runs through the Lehigh Valley and Bucks County (SD-16), where Mark Pinsley is running against Republican incumbent Jarrett Coleman.  Mark is ahead by one point, according to the latest polls.  

Mark's videos are funny and interesting.  You don’t have to be a tech wizard or even a social media fan to increase the reach of the videos that can change voters’ minds.

### Click here to [Watch, Like, Comment, and Share Mark's Facebook videos](https://www.facebook.com/VoteMarkPinsley/reels/). 

You can also find Mark on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/markpinsley/)
 and [Youtube](https://www.youtube.com/@voteformarkpinsley).

Here are six simple steps that go a long way.

1. WATCH the video till the end. This tells the algorithm people are liking and engaging with it.

2. LIKE the post, with the “love” or “wow” emojis rather than a simple “like.”

3. COMMENT on the video. Explain why you like it, using first person and emotive terms. For example: “This is why I love candidate Mark Pinsley – he tells it like it is."

4. SHARE the video on your social media feeds if you have them. Sharing is worth 30x more than a Like on the latest Facebook algorithm.

5. REPLY TO POSITIVE COMMENTS
Be emotive and use the first person. Do NOT respond to negative
comments or get into online arguments as this wastes your time and rewards their trolling.

6. AMPLIFY other comments by liking them, pinning them to the top of the comment thread or replying to the comment with phrases like “Right on! We need more people who will go out and vote like you will.” Follow up questions encourage others to comment, creating a “comment thread” which tells the algorithm the post is getting attention and should be offered to others. “My friends are all stoked to vote for candidate Mark Pinsley. Are you seeing the same enthusiasm?”

These are steps you can take easily, on your own schedule, whenever a candidate or volunteer posts something watchable. Instant gratification for you and an instant boost for your cause.

events.title: Alcona County Canvass Observation

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Since November 2020, the League of Women Voters of Michigan and their Pro-Democracy Partners have worked to be the public’s eyes and ears at Michigan’s county canvass of votes cast during an election. Each year they work together to ensure that trained volunteers observe County Board of Canvassers (BOC) meetings, across the state of Michigan, watching the process by which local results are reviewed and certified.

This consistent, nonpartisan observation promotes transparency and accountability, helps identify potential issues that could put timely certification at risk, and reassures Board of Canvassers members and election staff that the public is engaged in their work. Should observation uncover anything beyond the canvassers’ ministerial, nondiscretionary duties, LWVMI can elevate the issue to the Secretary of State’s office or an election attorney.

### Your Role As An Observer:
- Our BOC Observer are an important aspect of our volunteer election work! 
- Our observers not only serve to build trust in the community as well as between local government and the League, but they also help to ensure our elections are running as the laws intended. 
- Reporting from our observers helps us understand the health of our democratic systems, where issues are happening, and where things are running smoothly.  
- These insights are important to all of us working to support our democracy, and ultimately support our communities in ensuring their voices are heard! 

We hope you will join us, volunteer, and bring a friend to be a part of this election work!

PS: Shifts are subject to change, as county clerks work to finalize the details of the county canvass. If your shift is cancelled, you will be contacted by a representative from the League of Women Voters.

This consistent, nonpartisan observation promotes transparency and accountability, helps identify potential issues that could put timely certification at risk, and reassures Board of Canvassers members and election staff that the public is engaged in their work. Should observation uncover anything beyond the canvassers’ ministerial, nondiscretionary duties, LWVMI can elevate the issue to the Secretary of State’s office or an election attorney.

events.description:
Join Tree Pittsburgh this Fall in the Mon Valley for a free tree education series!

Whether you're new to tree planting and care or want to build your skills, these sessions will give you practical, hands-on experience and useful knowledge you can apply to the trees in your neighborhood.

*Register now to stay up to date on session dates, locations, and other event details.* 

Throughout the series, you'll learn about tree planting, tree care, tree health, and common tree stressors through a mix of hands-on activities and classroom-style learning. We'll host most sessions in *Braddock, PA *, with additional sessions in *Rankin, PA*. Some sessions will use a hybrid format with an online portion.

You can attend the sessions that work for your schedule. We'll provide refreshments at most in-person sessions.

*Come prepared for the weather!* We plan to hold outdoor sessions rain or shine and will only cancel or reschedule when severe weather, such as thunderstorms, makes it unsafe to continue. 

*Need accessibility support?* Email the ReLeaf team at releaf@treepittsburgh.org or call 412-781-8733 (x213).  Please contact us at least *72 hours before the event you plan to attend* so we can best support your participation. 

Complete all sessions to earn your Tree Tender certification and receive a pair of hand pruners. Come learn with us, build your tree knowledge and tree care skills!

events.title: Brookline Rally for Democracy, December 2026
events.description:
Brookline Rally for Democracy

Every Saturday at 1:00 PM | Coolidge Corner

Join members of three Brookline pro-democracy groups — indivisible Activist Evenings, Brookline Pax, and Speak Out, Seniors! — for our weekly rally at Coolidge Corner.

We gather to raise our voices and our signs in defense of democracy, justice, and decency — and to stand united against the abuses of the Trump administration and the forces that threaten our rights and freedoms.

We stand for:

• Immigrant rights, human rights, and racial justice

• Free speech, the Constitution, and the rule of law

• Access to health and healthcare for all

• Protection of our planet and the future we leave to the next generation

We choose empathy over cruelty, peace over violence, and hope over fear.

Our rallies are peaceful, spirited, and uplifting — a chance to connect, recharge, and stand up for what matters. Bring your friends, your voice, and your sign (or borrow one of ours!).

All are welcome!  The rally is multi-generational and family-friendly; those using walkers or other mobility devices may use them to sit to participate.

In the event of inclement weather, we’ll each use our best judgment about whether to attend. We hope you’ll do the same! 

Please join us, one rally at a time.  We’ll continue for as long as it takes.
events.accessibility_notes: All are welcome, including participants with walkers, wheelchairs, scooters, and other mobility devices.

events.title: Latino Media Network Miami Party At The Polls!
events.description:
# **LET’S PARTY AT THE POLLS!** 🗳️

*Celebrate our community. Cast your vote.*

We’re turning the ballot box into a block party! Come for the community, stay for the fun, and let’s make our voices heard together. It’s time to celebrate our power and show up for the neighborhood we love.

Join Latino Media Network Miami for a celebration of civic power, music, and community spirit!

**THE VIBE:**

We’re bringing the energy to the ballot box! Whether you’re voting early or on Election Day, come hang out, meet your neighbors, and celebrate democracy in action.

**WHERE & WHEN:**

📍Ben Sheppard Elementary School: 5700 W 24th Ave Hialeah, FL

📅 11/3 11a-1p

**FEATURING:**

Refreshments, snacks, live music and games

**LET’S VOTE TOGETHER!** 

Bring a friend, meet the community, and let’s make it count.

**Any food, entertainment, buttons, stickers, or any other free items at this event are available to voters and non-voters alike. This is a nonpartisan event.**

events.description:
Since November 2020, the League of Women Voters of Michigan and their Pro-Democracy Partners have worked to be the public’s eyes and ears at Michigan’s county canvass of votes cast during an election. Each year they work together to ensure that trained volunteers observe County Board of Canvassers (BOC) meetings, across the state of Michigan, watching the process by which local results are reviewed and certified.

This consistent, nonpartisan observation promotes transparency and accountability, helps identify potential issues that could put timely certification at risk, and reassures Board of Canvassers members and election staff that the public is engaged in their work. Should observation uncover anything beyond the canvassers’ ministerial, nondiscretionary duties, LWVMI can elevate the issue to the Secretary of State’s office or an election attorney.

- Reporting from our observers helps us understand the health of our democratic systems, where issues are happening, and where things are running smoothly.  
- These insights are important to all of us working to support our democracy, and ultimately support our communities in ensuring their voices are heard!

events.title: Election Protection: Virtual Poll Monitoring Training
events.description:
Join Bridge North Texas (Dallas County), the Election Protection Coalition, and 866-OUR-VOTE to protect the vote and ensure fair, accessible elections in our community! We are partnering to provide training, resources, and ongoing support for nonpartisan election work, canvassing, and poll monitoring.
Whether you're ready to dive right in or want hands-on assistance getting started, we have two simple pathways to help you get involved:

Choose How You Want to Join:
  Option A: Self-Paced / Direct Sign-Up
   Sign up via our link anytime to complete the online training with Common Cause Texas. Once finished, you will be connected directly with a local Bridge North Texas organizer to coordinate picking up your materials.

  Option B: Hands-On Setup & Walkthrough
   Sign up ahead of time with Bridge North Texas! Our team will walk you through the registration process step-by-step, assist with setting up your training, and prepare your materials for pickup.

What You'll Be Doing:
  Poll Monitoring: Help observe voting locations to protect voters' rights and ensure smooth election site operations.

  Canvassing & Community Outreach: Distribute voter education information, answer questions, and direct voters to key resources.

  Rapid Response Support: Work in tandem with the national 866-OUR-VOTE hotline network to address nonpartisan voting issues in real time.
Sign up today to protect democracy in North Texas!

events.title: Van Wert County Anytime Canvass - Oct. 4 - Nov. 3
events.description:
Join the HD-82 campaign’s **Van Wert County Anytime Canvass** from **October 4 through November 3**.

The Anytime Canvass is designed to make volunteering flexible. Instead of signing up for a specific scheduled shift, you can help when it works for you—whether you have an hour after work, a free afternoon, or several hours on a weekend.

Volunteers can choose how they would like to participate:

- **Direct voter contact:** Knock doors and speak with voters using an assigned canvassing list.
- **Literature delivery:** Help distribute campaign literature to assigned households without conducting voter conversations.

No previous canvassing experience is required. Instructions and the information you need to complete your assigned area will be provided.

After signing up, we’ll coordinate with you on an available area in **Van Wert County**, provide the necessary canvassing information and materials, and make sure you know how to report your completed area.

You can participate more than once throughout the month. If you finish an assignment and want another, we can provide an additional assignment.

**Sign up, choose the type of canvassing that works for you, and help cover Van Wert County on your own schedule between October 4 and November 3.**
events.accessibility_notes: This is a flexible, community-based canvassing opportunity rather than a traditional event at a single venue. Volunteers may choose between direct voter contact and literature delivery. If you have accessibility needs or need an accommodation to participate, please contact the campaign so we can work with you to find an appropriate way to volunteer.

The Anytime Canvass is designed to make volunteering flexible. Instead of signing up for a specific scheduled shift, you can help when it works for you—whether you have an hour after work, a free afternoon, or several hours on a weekend.

Volunteers can choose how they would like to participate:

Direct voter contact: Knock doors and speak with voters using an assigned canvassing list.

Literature delivery: Help distribute campaign literature to assigned households without conducting voter conversations.

No previous canvassing experience is required. Instructions and the information you need to complete your assigned area will be provided.

After signing up, we’ll coordinate with you on an available area in Paulding County, provide the necessary canvassing information and materials, and make sure you know how to report your completed area.

You can participate more than once throughout the month. If you finish an assignment and want another, we can provide an additional assignment.

Sign up, choose the type of canvassing that works for you, and help cover Paulding County on your own schedule between October 4 and November 3.
events.accessibility_notes: This is a flexible, community-based canvassing opportunity rather than a traditional event at a single venue. Volunteers may choose between direct voter contact and literature delivery. If you have accessibility needs or need an accommodation to participate, please contact the campaign so we can work with you to find an appropriate way to volunteer.

events.title: Kanawha County IEP Circle
events.description:
IEP Circles WV is a parent-led community where families of exceptional learners come together to find support, build knowledge, and create change. If you're navigating an IEP, 504 Plan, evaluations, school communication, or accessing services, these gatherings are designed to help you feel informed, connected, and supported.

Each meeting brings caregivers together with experienced advocates, education attorneys, and community partners who provide practical guidance, answer questions, and facilitate meaningful discussions. You'll have opportunities to share experiences, learn from other families, discover helpful resources, and build lasting relationships with people who understand the challenges you face.

Beyond individual support, IEP Circles helps families understand the larger issues affecting special education. We'll explore how school funding, staffing shortages, IDEA funding, and state and federal policy decisions impact the services available to students. By connecting personal experiences to these broader challenges, families can better understand why obstacles exist and how they can work alongside educators and other parents to improve public education.

For those interested in taking the next step, IEP Circles also offers opportunities to develop advocacy skills through workshops on legislative advocacy, storytelling, public speaking, community organizing, and civic engagement. Whether you simply want support or hope to help shape the future of special education in West Virginia, you'll find a welcoming community where your experiences are valued and your voice matters.

Together, we can strengthen support for our children, build stronger communities, and advocate for a public education system that works for every student.

events.description:
# Rally Against The Regime – Election Season

## 🗳️ Election Season Is Here, and We're Taking It to the Overpass

From now through the November election, our weekly **Rally Against The Regime** moves to the **I-5 Overpass at NW Stewart Parkway**. Thousands of drivers pass this spot every day, and we want every one of them to see our message:

**Vote the Trump administration and its Republican enablers out of power. End fascism. Take our country back to the democracy it was meant to be.**

Ballots are coming. This is our moment, and it starts at the mailbox.


## 📍 When & Where

- **When:** **Monday, November 2nd,** **12:00 pm – 2:00 pm**

- **Where:** **I-5 Overpass & NW Stewart Parkway** (on the sidewalk)
  3599 NW Stewart Pkwy, Roseburg, OR 97471


## 🧰 What To Bring

This isn't just a protest. **It's people power on display.**

### 📣 Make Your Voice Visible

**Go BIG.** Drivers are moving fast, so **large signs with short messages** in thick, high-contrast letters work best. Here are some ideas:

- **VOTE EARLY. VOTE THEM OUT!**

- **MY BALLOT IS MY VOICE!**

- **DOUGLAS COUNTY VOTES BLUE!**

- **FILL IT OUT. MAIL IT IN. VOTE EARLY!**

- **REPUBLICANS HAD THEIR CHANCE!**

- **HONK IF YOU'RE VOTING EARLY!**

- **BALLOTS ARE HERE. USE THEM!**

- **REAL CHANGE STARTS AT THE MAILBOX!**

👉 Or create your own. **Be bold. Be direct. Don't hold back.**

### 🎨 Get Creative

- 🪆 Giant puppets

- 🎭 Creative props

- 🧥 Costumes

- 🚩 Banners & flags

- 🎶 Street-theater vibes


### 🥤 Stay Comfortable

- 💧 Water

- 🍎 A snack

- 🕶️ Sunglasses & sunscreen

- 🧢 Hat or umbrella for sun or rain

- 👟 Comfortable shoes

- 💊 Any medications you need

⚠️ **No bathrooms on site. Plan accordingly.**


## 🕊️ Our Commitment to Nonviolence

This is a **peaceful, nonviolent demonstration**. Please:

- **Stay on the sidewalk** and keep it clear for people walking by. Never step into traffic.

- **Secure your signs and banners** so the wind can't carry them onto the roadway below.

- **Don't engage with counter-protesters**, and help calm things down and de-escalate if tensions rise.

- **This is a non-violent action. Leave all weapons at home.**

---

**See you on the overpass. Let's vote them out.** 🇺🇸

**Note on Parking:** To access the overpass facing the Northbound I-5 traffic, park in the empty lot all the way at the top of Boulder Drive on your left (go up the curved road behind Oregon Pacific Bank off of Edenbower Blvd and Boulder Drive) or along the roadway. Crossing to the other side of the overpass (facing Southbound I-5 traffic) is done at your own risk.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Weekly Meade Ave Bridge Bannering Over I-805 | Tuesdays
events.description:
Meet on the Meade Ave bridge over I-805.

We provide large physical messaging in the real world to connect with and activate voters to demonstrate that resistance is possible. Bring a sign for cars on the bridge or just wave to the cars passing below. You can also bring a flag, chair, bubbles, music, or anything else you want in order to have a good time!

Rules and Protocols

1. We avoid doing anything that could either harm ourselves or anyone else. This includes stepping into traffic, holding a sign where it could fall onto cars below, climbing fencing, etc.

2. We must not block pedestrian and bike traffic, so please keep the middle of the overpass and/or sidewalk clear to allow them to pass.

3. We supply the messages, you supply the waves. However, you are welcome to also display your own poster boards. Just avoid any messaging that would be rated above a PG-13.

4. We don’t litter. If we find litter, we pick it up and throw it away.

5. We don’t use stickers or anything that leaves a permanent mark on the overpass. However, chalk is okay and even encouraged.

6. If someone from the ‘opposition’ comes up to talk with us, do not engage with them. Best to just ignore them. One member will be designated to handle them and video record any aggressive interaction so that you can go right on waving.

7. We take lots of pictures and videos during our action for circulation on social media. If you prefer not to be included, please let us know and/or consider wearing a mask.

8. Should law enforcement pay us a visit, only the designated point person from the group should address them.

9. Ignore the middle fingers and negativity coming from some of the cars below. For every one of those confused folks, you are providing hope to another 100 people!

10. The Visibility Brigade is a non-violent, informal volunteer group in which we all participate with an understanding that our own actions are our personal responsibility and we accept our own personal liability. You participate with this understanding.

events.title: Canvass with us in Indiana Congressional District 5!

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
CD-5 is the most flippable red seat in Congress in Indiana - but we need YOUR help talking to voters to make that happen. 

In 2022, Indiana had the LOWEST midterm voter turnout in the country at 40%. There is a pervasive sense of "Indiana is red and always will be." But in truth: 

**Indiana is a purple state that DOESN'T VOTE.** 

We have the chance this month to use our votes to end the corruption. End the violence. End the lies. A House majority would give Democrats the ability to rein in Donald Trump.

And so...we are going on offense.

**Join one or more of our canvassing shifts to knock on doors in Congressional District 5 to help elect J.D. Ford.**

The voters we will canvass are just folks who need a little nudge to remind them to vote blue. You won't be talking to anyone MAGA or hard right. 

Democrat J.D. Ford is a well regarded and well liked sitting Indiana State Senator who is running against CD-5's current congressperson, Republican Victoria Spartz, for the congressional seat just north of Indianapolis. Rep Spartz has a reliable voting record in support of Donald Trump's agenda. 

So what can you do?

**You can join us.** 

If you haven't canvassed before, we will make it easy. You show up for your shift at a meeting spot with a shift leader and other canvassers to get your voter addresses and instructions. 

**Feeling shy, but you want to try it?** 

Simply sign up for a canvassing shift and a link to a general training about talking to voters will be sent to you. We can pair you with another canvasser, or you can bring a friend to walk with you while you knock on doors. 

Upon arrival at the meetup location, you will receive canvassing tips and JD Ford handouts to share at each door. You will be able to easily enter results as you canvass into the [MiniVAN app](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tv9-HHb1VQA) on your smartphone. 

A lot of canvassers like to make a fun day out of it: you can bring a friend and go out together for lunch or dinner after your shift. You can feel the satisfaction of doing your part for our democracy while getting in quality time with a friend. Win-win!

Registering for one or more shifts confirms that you agree to our [Code of Conduct and our Volunteer Waiver](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1cpXG6qbL36S10EYFRqAVAIzfdSFiOG0utHdCFWdZ-9E/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.l1k2qhtuewim).

events.description:
Build new alliances and find ways to stand up for democracy! Indivisible Auburn WA typically meets the first Thursday of each month, 6:10 - 7:40. (First-time attendees are welcome at an optional getting started session starting at 5:40.)

Our November meeting will include continued discussion of election protection - ensuring every ballot is counted and all elected officials are seated. events.title: Keweenaw County Canvass Observation

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Since November 2020, the League of Women Voters of Michigan and their Pro-Democracy Partners have worked to be the public’s eyes and ears at Michigan’s county canvass of votes cast during an election. Each year they work together to ensure that trained volunteers observe County Board of Canvassers (BOC) meetings, across the state of Michigan, watching the process by which local results are reviewed and certified.

This consistent, nonpartisan observation promotes transparency and accountability, helps identify potential issues that could put timely certification at risk, and reassures Board of Canvassers members and election staff that the public is engaged in their work. Should observation uncover anything beyond the canvassers’ ministerial, nondiscretionary duties, LWVMI can elevate the issue to the Secretary of State’s office or an election attorney.

### Your Role As An Observer:
- Our BOC Observer are an important aspect of our volunteer election work! 
- Our observers not only serve to build trust in the community as well as between local government and the League, but they also help to ensure our elections are running as the laws intended. 
- Reporting from our observers helps us understand the health of our democratic systems, where issues are happening, and where things are running smoothly.  
- These insights are important to all of us working to support our democracy, and ultimately support our communities in ensuring their voices are heard! 

We hope you will join us, volunteer, and bring a friend to be a part of this election work!

**Shifts are subject to change, as county clerks work to finalize the details of the county canvass. If your shift is cancelled, you will be contacted by a representative from the League of Women Voters.**

events.title: Banned Book Club - To Kill A Mockingbird by Harper Lee
events.description:
For the remainder of October and throughout November we will be exploring How To Kill A Mockingbird by Harper Lee. I feel it is important to advise that this book may have triggers for some people. If you feel you might not be in an emotional space to handle the topics mentioned, or that this title just isn't for you, please feel free to skip parts or the book in full and stay tuned for December's title.

Content Trigger Warnings for To Kill A Mockingbird by Harper Lee include the following subjects:

• Abuse
• Murder
• N-word
• Racism
• Rape (mentioned)

Join us each month for a new book from our ever growing banned or challenged book list. Where we choose a new title each month and combine reading out loud in a group setting, reading alone, and discussing how the books might correspond to the world around us.

This month we will finish To Kill A Mockingbird by Harper Lee.

Please make sure to add any suggestions to the Google spreadsheet shared in the Zoom chat before the third week of the month to have a chance at it being selected for the next month. The event name will be updated once the title is selected.

The meetings are 90 minutes long and broke down into 3 parts. The first half hour is spent discussing the section that was designed or our anticipations on what the book might be like. The middle section we read out loud, and the last half hour is spent going over what we read and assigning the next section.

So far we have read the following titles and discussed how they correlate with our present day. 

• The Diary of a Yong Girl - Anne Frank 
• 1984 - George Orwell 
• Animal Farm - George Orwell 
• Fahrenheit 451 – Ray Bradbury 
• Looking Backward – Edward Bellamy 
• The Age of Reason - Thomas Paine 
• Howl and Other Poems - Allen Ginsberg
• Civil Disobedience - Henry David Thoreau

All are welcome and even if you haven’t picked up the book feel free to join us for the discussion and reading.

events.title: Camp Verde ALPR Community Discussion & Next Steps
events.description:
The conversation continues — and we need you there.

Join your Camp Verde neighbors for a community discussion about Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) technology currently being used in our community.

📅 Saturday, November 7
⏰ 9:00 AM
📍 Camp Verde Community Library
130 N. Black Bridge Loop, Camp Verde, AZ

This meeting is an opportunity to come together, share what we’ve learned, ask questions, and talk about what comes next.

We’ll discuss:

🔹 What we know about the ALPR technology being used in Camp Verde
🔹 Questions and concerns from our community
🔹 What we’ve learned so far
🔹 How we can continue educating our neighbors
🔹 What steps we can take to encourage the Town to reconsider this technology
🔹 How YOU can get involved

You don't need to be an expert or have followed this issue from the beginning. If you care about privacy, transparency, and having a voice in decisions that affect our community, you are welcome.

📚 Want to get caught up before the meeting?

Visit: CampVerdePrivacy.org.

There you can learn more about the ALPR technology being used in Camp Verde, read background information and previous meeting materials, find educational resources and literature, and sign our community petition.

Whether you're just learning about this issue or have been involved from the beginning, there's a place for you in this conversation.

Come bring your questions, your ideas, and your voice.

❤️ Together, let's figure out what comes next.

events.title: Reach Your Friends. Help Pat Win.
events.description:
The most powerful political conversation isn’t always with a campaign volunteer or an advertisement, it’s with someone you already know and trust.

That’s why Team Halpin is launching Reach, a simple tool that lets you connect with friends, family, neighbors and coworkers who live in the district and personally encourage them to vote.

With Election Day just weeks away, we need supporters like you helping us have thousands of real, personal conversations about what’s at stake in this election.

Here’s how it works:
1. Sign up here on Mobilize.
2. You’ll receive a link that takes you directly into the Reach App
3. Reach will help you identify people you know who may live in the district.
4. You can then send them information about the campaign, use content and videos for social posts. 
5. Follow up and make sure they have a plan to vote.

You don’t need a script. You don’t need campaign experience. And you can do it from anywhere.

Even reaching out to 5 or 10 people you know can make a difference.

This is one of the most important midterm elections of our lifetimes. The decisions Washington makes over the next two years will affect the cost of living, healthcare, housing, Social Security and Medicare, public safety, our environment, and the future of our democracy.

The best messenger to someone you know is YOU.

Sign up, open Reach, and start a conversation today.

Let’s win this one conversation at a time.

events.title: Florida NOW Film Screening: Reimagining Safety
events.description:
Join us as we close out the series with a screening of Reimagining Safety, a documentary filmed in the aftermath of the 2020 murder of George Floyd and the worldwide protests that followed. The film brings together 10 experts, including abolitionists, social workers, scholars, a former LAPD detective, and a former district attorney, to examine how policing and incarceration shape our ideas about safety.

The film revisits the 2020 protests and the growing calls to defund and abolish the police, while exploring the history and ongoing impact of police violence, racism, mass incarceration, mental health crises, housing insecurity, and the criminalization of poverty. It also highlights restorative justice, violence prevention, community responders, and other approaches that seek to build safety through care, accountability, and community rather than punishment and isolation.

Stay after the screening for our final community reflection and conversation in this series.

events.title: Michigan Voter Registration Calls with Rust Belt Rising
events.description:
Join Rust Belt Rising to help make sure that everyone is able to vote in this year's General Election!

Rust Belt Rising's innovative voter registration programs helped thousands of Great Lakes state residents register the last three cycles and will do so again this year.

Here's how it works: RBR partners at Civitech find targets of people who would likely vote our way but are unregistered at their current address as they compare commercial mail lists and voter files. They will mail these targets a pre-filled voter registration form with a motivational flyer and postage to their clerk. That's where we come in. In addition to our texting them, we need volunteers to call these targets to encourage them to complete the easy process of registering.

We would love for you to be part of a team that makes these calls to Michigan voters as part of our virtual voter registration chase! 

We'll teach you everything you know over Zoom and get you calling to remind voters to register because there is an election coming up!

events.title: 24th Annual ReLeafing Day at Glen Leven Farm!
events.description:
Join the Nashville Tree Foundation for the 24th Annual ReLeafing Day!

Held each year on the Saturday before Thanksgiving, ReLeafing Day is our signature community tree-planting event. Following the devastating 1998 tornadoes, our founders launched this initiative as a major restoration effort - raising $1,000,000 in six months and planting over 6,000 trees across the city. Today, that legacy continues as we focus on planting new trees in Nashville every November.

This year, we invite you to dig deep and plant trees at the beautiful Glen Leven Farm on Saturday, November 21st. We are proud to be supported by Root Nashville, helping drive the citywide goal of planting 500,000 trees by 2050, and funded by the Cumberland River Compact.

Whether you are an experienced tree planter or a first-time volunteer, this is the perfect way to connect with nature, meet fellow tree lovers, and actively grow our urban forest!

What to Expect: 
We will start the morning with a brief introduction and an overview of the day's goals. Our team will provide a step-by-step tree planting demonstration and review essential safety guidelines so you feel completely confident. Then, we'll plant our trees!

events.title: A District That Works for Children, Youth, and Families
events.description:
**What would it take to build a District that truly works for all children, youth, and families?**

That’s what we will be asking at our end-of-year summit on **Thursday, December 3, from 6:30-8:00 pm.** At DC Action, we’re bringing together the DC Out-of-School Time Coalition, Under 3 DC, and the Youth Economic Justice Coalition to lead a bold conversation with the mayor-elect and elected leaders from across the District, and we want you to join us. 

This is a critical moment for the District, with a new mayor for the first time in a dozen years, major turnover on the council, and continued uncertainty about the economy. The budget and policy decisions made over the coming months, and the plans carried out in the next few years, will impact the District for generations to come. 

It’s vital that the needs of Black and brown children, youth, and families be at the center of these discussions. That’s why this event will be led by young people, parents, and direct service providers from the three coalitions, who will share their experiences and what they want to see from our elected leaders, from making child care more affordable, to expanding out-of-school time programs, and committing to ending youth homelessness.


**Doors open at 5:30pm.**
events.accessibility_notes: Child care is available on a first-come, first-served basis.

events.title: Mondays @ McCormick's - - 2000 Market St. Every Monday @ noon - Demand Dave McCormick meet with us!
events.description:
We call on Dave McCormick to say no to Trump and to say yes to reason & compassion.

We demand a meeting with his policy staff, the Senator and members of the PA Network for peace, justice and sustainability.


We rally each week at NOON
Outside Dave’s Office, 
2000 Market St. Phila PA 19103

Resistance is NOT futile - it is essential. 

We launched "Monday's at McCormick's" after his election when he refused to meet with us.

We gather each Monday at noon - rain or shine - to assemble peaceably - as is our constitutional right - outside Senator McCormick's Philadelphia office until Senator McCormick agrees to meet with us and support our demands: (These will change as conditions develop)

 1 - Stop voting for legislation inspired by Trump's project 2025 agenda - a plan to slash Medicaid, gut school lunch programs, push back on environmental protections in service of big oil and the extration industries, and shut down nursing homes while handing more power to billionaires like Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos and others. 

2- Roll back Trump's mean spirited and Unconstitutional funding pauses. Shutting down USAID is already killing people in need all over the World. Cuts to programs here in the US could do the same. Funding for these programs are up to the Congress and the US people to decide, not Trump! 

3 - Stop the Administration's wars of choice around the world.

4 - Re-engage with nuclear arms treaty regimes to reduce and eventually eliminate Nuclear weapons and ALL weapons of mass destruction

That's just for starters. Overall we want Senator McCormick to represent us all, not just his rich friends. We want Senator McCormick to DO HIS JOB!

The stakes could not be higher. The administration is pushing an authoritarian agenda that threatens our democracy, our rights, and the well-being of millions here at home and around the planet. 

We have the power to resist—and we must use every tool at our disposal to stop them.

events.title: SATS: Know Your Rights Outreach - Help protect SO. BRONX against ICE w/ TMNYC

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Show up in solidarity with your NYC neighbors in the South Bronx. We have tens of thousands of small business in New York City left to go, and we need your help to do it. No training required to join us for a shift.

Working in pairs, block by block, we will meet with owners, managers, and employees at their work sites. We use multilingual, legally vetted materials to ensure they know how to protect themselves now, what to do if ICE comes, what to do in case of detentions, and where to find additional resources.

Everywhere we've gone, we've had really good experiences helping store managers, bar/restaurants, parking lots, etc to prepare and better protect employees in the event of ICE raids.

You'll join volunteers with Target Majority NYC to talk to give business owners and managers the crucial Know Your Rights info they need to better protect their employees in the event of an ICE Raid. You'll help them put up signs to create as much protection as possible within their place of work, and declare solidarity.

We will provide training on the spot, but you can also start prepping now by visiting https://tinyurl.com/startSOS

**A core principle behind all Target Majority NYC events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. We recommend all participants review [Indivisible's safety and security resources](https://indivisi.org/safety) before this event**

events.title: Take Down First Sunday December
events.description:
## Take-Down Crew

This sign-up is **ONLY** for the **TAKE-DOWN CREW** for First Sunday. 

Take Down Includes **TWO PARTS:**

**1. Take Down Site** - Arrive at the First Sunday site at on Hillsboro St in Pittsboro by 4 pm on Sunday, December 6, take down and pack up the equipment, and then load it into your vehicle. 

[Download this PDF that tells you everything you need to know about taking down a CCDP tent event!](https://drive.google.com/file/d/166H68VYdekt4POF1CXZYRR0mdMTQy0yN/view?usp=sharing)

**2. Drop Off Equipment** - Sometime **the week of December 7-9** drop off the equipment at CCDP's office in the Food Lion Shopping Center, in Pittsboro near the urgent care. Call the CEC at 919-704-8669 to confirm hours and/or get directions, or visit the website at ccdpnc.org. 

It's most convenient if you have an SUV or a truck to transport the materials, but a small SUV works well, and a large sedan with trunk space works too.

To **join the set-up crew** on Sunday, December 6 at 11 am: [Sign Up Here](https://www.mobilize.us/chathamcountydems/event/1057184/)

events.title: Team Krueger/Aronson Volunteer Orientation
events.description:
Join us online for a 45-minute Volunteer Orientation to get out the vote with Team Krueger & Aronson!

Find out how you can make a difference on Manhattan's East Side. We'll walk you through volunteer roles and what to expect: talking with neighbors, helping at community events and candidate meet-and-greets, and building visibility at polling sites during early voting and on Election Day.

Why team up? State Senator Liz Krueger (Senate District 28) and Vanessa Aronson, candidate for State Assembly District 73, represent overlapping East Side communities and share a commitment to tackling the affordability crisis, expanding health care access, combating hate crimes, strengthening climate protections, and defending our democracy.

Whether you're new to volunteering or have helped before, we'd be glad to have you. Bring your energy, and we'll help you put it into action!

events.title: Rally: Keep Data Centers Out of New York!
events.description:
**Join us for a massive rally outside Governor Hochul's most important speech of the year to send her a clear, powerful message: Keep Data Centers Out of New York!**

Together, we won a moratorium on massive AI data centers in New York. Now, it's on all of us to keep them out for good. We've crisscrossed the state over the last few months and it's clear that New Yorkers everywhere oppose building these massive, polluting facilities in their communities. 

That's why we must bring the movement straight to Hochul's doorstep now. Together, we'll rally at the capitol to kick off the new year and show Governor Hochul and the Legislature that New Yorkers won't accept data centers in our state.

We can win this fight, but it's going to take a massive show of people power given the almost limitless budget on the other side.

*Sign up today to reserve your spot — transportation options from all corners of the state coming shortly.*

events.title: Lee County School Board Workshop
events.description:
Join FSPS-Lee at the Lee County School Board Workshop

Join Families for Strong Public Schools – Lee Chapter as we attend the Lee County School Board Workshop to stay informed and engaged in the conversations shaping our public schools.

What is a School Board Workshop?

A workshop is different from a regular School Board meeting. Regular meetings are where the Board takes formal action and votes on agenda items. Workshops are primarily working sessions where Board members receive information, ask questions, discuss issues in greater detail, and explore potential policies or decisions before they may come back for formal action.

That makes workshops an important part of the public decision-making process.

By the time an issue reaches a final vote, Board members may have already spent significant time discussing it during workshops. Attending or tuning in gives families and community members an opportunity to understand what is being considered earlier in the process—not just when it is time for a vote.

Why Tune In or Attend?

📚 Get informed early about issues and proposals that could affect Lee County public schools.

👀 See the process in action and hear the questions, concerns, and priorities Board members raise as they consider an issue.

📝 Be better prepared to advocate when an issue moves forward for future discussion or action.

🤝 Stay connected with FSPS-Lee and other community members working to support strong public schools.

You don't need to be an education policy expert to participate. You can simply attend, listen, learn, and become more familiar with how decisions affecting our schools are made.

Strong community engagement doesn't begin when the Board takes a vote. It begins by paying attention throughout the process.

Our schools. Our community. Our voice. 💙

Join FSPS-Lee at the workshop or tune in and stay informed about what's happening in Lee County public schools.

events.title: Knowledge is Power: The Nerd Reich
events.description:
Knowledge is Power is an inclusive and accessible group of progressive learners who are working to educate ourselves about the issues facing us today. From Central Ohio politics to climate change, we are arming ourselves with knowledge to actively work to better our world. More importantly, we are building community and supporting each other in these challenging times!

YOU ARE INVITED TO JOIN US! We meet monthly in Central Ohio to discuss a topic chosen by the group members. We offer multiple ways to access materials for each topic, from books and articles to podcasts and documentaries– because everyone learns best in different ways!

This topic came straight from suggestions by several group members, and it’s a hot one! For years, Gil Duran has been doing the heavy lifting of decoding and sifting through the flood of Silicon Valley weirdness. In his new book, The Nerd Reich, he pulls it all together and shines a bright light on it. Trust me, it’s even stranger than you think!  We will be reading excerpts from his recently published book, The Nerd Reich: Silicon Valley Fascism and the War on Democracy, as well as listening to an interview with him on the "Why Is This Happening?" podcast. The links are below.

P.S. - I am building the plane while flying it, so please bear with me.  If you have issues/suggestions/feedback, feel free to drop me an email at anaunderman@gmail.com

BOOK: The Nerd Reich: Silicon Valley Fascism and the War on Democracy, by Gil Duran (August 18, 2026).

Introduction and Chapter 1: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1oEkrEyd5ps4b2rwsjCgxeLSZ87XsQJmn/view?usp=sharing

PODCAST: Why Is This Happening? The Chris Hayes Podcast, "‘They are REALLY, REALLY DUMB’ about some things: Gil Durán EXPOSES Silicon Valley oligarchs" (August 31, 2026)

https://www.ms.now/video-podcast/they-are-really-really-dumb-about-some-things-gil-duran-exposes-silicon-valley-oligarchs-2512709699914

events.title: Down Home + FLIP NC Voting Information Text Banks
events.description:
Down Home and FLIP NC are teaming up to text local voting information and provide support to left-leaning voters across eleven counties in North Carolina.

We'll hold the text banks in Zoom. Each text bank shift is 2 hours long, and we stay in the Zoom together the whole time to answer questions and provide support.

We'll be using a user-friendly, web-based platform called Scale to Win to send the messages, so text bankers will need a laptop, computer, or tablet (and your personal phone number will not be used for texting).

Each text bank will begin with a brief training on how to use the platform and how to respond to questions from voters. All volunteers must attend the full training during their first shift before beginning text banking, so please arrive on time! 

Additional information about the text bank, including the Zoom link, will be shared via email prior to your shift(s).

On Saturday, Oct. 17, we will text county-level early voting information to voters in eleven Down Home counties.

On Saturday, Oct. 24, we will text lower-propensity voters who have not yet voted with their closest early voting site if they live in a county with four or more sites (six Down Home counties).

On Monday, Nov. 2, we will text voters who have not yet voted with their election day polling location and hours.

Thank you for joining us!

events.description:
When EIF receives food in bulk, we rely on volunteers to repackage that product into smaller portions for our agencies to give out to individuals and families facing food insecurity. Repacks are a fun activity for both groups and individuals looking to give back to their communities.

To ensure our team can prepare effectively for volunteer groups, evening community repacks will no longer operate "open hours" style. We ask that volunteers register prior to volunteering events and plan to stay for the duration of the repack. We’ll be hosting the repack on November 12th, from 4:30 - 6:30 PM. 

Our address is 2405 North Shore Drive, and we're operating out of our Volunteer Center. Please drive down North Shore Drive until you reach the end of the Cul de Sac, and the Volunteer Center is on the left hand side (there's a big sign, you can't miss it!). You'll enter through the door with the red awning.

Please keep in mind that while volunteering, the following are not allowed on the volunteer center floor:

Dangling jewelry (earrings/necklaces), 
Open-toe shoes, 
Tank tops and crop tops,  
Food/beverage containers, 
Gum

Thanks again for volunteering with EIF!

Swing by when you vote, or bring your family and neighbors. You'll find veterans, faith leaders, legal professionals, and community members creating a welcoming, nonpartisan presence outside the polls. It's about participation, not politics, and about our community showing up for each other.
