address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Join the Springfield Chapter of Neighbor to Neighbor for our Social Justice Book Club! Hosted by:  Neighbor to Neighbor Springfield Chapter

This Fall 2026, we are reading: "Emergent Strategies" written by Adrienne Maree Brown! *If support is needed to get the book, please reach out - copies available at N2N or at Olive Tree Books and Voices*

Our first gathering will be IN PERSON, on Saturday, October 17, 2026 from 6:30-7:45pm! We'll meet at the N2N Office downtown Springfield (Address: 1350 Main St., Floor 3, Suite 300)

This round, we'll discuss the first 3 chapters of the book! Readers of diverse reading levels are WELCOME!  

We intend for this book club to be a place where folks from all backgrounds can gather together around a central text and learn, connect and grow together. Social Justice is defined and understood differently by many people, but at the heart of Social Justice is the idea of equity, inclusion, power-building and change. Therefore, in addition to diving into this beautiful book, this book club will center discussion questions and themes around those ideas. The ideas shared within this book should not be considered a reflection of Neighbor to Neighbor's plans of action, but should instead be reflected on deeply by readers to guide how you understand resistance, revolution, community organizing and history as it relates to today. 

**Bring your whole self into this space** - your curious self, your radical self, your activist self into this space - heck, bring a friend (and make sure they sign up)! 

We'll bring snacks and a comfy place to connect together!

**SPECIAL THANKS TO OLIVE TREE BOOKS N VOICES for sponsoring this book club! Olive Tree is the ONLY Black Owned bookstore in Springfield, located at 97 Hancock Street, Spfld,MA. 

We STRONGLY ENCOURAGE participants to purchase/ order your copies from Olive Tree to support local entrepreneurship and small BIPOC owned businesses.

events.title: MICHIGAN Winning Working Families Majority
events.description:
# Phonebank to Take Back the People's House for Working People in November! 

Join People's Action Power and Team '26, a coalition of movement organizations across the country, to reach the working-class voters in must-win Congressional and Senate races that will decide who controls Congress -- and whether we save our democracy. 


### 🏥 Michigan Thursdays: Will Lawrence for Congress, MI-7, and Dr. Abdul El-Sayed for US Senate 

- Will Lawrence is the Sunrise Movement co-founder who helped win the largest green jobs program in US history and delivered hundreds of millions to Mid-Michigan. He co-founded Michigan Rent Is Too Damn High to win statewide renter protections. 

- Dr. Abdul El-Sayed is a medical doctor who realized broken politics was making people sick, and he went to work fixing government: rebuilt Detroit's Health Department after bankruptcy, got lead out of the schools, and canceled $700 million in medical debt for 300,000 Michiganders. He wrote the book on Medicare for All, and now, he's going to the Senate to make government work for you, not billionaires. 
 
The message from the primary season was loud and clear: Working Families candidates are winning. Working people aren't settling for just any candidate. They're demanding Movement Champions who answer to them, not big corporations and big money. 

Are you fired up? Sign up for the shifts leading up to Election Day. Share this link widely with your friends and family. 

No prior experience is required to join this phone bank. A laptop or tablet is recommended.

Let's go! Let's take back the People's House.

events.title: Michaela for Tennessee Election Night Watch Party
events.description:
Join Michaela’s Cavalry for an Election Night Watch Party at Printshop Beer Co!

Then come celebrate with us at 7 pm, where multiple screens will broadcast live results for the November 3 midterm elections. Whatever happens on NOV 3, East Tennessee will see this movement showed up and made history.

* Taco bar from Dia de Foods
* Popcorn and cotton candy from Something Borrowed by CLG
* Cookies from Rise for a Cause
* Hot cocoa and coffee (bring a mug!)
* Great beer from the Printshop brewers

Good to know:

* This is an indoor/outdoor event, so dress warm.
* Kids and dogs are welcome, but it may get crowded.

Together, we’ve built a strong community, and we could not have done this without you. Every door knocked, every sign planted, every call made got us here. Now it’s time to join together and celebrate.

events.title: Clarksville Election Day Hub
events.description:
Community members and organizations are invited to come together in Clarksville on Election Day to make sure that every Tennessee voter casts their ballot and makes their voice heard!

Our Election Hub will be open to volunteers on Tuesday, November 3, 2026 from 9:00 am to 5 pm CT. Join us at our hub for the day to:

• Plug in and volunteer with phone banking, texting, canvassing, and other GOTV efforts in the community. 
• Offer rides to and from the polls and provide interpreter services for voters who need additional assistance
• Support on-the-ground election and voter protection efforts. 

If you are coordinating your own GOTV efforts, you are welcome to use our hub for any 501(c)(3)-friendly activities. 

Be in community with other partners and friends You can join for as short or as long as you would like! No experience required - training available for anyone who needs it.

Even if you don't do work in Nashville, but you still want to support GOTV and election and voter protection efforts on Election Day, please join us and we will get you plugged in.

RSVP required via Mobilize - Breakfast and lunch will be provided!

If you have any questions about our Clarksville Election Day Election Hub including any accessibility needs or other needs so you can fully participate, please email Tiffany Perkins Tiffany@civictn.org.

Polls will be open for voting on Election Day from 7am to 7pm CT.

events.title: Make Your Voice Heard
events.description:
Join your community of like minded folks and make your voice heard!!!

To be heard is not just to have your words acknowledged. It’s to feel seen, valued, and understood. It’s to know that your presence matters.

Our voice is more than what we say. It’s our identity. Our power. For some, that voice shows up with bold resistance. For others, it’s the quiet courage to speak up after years of silence, to challenge injustice, and to stand in solidarity.

When we speak with clarity, we create space for connection and growth. It’s a practice that deepens how we show up in life and for others.

So let’s make our voices heard and fight for positive change!

events.title: [Phoenix] Día de los Muertos Day of Action - End the ICE Age

location.venue: Margaret T. Hance Park, East Ramada

events.description:
This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

We'll gather and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

The plan is to meet at Hance Park, the East Ramada (covered picnic area), near the volleyball court, to hear a number of faith and community leaders speak, then after that we'll have a procession to the ICE Phoenix Field Office, where we'll read the names of, and remember, the people killed by ICE.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.description:
Join Connecticut Working Families Party for a Virtual Post General Elections debrief celebration on Tuesday, November 10th from 7pm-8pm as we reflect on the results of the 2026 Connecticut General Elections, celebrate the work that made these victories possible, and talk about what comes next.

events.title: Tree Planting in Braddock
events.description:
Join Tree Pittsburgh to plant trees in Braddock to support our work with ReLeaf! Together, we will plant about 7 trees in the community.

Register now to stay in the loop about event details.

Tree Pittsburgh will provide all the safety gear and tools necessary to get the work done!  Boots or sturdy sneakers are always recommended at Tree Pittsburgh Events. Long pants and sleeves are encouraged. 

**New to volunteering with Tree Pittsburgh? All new volunteers must [complete this form](https://action.treepittsburgh.org/a/volunteer-agreement-form) before their first event with us.**

All volunteers under the age of 18 must be accompanied by an adult for the duration of the event. Please reach out to volunteer@treepittsburgh.org with any questions!

Volunteer Events are held rain or shine, but events will be cancelled for extreme weather. Review Tree Pittsburgh's [Volunteer Event Weather Policy](https://www.treepittsburgh.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Tree-Pgh-Volunteer-Event-Weather-Policy.pdf) here and reach out with any questions!

events.title: Lee County Public Schools Coalition Launch
events.description:
Lee County Public Schools Coalition Launch
Saturday, November 14, 2026
1:30 PM – 4:00 PM
Fort Myers Regional Library — Meeting Rooms (Separate Building)
Fort Myers, Florida

Families for Strong Public Schools Lee invites local organizations, community leaders, parent groups, educators, advocacy organizations, and other partners to join us for a collaborative gathering focused on one shared goal:
Strengthening public schools in Lee County.

This will be an opportunity for groups from across our community to come together, build relationships, share priorities, and strategize about how we can more effectively support students, educators, families, and strong public education.

We know there are many organizations throughout Lee County already doing important work. Rather than working in separate silos, we want to create opportunities to connect our efforts, share information, identify common goals, and build a stronger coalition for our public schools.

What to Expect

Join us for light refreshments and an informal but productive conversation about:
The biggest challenges currently facing Lee County public schools
Opportunities for collaboration between community organizations
Supporting and amplifying educators, parents, students, and school
communities
Improving public awareness and engagement around education issues
Coordinating advocacy and community outreach
Identifying shared priorities and opportunities for collective action
Creating stronger communication between organizations working to support public education

This is not about every organization agreeing on every issue. It is about finding the areas where we do agree and determining how we can work together to make a greater impact.

Who Should Attend?

We welcome representatives from parent and family organizations, education advocacy groups, teacher and employee organizations, civic and community organizations, neighborhood and grassroots groups, student organizations, nonprofits, faith and community partners, and other organizations whose work intersects with our children.

events.title: Text and Phonebank for No on 3 - Voter Rights MA
events.description:
Don’t let billionaires buy our elections.

This November, Question 3 would replace our current primaries with a “jungle primary,” where only the top two finishers advance to the general election, even if both are from the same party. The measure is funded by a small group of wealthy donors, mostly private equity executives. It would mean less choice for voters and more power for big money, and it would shut out minority and working class candidates from the November ballot.

Voters in other states rejected this same playbook in 2024. Help make sure Massachusetts does too.

What you’ll do:

Text or call voters with us!

Join us on Zoom (link sent when you sign up) for a quick training, then choose how you want to help: reply to texts from Massachusetts voters who’ve responded to our outreach, or call voters in a phonebank. Either way, you’ll answer their questions, share why we’re voting No on 3, and ask them to pledge their vote. No experience needed. We’ll give you suggested replies for texting, a script for calling, and support the whole time. Every conversation counts!

events.title: It's Up to Us: Early Vote Phone Bank - Mondays
events.description:
It’s up to us to make sure every voter in our community has a plan to make their voice heard! Join Indivisible Ogle County for our virtual Get Out the Early Vote  phone bank. We will be reaching out to local voters to ensure they know when, where, and how to cast their ballot early and share information regarding endorsed candidates Paul Nolley and Julianna Stratton.

Whether you’re a seasoned caller or phone banking for the first time, we’ll start with a brief training, walk through the script together, and support each other live on Zoom while we make calls.

## Before You Join: Required Tech & Setup
To ensure a smooth experience, please complete these two steps before the event begins:

Create an ActionID Account:

Our calling platform uses ActionID to secure your account and save your progress. If you don't already have one, please create an account ahead of time at VAN ActionID Login. - Directions will be sent upon sign up.

Prepare Two Devices:

For the best phone banking experience, you will need two separate devices:

Device 1 (Laptop, Tablet, or Computer): To log into Zoom for our team check-in, live support, and to view the call script/voter list.

Device 2 (Cell Phone): To make the phone calls.


## What to Expect
First 15–20 Mins: Welcome, ActionID check-in, and quick training on the script.

45–60 Mins: Live phone banking with the group (on mute in Zoom, but with chat/support available if you have questions).

Final 10 Mins: Quick wrap-up, debrief, and celebrating our impact!

# Every call counts. Sign up today and help us lock in the early vote!

events.title: Vote Tripling at Early Voting sites in DeKalb: Oct 13-Oct 30
events.description: One of the most impactful campaign activities can only be accomplished during Early Voting.  Vote Tripling (aka "Remind 3 Friends") is an proven way to both capture a voter's focus on voting AND convince them to triple their voting impact by reminding 3 friends (contacts in their phone) by texting them right away to VOTE.  Research shows that people are much more likely to vote if encouraged by a friend or family member than by a stranger.  In an election that is expected to be very close YOUR efforts could be the difference!  Sign up here and we'll connect with you to find a time and Early Voting location that suits your schedule!

events.title: Urgent Opposition to Livestreaming Nidal Hasan’s Execution – Write to Your Members of Congress NOW!
events.description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Dear Representative [Last Name],

I am writing as your constituent to express my profound objection to the Pentagon’s announced plan to livestream the execution by firing squad of Nidal Hasan, scheduled for December 3, 2026. This would be the first military execution in more than 60 years and the first public execution in the United States in nearly a century. I strongly urge you to publicly oppose this decision and to exercise congressional oversight to prevent the Department of Defense from turning a solemn act of military justice into a public spectacle.

I want to be clear: my objection is not rooted in sympathy for Hasan or in any doubt about the gravity of his crimes. He murdered 13 unarmed soldiers and wounded more than 30 others at Fort Hood in 2009, and he has never claimed innocence. The families of the victims and the survivors deserve justice and closure. But justice and spectacle are not the same thing, and the decision to livestream this execution is a profound mistake that will harm our nation’s moral standing, endanger our security, and undermine the very principles we claim to uphold.

The livestream would violate fundamental human rights standards.

The United Nations human rights office has warned that livestreaming an execution would amount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition on torture under international law. A UN spokesperson described the prospect of a government executing someone “in front of live cameras” as “abhorrent”. Amnesty International has condemned the plan as “reprehensible,” noting that international human rights bodies have long found public executions incompatible with the prohibition on cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment. The United States should not join the ranks of nations that carry out public executions; according to Amnesty International, only Iran and Afghanistan are known to have done so in 2025. This is not who we are—or who we should aspire to be.

The livestream would make us less safe, not more.

Senator Jack Reed, Ranking Member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, has warned that livestreaming the execution “only gives the shooter what he wants: more attention and more control” and that it is “a gift to anti-American terrorist recruiters”. Congressman Jason Crow, a former Army Ranger, has similarly stated that a public execution “only gives our adversaries fodder for anti-American propaganda that makes us less safe”. Hasan has said he acted to stop soldiers from deploying to Afghanistan; broadcasting his death to a global audience would hand extremists a powerful recruitment tool and validate their narrative that America is at war with Islam. The last thing our national security needs is a propaganda victory for those who wish us harm.

The livestream would degrade our military and our legal system.

Army Regulation 190-55 governs who may witness military executions and does not provide for unrestricted public attendance. There is no regulation or precedent for a military execution to be livestreamed, and experts have noted that public executions are typically held in authoritarian countries to instill fear and demonstrate government power. Republican Senator Thom Tillis has said that public executions are what “oppressive dictatorships do” and called the plan “beyond disgusting”. Democratic Senator Chris Murphy accused the Secretary of Defense of “mimicking ISIS”. When lawmakers from both parties use the same language to describe an American policy that they use for our enemies, something has gone deeply wrong.

The livestream would traumatize victims and survivors.

Alonzo Lunsford, a former Army sergeant who was shot seven times during the attack and who plans to attend the execution in person, has said he does not agree with making the event publicly available without censorship. The families of the fallen and the survivors deserve to mourn and to seek closure in a manner that respects their dignity, not to have their trauma broadcast to the world as entertainment. As Senator John Curtis has warned, a civilization “erodes when it cultivates an appetite for executions as a form of entertainment”.

What I am asking of you. I respectfully urge you to take the following actions:

1.	Publicly denounce the Pentagon’s plan to livestream Hasan’s execution and call on Secretary Hegseth to reverse the decision. Bipartisan voices—including Senators Reed, Tillis, Murkowski, and Curtis, and Representatives Crow and Smith—have already spoken out. Your voice would add needed weight.
2.	Exercise congressional oversight. The House and Senate Armed Services Committees should demand transparency regarding the legal authority for this livestream, the financial arrangements (including any potential monetization), and the consultation process that led to this decision. A letter from former national security officials has already raised serious questions about whether the execution could be used for “commercial gain or partisan political propaganda”. Congress must investigate.
3.	Support legislative or regulatory action to ensure that no future military execution is livestreamed or otherwise made available to the public for entertainment or political purposes. The default should be the solemn, limited-witness procedure prescribed by Army Regulation 190-55.

The death penalty itself is a matter of serious moral and legal debate, and I respect that Americans of good faith disagree on it. But whatever one’s position on capital punishment, livestreaming an execution is beyond the pale. It is cruel, it is dangerous, and it is beneath the dignity of the United States. Hasan’s crimes were horrific, but responding with a public spectacle does not honor his victims—it exploits them. It does not strengthen the rule of law—it makes a mockery of it. And it does not make us safer—it makes us a recruiting poster for our enemies.

I urge you to act swiftly and forcefully. Please let me know what steps you plan to take.

Respectfully,

[Your Name]
[Your Address]
[City, State, ZIP]
[Email Address]
[Phone Number]

events.title: Carrollton AREA Democrats - Nico Nights with Neighbors

location.venue: Nico's Cocina - Event Room (to right of restaurant)

events.description:
WELCOME to our once a month (third Wednesday) meeting of the Carrollton AREA Democrats Club.  Our focus is to get to know our Neighbors - to meet like-minded folks for fellowship, education, solidarity and purpose.  Learn how WE can shape our plans as we seek to SAVE OUR COUNTRY AND DEMOCRACY!  

For our October 21st Meeting, we will be hosting a Candidate Forum - as an opportunity to understand a little more about the core values of the folks we will be choosing to represent us in Federal, State, and County offices. Seeing their real personalities approaching real issues will assure confidence when we vote - and more importantly - when we tell others about our qualified candidates. 

Invited Guests:

* Steven Shook - US Congressional Representative 26 

* Candace Valenzuela - Denton County Commissioner PCT2

* Stephanie Draper Denton County Commissioner PCT 4

* Nick Papas - Denton County Judge

* Georgiana Bustos for Vikki Goodwin - Texas Lt Governor 

******************************************************************

* Michelle Butler - Denton Justice of the Peace PCT 6 (unconfirmed)

* Dale Frey - Denton County Clerk (unconfirmed)



And as a special treat - we will be experiencing the newly updated Event Room at Nico's Cocina. Totally updated walls, flooring, lighting, air conditioning. 

We are looking forward to presenting additional educational topics at future meetings for all of us to learn about, understand, and appreciate our commonality. 

Candidate literature & signs are welcome and space will be provided.

Carrollton Democrats supply of Talarico and Gina signs have been depleted,=.  However - the Candidates are welcome to bring their signs.

THE MEETING WILL BEGIN A LITTLE BEFORE 7PM, so please arrive around 6 or 6:30 to order food and beverages and mingle with candidates and your new friends. 

We are a Grass Roots Group dedicated to preserving our American way of Life that honors the Individual with Diversity, Equality and Dignity. Learn about ways you can participate in ACTIVISM.  Learn how you may participate in our HIVES (Precinct) project.  We are Creating FUN Caring Communities - and Winning Elections!  And we are building on our momentum from 2025 thanks to your growing enthusiasm! 

Let us help you find ways that you may use your skills, talents and strengths to participate in our fight to take back our country thru activism, demonstrations, precinct building, voter registration and much more.  

Our Goal is to be a source of Information to all Carrollton AREA Democrats so they may make informed and wise decisions at the voting booth. 

We now have a Web Site: https://www.carrolltondemocrats.com/. This will provide our Carrollton Democrats the resources they need whether they live in Denton or Dallas County.  

JOIN US every 3rd Wednesday of the Month:
Nico Nights with the Neighbors - Nico's Cocina (6:30 to 8:30). 

3065 N. Josey Lane, Carrollton, TX 75007

We meet in the EVENT ROOM to the right of the restaurant. Children are welcome (just keep and eye on them).  There is an outside playground - and there will be a kids craft table near the play ground door.

Please sign up on Mobilize so we may prepare enough materials for everyone. 

If you wish to be placed on our email list, (only 3-4 a month) please SIGN UP on CarrolltonDemocrats.com.  And we'll be able to introduce you to your neighbors in your precinct.   

Again - we are happy you have found us - look forward to meeting you!

events.title: Carrollton AREA Democrats - ELECTION WATCH PARTY -  Wingtown & Grill
events.description:
We've put in the hard work. We've phone banked, block walked, texted, written postcards and letters, stuck signs in the ground, attended so many events and meetings, talked to so many people, donated money, raised money, spent many hours burning the midnight oil. 

On Tuesday, November 3rd at 7PM - all that hard work will pay off.  We want to share the moment when everything becomes real. Did we do enough? We hope so. And now we want to share that moment with those who understand the work that has gone into this year's efforts. 

AND BE THE FIRST TO CONGRATULATE OUR 🏆 WINNERS!

events.title: Indivisible Boca Raton presents “Immigration at a Crossroads”
events.description:
Immigration detentions by ICE and local law enforcement is surging in the country, South Florida, and in Palm Beach County. Family separation is rampant, detention centers are overcrowded and ripe with serious human rights abuses. People are dying from ICE shootings and in ICE custody.

The data shows that the overwhelming majority of the immigrants being detained are hard-working, family oriented, and net contributors to our community. They are our neighbors, not criminals.

This immigration enforcement regime can only exist by taking away people’s constitutional rights and by covering up their immigration operations from public view. On Monday, November 16, 6:00- 7:30 PM, at the Dr. Andre Fladell Civic Center, 16700 Jog Rd., Delray Beach, FL 33446 come hear the experts.
Moderator: Barbara Eriv, Indivisible Immigration Coalition (PBCIIC).
The current immigration policy landscape and possible policy change opportunities from the 2026 midterms and into the 2027 municipal election-Renata Bozzetto, Deputy Director at the Florida Immigrant Coalition
A profile of the immigrants in our community and the effects from family separation: Ruth Rosa MACP, Post-Release Services Clinician at Urban Strategies.
The legal and constitutional rules of the current administration and impacts on detainees and families-Jennifer Smith, Senior Litigation Attorney at Americans for Immigration Justice.
The longer term consequences to our community and economy-Philip Lewin, Associate Professor of Sociology, Director of Graduate Studies at the Florida Atlantic University (FAU)

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Public Hearing: Tell IDEM Not to Rubber-Stamp Amazon Jasper County Data Center's Dirty Diesel Permit
events.description:
The Indiana Department of Environmental Management (IDEM) has published a draft air permit for Amazon’s Project Orion AI data center, a sprawling 13-building complex under development in Wheatfield that would allow about 384 polluting backup diesel generators — millions of gallons of fuel — near homes and right next to the Schahfer coal and gas plants and the Kankakee River watershed, which will be impacted by tens of millions of gallons of discharge and intake daily from the cumulative impact of these facilities. 

Amazon's own filings show the data center would release thousands of tons of smog-forming air pollution and carbon monoxide each year without strict controls, impacting Jasper County residents, farm families, and downwind neighbors. 

Jasper County deserves clean air now! Join the virtual public hearing on November 10th to tell IDEM to protect our communities and airways from Amazon’s dirty diesel generators permit. 

*The hearing begins at 6:00 PM CT and will conclude as soon as public comments are done, or no later than 9:00 PM CT.

Please sign and share our petition to send a quick comment on the permit: www.jtnwi.org/no-dirty-diesel-amazon.

And use our toolkit to develop your comments and learn more about the permit: www.jtnwi.org/amazon-hearing-toolkit.

events.description:
This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor, and remember the lives taken by ICE, and Border Patrol. As we demand an end to the violence, and an end to the ICE Age.

We'll gather, and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody, and have been killed by ICE, and Border Patrol agents. Drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country, through October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: The "No Matter What" Post Election Party
events.description:
## We deserve to celebrate - **NO MATTER WHAT!**

**No matter what** will be the result of this Midterms, **NE Lake County Indivisible chooses to come together in celebration.** Whether all our wishes come true, our worst fears are realized, or something else entirely unexpected happens, we will want to be back in community and in gratitude for all our hard-working volunteers and partners. 

## Join us on **Thursday 11/12** at the **Waukegan Public Library** as we hold a **"No Matter What" Post Election Party!** 

We do not yet know whether we will feel in need of joy or consolation, but we DO know we want to be together with the neighbors, partners, and friends we have worked alongside during the Midterms season.

The agenda for this event is sure to feature some light refreshments, gratitude, and good company. **So mark your calendars and join us** as we choose to come together and celebrate… *”NO MATTER WHAT!”*


~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

### ABOUT NE LAKE COUNTY INDIVISIBLE:
NE Lake County IL Indivisible is a nonpartisan grassroots organization founded in 2025 in defense of democracy. We are Lake County residents working together to protect elections and neighbors. We aim to support targeted populations and take action on a local and national level to push back against authoritarianism. We welcome everyone, whether you voted this way or that way, or didn't vote at all in 2024.

**More about us can be found here:**
https://nelakecounty-indivisible.org
https://linktr.ee/nelakecountyindivisible

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

**Some quotes from past participants:**

* "It was great working with like minded people who care so much about what's going on in our country. We want and are working for change that helps all Americans"

* "It was fun working with people who share your feelings about what's happening in our country and overseas. I find it inspiring and it gives me hope."

* "great turnout, super well organized. welcoming and fun."

* "Well organized. Liked the materials included in the kits. Good location. Nice people. Thank you very much!"

* "I took action for NE Lake County IL Indivisible because last time we put together whistle kits, I was impressed by how organized the work was, how professional, encouraging and friendly the leaders were. It was the same this time. The leaders told us about other opportunities with the organization. They sat and chatted with the groups at each of the tables. The volunteers were all friendly. I felt able to speak freely. We didn't speak of frustrations. We talked of opportunity for helping others."

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

These efforts cost money to put together! If you are able to financially support us, please consider making a donation here: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/indivisiblenelc1350105033

events.title: Community Screening + Discussion of "No Country for Mothers"

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
For too long, mothers have been divided through cultural wars that work to disconnect us from our collective power: but it’s time that we change that.

Join us for a community screening of the documentary "No Country for Mothers" on November 14 from 1:30-5pm.

RSVP HERE: https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/this-is-how-we-care/community-screening-of-no-country-for-mothers

*Only valid tickets purchased through TicketLeap will be admitted to this event.* 

"No Country For Mothers" is a documentary film made by the nonprofit organization MomsFirstUS, and it’s intentionally being shown through community screenings only — because we need to watch this together.

Not only will we watch this documentary in community (vs on our couches alone), we will have time to connect and debrief afterwards.

This is not simply a "screening": this is a gathering of mothers and their allies, where the film informs our conversations and connections afterward; where relationships form that can create real change.

This is the power of coming together: not only can we share and be witnessed in our own experience, but we can do something with whatever this film stirs within us.

Bring a friend or come solo and meet some friends there. We can't wait to have you with us. 

———

Tickets for this event are subsidized with the thanks to our sponsors: This is How We Care, Karon Dickonson Real Estate, Cycle Sanctuary, Fig Tree Pediatrics, Hope For Tomorrow Counseling , and Real Food Roots .

We need volunteers to help protect and support our vulnerable friends and neighbors, particularly at food distribution locations where safety is a growing concern. The location is just north of Gresham.
Our goal is to serve as extra eyes and ears in the community, monitoring for Migra/ICE activity and promptly notifying organizers of any reported or observed presence.

Volunteers will be stationed at designated access points and equipped with two-way radios and whistles to communicate potential threats and alert organizers and attendees when necessary. Our role is to observe, report, and help maintain a safe and welcoming environment for everyone.
If a volunteer shift is marked as full but you are still able to attend, please join the wait list! This will help ensure we have backups in the event of a last minute cancellation.
Before signing up for a shift, volunteers are encouraged to attend an [Upcoming ICE Watch & Community Defense training](https://statesatthecore.substack.com/p/community-defense-and-ice-watch), or a similar[Ice Watch Training](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1gie3cVfoILY6lRGLVIeWLcN06mme8ai4DgUzPrMKWYA/edit?usp=sharing). events.title: After the Midterms -- Now What? with Professor Sam Wang
events.description:
We don't yet know the outcomes of the 2026 midterm elections, but there's no doubt we'll need to regroup, reset our priorities, and -- hopefully! -- celebrate. Happily, there's no one better to strategize with than Professor Sam Wang. Many of us were impressed with Dr. Wang when he ran for US Congress in NJ's 12th district, and we are thrilled to have the opportunity to hear from him again. He'll address the fallout from the election, how to think about the impacts both short- and long-term, and what this means for our local activism. Please join us for this lively and thought-provoking discussion!

**About Sam Wang**

Sam Wang is a professor of neuroscience at Princeton University and a pioneer in the fight for our democracy and against gerrymandering. He has authored books on how the brain functions, and he worked on science and education policy in the US Senate. In 2026, he ran for the US Congress in New Jersey's 12th Congressional District, and while he didn't win in the primary election, for many of us, he won our highest regard. 

Sam is now continuing the campaign in the form of Third Mountain Action, an organization to save and rebuild democracy and science.

It's more fun with more people, so share this with friends and sign up for as many shifts throughout the day as you'd like. 

Responsibilities are minimal and this is typically an exciting and energizing event. We have signs you can hold. And we also have chairs in the shade if you just want to join us for a bit. There is always a collection of Halloween candy and other goodies to keep us going. 

Committee members, if you are able, please commit to at least an hour, or join us for set up or clean up. Do you lean blue, but you're not a member?  You are very welcome to join us. We would love your help!  

Set up will begin at 6:45 and should only take about 15 minutes.

Clean up begins near the end of the 7:00 pm shift. There is no separate shift for clean up. If you can't help with clean up, you can still sign up for that shift. Signing up for that shift does not require you to clean up.

events.title: Final Weekend GOTV Volunteer Blitz
events.description:
Final Weekend GOTV Volunteer Blitz

Saturday, Oct. 31 through Election Day, Tuesday, Nov. 3 | 10 AM-6 PM | 75 Queensway Drive

This is it. Four days remain, and every conversation we have between now and 6 PM on Tuesday could be the one that gets a neighbor to the polls.

We’re opening HQ for a final weekend GOTV volunteer blitz, and we need you. Using updated voter data from the election board, we’ll be reaching out to voters who haven’t cast a ballot yet. They need a friendly reminder, a plan to vote, and a little encouragement, and that’s where you come in.

What you’ll do

Phone bank from HQ, calling voters who haven’t voted yet
Canvass by knocking on doors in your neighborhood or nearby areas
Help people find their polling place, confirm their hours, and make a plan to vote

How it works

Shifts are 2 hours long, running from 10 AM to 6 PM each day: 10-12, 12-2, 2-4, and 4-6
Sign up for one shift or several. The more the better!
No experience needed. We’ll train you when you arrive and give you everything you need: scripts, walk lists, and a team to work with.

Dates

Saturday, Oct. 31
Sunday, Nov. 1
Monday, Nov. 2
Tuesday, Nov. 3 (Election Day, until polls close at 6 PM)

events.title: It's Our Turn to Run: 2026 Midterm Results Roundup
events.description:
Join us on November 19 at 8pm ET for an exclusive Midterm Results Roundup Event as we analyze the results of this election cycle and discuss how young leaders can run for office in 2027 and 2028 featuring RFS Co-Founder Amanda Litman!

We’ll share actionable ways you can start a campaign and provide an overview of available seats open for you to run for in the near future.

Attendees will also hear from a Run for Something candidate who just won their election this November.

Crucially, this event is all about building the next wave of leaders! You'll hear directly from Run for Something leaders and former candidates about:

- Key results and takeaways from the 2026 midterm elections

- Opportunities and available seats to run for in 2027 and 2028

- Actionable steps you can take to explore running for local or state office

- Exciting new tools and resources coming from ActBlue to support future candidates

- First-hand experiences from a featured RFS alum who won their election this November

Whether you're just beginning to consider running for office or already taking steps toward a campaign, you'll leave with a better understanding of what's ahead and how to get involved.

Run for Something recruits and supports Millennial and GenZ progressive candidates (born 1981 or later) running for local and state office. If you don't meet our endorsement criteria, you're still welcome to join the call to learn more about running for office and available resources.

Email us at campaigns@runforsomething.net with any questions. We hope to see you there!

Have accessibility requests or questions? Reply to your registration email to share them with us.

events.title: Virtual Community Support Circle for Activists and Allies · Indivisible Turning the Tables
events.description:
In the face of the current regime’s devastating actions, it is normal that we are all experiencing grief, outrage and overwhelm. As witnesses and advocates, we are likely to be experiencing collective trauma.

In response to these recent events, we are offering a dedicated online support space for local community activists. This will be a safe space to process any grief & loss that’s coming up, as well as a space to learn about vicarious trauma and compassion fatigue.

Facilitated by Michelle Ward, a trauma-informed therapist, this time together will be one for grounding, mutual support and healthy coping skills building. 

Please join us for a timely and important opportunity to receive support through your grief and loss, toward healing and strength in community with one another.

events.title: Get Corporate Money Out of Our Elections

location.venue: Unitarian Universalist Fellowship of Redwood City

events.description:
Since Citizens United in 2010, campaign finance laws allow corporations to significantly influence elections. California legislation (AB1984) introduced this year aims to reduce the impact of corporate dollars.

Join us in Redwood City for an engaging panel discussion and Q&A. We'll gather in-person to for a live webinar with political strategist Christopher Armitage, Tom Moore of the Center for American Progress, and Democratic California Assemblymember Chris Rogers. We'll explore how to use state power when the federal government is unreliable. 

After the webcast, stay for networking and more discussion with fellow activists about important actions we need to take post-midterm elections. If you are unable to attend in-person, a link will be provided for the webcast portion.

This event is co-sponsored by Indivisible Mid-Peninsula and Indivisible Portola Valley.

events.title: Duluth Indivisible Monthly Meeting (Zoom version): Gender and Authoritarianism
events.description:
For our November monthly meeting, Duluth Indivisible has asked Megan Peterson and Erin Maye Quade, the Executive Director and Senior Advisor, respectively, of [Gender Justice](https://www.genderjustice.us/) to present on "Gender and Authoritarianism". Because we are meeting in person and they are presenting on Zoom, we've decided to offer the Zoom version throughout MN08. Hence this Zoom version of the event. People who register will get the Zoom link a few hours before the event. 

Authoritarians regularly use gender as a wedge issue to create fear, divide people, and reinforce traditional hierarchies and patriarchy. The Trump regime is following this playbook on many fronts: trans youth participation in sports, Hegseth's attacks on diversity in the military, the SAVE Act to disenfranchise women voters, blocking health care for trans youth, and on and on. Gender Justice's presentation will outline these issues in a potent and coherent way and better equip us to protect the rights of ALL people to live fully and freely with respect to gender. 

We will still meet in person in Duluth for a potluck at 5:00 PM, with the presentation at 6:00, followed by discussion and planning on how gender advocacy might fit into our 2027 planning. To sign up for the **in-person session**, please do so through this Mobilize link: [Gender and Authoritarianism: In Person](https://www.mobilize.us/duluthindivisible/event/1040294/)

Please spread the word.

events.title: Love as Action: San Francisco
events.description:
# Love as Action: Resisting Authoritarianism

### Quaker public witness has stood in opposition to cruel and authoritarian actions in our country before. It is time for us to show this love in action again. 

Please join the American Friends Service Committee and San Francisco Friends Meeting to bear witness to the authoritarian actions of ICE in our country. 

On Monday November 2 from 4 to 9, we will gather at the Festival of Altars in Potrero del Sol Park to honor those we've lost due to ICE's harmful, callous tactics. The altar we are building is intended to help us know their names, remember them, honor them, and ensure they know their deaths were not in vain. Please contact the organizers to sign up for a one-hour slot with the altar during the 4 to 9 time window.

Our hope is that our presence will give hope to all who see us – to show that we can choose resistance - and remind everyone of our moral obligations to one another.

We gather in communities across the country, showing love in action as a public witness of our Quaker values in a time of rising fascism.

Join us! 

To find our more about Love as Action nationally and get more resources visit us at [afsc.org/love-action](www.afsc.org/love-action)

📅 When: Thursday, Nov 5, 6:00 PM - 8:00 PM

Join us for a Marshal Training to learn how to keep marches and protests safe. Whether you’re brand new or just want to brush up on your skills, this session will cover both and is open to anyone ready to learn and support actions in any role.

On November 7, the Saturday after the elections, many thousands of New Yorkers will mobilize for a national day of action - a mass protest against President Trump's abuses of power and federal attack on our elections. Together, we'll send a clear message: we are fighting for our democracy! 

📣 This training will be interactive and discussion-based. You’ll leave with real tactics, scripts, and tools you can use right away. ### Speak with Sunrise Orlando during Public Comment @ Orange County Board of County Commissioners Meeting! 🌅

Join us for the Orange County Board of County Commissioners' weekly Public Comment to learn and discuss the decisions being made in our county, connect with the community, and advocate for a more affordable, walkable, and sustainable Orlando.

**What is Public Comment?**

Public Comment refers to the period scheduled during the beginning of the morning session of the Board of County Commissioners’ meeting. It is time set aside at each BCC meeting for members of the public to speak on general topics of interest or concern within the BCC’s authority.

**What does Public Comment with Sunrise Orlando look like?**

When participating in public comment with us, you can expect to:

- Meet up with Sunrise Orlando members and community supporters.
- Attend the public meeting together in the morning.

- Participate in public comment if appropriate and available.

- Learn how local decisions affect our communities and how we can take action.

You don't need to be a Sunrise Orlando member or a policy expert to join us! Whether it's your first public meeting or you're one of our regulars, we'll be there to help you with talking points, information, and encouragement!

events.title: Big Tech, Bigger Questions: How Illinois Can Regulate AI
events.description:
As Big Tech expands its reach, Illinois needs stronger protections for consumers, communities, and utility customers.

Join Citizen Action/Illinois on November 5 at noon to learn about two bills we're supporting during Veto Session. We'll hear from the Illinois Environmental Council, UFCW Local 881, and AFSCME Council 31. 

The POWER Act (SB 4016/HB 5513) would protect communities and utility customers from the growing energy and water demands of data centers.

Surveillance pricing legislation (HB 4248/SB 2255) would protect consumers from companies using personal data to set individualized prices for goods and services.

Finally, HB 4980 (Human Control of AI Act) would help ensure that humans remain accountable for decisions made using artificial intelligence.

Hear from coalition leaders about what's at stake for Illinois residents and how you can help advance these protections.

events.title: Fight the (F)right: Phone Bank with SURJ to Haunt the House and Senate!
events.description:
## **Fight the (F)right and haunt the House (and Senate) with SURJ in the final days before the midterm election!**

We'll have exclusive SURJ merch giveaways, special guests, games, and more as you work with us to call white voters in strategic races across the country where we're working to flip the House and Senate left. 

Come as you are to any shifts - no experience needed! Each phone bank includes full training & lots of support as you go. _No tricks, only treats and wins here!_

## Fight the (F)right - Full Schedule:

- **10/31 - Halloween Costume Contest:** come dressed as something that would scare MAGA (or just your best costume). Prizes await those whose costumes go above and beyond!
- **11/1 - Dial-a-thon:** Join us for special guests, Phone Bank Bingo, prizes galore, and more while we dial all day! Special SURJ merch pack given to those who join all shifts. 
- **11/2 - Michigan's a Winner:** We're calling in to Michigan to kick MAGA to the curb in the mitten state. MI movement candidates will join us as we move Michigan left!
- **11/3 - Election Day Finale:** Bingo! Punch Cards! Prizes! It's all happening on election day while we secure the final votes for our movement-aligned candidates and block MAGA from gaining any more ground. 



**Join SURJ in doing our part to help flip the House and Senate and block MAGA while sending a crop of true movement champions to Congress.**

**For a full list of the candidates we're supporting, visit https://surj.org/2026-election/**
      
***

## Logistics:

-   These phone banks are online on the Zoom platform. Log into the call on Zoom on your computer and bring your phone to make the calls (if you only have one device, still come!).
-   We have a robust training on the call to give you all the information you need -- a script, technical support, and coaching throughout.
-   Returners can start early.
-   You will receive an email with orientation materials ahead of time.
-   ***Please note the time zone for call time.***
    
***

## Feeling Unsure?

-   **Our model works** - learn from the best! Our phonebanks have one of the highest rates of success in the country. No matter whether you're brand new caller or a seasoned organizer, if you join our banks, you can trust that you are putting your effort into a method that works. And you'll get to learn powerful organizing skills from seasoned leaders!
-   Our conversations are based on **open-ended questions** and **deep listening.  You do not need to be an expert** on the issues or a candidate - our phone banks are successful because we deeply connect with voters and make them feel heard.
-   Want to hear what a phonebank is like? Check out [this video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U3w4tNKPTY8) interviewing SURJ phonebankers.
    
***

## About SURJ:

[Showing Up for Racial Justice](https://surj.org/) (SURJ) is the largest organization in the country that explicitly organizes white communities for justice. Instead of choosing racism, silence, or complicity, we help white communities choose justice. We have thousands of national members and dozens of chapters across the US and Canada.

events.description: What a year it's been for sex education! So don’t wait — register today. We can make 2027 the year sex ed fights back and wins, if we all get in formation together now.

events.title: Lifeline DC 2027: Walk For Lives
events.description:
On Saturday, September 11, 2027, we walk together in Washington, D.C.

Walk for Lives D.C. is the closing day of Lifeline DC, three days in the nation’s capital following Hill Day and the Synthetic Drug Summit. It brings the families, survivors, and advocates who walked in their own cities and towns in May to the National Mall, side by side, in one place.

We walk for the sons and daughters, brothers and sisters, parents and friends we have lost to fentanyl. We walk for the families still in the fight, and for the young people we can still protect. Every step says the same thing to the country: these lives mattered, and this crisis demands a response.

We walk on a date this nation already holds for remembrance. We carry that spirit with us, honoring every life that should still be here.

What to expect

A morning program with family speakers and a moment of silence
A gentle, accessible walk of about one mile, open to all ages and abilities
A Community Resource Village with treatment, recovery, and public health organizations
Time to connect with families who understand

Bring a sign. Carry the name or photo of someone you love, or a message you want Washington to see.

Schedule [CONFIRM]

8:30 AM: Check-in opens
9:00 AM: Opening program
10:30 AM: Walk steps off
11:00 AM to 12:30 PM: Community Resource Village

Location [CONFIRM]
Floral Library Gardens, Tidal Basin, National Mall, Washington, D.C.
Nearest Metro: Smithsonian (Blue, Orange, Silver lines)

Walk for Lives D.C. is free and open to everyone. Please register so we can plan for you, and share this event with someone who should be walking beside you.

Can’t be in D.C.? Walk for Lives returns to cities and towns across America on Saturday, May 15, 2027.

About United Against Fentanyl
United Against Fentanyl is a nonpartisan, nonprofit organization that interrupts the use of illicit fentanyl through innovative, bold, and effective initiatives.

Questions? info@unitedagainstfentanyl.org

events.description:
**Thursday, September 9, 2027 · U.S. Capitol, Washington, D.C.**

On Hill Day, families from every state go to Capitol Hill together and meet with their own senators and representatives. They carry the names and photos of the people they lost to fentanyl into the offices of the lawmakers with the power to act.

You do not need any experience to take part. Each state's delegation is led by a State Captain, who sets up the meetings and makes sure no one walks into an office alone.

**What to expect**

- A morning welcome and briefing with the United Against Fentanyl team
- Meetings with your senators and your representative, alongside other families from your state
- A clear, simple ask to share in every meeting, provided in advance
- Afternoon and evening program: TBD

**Before Hill Day**

- RSVP here so we can place you with your state's delegation.
- Your State Captain will contact you before September 9 with your meeting schedule.
- Open the Lifeline DC app for your schedule, maps, and Hill Day details: lifelinedc.org

**Details**

- Start time and meeting point: TBD
- What to wear: TBD
- Hotel block: TBD
- Accessibility: TBD. Please tell us what you need when you RSVP, and we will plan around it.

**Want to lead your state?** Become a State Captain: TBD

**Can't make the trip?** Write a Dear Washington letter and your State Captain will carry it into the meetings for you: act.unitedagainstfentanyl.org/DearWashington

Hill Day is part of **Lifeline DC**, three days in Washington, September 9 to 11, 2027: Hill Day on Thursday, the Summit on Synthetic Drugs on Friday, and Walk for Lives D.C. on Saturday.

WILL CALL OR TEXT YOU FROM 252.619.6078 to discuss scheduling a shift at your preferred location.
WHAT'S A POLL GREETER?
Poll greeters are the volunteers outside voting locations, who offer the Dem Sample Ballot to voters. How does this effort make a difference?  Unlike the top of the ticket (U.S. Senator, U.S. Congress), where the party for each candidate is marked clearly on the ballot, local candidates for City Council and School Board are NOT labeled by party. The Dem Sample Ballot clearly indicates the candidates who are endorsed by the Democratic Party.  That is how Poll Greeters make a difference - they help get ALL Dem candidates elected! The Sample Ballot also supports voting YES on the 3 Virginia Constitutional Amendments.

events.title: Michigan Get Out the Vote Election Day Phone Bank
events.description:
Michigan Election Day Phone Bank

Tuesday, November 3 (Election Day) at 3pm Eastern Time / 12pm Pacific Time

Join us on Election Day as we call MI-07 voters to make sure they cast their ballot before polls close at 8pm.

We’re reaching voters across Michigan’s 7th District, home to Lansing and one of the most competitive House races in the country. Michigan voters are also deciding an open U.S. Senate seat and an open governor’s race. These are high-stakes elections, and turnout will decide the outcome. Today, we’re making sure no voter is left behind.

Early voting has ended, so Election Day is the last chance to vote. We’ll help voters with absentee ballots get them in on time: it’s too late to mail them, but they can be dropped off at a ballot drop box or their local clerk’s office by 8pm. We’ll help everyone else get to their polling place. Voters who aren’t registered can still register and vote at their local clerk’s office until 8pm. We’ll also send follow-up texts with polling locations, drop box information, and the Election Protection Hotline.

Volunteers will have real conversations with voters and help turn intention into action, making sure ballots are cast and votes are counted.

📞 Election Day phone bank: Tuesday, November 3 at 12 p.m. PT / 3 p.m. ET

🔥 No experience needed. Training, scripts, and support provided.

This is how we win close races: by making sure every vote counts. Your call could be the reason someone follows through. Sign up now and help power turnout in Michigan on Election Day!

events.title: Tending Environmental Grief: Part Two
events.description:
We are living in an era of significant environmental change and loss. In recognizing that these times are challenging to live in, adapt to, and cope with, it’s essential that we come together as a community to process our experiences. Supporting ourselves and one another is just as important as stewarding the land and waters. 

Join Sky Island Alliance and [Maria Renée](https://www.maria-renee.com/) on Thursday, Dec. 10, at 9:30 a.m. for a dedicated time to understand the terrain of environmental grief, work through emotions, celebrate this beautiful region, and practice building resilience together. This free webinar is the second in a series of opportunities to contribute your creative responses to a changing region, whether they come from grief, hope, or anything in between. Participants will have a chance to share their reflections and experiences in response to a series of prompts this fall.

_See [Tending Environmental Grief: Part One](https://skyislandalliance.org/2026/10/tending-to-environmental-grief/) >>>_

events.title: Election Day Volunteer Poll Greeters in North Suffolk
events.description:
The Suffolk Democratic Committee is working to fill Suffolk's 30 voting locations with Poll Greeters on Tuesday, Nov. 3. We need "all hands on deck" to ensure Dem candidates are elected in this important mid-term race.  Shifts (3 or 4 hours) are available throughout North Suffolk. Sign up and BOROUGH CAPTAIN ROBIN H. WILL CALL OR TEXT YOU FROM 252.619.6078 to discuss scheduling a shift at your preferred location.
WHAT'S A POLL GREETER?
Poll greeters are the volunteers outside voting locations, who offer the Dem Sample Ballot to voters. How does this effort make a difference?  Unlike the top of the ticket (U.S. Senator, U.S. Congress), where the party for each candidate is marked clearly on the ballot, local candidates for City Council and School Board are NOT labeled by party. The Dem Sample Ballot clearly indicates the candidates who are endorsed by the Democratic Party.  That is how Poll Greeters make a difference - they help get ALL Dem candidates elected! The Sample Ballot also supports voting YES on the 3 Virginia Constitutional Amendments.

events.title: Banned Book Club - December's Title TBD
events.description:
Join us each month for a new book from our ever growing banned or challenged book list. Where we choose a new title each month and combine reading out loud in a group setting, reading alone, and discussing how the books might correspond to the world around us.

Please make sure to add any suggestions to the Google spreadsheet shared in the Zoom chat before the third week of the month to have a chance at it being selected for the next month. The event name will be updated once the title is selected.

The meetings are 90 minutes long and broke down into 3 parts. The first half hour is spent discussing the section that was designed or our anticipations on what the book might be like. The middle section we read out loud, and the last half hour is spent going over what we read and assigning the next section.

So far we have read the following titles and discussed how they correlate with our present day. 

• The Diary of a Yong Girl - Anne Frank 
• 1984 - George Orwell 
• Animal Farm - George Orwell 
• Fahrenheit 451 – Ray Bradbury 
• Looking Backward – Edward Bellamy 
• The Age of Reason - Thomas Paine 
• Howl and Other Poems - Allen Ginsberg
• Civil Disobedience - Henry David Thoreau
• To Kill A Mocking Bird - Harper Lee

All are welcome and even if you haven’t picked up the book feel free to join us for the discussion and reading.

events.title: Beacon Shine the Light Thursdays Great Neck
events.description:
Join The Beacon for Thursday Shine the Light, as we bring our voices to the street every Thursday from 12:00-12:30 PM.  (NOTE NEW EARLIER TIME!)

Each week, we make our voices heard wherever we are. As beacons, we shine light by making a sign and bringing it outside. Don't have a sign? Don't worry! You can borrow one of ours.

Together, we are building visible resistance and organized compassion, meeting our neighbors, and joining together in acts of solidarity. We find joy in resistance through community, music, comedy and street theater.

Across the country, communities are organizing to disentangle local law enforcement from federal immigration enforcement. Here in Nassau County, families continue to live in terror of separation, detainment, detention and deportation.

We stand weekly in opposition to this unprecedented assault on the rights, safety, and economic security of people in this country. For 30 minutes every Thursday, we say ICE OUT OF OUR COMMUNITIES! ICE OUT FOR GOOD! and we stand in favor of compassionate democracy and against cruelty, fear and despair.

People that come together in solidarity and say NO to ICE are a critical bulwark against mass deportations and the erosion of civil rights. There is much that we can do locally. And there is much that our elected officials can do — if we demand courage and leadership. Join us!

There are Beacon groups all over the USA. Our local Great Neck group meets every Thursday from 6:00-6:30 pm. We are joined by the Singing Resistance Great Neck to sing songs of solidarity and resistance, old and new.

For more information on The Beacon, visit www.beaconfordemocracy.org

A core principle behind all ICE Out For Good events is a commitment to nonviolent action and no civil disobedience. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values, and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events. All events should be held in public spaces or on public property.

Each week, we make our voices heard wherever we are. As beacons, we shine light by making a sign and bringing it outside. Don't have a sign? Don't worry! You can borrow one of ours.

Together, we are building visible resistance and organized compassion, meeting our neighbors, and joining together in acts of solidarity. We find joy in resistance through community, music, comedy and street theater.

Across the country, communities are organizing to disentangle local law enforcement from federal immigration enforcement. Here in Nassau County, families continue to live in terror of separation, detainment, detention and deportation.

We stand weekly in opposition to this unprecedented assault on the rights, safety, and economic security of people in this country. For 30 minutes every Thursday, we say ICE OUT OF OUR COMMUNITIES! ICE OUT FOR GOOD! and we stand in favor of compassionate democracy and against cruelty, fear and despair.

People that come together in solidarity and say NO to ICE are a critical bulwark against mass deportations and the erosion of civil rights. There is much that we can do locally. And there is much that our elected officials can do — if we demand courage and leadership. Join us!

There are Beacon groups all over the USA. Our local Great Neck group meets every Thursday from 6:00-6:30 pm. We are joined by the Singing Resistance Great Neck to sing songs of solidarity and resistance, old and new.

For more information on The Beacon, visit www.beaconfordemocracy.org

A core principle behind all ICE Out For Good events is a commitment to nonviolent action and no civil disobedience. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values, and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events. All events should be held in public spaces or on public property.

National partners include Detention Watch Network, NDLON, Maremoto, Public Citizen, the Workers Circle, Popular Democracy, AFSC and more.

events.description:
Want to support organizers across NYC to run powerful art builds? Looking for a creative way to get involved with social movement work? Want to learn more about Many Hands Workshop?

Come to our November co-host training at our space in Chelsea! 

Our co-host training is Many Hands Workshop 101 - a place to build our faciliation skills, get familiar with the workshop, and dig in deep together about why art is essential to beating fascism. 

Together we'll...

- Level up our art facilitator skills 

- Learn how to welcome new people into Many Hands Workshop and plug them into art builds and organizing

- Practice teaching skills like stenciling, heat press, and painting banners and signs

- Talk about the role of community-based art making in fighting fascism

- Go over some of the basic FAQs of the workshop, like “Where is the bathroom?” and “How do I clean my paint brush?”

If you’ve ever come to an art build at Many Hands Workshop and wanted to get more involved, becoming a co-host is one of the best ways to do that. After the training, you will be invited to use your co-hosting skills at one of our upcoming public art builds.

Even if you’ve volunteered to be a co-host at a past art build, we still encourage you to go through the Co-Host Training. This training will be slightly different from the host orientations that happen before art builds. The MHW core team is working on building a standardized baseline of things every co-host should know. This co-host training is where we’ll go over that baseline information and all get synced up!

📅 Dates: Thursday, October 22 · Thursday, October 29 · Thursday, November 5, 2026 
⏰ Time: 6pm-7pm MST
📍 Location: Zoom (link sent after you sign up)

🔥 We are ramping up to DEFEND DEMOCRACY and we need YOU! 🔥

We've spent the last two years building power across rural Arizona. We've trained volunteers in organizing skills, registered voters, knocked doors, and shown up for our communities. Now it's time to answer the call! Sign up once and you're in for all three of our Democracy Defense Mass Calls.

Why This Work Matters: Our vote is our voice, and no one gets to take it from us. Every eligible voter deserves to cast their ballot, and every valid ballot deserves to be counted. The fight doesn't end when the polls close. It goes all the way through certification, and we're going to be there every step of the way! When our communities show up together, organized and ready, we WIN. 💪

What's Involved: Three calls. One team. Everyone ready.
🗣️ Call 1, "Meeting the Moment" (Oct 22): Kick things off with Election Protection volunteers and Democracy Defense Teams from Cochise, Pinal, and Yuma. Learn the plan and claim your spot on your county team!
🛡️ Call 2, "De-escalation + Scenarios" (Oct 29): Get trained and ready for anything. Walk through real Election Day situations, learn exactly what your role is, and find out how our Response Team activates Democracy Defense Teams when it counts.
🏛️ Call 3, "After-Election Plan" (Nov 5): Come together after the election, then get ready to PACK THE ROOM at Board of Supervisors meetings and demand they certify the results, as is their duty to us, their constituents!

Missed a call? No problem! Sign up anyway and we'll send you the recording so you can jump right in. 🙌

Faith leaders, nonprofit leaders, club presidents: bring your people! This is a moment for all of us.

✨This is nonpartisan, lawful, and peaceful work. Every eligible voter. Every valid ballot. Every county certifies.

events.title: Mid-Week Student Volunteer Phone Banking and Canvassing (PAID)
events.description:
Join the **Central Mississippi Central Labor Council** to help reach voters! We are looking for paid workers and union volunteers to dedicate a few hours to crucial phone banking and door-to-door canvassing efforts. 

**Canvassing Priority:** ***Our primary focus is door-to-door canvassing at this time.***

**Phone Banking Limit: **Phone banking is strictly limited to the first 7 volunteers on a first-come, first-served basis.

**TRAINING REQUIREMENTS**

**- Mandatory Training:** You must complete training before working your first shift.
**- Canvassing Training:** Must be completed in person.

**SHIFTS, HOURS & PAY INCENTIVES**

- **Door-to-Door Canvassing: 10:00 AM – 5:30 PM.** Conducted in pairs (we will match you if needed).
- **Canvassing Incentive:** Come to the CWA Hall/MS AFL-CIO building (760 N West St, Ste B) to canvass. Pay is $15/hour, and drivers receive a $40 gas gift card!
- **Phone Banking: 10:00 AM – 7:00 PM **(strict cutoff). Canvassers may switch to phone banking after 5:30 PM to get extra hours.

**TIME TRACKING & ACCOUNTABILITY**

**- Software Tracking:** You will receive unique logins that track your activity. System inactivity may affect pay eligibility.
**- Campus Volunteers:** You must text 769-208-3581 exactly when you start and stop phone banking (e.g., "starting phone banking" / "stopping phone banking").
**- Timesheets: **Keep a personal log of your hours. Documented time will be checked against software reports; failure to document your time properly may cause payroll issues. 
**- Tech Support:** Contact Joshua immediately if you experience any software or login issues.

**PAY DISTRIBUTION**

**Check Pickup:** Available at the **CWA Hall/AFL-CIO building on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, beginning at 5:00 PM.** 
- **Payroll Questions:** Direct all inquiries to treasurer@msclc.org.

events.title: Parents of Students with Disabilities: Get Out the Vote Together
events.description:
Our kids can’t afford for us to sit this election out.

As parents and caregivers of students with disabilities, we know how much is at stake when it comes to public education. Our children deserve schools that have the resources, staff, and support they need to thrive. The people we elect help shape that future.

Join fellow parents and caregivers of students with disabilities for a virtual Get Out the Vote (GOTV) text bank! We’ll come together as a community to send personal texts to our friends and family, encourage them to vote, and help make sure they know which pro-public education candidates are on their ballots.

You don’t need to be a political expert or an experienced organizer. Just bring your phone, your people, and your passion for our kids. We’ll provide the tools and support you need to make a difference.

We spend so much time advocating for our children in IEP meetings, at school board meetings, and in our communities. Now, let’s bring that same energy to the ballot box.

Our kids deserve champions. Our schools deserve support. And our voices matter.

Let’s show up for each other, for our kids, and for the future of public education. Every conversation counts. Every text matters. Let’s get out the vote - together!

events.title: Canvass with SURJ in Western North Carolina!
events.description:
Come take action with SURJ and Down Home North Carolina!
The stage for the midterm elections is set, and the stakes for our movement and democracy couldn't be higher.

Join SURJ in doing our part to help flip the House and Senate and block MAGA while sending a crop of true movement champions to Congress. In North Carolina, we will be hitting the doors for House candidate Jamie Ager (NC-11) and NC Supreme Court Justice Anita Earls.

All canvasses will include a comprehensive training. No previous canvassing experience necessary!

- **North Carolina Congressional District 11** *(Block the Right Race)* - **Jamie Ager**, who is a fourth generation Western NC farmer. Running on making healthcare accessible, lowering costs, stopping government waste and corruption, and getting necessary relief to Hurricane Helene survivors.

**North Carolina Statewide** *Build Race- Movement Champion*- **Anita Earls** is an associate NC Justice running for re-election. On the NC Supreme Court, Earls has championed healthcare access, education, and protecting the right to vote. Earls is a critical line of defense to protect and re-institute fair maps for NC voters.

Logistics:
These canvasses will take place in-person with our movement partner, Down Home North Carolina. You will receive an email with orientation materials and meet-up location information ahead of time.

Feeling Unsure?
Our model works - learn from the best! Our relational conversation model works— SURJ phonebanks have one of the highest rates of success in the country. No matter whether you're brand new canvasser or a seasoned organizer, if you join our banks, you can trust that you are putting your effort into a method that works. And you'll get to learn powerful organizing skills from seasoned leaders!

Our conversations are based on open-ended questions and deep listening. You do not need to be an expert on the issues or a candidate - our canvasses are successful because we deeply connect with voters and make them feel heard.

Context:
As Trump and Republicans defund the social safety net and peddle more racist lies, millions of people are increasingly feeling the effects of the billionaire agenda. We know this fight is on multiple fronts, and this fall we have an opportunity to harness the energy of the streets and rising resentment towards November’s elections – to not only wrest power from MAGA, but to put candidates in office who are willing to stand up to Trump and fight for working class people. BOTH the House AND Senate are in play for Democrats to take back control and this year we aim to put progressive working class champions in a position to WIN.

This year is an opportunity to deliver strategic blows to the MAGA agenda and throw down a gauntlet to force the Democratic Party to reckon with true progressive, working class fighters.

To do this, we are protecting or flipping key Senate seats in North Carolina, Georgia, Maine and Mississippi and flipping critical house seats in North Carolina 11, Michigan 7, Tennessee 9 and California 22.

These races will affect millions of working class people this year. Riding the high from many wins for progressive champions throughout primary season, we are well positioned to send some of these same folks to the halls of Congress. We will continue to build power to stop MAGA, by supporting unapologetically progressive working class champions, while showing up in key races to block MAGA and showing up in solidarity alongside Black racial justice leaders in the south who are fighting back and beginning the long-build back from the gutting of the VRA. Alongside our partners across the country, this is the time for our movements to offer a bold vision and bring our people into it.

About SURJ:
Showing Up for Racial Justice (SURJ) is the largest organization in the country that explicitly organizes white communities for justice. Instead of choosing racism, silence, or complicity, we help white communities choose justice. We have thousands of national members and 150+ chapters across the US and Canada.

events.title: Hold the Line practice: what would your team do?
events.description:
Tactical decision games are a form of scenario-based training used by militaries, firefighters, healthcare workers, and others to build judgment fast. They help newer people see themselves as capable decision-makers.

Join this call to play a game set inside one of the Hold the Line scenarios. You'll be part of a small Hold the Line team facing one hard moment, and you'll decide what your team does next.

There are three rules to TDGs.

The first is "If you are in the room, you are in the game."

Please join from a place where you can fully participate with your camera and mic on, type in the chat, and see a screenshare.

You'll learn the other two rules on Wednesday.
