events.title: Vote Yes on the War Powers Resolution
events.description:
✊Vote Yes on the War Powers Resolution

Dear friends,

I am one of the millions of Americans who believes that only Congress has the power to declare war—and that no President, Democrat or Republican, should be able to drag our country into a costly, unauthorized conflict without a vote. Right now, Congress has a historic opportunity to reassert its constitutional authority and end an unauthorized war. But we need to make sure our representatives finish the job.

🚨 Our Constitution Is in Danger!

Here's what's happening:

•	On February 28, 2026, the Trump administration launched Operation Epic Fury, a major military campaign against Iran—without congressional authorization

•	The war has cost billions of taxpayer dollars, driven gas prices up 69% in some states, and put our brave servicemembers in harm's way 

•	The House has passed a War Powers Resolution three times—but it has never reached the President's desk 

•	The Senate passed a companion resolution 50–48 on June 24, 2026—the first time both chambers passed a war powers resolution since 1973
 
•	But the White House is ignoring it, claiming the War Powers Act is "not constitutional" and "not binding" 

•	Congress has still not held public hearings or voted on a formal Authorization for Use of Military Force (AUMF)

Our Constitution is not optional. Our votes are not a suggestion. Congress must act.

📢 "Vote Yes on the War Powers Resolution" – That's Our Message

We are saying YES to:

•	✅ YES to the Constitution – Article I gives Congress, not the President, the sole power to declare war 

•	✅ YES to accountability – The American people deserve a vote before our troops are sent into harm's way

•	✅ YES to ending an unauthorized war – The War Powers Resolution of 1973 requires the President to withdraw forces within 60 days unless Congress authorizes the action

•	✅ YES to diplomacy – The administration launched this war while negotiations with Iran were actively ongoing 

•	✅ YES to our troops – They deserve clear objectives, an exit strategy, and the full support of a Congress that has debated and authorized their mission

Our Constitution is not a suggestion. Our votes are not optional. Congress must act NOW.

The American people deserve a vote. Our troops deserve a strategy. Our Constitution demands accountability.

Please act now. Our democracy depends on it.

events.title: Election Day Poll Greeter - Precinct 602
events.description:
### You don't have to live in this precinct to be a Poll Greeter here. ###

#### Greeters at the polls = more votes for Democrats! ####


Poll Greeters are the last contact with voters before they enter the polling location. They offer our Democratic candidate information (sample ballot), remind voters to vote for _all_ the Democrats on their ballot, and watch for issues that may occur outside the polling place.

**You must pick up your greeter supplies from the FCDP HQ, 723 Coliseum Drive, W-S between October 30 and November 2 during these hours:**

- Friday, October 30, 10am – 2pm
- Saturday, October 31, 10am – 5pm
- Sunday, November 1, 1pm – 5pm
- Monday, November 2, 10am – 3pm

**Training**: Due to changes in voting regulations, all Poll Greeters must be trained. If you were not a Poll Greeter during Early Voting, please view the short training video and manual, linked in your confirmation email. In addition, we will be trying something new on Election Day, and there will be a brief virtual meeting on November 1 at 7pm.

**Notifications**: After you sign up for a shift you will receive a confirmation email from Forsyth County Dems via Mobilize. Please read it carefully. If you don't find your confirmation email, check your spam folder. Still not found? Contact info@fcdpnc.org.

**To check your schedule**, go to **Menu** at the top right of this page; then **My schedule**.

**_Thank you for your time and efforts supporting our candidates by being a Poll Greeter! Invite your friends to sign up for a shift too!_**   💙

events.title: SpaceXAI Has Gotta Go
events.description:
Did you know that SpaceXAI is in Palo Alto on Page Mill Road and has virtually no signage? It's almost like Elon Musk doesn't want to let anyone know who owns that building and what goes on inside.

Shocking!

To be fair, if we were a sociopathic billionaire like him, hell bent on destroying everything that makes life worth living, we wouldn't want anyone to know what buildings we owned either.

That's why every Monday from 5-6 pm we show up to provide the signage that the world's wealthiest man doesn't. Not surprisingly, SpaceXAI doesn't like us being there even one little bit. Didn't anyone tell them that ignoring people like us is a better plan than letting us know we're getting under their skin?

Apparently not.

Our weekly visit to Page Mill isn't better than a warm chocolate chip cookie, but it's close. Join us!

events.title: Henderson Día de los Muertos: Vigil for Victims of ICE

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

We'll gather and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: Team Shawn P2P Text Banking
events.description:
## Join Team Shawn for P2P Text Banking!

**Send texts. Reach voters. Help people get out and VOTE!**

Early voting is underway, and we need your help connecting with voters across Georgia's 14th Congressional District!

Join Team Shawn for peer-to-peer (P2P) text banking! From your computer or tablet, you can connect with voters, share important election information, answer questions, and help people make a plan to vote.

### What to Expect:
- Send texts to voters across GA-14.
- Share early voting locations, dates, and hours.
- Answer voter questions and help people make a plan to vote.
- Get training and support from our team if you're new to texting.

**Already an experienced texter? Great! Join us and jump right in!**

**New to text banking? No problem!** We'll provide the training, tools, and approved messages you need to get started. Your personal phone number stays private.

Whether you have 30 minutes or a few hours, there's a place for you on Team Shawn!

**Every text is an opportunity to connect with a voter and help them get to the polls. Sign up today and help us get out the VOTE!**

**Leadership Matters!**

events.title: Election Day Poll Greeter - Precinct 121
events.description:
### You don't have to live in this precinct to be a Poll Greeter here. ###

#### Greeters at the polls = more votes for Democrats! ####


Poll Greeters are the last contact with voters before they enter the polling location. They offer our Democratic candidate information (sample ballot), remind voters to vote for _all_ the Democrats on their ballot, and watch for issues that may occur outside the polling place.


**You must pick up your greeter supplies from the FCDP HQ, 723 Coliseum Drive, W-S between October 30 and November 2 during these hours:**

- Friday, October 30, 10am – 2pm
- Saturday, October 31, 10am – 5pm
- Sunday, November 1, 1pm – 5pm
- Monday, November 2, 10am – 3pm


**Training**: Due to changes in voting regulations, all Poll Greeters must be trained. If you were not a Poll Greeter during Early Voting, please view the short training video and manual, linked in your confirmation email. 

**Notifications**: After you sign up for a shift you will receive a confirmation email from Forsyth County Dems via Mobilize. Please read it carefully. If you don't find your confirmation email, check your spam folder. Still not found? Contact info@fcdpnc.org.

**To check your schedule**, go to **Menu** at the top right of this page; then **My schedule**. 

**_Thank you for your time and efforts supporting our candidates by being a Poll Greeter! Invite your friends to sign up for a shift too!_**   💙

events.description:
**Be a Parking Lot Greeter on Election Day!**

See Vote Center locations https://tinyurl.com/yae5pje7

Please make a selection using the Vote Center Selection dropdown menu
 to the right. If you want to work at more than one Vote Center, please select one in the dropdown, then list the additional Vote Centers and times in comments. 

Help support Democratic candidates across Cochise County by volunteering as a Parking Lot Greeter at a local vote center!

We need to staff all 18 Cochise county vote centers.

You’ll greet voters outside the 75-foot restricted zone and answer questions from those who would like more information about our Democratic candidates. 

We’ll provide a slate card listing all Democratic candidates running for office so you can share information with voters.

**Flexible shifts — volunteer on your schedule!**

•	Work when you want and for as long as you want or would you be willing to be assigned and work where most needed? 

•	Sign up, and we’ll match you with the vote center closest to your home or one of your choosing.

•	No special experience is necessary — just a friendly attitude and a willingness to help!

Sign up today and help Cochise County voters learn about their Democratic candidates!

events.title: Public Hearing: Tell IDEM Not to Rubber-Stamp Google Michigan City Data Center's Dirty Diesel Permit
events.description:
The Indiana Department of Environmental Management (IDEM) has published a draft modification to Google's Building 2 air permit for its facility under construction at 402 Royal Road in Michigan City.

The permit would add 66 more large diesel backup generators, on top of the 66 already permitted for Building 1. If finalized, the campus could run 132 critical diesel engines, ~725,000 gallons of on-site diesel, and even bigger engines than Building 1, with ZERO modern pollution controls in this draft. 

Krueger Middle School and Paladin - Head Start are each about a third of a mile from the site's property line, and residences are nearby. The site is a contaminated brownfield under active IDEM oversight. Michigan City residents have shown up to speak out against Building 1, packed Council chambers, and demanded accountability for the past year, while local permits for Building 2 may still be pending. This state permit will determine whether Indiana allows a second diesel power plant next to our schools and homes without basic safeguards.

Michigan City deserves clean air! Join the virtual public hearing on November 17th to tell IDEM to protect our communities and airways from Amazon’s dirty diesel generator permit.

Sign and share our petition to send a quick comment on the permit at www.jtnwi.org/no-dirty-diesel-google.

*The hearing begins at 6:00 PM CT and will conclude as soon as public comments are done, or no later than 9:00 PM CT.

events.title: CCUI Monthly Meeting: Are We Meeting Our Mission

sponsor.name: Camel City United Indivisible North Carolina

tags.name: Gotv, Get Out The Vote, Vote

events.description:
Election Day is November 3, so we're moving our regular first-Tuesday meeting to Wednesday, November 4!

It's time to come together, reflect on our work, and ask the question that now guides our monthly meetings: Are We Meeting Our Mission?

Over the past several weeks, Camel City United Indivisible has been in action across Forsyth County—from our No Kings mobilization to voter education, early voting outreach, neighborhood organizing, and helping our neighbors get to the polls.

Now it's time to assess our progress, celebrate our volunteers, and determine what comes next.

Our November conversation will focus on:

Getting Out the Vote: Reviewing our early voting efforts, voter protection activities, rides to the polls, and Election Day mobilization.

No Kings Debrief: What did we accomplish, what did we learn, and how do we turn participation into sustained community action?

Are We Meeting Our Mission? Measuring our impact in neighborhoods and communities across Forsyth County.

Moving Forward Together: Identifying our next steps beyond Election Day and strengthening our neighborhood organizing.

This isn't just another monthly meeting. It's an opportunity to evaluate whether our actions are making a difference—and how we can do even better.

Whether you've been canvassing, greeting voters, organizing events, providing rides, or simply looking for a way to get involved, your voice matters.

Join us Wednesday, November 4, at 6:30 PM on Zoom.

Register through Mobilize to receive the meeting link.

Camel City United Indivisible (CCUI)

Organizing our communities. Building lasting power. Meeting our mission.

events.title: Sunrise Orlando @ Public Comment: LYNX Board of Directors Meeting
events.description:
### Speak with Sunrise Orlando during Public Comment @ the LYNX Board of Directors Meeting! 🌅

Join us at the LYNX Board of Directors Meeting to learn about and discuss decisions that will shape our public transportation and to advocate for a more affordable, walkable, and sustainable Orlando.

**What is Public Comment?**

Public Comment refers to the time scheduled at the beginning of a meeting for public input. At each LYNX Board of Directors meeting, time is set aside for members of the public to speak on general topics of interest or concern listed on the meeting agenda. Members can provide in-person, virtual (Zoom), or written comments before the board.

**What does Public Comment with Sunrise Orlando look like?**

When participating in public comment with us, you can expect to:

- Meet up with Sunrise Orlando members and community supporters.

- Attend the public meeting together in the morning.

- Participate in public comment if appropriate and available.

- Learn how local decisions affect our communities and how we can take action.

You don't need to be a Sunrise Orlando member or a policy expert to join us! Whether it's your first public meeting or you're one of our regulars, we'll be there to help you with talking points, information, and encouragement!

events.title: Young Adult Indivisible: Storytelling for Computer Game Design and a Better United States
events.description:
Adventure games, open world games, and interactive visual novels are great ways to help people envision a better future and a better United States! 

Through game experiences it's possible to not only normalize a different world, but learn how to behave in that world and make meaningful choices. We learn that different is not neccessarily scary--sometimes it's cosy as well as exciting! 

Through games we want people to embrace a country that shares power, and supports the well-being of all its citizens.

Speaker Katherine Phelps has a PhD in storytelling for computer game design, which she lectured on for nearly a decade. She also taught how educators can bring gaming into their classes in order to inspire students to dig deeper into a variety of education topics. 

In this online class Katherine will help you to learn how to make effective interactive stories, and perhaps even make your own game!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.description:
One team. One South Carolina. Working together towards victory.

Help us Flip the Future statewide in South Carolina by reminding South Carolinians that polls are open and it’s time to Get Out the Vote! Every voter we talk to increases the likelihood of them voting and brings us one step closer to winning.

This action is the party’s number one priority for volunteers through Election Day.

This phone bank is VIRTUAL and includes training on how to use our phone banking website and how to talk to voters. You need a phone with internet connection. A laptop/tablet and headset/headphones are strongly recommended but not required. Once you have the link to your phone bank you can call at any time.

Invite your friends and call voters together!


Note: Shift times to the right are only suggestions. You can log in any time from 10 am to 8:00 pm and call for as long as you want! Once you’ve logged in for one shift and received the link to the phone bank, you can call any time you want – no need to sign in for another shift (unless you want a reminder)!

events.title: When We All Vote Party at the Polls Text Bank
events.description:
We have a big number to share: **37 million voters**. That’s how many people we’re reaching this election season with direct voter contact text messages. When a voter replies to our initial text, they deserve a real person on the other end, and we need your help to make sure every single one of those replies gets a response.

Here’s the ask: **We need volunteers to respond to voter texts over the next two weeks.**  When a voter has a question or needs a reply, you’ll be the one who answers. It’s flexible, it’s meaningful, and every text you answer is a voter who knows we’ve got their back.

Texting is fun and easy! Once you sign up we'll send over the following: 
 
- A link to sign up for our Volunteer Texting Slack community where you'll get assigned your texts, have a space for questions and being able to text with others! 
 - A quick training guide that walks you through how to use the Scale to Win platform, what texts we're sending, and how to respond to voters. 
 - A link to sign up for a daily textbank at 1pm ET where we'll throw on some jams and text together! 

This is one of the most direct ways to touch the work we’re all here for: real conversations with real voters, at a moment when it matters most.

**NOTE:** This is a nonpartisan volunteer opportunity. Party at the Polls and When We All Vote do not support or oppose any candidate, political party, or ballot measure. Our only goal is to give every voter accurate, helpful information so they can make their plan and cast their ballot.

events.title: Westlake Voting Honk & Wave with League of Women Voters of Westlake/North Olmstead and Bay Village
events.description:
It's Election Eve—let's leave it all on the field! Join the League of Women Voters of Westlake/North Olmstead and the League of Women Voters of Bay Village for a nonpartisan celebration of civic power and community spirit!

Ohio is voting! We're so excited, and we want to make sure our community is excited, too.

How does it work? We stand on the corner and act like the voting hype team we are, with pro-voting signs and cheers. Drivers honk and wave as they pass by. Smiles are had by all.

Why does it work? Because it brings extra attention to voting and reminds our neighbors that voting is a celebration! Endless campaign ads and partisan bickering can make it easy to forget, but exercising our hard-won right to vote is a joy, and we are here to show it.

📍 Corner of Detroit & Crocker in Westlake, OH, 44145

📅 November 2 | 4pm – 6pm

We'll bring the signs, you bring your voice, and together we'll bring good voting vibes. We'll see you on the street!

events.title: DC Press Conference and Altar, Día de los Muertos Day of Action - End the ICE Age

location.venue: The National Mall at 3rd Street SW between Madison Dr. & Jefferson Dr.

events.description:
***EXACT LOCATION: Our location got moved a block to 4th Street SW between Madison Dr. & Jefferson Dr. Google Maps pin here: maps.app.goo.gl/7s7paoP3stnEFAwHA***

This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

We will gather at the National Mall at 3rd Street SW between Madison Dr & Jefferson Dr in front of the U.S. Capitol for a press conference and altar to publicly grieve for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: Get-out-the-vote Phonebank
events.description:
**Ready to Help Get Out the Vote?** 

Thank you for volunteering! Your calls can make a difference.

Click the link to call Klobuchar supporters who may need a little encouragement to vote. Ask them to make a plan to vote for Erik Osberg on or before November 3rd.

**Two Important Rules**

- **Always leave a voicemail.** If no one answers, leave a message encouraging them to make a plan to vote for Erik Osberg on or before November 3rd.
- **Please call between 9:00 AM and 8:00 PM.** Do not make calls before 9:00 AM or after 8:00 PM.

**How to Get Started**

**Step 1: Open the phone bank.**

Click or tap the link that says “Click here to make some calls.” This will take you to the virtual phone bank, where you can make calls from your computer or phone.

**Step 2: Sign in or create an account.**

Follow the instructions on the screen to sign in or create an account. You will also receive a separate email from Mobilize with instructions for using the phone bank and a link to return to it later.

**Step 3: Start making calls!**

Follow the instructions in the phone bank to begin calling voters. Be friendly, have fun, and represent the campaign well!

**Need Help?**

If you have any questions or need help getting started, please email Evan at **evanm@erikosberg4congress.com**. We’re happy to help!

Thank you for giving your time to help elect Erik Osberg. Every call counts, and your help is greatly appreciated!

To make sure every community is ready to turn out, Mary Peltola has been crisscrossing the state and she’ll be in Fairbanks on November 2nd (Election Eve), for a Fairbanks Get Out The Vote Rally, and she’d love to see you there. 

This is the final stretch, and every vote counts. Alaska elections are often decided by narrow margins, and turnout in communities like Fairbanks can make the difference. Mary has built this campaign by listening to Alaskans about what’s working, what isn’t, and what needs to change. Now it’s time to make those voices count at the ballot box.

Election Day is November 3, and absentee ballots must be postmarked by that date.

events.title: Election Eve Phone Bank
events.description:
### We are calling Black voters in Virginia, Georgia and Texas, encouraging them to vote in the upcoming November 3rd general election and providing resources that make it easier to check where they are registered and find the voting information they need.

#### Last chance to make calls with us, the day before Election Day!

Beginning phone banker? We start each call with a training for anyone who needs it. You can also train yourself beforehand by checking out [our training slides](https://www.canva.com/design/DAGstUCSwjE/oWn7cjYLXJDiksQn6VbPww/view?utm_content=DAGstUCSwjE&utm_campaign=designshare&utm_medium=link2&utm_source=uniquelinks&utlId=h1f8f5f4824).

Experienced? You can start making these calls immediately and pop back into the zoom with any questions along the way.

You can also make these calls on your own time 9am-8pm within the target state's time zone - no need to wait for an event!

For more information about this phone bank, please visit the [CFCG Phonebank Page](http://centerforcommonground.org/phonebanks)

events.title: GOTV Final Canvass Countdown in Loveland 🏆
events.description:
### 🎶 Come On, Eileen! Come On, Canvass! 🎶

It's time to get the vote out. We have one week to make sure Eileen voters cast their ballots and I can't do it without you. 

Join Team Eileen as we knock on doors in Loveland! Talking directly with voters is the most effective way to earn votes-- and in this race, every vote counts.  

Whether you’re an amateur or a pro, you can make a real difference in your community by canvassing with us! _(Times are only an estimate. 30-minute training will take place at the start of the session, and once concluded you will be able to canvass at your own pace.)_

#### Full training, scripts, and materials will be provided. Plus snacks and coffee! 
- Once you sign-up, you'll receive an email with prep instructions and helpful hints, or access directly [HERE](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dPmddLGjvgWLCJjDzB2ggFCWVVc7_8cGKgITYvmH8vU/edit?usp=sharing).
- _**If you have ANY accommodation requests**_ (time restraints, difficulty with technology, need for a driver, etc.), please reach out to Constance at constancey@eileenforcolorado.com or (505) 234-2758. We'll do what is needed to have you feeling ready!

**Note:** Look at the cover photo for the next date that Eileen will join us to launch!

events.title: March for an AI Treaty: Washington, DC
events.description:
On November 18, world leaders gather in Shenzhen, China for the APEC summit. Trump plans to meet Xi Jinping there.

So on November 14, we march from the Capitol to the White House, demanding Trump and Xi make a deal to stop the AI arms race.

The CEOs of OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind have [signed a statement](https://www.safe.ai/statement-on-ai-risk) warning that AI poses a risk of human extinction. Each says it can't slow down while the others race, and while China races. Only a deal between the US and China can break that deadlock.

We're not asking either country to stop alone. We're asking both to stop together, with verification.

The same day, we march in San Francisco and New York. All cities: [aitreatymarch.org](https://aitreatymarch.org)

📅 SATURDAY, NOV 14 || 11 AM → 1 PM ET

11:00 🗣️ Rally at Pennsylvania Ave & 3rd St NW, at the foot of the Capitol
11:40 🚶 March up Pennsylvania Ave to the White House
12:20 📢 Final rally at Lafayette Square

The route is about 1.3 miles. The final route is still being confirmed, and we'll update this page.

Bring a sign, and bring your friends!

This is a peaceful, nonviolent march. Please follow marshals' instructions. AI company employees are welcome.

Co-hosted with the DC AI Safety Collective.

Questions: contact@stoptherace.ai
events.accessibility_notes: Outdoor march on city sidewalks, about 1.3 miles. Can't walk the full route? Join us at the start or the end. Email contact@stoptherace.ai for accommodations.

events.title: 2026 Election Day Pollstanding

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Hello!
Thank you for signing up to poll stand with the Franklin County Democratic Party on Election Day! We’re excited to have you join us.

What is poll standing?
Volunteers will be stationed outside polling locations to hand out the FCDP Sample Ballot to voters as they arrive to cast their ballots. It’s a great way to help voters learn about our endorsed Democratic candidates before heading into the polls.

Shift Details & Expectations
Shift times: Most shifts are 3 hours long, with the final shift running from 3:30–7:30 PM. Please plan to work your full scheduled shift. If you can't work your scheduled shift, that's ok, we still need your help! Please let us know so we can plan accordingly

Start at our staging location: All volunteers must first report to the FCDP Election Day staging location to pick up sample ballots and receive their polling location assignments. The staging location is located at 1071 S High St Columbus, OH 43206. 

Arrive early if possible: We ask that volunteers arrive at the staging location 15 minutes before their scheduled shift, if possible, to allow time to check in and receive their assignments.

Flexible assignments: Polling locations will be assigned in real time based on where we’re seeing the greatest voter traffic and need. It’s important that everyone checks in at the staging location first so we can direct volunteers where they’ll be most helpful. If you are looking to pollstand in Gahanna, Hilliard, Worthington, Westerville, Dublin, or Grove City, please let me know ASAP as you will be directed to a different staging location. Please do not travel directly to a polling location unless instructed to do so.

Dress for the weather: Please dress warmly and wear comfortable shoes, as you’ll be spending time outdoors.

If your availability has changed or you can no longer make your scheduled shift, please let us know as soon as possible so we can plan accordingly.

If you have any questions, please reach out to Kim Agyekum at kim@fcdp.org.

Thank you for volunteering your time and helping us connect voters with information about our endorsed candidates. We appreciate your support and look forward to seeing you on Election Day!

events.title: Office Hours + Check-In: Cutting Off the Data Pipeline to ICE
events.description:
At our recent webinar, we learned how thousands of local law enforcement agencies share 911 caller data, victim and witness information, and other records with LexisNexis, a private data broker that sells access to federal agencies including ICE. This often happens without local officials or residents realizing it, even in sanctuary communities.

**We've started reaching out to our local officials and requesting public records. Now it’s time to compare notes.** Join this De-ICE Action Network check-in to share where your local effort stands, troubleshoot obstacles, and learn from organizers taking on the same fight in other communities. 

Whether you’ve filed a public records request, met with a city council member, hit a wall with your police department, or are still figuring out where to start, we want to hear from you.

**What to expect:**
• Discussion of progress, roadblocks and lessons learned
• Help working through the action toolkit
• Q&A and troubleshooting with Shawn Segal of FinePrint
• Opportunities to connect with others working on this issue

**Who should attend:** Anyone who attended or watched the recording of our earlier webinar, plus organizers, advocates, local officials and staff ready to take action. 

New to the issue? You’re welcome too! Email us at events@de-iceaction.org and we'll send you everything you need to get started.

**Registration required.** This is an interactive session, so we encourage you to join live. If you have questions but can't make it, email tips@de-iceaction.org.

events.title: Build Your Power: Politics for the Rest of Us

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Tired of feeling like your opinions don't matter after Election Day? Think advocacy is only for the politically connected? Think again.

This isn't about left or right - it's about your power.

Join the League of Women Voters of Pennsylvania (LWVPA) for an interactive training designed to turn your passion into action. Whether you care about election integrity, education, healthcare, the economy, or something else entirely, you'll learn the practical foundations of effective advocacy and how to hold elected leaders accountable for the issues you care about.

This training open to anyone who is civically curious! No experience is required. Perfect for: first-time advocates who don't know where to start; millennials ready to make real change happen; women who want to amplify their voice; and, anyone passionate about their community!

Come meet fellow changemakers, get the tools you need to advocate for the things you care about, and leave ready to make change in your community.

***participants only need to sign up for one shift or training. Each session will be the same offered at different times

events.title: HANDS OFF PA Post-Election Huddle
events.description:
In Pennsylvania, most of us believe that voters should choose their leaders, not the other way around. But from ballot seizures, to election-deniers installed in key positions, this administration has demonstrated they will do anything to hold onto power and undermine the will of the people. 

We demand all votes to be counted in a timely manner, for our elections to be certified, and for duly elected candidates to be seated as lawmakers. Any attempt to disrupt election certification over the next month, or refusing to seat congress in January, would be an ultimate move of desperation. It won't work, but only if we show up.

Join us for the HANDS OFF PA Post-Election Huddle to learn about what you can do to ensure every vote is counted, our elections are certified, and duly elected officials are seated.

events.title: LEHIGH: Hands Off Our Vote! ¡No se metan con nuestro voto!
events.description:
Join Make the Road Action PA and community organizations in defending democracy!

While we don't know how the November 3rd election and results will play out, we do know that this election matters. The threats that the election will be stolen or votes won't be counted are real -- authoritarian regimes don't often voluntarily leave power.

As we approach election day, and in the hours and days after our votes are cast, details about the nature of our response will come out. RSVP now to ensure you're able to join your coworkers and neighbors in mobilizing to defend democracy.



¡Únase a Make the Road Action PA y a las organizaciones comunitarias en la defensa de la democracia!

Aunque no sabemos cómo se desarrollará la elección del 3 de noviembre ni sus resultados, sí sabemos que esta elección es importante. Las amenazas de que la elección sea robada o de que los votos no sean contados son reales: los regímenes autoritarios no suelen ceder el poder voluntariamente.

A medida que nos acercamos al día de las elecciones, y en las horas y días posteriores a la emisión de nuestros votos, se darán a conocer detalles sobre la naturaleza de nuestra respuesta. Confirme su asistencia ahora para asegurarse de poder unirse a sus compañeros de trabajo y vecinos en la movilización para defender la democracia.

Its time to stand up.

location.venue: Cleveland County NC Democratic Party Headquarters

events.description:
Many thanks to all the volunteers who have so generously stepped up to this point. The voting numbers are looking good for us so far, but we can't let up for a minute.

THANK YOU IN ADVANCE!

events.title: Compost Hub Support: Dunsmore Park
events.description:
At our Compost Hubs, food scraps collected from the community are transformed into nutrient-rich compost, and we need your help to make it happen! As a Compost Hub Support Volunteer, you’ll gain hands-on experience working alongside our knowledgeable Compost Managers. Get ready to leave feeling accomplished, a little sweaty, and brimming with new compost knowledge. 

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
Roll up your sleeves and dive into a variety of engaging activities; whether it’s managing a three-bin system, tending to a compost pile, sifting finished compost, or exploring a mix of everything. There’s something for everyone, from beginners to seasoned pros! Plus, our Compost Hubs are situated in LA County’s most cherished green spaces: community gardens, urban farms, and beautiful parks. Join passionate community composters, learn to turn food scraps into rich compost, and connect with the local food system. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You will be working outdoors! Shade levels vary by site.
* Activity level can be adjusted to your comfort and abilities—just communicate with your Compost Manager.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome!
* If you sign up, we ask that you show up! We rely on volunteers, like you, to achieve our mission.  
* This site has public restrooms. 
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.
* Access to water, but please bring a filled water bottle. 

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under the age of 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 
VOLUNTEER WAIVER: Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. Access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver

CODE OF CONDUCT: All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

Llamar a miembros de la comunidad: Comunícate con votantes en los condados del Distrito Congresional 31 usando nuestro sistema de marcación automática.
Identificar apoyo y movilizar: Pregunta a los votantes sus preferencias y ayuda a asegurar una alta participación para Justin Early y nuestros candidatos aliados.

events.title: Online to Offline: Digital Organizing 101
events.description:
## Every strong movement starts with real human connection. In this connected world, that happens both online and offline.

Digital organizing uses digital tools to meet and engage people online, and then move them into in-person action. It doesn’t replace the real world relationship-building we must do to build movements that win change. It just provides another path to get there.

In this training we walk through how to use digital tools with the same discipline we bring to in-person conversations — to build real relationships, move people to act, and grow your base. 

### Our brand new Digital Organizing 101 training will cover:

- The foundational principles of digital organizing

- Using platforms like Whatsapp, Reddit, Facebook and Instagram to identify and engage supporters

- Real-world case studies to apply digital organizing principles

- The formula to craft personal and persuasive messaging 

- Digital systems and hygiene

This space will build a community of organizers with the skills to leverage the online world and make change offline. See you there!

_This training is co-lead by Public School Strong and the Alliance to Reclaim Our Schools._

We are opening our home for a community vigil and action gathering. The event will span two spaces:

The Ground Floor Hub (Fully ADA Accessible): Join us in the open garage and driveway to contribute to a community ofrenda. Bring photos or offerings for those impacted by ICE. We will have action stations, art-making, and refreshments available for all.

The Roof Deck Vigil: For those able to navigate two flights of stairs, we will host a sunset vigil on the roof overlooking San Francisco. Against the backdrop of our city's skyline, we will hold a space to reflect on the stark contrast between our city's reputation as a liberal sanctuary and the reality of ongoing surveillance and ICE presence within our borders.

Whether you come to light a candle, sign a petition, or simply stand in solidarity, your presence matters.

We will not stand by as families are disappeared, rights are dismantled, and democracy itself is eroded. 

Accessibility & Logistics Note: The main altar, community space, and action stations are located on the ground level in the open garage and driveway, which are fully accessible. Please note that restrooms will not be available at this event, so please plan accordingly. The roof deck vigil requires climbing two flights of stairs; however, we will be broadcasting the roof's view down to the ground floor so everyone can share in the moment of reflection together.

events.description:
This November, it’s going to take all of us to protect free and fair elections, so that WE, the people of North Carolina, get to decide our future. We’ve already seen how people in power in our state and in the White House are trying to silence Black and brown voters, students, working people, and anyone who disagrees with them. Our democracy is under attack but we’re not backing down! 

On election day, and on a few other key dates in November, we’re coming together to exercise and defend our vote and to show those in power that we are watching:

- Tuesday, November 10th: Last day for voters with absentee or provisional ballots to “cure” their ballots and make sure they are counted. We’ll come together in our counties that evening to celebrate historic voter turnout, thank the election officials who are working hard to make our democracy run, and to send a clear message: count every vote. 

- Monday, November 16th: Join us in the evening for a mass call with partners across the state to hear updates about what happened in the elections and during county certification, and what's next in the movement to protect our vote. We'll also get ready to make our voices heard when the NC General Assembly reconvenes in November.

- Tuesday, November 24th: Deadline for the NC State Board of Elections to certify all the NC election results. We’ll hold a peaceful rally between the NC General Assembly and the State Board of Elections on Halifax Mall, in Raleigh, ready to defend our vote. 

Sign up here to let us know you’re in, and we’ll follow up with more details!

events.title: Scales Consulting Presents: Vote & Vibe Election Day College Edition
events.description:
Your Voice. Your Vote. Your Vibe! 🎶

Democracy meets music, community, and good vibes!

Election Day is more than just casting a ballot. It’s an opportunity to celebrate our voices, exercise our rights, and come together as a community!

Join us for Vote & Vibe: Election Day College Edition, a high-energy, nonpartisan Election Day celebration designed to bring college students, young voters, and community members together for an evening of music, civic engagement, connection, and celebration.

Scales Consulting LLC, and When We All Vote, this event is all about empowering the next generation of voters, strengthening civic participation, and reminding everyone that our voices matter.

Whether you’re voting for the first time, have already cast your ballot, or simply want to connect with others who care about the future of our communities, there’s a place for you at Vote & Vibe!

📅 Event Details

* Date: Tuesday, November 3, 2026 (Election Day)
* Time: 6:00 PM to 9:00 PM EST
* Location: Grand Valley State University, Allendale Campus
* Room: 2266
* Address: 1 N Campus Drive, Allendale, MI 49401
* Admission: Open to all
* Event Type: Nonpartisan Civic Engagement and Election Day Celebration
* Transportation: Rides to the polls available

🎉 What to Expect

🎶 Music & Good Vibes

Celebrate Election Day in an energetic, welcoming environment that brings together music, culture, and community.

🗳️ Civic Engagement & Voter Empowerment

Connect with others who recognize the importance of civic participation. Learn why every election matters and how your voice can help shape decisions affecting our communities, campuses, and future.

🚗 Rides to the Polls

Need transportation to cast your ballot? Rides to the polls will be available to help eligible voters access their polling locations before polls close.

Community Connections

Meet fellow students, young leaders, advocates, and community members who are passionate about building a stronger, more inclusive democracy.

🌎 Youth Leadership & Collective Action

Explore the connection between voting and the issues that impact our generation, including education, economic opportunity, environmental sustainability, climate justice, and community well-being.

Why Vote & Vibe Matters

Our democracy is strongest when everyone has an opportunity to participate.

From decisions about education and the economy to climate change, public health, and civil rights, elections shape policies that affect our everyday lives.

Young people have tremendous power to influence the future, and Vote & Vibe is about creating a space where that power is recognized, celebrated, and encouraged.

We believe civic engagement should be accessible, inclusive, culturally relevant, and empowering. Voting isn’t just a responsibility. It’s an opportunity to make your voice heard and help shape the communities we want to live in.

📣 Everyone Is Welcome!

Whether you’re a GVSU student, a first-time voter, a seasoned voter, or a community member who believes in the power of collective action, we invite you to join us.

Come for the vibes. Stay for the community. Celebrate the power of your vote!

🗳️ Your Voice. Your Vote. Your Vibe!

- Divisadero neighbors

events.title: Phone Bank Party for Scott Colom for Mississippi Senate
events.description:
## Come phone bank with your neighbors, friends and SURJ!

We are now in a decisive phase of the fight against authoritarianism, the threat is real and the stakes are high. And people are fighting back. Millions have protested, and we've watched powerful organizing coming out of Minneapolis, Chicago, and other cities that have borne the brunt of ICE's assaults on our communities. Mass anger exists, but mass organization does not yet exist at the scale needed to win. Movements become real when they reach millions: organized, trained, and acting together.

The stage for the midterm elections is set, and the stakes for our movement and democracy couldn't be higher.

**Join SURJ in doing our part to help flip the House and Senate and block MAGA while sending a crop of true movement champions to Congress.**

Come as you are! No experience needed! Full training & lots of support included!

## Logistics:

- We're gathering to phone bank together at the address for this event (sent via email when you register). 
- You will log into a program with a script on your computer and bring your phone to make the calls (if you only have one device, still come!).
We have a robust training to give you all the information you need  — a script, technical support, and coaching throughout.
- People who have phone banked with SURJ before (Returners) can start early.
- You will receive an email with orientation materials ahead of time.

## Feeling Unsure?

- Our model works - learn from the best! Our phone banks have one of the highest rates of success in the country. No matter whether you're brand new caller or a seasoned organizer, if you join our banks, you can trust that you are putting your effort into a method that works. And you'll get to learn powerful organizing skills from seasoned leaders!
- Our conversations are based on open-ended questions and deep listening. You do not need to be an expert on the issues or a candidate - our phone banks are successful because we deeply connect with voters and make them feel heard.
- Want to hear what a phone bank is like? Ask your host to talk about their experience!

## Context:

As Trump and republicans defund the social safety net and peddle more racist lies, millions of people are increasingly feeling the effects of the billionaire agenda. We know this fight is on multiple fronts, and this fall we have an opportunity to harness the energy of the streets and rising resentment towards November’s elections – to not only wrest power from MAGA, but to put candidates in office who are willing to stand up to Trump and fight for working class people. BOTH the House AND Senate are in play for Democrats to take back control and this year we aim to put progressive working class champions in a position to WIN.

For the last six years, SURJ’s phone banking program has grown to be one of the strongest in the country, reaching millions of working class people with our vision of finding our shared interest in standing alongside people of color and rejecting white supremacy. This year is an opportunity to deliver strategic blows to the MAGA agenda and throw down a gauntlet to force the Democratic Party to reckon with true progressive, working class fighters.

To do this, protecting or flipping key Senate seats in North Carolina, Georgia, Maine and Mississippi and flipping critical house seats in Michigan 7, Tennessee 9 and California 22.

These races will affect millions of working class people this year. Riding the high from many wins for progressive champions throughout primary season, we are well positioned to send some of these same folks to the halls of Congress. We will continue to build power to stop MAGA, by supporting unapologetically progressive working class champions, while showing up in key races to block MAGA and showing up in solidarity alongside Black racial justice leaders in the south who are fighting back and beginning the long-build back from the gutting of the VRA. Alongside our partners across the country, this is the time for our movements to offer a bold vision and bring our people into it.

### About SURJ:

Showing Up for Racial Justice (SURJ) is the largest organization in the country that explicitly organizes white communities for justice. Instead of choosing racism, silence, or complicity, we help white communities choose justice. We have thousands of national members and 150+ chapters across the US and Canada.

events.title: White people’s work after the election
events.description:
No matter what happens in the midterm elections, white people will have a critical role in the post-election moment. We might be mobilizing to protect election results and working to ensure results are certified– or we might be getting into formation to keep up the momentum from big wins and push for a racial and economic justice agenda. Register to join SURJ on a mass call the day after the election to make sense of what happens and get your marching orders for what’s next.

Showing Up for Racial Justice (SURJ) is the largest organization in the country that explicitly organizes white communities for justice. Instead of choosing racism, silence, or complicity, we help white communities choose justice. We have thousands of national members and 50+ chapters across the US and Canada.

events.title: [ON YOUR OWN] Michigan Black Diaspora Phone Bank
events.description:
Got an hour? Make it count. Call Black voters across the diaspora from home, on your own schedule, any day between 9 a.m. and 9 p.m.

No need to wait for a group session. Pick a time that works for you, watch a quick training video, log in to our online dialer, and start calling. The script walks you through every conversation, and your personal number stays private.

Use a laptop, tablet, or smartphone with headphones and a mic, and find a quiet spot. A laptop is easiest for reading the script, but any device works.

Pick your time, sign up, and start calling.

GABA Foundation’s voter engagement is nonpartisan. We do not support or oppose any candidate or party.

location.venue: Friedhof Building in the Oak Room of Columbus

events.description:
Independent U.S. Senate candidate Dan Osborn will be at The Oak Room of Columbus on Monday, November 2nd from 2:00 pm - 3:00 pm (CDT) for a town hall.

An industrial and service mechanic, Osborn is a veteran of the U.S. Navy and Nebraska National Guard. He is running to break the stranglehold that billionaires have on our economy and government. Osborn will unite Nebraskans around a common-sense platform that works for workers, small businesses, and family farms and ranches.

All are welcome to join, to ask questions, and share thoughts and insights. This campaign is about truly listening to ALL Nebraskans, not just the politically connected.

Questions or concerns can be directed to info@osbornforsenate.com. If you want to help us get the word out about this event please send us an email!

events.title: A Gathering of Friends: Film Screening of No Country for Mothers
events.description:
We're hosting a screening of a documentary about what motherhood really looks like in America today. The film focuses on structural issues that often work to hold us back and keep us apart. 

This isn’t just about watching a film; it’s about being in a room where we can say things out loud that we’ve been carrying, and realize we’re not alone.

Moms First is a movement fighting for paid leave and affordable, accessible child care. Their goal is to educate, innovate, and advocate for the social and political policies that moms need and deserve. Their vision is a country that values motherhood and works in support of moms and families.

Please come for light snacks, refreshments, and affirming conversation!

You can view the trailer here: https://youtu.be/fNTiJMxLJUc

events.title: 2nd Annual Holiday Food Drive with NELC-Indivisible

location.venue: Annunciation of Our Lady Episcopal Church

events.description:
## Join NE Lake County Indivisible in partnership with Annunciation of Our Lady Episcopal Church as we spread holiday cheer and support our neighbors in need!


📆 **Date:** December 5

🕑 **Time:** 9:00am-11:00am 

📍 **Location:** Annunciation of Our Lady Episcopal Church, 5725 Stearns School Rd, Gurnee, IL 60031

**Come** *to support the Food Drive!* Donate non-perishable items from the list below and help Lake County neighbors in need. 

**Stay** *to enjoy a good time!* Nibble on some goodies, sing some resistance carols, and get busy with fun service projects to include whistle kits, postcards, and more.

If you cannot join the fun in person, we are gathering monetary donations as well. **The Northern Illinois Food Bank services pantries and neighbors right here in Lake County.** And donations are accepted online here: 
https://support.solvehungertoday.org/indi26 

Let’s show the world this holiday season what real democracy looks like when we gather in support of one another – in the spirit of giving and sharing, we very much look forward to seeing you and accepting your donations and non-perishable items, such as those listed below:

- Peanut Butter
- Canned Tuna/Chicken (in water)
- Cereal (any kind) / Oatmeal
- 100% Juice
- Dried Beans and Lentils
- Canned Fruits (in juice)
- Low/Reduced-Sodium Soups
- Plant-Based Milk (shelf-stable)
- Whole-Grain Pasta and Sauce
- Spices and Seasonings (no glass jars, please)

We are grateful for the many organizations who help promote and make this food drive happen.

Please feel free to park in the church parking lot for this event.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

### ABOUT NE LAKE COUNTY INDIVISIBLE:
NE Lake County IL Indivisible is a nonpartisan grassroots organization founded in 2025 in defense of democracy. We are Lake County residents working together to protect elections and neighbors. We aim to support targeted populations and take action on a local and national level to push back against authoritarianism. We welcome everyone, whether you voted this way or that way, or didn't vote at all in 2024.

**More about us can be found here:**
https://nelakecounty-indivisible.org
https://linktr.ee/nelakecountyindivisible

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

**Some quotes from past participants:**

* "It was great working with like minded people who care so much about what's going on in our country. We want and are working for change that helps all Americans"

* "It was fun working with people who share your feelings about what's happening in our country and overseas. I find it inspiring and it gives me hope."

* "great turnout, super well organized. welcoming and fun."

* "Well organized. Liked the materials included in the kits. Good location. Nice people. Thank you very much!"

* "I took action for NE Lake County IL Indivisible because last time we put together whistle kits, I was impressed by how organized the work was, how professional, encouraging and friendly the leaders were. It was the same this time. The leaders told us about other opportunities with the organization. They sat and chatted with the groups at each of the tables. The volunteers were all friendly. I felt able to speak freely. We didn't speak of frustrations. We talked of opportunity for helping others."

When:
 This weekend: Leave Friday, October 23,return Sunday, October 25.

 Final Election push: Monday, November 2 - Tuesday, November 3.

How:
 Canvassing to Get Out The Vote for Randy Villegas
 Poll & dropbox watching
 Driving and helping out the campaign

Cost:
 Zero: We got you covered for food, lodging, and gas

What You Get:
 Training for whatever you sign up for

Benefits:
 Have fun
 Make new friends
 Attend GOTV rally with AOC and Randy Villegas (Friday evening)

Wake up on November 4 with no regrets, knowing you made a huge difference to gain a pro-democracy Congress

events.title: VIRTUAL - Portland Chapter Get the Work Done Meetings
events.description:
**Please only drop in for the part of the agenda you are interested in. These are working meetings and you are not required to stay for the entire thing**

We are in the home stretch, a little over 2  years until we win health care for all in Oregon. As we prepare for session, it is now the time to go hard into getting the work done. We have the most passionate and on fire volunteers and I know when we fight together, we win.

This meeting is virtual and drop in. Drop in for the time session you are interested in. 

**For the meeting on November 9th, please expect the following agenda:**

-5pm-5:45pm Working on dissecting the universal health plan into digestible, educational pieces for the public. Includes writing material and turning it into a 5th grade reading level

-5:45pm-6:30pm Writing scripts for social media. Brave souls will make social media video content out of them. I'll show you how to not make that such a scary experience

-6:30pm-7:15pm Legislative research, who won elections, who are the Portland (and if we have time, greater Oregon) legislators now?

7:15pm-8pm Research and talking points on individual legislators, compiled

8pm-8:45pm Work on advertising labor rally on social media and maybe through canvassing or events?

Next meeting will have another agenda that will replace this description after this meeting ends.

events.title: ¡Fiesta del Voto!
events.description:
# **FIESTA DEL VOTO** # 

*Celebra nuestra comunidad. Vota.*

¡Estamos convirtiendo las urnas en una fiesta en bloque! Ven por la comunidad, quédate por la diversión, y hagamos que nuestras voces se escuchen juntos. Es hora de celebrar nuestro poder y presentarnos al vecindario que amamos.

¡Únete a PODER para celebrar el poder cívico, la comida y el espíritu comunitario!

** EL AMBIENTE: **

¡Estamos trayendo la energía a las urnas! Ya sea que vayas a votar temprano o el día de las elecciones, ven a pasar el rato, conoce a tu vecino  y celebra la democracia en acción.

**DÓNDE Y CUÁNDO:**


PODER 
3357 W 55th
St Chicago, IL 60632

Martes, 3 de noviembre de 14:00 a 18:00 

Ven a cantar un poco de karaoke, haz una manualidad, come algo y prepárate para VOTAR con PODER. Si vives cerca, acompáñanos a la Escuela Primaria Socorro Sandoval para emitir tu voto.

**VOTEMOS JUNTOS**

Traiga un amigo, conozca a la comunidad y hagamos que cuente.

**Cualquier comida, entretenimiento, botones, pegatinas u otros artículos gratuitos en este evento están disponibles tanto para votantes como para no votantes. Este es un evento no partidista.**

# **LET’S PARTY AT THE POLLS!** 🗳️

*Celebrate our community. Cast your vote.*

We’re turning the ballot box into a block party! Come for the community, stay for the fun, and let’s make our voices heard together. It’s time to celebrate our power and show up for the neighborhood we love.

Join PODER for a celebration of civic power, food, and community spirit!

**THE VIBE:**

We’re bringing the energy to the ballot box! Whether you’re voting early or on Election Day, come hang out, meet your neighbors, and celebrate democracy in action.

**WHERE & WHEN:**

📍 PODER
3357 W 55th St
Chicago, IL 60632

📅 Tuesday, Nov. 3rd form 2pm-6pm

**FEATURING:**

Come sing some karaoke, do a craft, eat some food and get ready to VOTE with PODER. If you're local, walk over to Socorro Sandoval Elementary School with us to cast your vote.

**LET’S VOTE TOGETHER!** 

Bring a friend, meet the community, and let’s make it count.

**Any food, entertainment, buttons, stickers, or any other free items at this event are available to voters and non-voters alike. This is a nonpartisan event.**

events.title: FLA Volunteering
events.description:
Join Future Leaders of America for our Get Out The Vote (GOTV) phone banking campaign! Whether you are a youth advocate taking your first step in civic engagement or an adult passionate about uplifting our community, your voice matters—and your efforts will empower others to use theirs.

This is a nonpartisan, community-first initiative. We aren't telling people who or what to vote for; we're simply ensuring that every member of our community has the information, resources, and encouragement they need to make it to the ballot box.

Why You Should Join Us
Amplify Community Voices: Help make sure our neighborhood's needs, perspectives, and priorities are represented at the polls.

Build Skills & Community: Meet like-minded youth and supporters, build leadership and communication skills, and work together toward a common goal.

Full Training Provided: Never phone banked before? No problem! We provide quick, thorough training before every shift, along with phone scripts and live staff support so you feel confident every step of the way.

What to Expect
Welcome & Check-In: Connect with the team and get energized.

Training & Walkthrough: Learn the nonpartisan phone banking tool and review key voting info.

Phone Banking Session: Make calls to voters in our community.

Debrief & Celebration: Share highlights and celebrate the impact we made together!

Together, we can ensure our community's future is shaped by the people who live here. Sign up for a shift today and bring a friend!

events.title: Atender el duelo ecológico: parte I
events.description:
Vivimos en una época marcada por cambios y pérdidas ambientales significativas. Dado que estos tiempos resultan difíciles de afrontar, a los que es complejo adaptarse y sobre los cuales es complicado reflexionar, resulta fundamental que nos unamos como comunidad para procesar nuestras vivencias. Cuidarnos a nosotros mismos y apoyarnos mutuamente es tan importante como velar por la tierra y el agua.

Acompaña a Sky Island Alliance y a nuestra comunidad el miércoles 4 de noviembre a las 4 p.m. en un espacio dedicado a explorar el terreno del duelo ecológico, procesar nuestras emociones, celebrar esta hermosa región y fortalecer nuestra resiliencia de manera colectiva. Este seminario web gratuito da inicio a una serie de oportunidades para compartir tus respuestas creativas ante una región en constante cambio, ya sea que surjan del duelo, la esperanza o cualquier otro sentimiento intermedio. Un segundo seminario web, más adelante, brindará a los participantes la oportunidad de compartir sus reflexiones y experiencias a partir de una serie de actividades que se realizarán en los próximos meses. 

_Fotografía de un álamo en la frontera, en La Noria._

events.title: Salmonberry Trail Planting Party - Help us Beautify Wheeler!
events.description:
Join the Planting Team in Wheeler!

The Salmonberry Trail is almost ready to open, and we need your help with the finishing touches! Come join our team of volunteers as we plant native and drought-tolerant plants along Wheeler’s new trail segment.

This is the first coastal section of the 82-mile Salmonberry Trail Rails and Trails project—a wonderful opportunity to create a welcoming, beautiful trail for residents, visitors, and wildlife.

🌿 What will we be doing?

Plants have been selected and locations planned. The planting process is straightforward, and everyone can help!

Unpot each plant and check its roots.

Score the roots if needed to encourage healthy growth.

Dig a hole where needed (some holes will be prepared in advance SO EVERY physical capability can help!).

Place the plant in its designated location.

Backfill with soil and add mulch to help retain moisture and support healthy growth.

Water each plant in to give it a good start and help settle the soil around its roots.

No special gardening experience is necessary—just bring your enthusiasm, a willingness to get your hands dirty, and a desire to make a difference!

🌼 Why come?

Together, we can:

Create native habitat for birds, bees, and butterflies, providing food, shelter, and support for local pollinators and wildlife.

Add natural beauty and greenery to the trail.

Help make the Salmonberry Trail a welcoming destination for our community and visitors.

Every plant we put in the ground is an investment in Wheeler’s future!

Can you spare a few hours on November 21? Bring a friend, meet your neighbors, and help us grow something wonderful!

🧤 Bring: Gardening gloves, sturdy shoes, and a water bottle. Planting tools and supplies will be provided as available.

Let’s plant the future of the Salmonberry Trail—one plant at a time! 🌱

If you are coming from the Portland Metro area, let us know if you need to carpool with someone and will help arrange a ride!

[Please read the volunteer waiver](https://salmonberrytrail.org/volunteer-waiver)

[You Can Make A Donation Here](https://salmonberrytrail.org/donate)

events.title: Get Out The Vote: Phone Banking with Battleground Texas
events.description:
Every voter deserves to feel prepared and confident heading into Election Day. Join the Battleground Texas team for a Get Out the Vote (GOTV) volunteer opportunity where you can make a meaningful impact through simple, one-on-one phone conversations with voters in your community.

### Through this virtual phone banking shift, you’ll help South Texas voters create a plan to vote by making sure they know:

- WHERE they’ll vote by identifying their polling location.
- WHAT is on their ballot by reviewing their sample ballot.
- WHEN they plan to vote by confirming their day and time.
- WHAT THEY NEED to cast their ballot, including an acceptable form of ID and a ride to the 
   polls if needed


### Small Conversations. Meaningful Impact.
Helping someone make a voting plan is a simple but powerful way to support civic engagement. By taking a few minutes to connect with voters, answer questions, and help them prepare, you can help make the voting process feel more accessible and less overwhelming.
### The Battleground Texas team will provide training, resources, and ongoing support so you feel confident connecting with voters. During phone banking shifts, we'll be together on Zoom as a team, giving you the opportunity to learn, ask questions, and make an impact alongside fellow volunteers.

- No prior experience is required! Just bring your willingness to connect with your community and help more Texans feel ready to participate in this election.

events.title: Young Adult Indivisible: Storytelling for Computer Game Design and a Better United States
events.description:
Adventure games, open world games, and interactive visual novels are great ways to help people envision a better future and a better United States! 

Through game experiences it's possible to not only normalize a different world, but learn how to behave in that world and make meaningful choices. We learn that different is not neccessarily scary--sometimes it's cosy as well as exciting! 

Through games we want people to embrace a country that shares power, and supports the well-being of all its citizens.

Speaker Katherine Phelps has a PhD in storytelling for computer game design, which she lectured on for nearly a decade. She also taught how educators can bring gaming into their classes in order to inspire students to dig deeper into a variety of education topics. 

In this online class Katherine will help you to learn how to make effective interactive stories, and perhaps even make your own game!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: November 2/November 3 Polling Site Volunteers
events.description:
# Final Two Days of Voting! LD13 Polling Site Volunteers

**Monday, November 2 & Tuesday, November 3 (Election Day)**

The 2026 General Election is almost over, and LD13 Democrats will be out at voting locations for the final two days!

Join us to greet voters, distribute voter guides, and provide information about candidates and ballot choices as voters head to the polls.

**Whether you can volunteer for a few hours on Monday, Election Day Tuesday, or both, we'd love to have you!**

## How Volunteer Assignments Work

- **Choose Your Shifts:** Register for the dates and times that work best for you.
- **Stay Close to Home:** We'll make every effort to assign you to a voting location as close to your home as possible.
- **Get Your Assignment in Advance:** Your specific voting location and instructions will be provided a few days before each scheduled shift.
- **Materials and Guidance:** We'll coordinate voter guides and electioneering materials and provide instructions before your shift.

## What Will You Do?

- Greet voters as they arrive at voting locations.
- Offer LD13 voter guides and information about candidates and ballot choices.
- Help voters find additional election resources.
- Follow applicable electioneering rules and remain outside designated restricted areas.

## What Should You Bring?

You'll likely be spending time outdoors, so we recommend bringing:

- **A hat and sunglasses** for sun protection.
- **Sunscreen** to protect against Arizona's sunshine.
- **Comfortable shoes** suitable for standing and walking.
- **Charged Cell phone** to report issues with voting or request assistance
- **Water** and refreshments will be provided to all sites.

events.title: Get Signs to Polling Places in Sarpy County!
events.description:
Hello Sarpy Democrats!

We have about 80 polling locations in Sarpy County where we will be placing candidate signs for the Midterm Election. 

We need your help! Many hands will make light work of this.

Please contact Christine at clercforbps@outlook.com or 402-216-4371 with your:
1) home address, 
2) mobile phone, and 
3) about how many sites you would like to place signs. 

Then Christine will assign you locations that are closest to your home area.

If you prefer to go to any specific polling places that you are familiar with, please let me know that as well. 

You can find a list of Sarpy County polling locations here: https://www.sarpy.gov/689/Polling-Place-Information

Volunteers will:

- Pick up signs on the evening of Monday, November 2nd, between 4:00 - 6:00 p.m. at Vivere Apartments, 8216 City Centre Dr, La Vista, NE 68128.(If you need any later, please let me know.) 
 
- Place signs at polling places Monday evening or the morning of the Election on Tuesday, November 3rd, prior to 8:00 a.m. when the polls open. 
 
- Recover signs from polling places on Tuesday evening, prior to or around the close of the polls at 8:00 p.m. 
 
- Return signs at our next monthly meeting, Wednesday, November 18th, 6:30 - 7:00 p.m., at the Carpenter's Union Training Center in La Vista, or anytime to Christine.


Signs should be placed, in accordance with Nebraska law, greater than 200 ft from the polling place to avoid electioneering, and avoiding private property. They should mark the distance with an orange cone. If not sure, you may see other signs and can place ours nearby.


Contact Christine at clercforbps@outlook.com or text (402) 216-4371 with any questions or concerns.

Thanks so much for helping! This is our last big push for visibility for our awesome candidates!

events.title: Social Bank on Your Own Time with Stand Up America
events.description:
Bots and overseas accounts have been flooding social media with MAGA content for years. Volunteers like you can help fight back, on your own schedule.

Social banks work like a phonebank, but instead of a call list, you get posts from Senate candidates in key states who are standing up to Trump’s corruption and need help reaching undecided voters. You don’t need to live in a swing state to make a difference.

Why it works: when you engage with a post, the algorithm shows it to more people, including voters who are still making up their minds.

**What to expect**

After you sign up, you'll be taken to Prosocial, the tool we use to share posts. Pick the platforms you use (Facebook, Instagram, Threads, TikTok, Twitter/X, YouTube), and Prosocial will show you posts to engage with. 

You'll also receive an email with a [step-by-step guide](https://app.tango.us/app/workflow/Social-Bank-with-Stand-Up-America-using-Prosocial-644621c9d279469f86f6097f5338f419) on how to use Prosocial if you get stuck.

Social bank whenever you have a few minutes. Every like, comment, and share helps before Election Day on November 3.

**What you'll need**

Your phone or computer, and your social media accounts, logged in on the device you’ll use. No experience necessary.

Want help getting started? Join a live Social Bank training: [Social Bank training](https://www.mobilize.us/standupamerica/event/1048294)

events.title: Compost Hub Support: Syd Kronenthal Park
events.description:
At our Compost Hubs, food scraps collected from the community are transformed into nutrient-rich compost, and we need your help to make it happen! As a Compost Hub Support Volunteer, you’ll gain hands-on experience working alongside our knowledgeable Compost Managers. Get ready to leave feeling accomplished, a little sweaty, and brimming with new compost knowledge. 

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
Roll up your sleeves and dive into a variety of engaging activities, whether it’s managing a three-bin system, tending to a compost pile, sifting finished compost, or exploring a mix of everything. There’s something for everyone, from beginners to seasoned pros! Plus, our Compost Hubs are situated in LA County’s most cherished green spaces: community gardens, urban farms, and beautiful parks. Join passionate community composters, learn to turn food scraps into rich compost, and connect with the local food system. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You will be working outdoors! Shade levels vary by site.
* Activity level can be adjusted to your comfort and abilities—just communicate with your Compost Manager.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome!
* This site has public restrooms
* If you sign up, we ask that you show up! We rely on volunteers, like you, to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under the age of 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 

VOLUNTEER WAIVER: Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. You can access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver 

CODE OF CONDUCT: All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

events.title: Love as Action: National Organizing Call
events.description:
As communities across the country prepare for the weeks surrounding this fall's elections, many of us are asking how we can continue showing up for democracy, our neighbors, and one another.

Join Friends and people of conscience from around the country for a Love as Action National Organizing Call. Together, we'll reconnect, hear updates from communities continuing this public witness, and prepare for a season of visible, peaceful presence against authoritarianism.

We'll also discuss opportunities to organize or participate in Love as Action vigils and how communities can serve as public witnesses for peace, democracy, and community care during a time when these values may be tested.

Whether you have hosted a vigil, attended one, signed the [Declaration of Resistance](https://afsc.org/action/declaration-resistance), or are simply looking for ways to get involved, we hope you'll join us.

Monday, November 16
8:00 PM ET / 5:00 PM PT


The moment calls for public witness.
The moment calls for community.
The moment calls for Love as Action.

👉 Love as Action vigils are taking place across the country. Join us on the next Love as Action Weekend - Nov. 7-8

Ready to host or attend a vigil? Visit the Love as Action page for resources and event listings: [afsc.org/love-action](afsc.org/love-action)

events.title: Love as Action: Memphis
events.description:
# Love as Action: Resisting Authoritarianism

### Quaker public witness has stood in opposition to cruel and authoritarian actions in our country before. It is time for us to show this love in action again. 

Please join Memphis Friends Meeting as it hosts the November vigil of Memphis' Immigrant Relief Task Force to bear witness and show resistance to the authoritarian actions in our country, particularly as it has impacted our immigrant neighbors. 

On November 12 at 6 pm we will gather in the front yard of Memphis Friends Meeting (3387 Walnut Grove) for 45 minutes of candlelit worship in the tradition of Friends. Afterwards we will gather inside for fellowship and refreshments and a service project to benefit Monarch Hospitality House in Mason, Tennessee.

Our hope is that our presence will give hope to all who see us – to show that we can choose resistance - and remind everyone of our moral obligations to one another.

The American Friends Service Committee gathers monthly in communities across the country, showing our communities love in action as a public witness of our Quaker values in a time of rising fascism.

Join us! 

To find our more about Love as Action nationally and get more resources visit us at [afsc.org/love-action](www.afsc.org/love-action)
