events.title: November 2026 General Meeting
events.description:
Election Impacts on Our Local Environment

Environmentalist Gary Beverly presents information on how federal, state, and local policies impact our global, regional, and local environment. Says Beverly, "Current federal policy has caused long-lasting, extremely harmful damage to public lands, public health, and climate change, all with local impacts. Flipping the Senate and House is only a partial solution. Restoring and improving Federal environmental policy will require new leadership at EPA, Interior, and Agriculture that can only be accomplished by a new President - even then years of work will be required."

Gary Beverly is the Chair of the Yavapai Group and vice-chair of the Grand Canyon Chapter of the Sierra Club. He is a leader in the Citizens Water Advocacy Group. Both roles focus on protecting the upper Verde River.

Given the timing of the meeting, it will open with an election debrief before we proceed to Gary Beverly’s presentation.

### IMPORTANT NOTE
**Our meetings have grown! To accommodate our space restrictions, please see below for registration instructions.**

Please choose the **5:30-7pm shift** if you are planning to attend in person so we can plan for dinner. Registration for in-person attendance will close when the space's capacity limit has been reached.

events.title: Seattle Día de los Muertos Day of Action - End the ICE Age
events.description:
This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

We'll gather and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. events.title: Warren Wilson: Without Shade, Without Rest
events.description:
Join us November 20, at 6pm in Kittredge Theater for a screening of the film Without Shade, Without Rest. There will be light refreshments provided and a discussion of farm and food worker rights following the film.

WeCount! is a non-profit, human rights organization that represents immigrant workers and families in South Florida, including plant nursery workers. WeCount!’s advocacy on extreme heat is the subject of the new documentary, Without Shade, Without Rest by Six Eye Films and Working Films. This documentary tells the story of two organizations, WeCount! and the Coalition of Immokalee Workers, and our efforts to win heat protections for Florida’s outdoor workers. In the face of intense industry lobbying and aggressive state preemption, the fight in Florida continues. Their work has helped put extreme heat in the national conversation and inspired advocacy for workplace heat standards across the country. 

While “Without Shade, Without Rest” is primarily focused on Florida, we believe this film can be a helpful tool for workers, advocates, organizations, and community members across the country and world, who are similarly grappling with the growing and existential threat of climate change and extreme heat. We hope the film helps shine a light on an urgent labor and human rights issue and contributes to meaningful dialogue and connections across our movements. In Asheville, a new campaign Planting Justice (Sembrando Justicia) is being launched by WeCount! and local partners in support of workers in the house plant industry who work locally with little labor protections. The food we eat and the plants we enjoy are nothing without the workers who plant and nurture them.

events.title: Phone Bank Party in Lansing for Will Lawrence and Abdul El-Sayed

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
## Come phone bank with your neighbors, friends and SURJ!

We are now in a decisive phase of the fight against authoritarianism, the threat is real and the stakes are high. And people are fighting back. Millions have protested, and we've watched powerful organizing coming out of Minneapolis, Chicago, and other cities that have borne the brunt of ICE's assaults on our communities. Mass anger exists, but mass organization does not yet exist at the scale needed to win. Movements become real when they reach millions: organized, trained, and acting together.

The stage for the midterm elections is set, and the stakes for our movement and democracy couldn't be higher.

**Join SURJ in doing our part to help flip the House and Senate and block MAGA while sending a crop of true movement champions to Congress.**

Come as you are! No experience needed! Full training & lots of support included!

## Logistics:

- We're gathering to phone bank together at the address for this event (sent via email when you register). 
- You will log into a program with a script on your computer and bring your phone to make the calls (if you only have one device, still come!).
We have a robust training to give you all the information you need  — a script, technical support, and coaching throughout.
- People who have phone banked with SURJ before (Returners) can start early.
- You will receive an email with orientation materials ahead of time.

## Feeling Unsure?

- Our model works - learn from the best! Our phone banks have one of the highest rates of success in the country. No matter whether you're brand new caller or a seasoned organizer, if you join our banks, you can trust that you are putting your effort into a method that works. And you'll get to learn powerful organizing skills from seasoned leaders!
- Our conversations are based on open-ended questions and deep listening. You do not need to be an expert on the issues or a candidate - our phone banks are successful because we deeply connect with voters and make them feel heard.
- Want to hear what a phone bank is like? Ask your host to talk about their experience!

## Context:

As Trump and republicans defund the social safety net and peddle more racist lies, millions of people are increasingly feeling the effects of the billionaire agenda. We know this fight is on multiple fronts, and this fall we have an opportunity to harness the energy of the streets and rising resentment towards November’s elections – to not only wrest power from MAGA, but to put candidates in office who are willing to stand up to Trump and fight for working class people. BOTH the House AND Senate are in play for Democrats to take back control and this year we aim to put progressive working class champions in a position to WIN.

For the last six years, SURJ’s phone banking program has grown to be one of the strongest in the country, reaching millions of working class people with our vision of finding our shared interest in standing alongside people of color and rejecting white supremacy. This year is an opportunity to deliver strategic blows to the MAGA agenda and throw down a gauntlet to force the Democratic Party to reckon with true progressive, working class fighters.

To do this, protecting or flipping key Senate seats in North Carolina, Georgia, Maine and Mississippi and flipping critical house seats in Michigan 7, Tennessee 9 and California 22.

These races will affect millions of working class people this year. Riding the high from many wins for progressive champions throughout primary season, we are well positioned to send some of these same folks to the halls of Congress. We will continue to build power to stop MAGA, by supporting unapologetically progressive working class champions, while showing up in key races to block MAGA and showing up in solidarity alongside Black racial justice leaders in the south who are fighting back and beginning the long-build back from the gutting of the VRA. Alongside our partners across the country, this is the time for our movements to offer a bold vision and bring our people into it.

### About SURJ:

Showing Up for Racial Justice (SURJ) is the largest organization in the country that explicitly organizes white communities for justice. Instead of choosing racism, silence, or complicity, we help white communities choose justice. We have thousands of national members and 150+ chapters across the US and Canada.

events.title: ROCHESTER+ Vote WFP 2026 EDAY Canvass/Poll Site Visibility
events.description:
### ELECTION DAY is TUESDAY NOV 3rd, and we need YOUR help in getting out the vote for the Working Families Party ballot line! 

Join us across MONROE COUNTY to talk to voters either at their door or on their way to the polls! Pick an area when you sign-up and we'll follow-up to confirm whether you prefer to canvass door to door or do poll site visibility at a priority site.

The only way we protect our democracy from Trump and MAGA’s power grab is by organizing together to defend our votes. **Here’s the bottom line: There’s a lot at stake in this election.**

First, we must get hundreds of thousands of votes on the WFP line for Kathy Hochul to keep existing as a party and to block MAGA Republican Bruce Blakeman.

This election is not just about defeating Blakeman — it's also about sending a clear message to Kathy Hochul and all of our elected officials that we want a government that centers working families and the urgent need for a more affordable New York for everyone.

### Never done canvassing/poll site visibility before? No worries!! We will get you trained up and ready to go.

_If you’re not able to participate in canvassing/poll site visibility and want to help turnout voters, join our Vote WFP phone banks on Mondays @ 6-8pm → [SIGN UP!](https://mobilize.us/s/gB5FFs)_

events.title: Indivisible Community Meeting - Defend Election Results
events.description:
This a local Indivisible event hosted by Defend Democracy Indivisible.

While polls appear somewhat favorable, there is no assurance that court room shenanigans and other obstructionist actions by the disgruntled and desperate will not happen 

The Indivisible coalition is asking folks to be ready to defend the results.  This meeting will discuss what that means for us locally and how we are planning as a group to be prepared for possible calls for peaceful resistance.

And, with a bit of hopefulness, we will also be enjoying cookies and music and socializing (meeting, greeting, exchanging resistance stories) with each other. 

We have all done so much since the beginning of this election cycle - postcards, canvass, volunteering at the polls, $$'s -- we should stop and enjoy a moment in time where we rest and recharge.  Hope you can join us

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Salmonberry Trail Special Art Installation- Opening Reception!
events.description:
The Salmonberry Trail is hosting an art show in collaboration with the local non-profit, One Room Studios. We will also be featuring local "On the Trail" Artists to further the Salmonberry Trail's mission to connect local businesses to the greater community!

Jeff Beers will be featuring his collection "Paper and Raincoat" on the first floor of the Salmonberry Trail Office. On the second floor, we will be featuring local trail artists Alison Graves from Buxton Hill Farms, and Richard Knight of Richard Knight Studios in Timber.

### Gallery Hours (Thurs Nov 12 through Sat Nov 21):

- Opening Reception is Thursday, November 12 from 5-8PM
- Thursday and Friday from 5-8PM
- Saturday from 12-8PM


#### About the Artists:

##### Jeff Beers:
"“Paper & Raincoat” are the two main ingredients of a new series that unfolds like a myth cycle of life and death. Beers painstakingly made it out of scraps of thin sheets of paper that he’s aged for 30 years, and surplus raincoat material from Columbia Sportswear. (Beers got the latter from the local nonprofit SCRAP Creative Reuse.) After 16 months of meticulous work, these two simple ingredients have found cosmic depths in this series of 8 pieces."

##### Alison Graves:

"Set in the foothills of the Coast Range, Buxton Hills Farm is an 80-acre historic homestead and small woodland. The naturally abundant land, originally the homeland of the Atfalatl and Kalapuya people, remains home to deer and elk, owls and hawks, newts and frogs, bobcats and coyotes. Since the early 1900s the farm has been home to the Genzers, Raffertys, Wilsons, Mitchells and now the Graves family. Along the way the families have grown strawberries, prunes, hazelnuts, dairy cows and Christmas trees.

Since 2015 we have cultivated the small woodland for recreation and wildlife, with an emphasis on sharing the land with friends and family to learn about forestry and farming while having fun. We partner with organizations that share our interests to celebrate the seasons and learn together about the plants and animals that call this place home."


##### Richard Knight:

"Richard Knight Gallery is a craft store you should certainly visit, as you're sure to find something that will catch your attention. I offer a variety of wooden boxes, metal rose's(copper, steel and brass), beaded necklaces, pearls, and jade. I make use of a variety of sturdy materials in my crafts, but some things remain consistent in all my designs – a keen eye for detail and impeccable design, for starters."

Hosted by Lucinda and sponsored by SMCDP.  Join us for a fire pit and potluck to pause, come together, reflect back on the pivotal election year, and look forward to the coming winter and holiday season.  

We can dwell on what went right, what lessons we learned from what didn't, our candidates' sacrifices, and the campaign supporters' hard work.

This is a non-alcoholic, lower-the-vibe, re-group, and re-energize event.  Musicians welcome.  If any hand drummers come, you are welcome to use mine and help further entrain our gathering.

Please note your carry-in dish on the signup.  Thank you!

Party members and friends from surrounding counties are also welcome to attend.

Come stare at fire with friends and get your spark back. ~ Lucinda

events.title: Barbara Jordan Leadership Institute/Praire View Party at the Polls!
events.description:
LET’S PARTY AT THE POLLS! 🗳️💜

Celebrate our community. Cast your vote.

We’re bringing civic engagement to the Hill! Join the Barbara Jordan Leadership Institute (BJLI) at Prairie View A&M University for our March to the Polls! We’re bringing students and community members together to celebrate civic participation, build community, and make our voices heard.

This is more than a march — it’s an opportunity to come together, exercise our civic power, and encourage our community to participate in the democratic process.

THE VIBE:

We’re bringing the energy, the community, and the Panther pride! Join BJLI as we rally students, connect with fellow Panthers, and march to the polls together. Whether you’re voting for the first time or are a seasoned voter, this is your chance to be part of a collective effort to make civic participation a priority.

WHERE & WHEN:

📍 Prairie View A&M University — Prairie View, Texas

📅 Date: 11/03/2026

⏰ Time: 12:00pm-1:30pm

FEATURING:

💜 March to the Polls — Walk together in support of civic engagement and voter participation.

🗳️ Voter Education & Engagement — Connect with the Barbara Jordan Leadership Institute and learn more about participating in the electoral process.

🤝 Campus & Community Engagement — Bring your friends, fellow students, and neighbors together for an event centered on civic pride and community involvement.

🐾 Panther Pride, Our Voices, Our Future — Celebrate the power of participation and the importance of making your voice heard.

LET’S MARCH TO THE POLLS TOGETHER!

Bring a friend, bring your Panther pride, and join the Barbara Jordan Leadership Institute as we show up for our community. Let’s make civic engagement a movement!

Any food, entertainment, buttons, stickers, or any other free items at this event are available to voters and non-voters alike. This is a nonpartisan event. 💜🗳️

events.title: FINAL FOUR - Monday Canvass: Dan Osborn for US Senate - Scottsbluff
events.description:
Come join other volunteers as we knock on doors and talk to voters about Dan Osborn! We're in the last few days for Election Day and we need your help to talk to your neighbors about getting out the vote. Every conversation is going to make a difference in this close race.

Whether you’re a seasoned canvasser or brand new to volunteering, you are welcome here. We will provide a complete training session, your canvassing list, and all the materials you need before you head out. If you've never used miniVAN or need a quick refresher, our team will get you fully prepared.

Bring a friend, wear comfortable walking shoes, and let’s power our community through the finish line!1

What to Bring: - A smartphone with the miniVAN app downloaded (optional, but helpful) - Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing - Water and a lot of energy!

events.title: November Community Gathering
events.description: This a local Indivisible event!  Welcome to our 13th Community Gathering in Lynchburg.  Our Community Gathering is part of Indivisible Lynchburg where we gather to develop and/or implement non-violent resistance and non-cooperation strategies in response to the Trump regime's would-be authoritarianism.  A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.  Along with strategies, we find and build community and, with it, courage to stand in support of our democracy.  Newcomers/first-timers are more than welcome; we need you.

events.title: Election Night Watch Party!
events.description:
We’ve done all the work in community. So, it certainly seems fitting to spend this evening in community too! Whether you just want to stop by for a couple of minutes or stay for a couple of hours, it will be great to be together!
This an unstructured event. No speakers. No work. We’ve done it all for today. Now, just good conversation and a chance to whine and dine together with occasional results reported.

Fate Brewing has graciously given us the opportunity to spend this evening  together. So if you’re going to eat or drink anywhere this evening, this seems like place to do it. 

Please bear in mind that the gallery room (with the TV) may not have enough seating for all. We’ll have plenty of additional seating at tables and booths right outside this space, where we can linger at tables with friends.

Please be thoughtful and signup if you can join us and cancel if your plans change. It’s essential for Fate’s planning and ours.

A core principle behind all Desert Democracy events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: HB4Democracy Fall Community Kickback
events.description:
# Community Potluck Picnic

**Saturday, November 7th | 11:00 – 1:00 PM**
**Triangle Park**
521 Main St, Huntington Beach

---

Come out and share a meal, a laugh, and a little sunshine with your neighbors. This is a free, casual gathering open to everyone — bring your people and help us grow our community right here in Huntington Beach.

---

## What to Expect

Good food, good company, and a relaxed afternoon at one of HB's favorite outdoor spots. This is a great chance to connect with fellow attendees from **No Kings Vote Early at the Pier** and our **weekly Sunday rally at City Hall** — familiar faces and new friends alike.

We will have **beverages and water on hand**, plus a **button-making station** that is equal parts activity for the kids and irresistible for crafty adults.

---

## What to Bring

- **A potluck dish** — pick your favorite thing to share with the crowd
- **A picnic blanket** — claim your patch of grass and get comfortable
- **Games and activities** — frisbees, soccer balls, board games, whatever you love
- **Friends and family** — the more the merrier

---

## About the Host

This event is hosted by **HB4Democracy**, a proud city team of **@OCIndivisible** — a local group committed to building a stronger, more connected community right here in Huntington Beach.

---

*Come hungry, come curious, and come ready to have a good time.*

events.title: Phonebank for Veronicka Vega - District 49 deserves a Working Families Champion!
events.description:
**Woonsocket and North Smithfield deserve leadership that puts constituents first.**

Jon Brien has held this seat since 2022. He calls himself an Independent. But his record is defined by one idea: "we can only pay for the government we can afford, not the government we want."  This manifests in leaving problems unsolved, to preserve corporate interests.

Veronicka Vega disagrees. She experienced homelessness, lived in a motel, and worked her way through school. She now works in housing policy and has spent her career fighting for the things District 49 actually needs: affordable housing, fully funded schools, and local businesses that stay. She is the true working class champion that Woonsocket and North Smithfield deserve. 

We need you to help us reach voters in HD 49. This race will be won or lost by whether we talk to enough neighbors.

**What to expect:**

This is a virtual phone bank! After you sign up, a link will be provided for you to join from your computer or phone. 

No experience needed! We’ll train you and will be there to help!

events.title: Love as Action: Eugene, OR
events.description:
# Love as Action: Resisting Authoritarianism

### Quaker public witness has stood in opposition to cruel and authoritarian actions in our country before. It is time for us to show this love in action again. 

Please join the American Friends Service Committee and Eugene area Friends to bear witness and show resistance to the authoritarian actions in our country. 

On Monday November 9 at 11:00am we will gather at Eugene Federal Building for one hour of silent public worship.

Our hope is that our presence will give hope to all who see us – to show that we can choose resistance - and remind everyone of our moral obligations to one another.

We gather monthly in communities across the country, showing our communities love in action as a public witness of our Quaker values in a time of rising fascism.

Join us! 

To find our more about Love as Action nationally and get more resources visit us at [afsc.org/love-action](www.afsc.org/love-action)

location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Join us on Tuesday November 3rd for an Election Night Watch Party!  It is an important year, both locally and nationally.  We will watch (and celebrate) the results for local candidates like State Rep Kenny Nguyen and State Senator William Lindstedt, the numerous local and State ballot initiative's, and critical House and Senate races nationwide.  This promises to be an exciting night of food, drinks, and conversation.

The party starts at 6:00 PM!  RSVP for location.

events.title: African-American Caucus
events.description: The purpose of the Caucus is to engage African-American Georgia Democrats in the political and legislative processes and within the party; ensure appropriate African-American representation in party positions; and to recruit and support candidates who are committed to the concerns of African-Americans.

events.title: Party at the Polls: Ward 3, Division 18, 10:00 AM to 11:15 AM

events.title: Get Out the Vote in Fitchburg with Team Massachusetts!
events.description:
Team Massachusetts is launching a series of door-knocking canvasses across the Commonwealth to reelect Governor Healey, Lt. Governor Driscoll, Senator Markey, and Democrats up and down the ballot.

The 6pm and 8pm shifts will not be door knocking, but just putting doorhangers on doors!

We're building the grassroots organizing effort that will power Democratic victories across Massachusetts, and we want you to be a part of it. Together, we'll have conversations with voters, identify supporters for Democrats, and help to make sure voters have a plan to vote this November.

We'll begin with a brief training, where you'll receive your turf, materials, and everything you need to hit the doors with confidence. Whether it's your first time canvassing or your hundredth, we'll make sure you have the tools and support you need.

Electing Democrats up and down the ballot is how we continue delivering results for Massachusetts. We need all hands on deck.

We can't wait to see you there.

events.title: Texas Together Block Walk: GOTV ELECTION EVE-Green Oaks-Arlington
events.description:
### Join Texas Together in Southeast Arlington as we ramp up the action to Get Out The Vote and knock doors to support **Texas Democratic** nominees up and down the ballot. 

It’s time to organize, unify, and build the movement that will carry us through the last 31 days until Election Day, November 3, 2026.

During the block walk, volunteers will:

- Identify Democratic supporters

- Share information about our Democratic ticket

- Listen to voters about the issues impacting their families and communities

Every door knocked strengthens our grassroots efforts and brings us one step closer to winning up and down the ballot.

No experience necessary! We’ll provide training, materials, and turf at the start of each shift. 

Just bring comfortable shoes, a fully charged phone, water, and a friend.
**RSVP today and be part of the team building Democratic wins in Texas — one conversation at a time.**

events.description:
Description

This is an opportunity for new members to meet current members and learn about volunteer opportunities, upcoming events, and more.  This is also a great time to bring your friends and neighbors into the fight for Democracy. Polls show that Democrats and Republicans agree on a lot of the issues that are closest to our hearts: belief in the right to fair housing, gas, and food costs, and the need to ensure we can all afford good healthcare when we need it. No one wants the wars, and no one knows why they need a mega data center in the field behind their house.
Politicians have had their fun with us, stirring up senseless division. But now it is more important than ever to hold their feet to the fire until we get the government we all want, one that listens and responds to those who fund it. And no one wants their government funded by a handful of corporations and billionaires. We have seen how quickly our rights and freedoms erode under that sort of tyranny. Let's come together en masse and plan for our future, as citizens of this one country. Not to make it anything, "AGAIN", because there have always been troubles. But to make it like new, where every spice in this melting pot brings its own flavor, creating something truly spectacular.

The election is over, but as important as it was, it was only our MidTerm. Let's come together and discuss what is next. Of course, we will follow the national Indivisible guidelines, but locally, what do we face over the next two years?

###Bearing Witness, Building Hope
Quaker public witness has stood in opposition to cruel and authoritarian actions in and by our country in the past when the need arises. We must show this love in action again.

Please join Birmingham Friends Meeting to bear witness to the values of peace and compassion and to show our resistance to authoritarian actions across our country.

On the second Saturday of each month at 11 am we will gather at the street corner next to the Royal Oak Farmer's Market for one hour of silent public worship.

Our belief is that our presence will give hope to all who see us – to show that we can choose both love and resistance - and remind everyone of our moral obligations to one another.

Alongside the American Friends Service Committee, we gather monthly in communities across the country, showing our love in action as a public witness of our Quaker values in a time of rising abuses of power and injustice.

Join us!

To find our more about Birmingham Friends Meeting, visit https://birminghamfriendsmi.org/

events.title: Election Night Virtual Watch Party on Zoom
events.description:
# ELECTION NIGHT 2026

**Every Vote Counts! Every Voice Matters!**

## CBFD Indivisible Virtual Election Night Watch Party

**Tuesday, November 3, 2026**
**Time:** 6:00 PM – 10:00 PM Pacific
**Location:** Online via Zoom**
**Hosted by:** CBFD Indivisible

## Democracy Is Worth Showing Up For!

The votes are in, the polls are closing, and Election Night is here!

Join CBFD Indivisible for a virtual Election Night Watch Party as we come together to follow the 2026 midterm election results, connect with fellow community members, and celebrate civic participation.

Whether you're joining from your couch, kitchen table, or with a group of friends, you're invited!

## What to Expect

- **Live Election Coverage:** Follow national, California, and San Diego election results.
- **Election Updates:** Important races, ballot measures, and developing results.
- **Community Connection:** Share reactions, reflections, and experiences.
- **Interactive Trivia:** Test your knowledge of democracy and elections.
- **Election Protection Updates:** Learn about election integrity, ballot counting, and how to stay informed.
- **What's Next?** Discuss ways to stay connected and engaged after Election Night.

## Proposed Evening Schedule

**6:00 PM – Welcome & Virtual Social Hour**
Meet fellow participants, share Election Day experiences, and enjoy democracy trivia.

**6:30 PM – Live Election Watch Begins**
National and local election coverage, updates, and community discussion.

**7:00 PM – California Polls Close**
Follow early reporting as California polls close at 8:00 PM Pacific; discuss what to watch for.

**8:00 PM – California Polls Close**
Watch initial California results and discuss ballot-counting timelines.

**8:30 PM – Election Protection & What's Next**
Updates on election protection resources, peaceful civic engagement, and community next steps.

**9:30–10:00 PM – Closing Remarks**
Results may still be developing. Stay informed, connected, and engaged.

## Bring Your Election Night Essentials!

Your favorite snacks, beverages, comfortable clothes, and enthusiasm for democracy!

events.description:
Join us for a vigil altar and picnic. We will honor with a tree of hope, marigolds, photos, and food. We will honor those who have passed by ICE and detentions camps, while including our own loved ones by bringing their favorite foods to enjoy during the picnic. We will include some last activity reminders for "getting out the vote" before Election Day on November 3rd.
This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

We'll gather and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: Poll Greeter Training -- Online
events.description:
**Online Training for Poll Greeters--Optional** 

Would you like to support all of our Democratic candidates on November 3rd by training to be a Democratic Poll Greeter? Have you done it before but want to brush up on what it takes? Or, come share your experience as a greeter! Join our campaign's Poll Greeter Training!

Each election, local Democratic Party committees staff a greeting table outside each polling place. We want to make sure you feel comfortable as a poll greeter in your precinct. And we are working to staff any areas where local greeters are not available. We may ask you to drive some distance to a polling location that needs you. 

Greeters welcome voters at each polling place, providing accurate information before a voter enters the actual polling place, and appreciation after they vote.

If you would like to volunteer to greet, we are offering brief online training in the week before the election. **Sign up for just ONE of the online sessions--every session covers the same material.**

This training is completely optional--you do not need it to serve as a greeter. In fact, the best training may be to partner with an experienced greeter. However, for those new to the job or who might otherwise find it helpful, it will give you much of what you need.

This session is virtual. Registrants will receive a google meet link by email at registration, and will need an internet browsing device (like a smart phone or computer), and internet access.

events.title: Battery Energy Storage 101: Understanding the Technology and Its Role in Our Clean Energy Future

sponsor.name: New Jersey League of Conservation Voters

events.description:
Battery energy storage systems are becoming an increasingly important part of our clean energy future, helping store electricity and make it available when it’s needed most. But as battery storage expands, questions and misconceptions about the technology can create barriers to adoption.

Join us for an educational webinar exploring the basics of battery energy storage, how these systems work, and the important role they play in building a cleaner, more reliable energy grid. We’ll address common questions and safety concerns, separate fact from fiction, and discuss why expanding energy storage is critical to supporting New Jersey’s clean energy goals.

Whether you’re a concerned resident, policymaker, or clean energy advocate, this webinar will provide the information you need to better understand battery storage and its benefits.

No knocking. No conversations. No experience necessary! Just stop by Democratic HQ, grab a stack of door hangers and an assigned route, and hit the doors. It's that easy!

On Monday, we'll be reminding voters that TOMORROW IS ELECTION DAY! On Tuesday, we're making one final push to remind everyone that TODAY IS THE DAY TO VOTE!

events.title: 2026 Dare County GOTV Phone Bank
events.description:
## Join us in making a real difference in this election!
 
Our phone bank is open to everyone—whether you have 30 minutes or a few hours to spare. You can log in and start making calls anytime between 9:00 AM and 8:00 PM, any day of the week right up through Election Day. 
Every call you make helps make sure our neighbors have a clear plan to vote, access to rides to the polls, and the encouragement they need to turn out. No experience is necessary, and we provide all the training and scripts you need to get started. Sign up today and help us drive the vote!


**What you’ll need & how to prepare:**

A computer or tablet to view the phone banking system (OpenVPB) and screen script.

A phone to make the calls.

Optional Prep:  If you'd like a quick preview of how the system works, watch this [Open Virtual Phone Bank Tutorial Video.](https://youtu.be/YVhBQlhLSIs?si=omAh4t1C8y5XSGSd)

events.title: Help your friends and family make a plan to vote!
events.description:
Talking to the people you know is one of the most powerful things you can do this election. People trust information more when it comes from someone they know than from an ad or a stranger. You can make those conversations happen on your own schedule.

Your network reaches further than you think. Whether it be a college roommate in Michigan or a cousin in North Carolina, the people in your life who live in battleground states and districts could help decide control of the House and Senate. You don’t need to live in a swing state to help elect a Congress that will put a check on Trump’s corrupt agenda.


**What to expect**

After you sign up, you can use our relational tool, Rally, to track the conversations with your friends and family.

You’ll also receive an email with the
[step-by-step guide](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1hEA6AMoU9XeUTylWj5ZQDmKvktM4MzK3wpUwzhDmmAA/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.bxwal297v5dh) to using Rally. 

Reach out to your people whenever you have a few minutes. Every person you help get to the polls makes a difference!

**What you'll need**

Your phone and a few minutes to think about who’s in your life. No experience necessary.

Have questions? Join a live relational training: https://www.mobilize.us/standupamerica/event/1059696/

events.title: No Kings Post-Election Call: What Happened
events.description:
In the event of election interference or sabotage, the No Kings movement will gather on November 4 to share real-time updates, align on the election defense strategy, and provide clear next steps for attendees to take in defense of democracy. 

Save the date for this call in case we need to gather together as a movement in a rapid response scenario. If there is no need to share critical election interference or sabotage updates, we will notify you. In that case, the call will likely be canceled and we will share other avenues for receiving updates from the No Kings coalition.  

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action and no civil disobedience. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values, and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events. All events should be held in public spaces or on public property.
No Kings events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*By registering for this event, you agree: (1) that Indivisible and ACLU can contact you about No Kings and other ways to take action or support their organizations and otherwise use any data collected from or about you on this form according to the applicable privacy policy: Indivisible Privacy Policy (https://indivisible.org/privacy-policy) and ACLU's Privacy Statement (https://www.aclu.org/about/privacy/statement); and (2) subject to its privacy policy, Indivisible may also share the information you provide to other No Kings partner organizations, which may also contact you.*

In CA-48, help us replace the ulta-Trumpy outgoing Rep. Darrell Issa with a strong Democratic candidate who will fight for California families. Marni von Wilpert is ready to go to work for working families, older adults, and ALL Americans!

Gather with like-minded activists from the Los Angeles area to make a difference in the November election, reunite with old acquaintances, and make some new friends!  The WDHQ is the best place to be in the days before Election Day.

Whether you’re a seasoned phoner or brand new, you’ll be supported every step of the way by our in-house phone bank coordinators. We use a dialer call system to make the calls more efficient.

events.title: WTF Happened?! California WFP's 2026 Post-Election Debrief
events.description:
California WFP's 2026 Post-Election Debrief

The votes are in, the dust is settling, and it's time to talk about WTF just happened in the 2026 elections.

California Working Families Party went into this election with our biggest slate of candidates in history, endorsing more than 220 candidates up and down the ballot, from school boards and city councils to Congress and statewide office.

After months of organizing, knocking doors, making calls, and taking on billionaires and corporate special interests, we're bringing our WFP community together to unpack the results.

What happened? What surprised us? What did we win? What did we learn? And what the hell comes next?

Join California WFP leaders, organizers, and members from across the state for an honest, unfiltered conversation about the 2026 election results. We'll break down the biggest races, celebrate victories, discuss setbacks, and reflect on what this election means for the future of working-class politics in California.

Whether you're feeling fired up, frustrated, hopeful, or just trying to make sense of it all, this conversation is for you.

Tuesday, November 10 | 6:00 PM PT | Zoom

Come ready to celebrate, reflect, ask questions, and talk about what's next.

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
# Get on the Bus, Get Organized! 🚌✊

With the midterms behind us, it’s time to lock in to win dedicated transit funding in 2027! Every conversation with a fellow rider or transit operator is a chance to build connections, grow our movement, and organize. If we want to restore and expand transit service across the Commonwealth, we need all hands on deck!

Join **Pittsburghers for Public Transit (PPT)’s Organizing Committee** for a monthly canvassing series to connect with our communities, talk about the issues impacting transit riders, and build people power for the transit system we deserve.

**Our first mission?** Making public transit a top priority for Pennsylvania’s governor!

**Never canvassed before? No problem!** Whether you’re a first-timer or a seasoned organizer, there’s a place for you. Come meet fellow transit advocates, talk with your community, and help build the grassroots power we need to win.

**Let’s get organized! Ride with us and fight for better transit for everyone!**


**Are you a confident canvasser willing to lead a small group of canvassers on the bus?** Volunteer to be a Canvass Lead - support a small group of canvassers by making sure folks don’t get lost and board the correct buses, and have the chance to debrief after their ride. Think this might be you, but need more information? Awesome! You can select either option as you register for your canvassing session. 


## What to expect

- **Training and practice** will take place at the beginning of each event.
- **Small groups** of canvassers will be led by an experienced Canvass Lead to various bus stops in the downtown area.
- **Bus rides and bus stops** are where canvassing will take place. Canvassers will ride the bus for about 30 minutes outbound, then return back downtown.
- **Social hour** afterwards will serve as the space to debrief, compare notes and connect with one another.

### Accessibility

While PPT will work to create a comfortable environment for participants, there may be barriers to participation. We cannot guarantee the accessibility of bus stops or the bus. Buses may be loud and crowded. We cannot obtain ASL for these events.

events.title: Defend Democracy Demonstration
events.description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Join Mobilize Arcata for our Weekly Demonstration on the Plaza.

The Trump regime violates the constitution and breaks countless laws on a daily basis. Our community has to stand up and demand accountability. Impeachment, Conviction, Removal. No less.

This regime has to be stopped. We have to defeat the fascists! Our neighbors need our support. Our democratic leaders need to hear from us. Come out for solidarity and make your voices heard in defense of democracy.

Especially now, the weeks following Election Day will be important to show our readiness to respond  to attempts of election sabotage. We need to defend not only the vote count but also the vote certification and ultimately the seating of the next Congress: Our votes shall be heard!

Every Saturday @ Noon next to the Jacoby's Storehouse.


*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Brown County Dems November Meal & General Meeting at West High Commons

location.venue: West High School Commons - park in the lot east of school

events.description:
Celebrate, Connect & Shape Our Future! 💙

Brown County Democrats November 19 General Meeting

Our work is just beginning! 

Join us as we celebrate our November 3rd election victories, recognize the incredible people who made them possible, and turn our energy toward building an even stronger County Party in 2027 and beyond!

6:00 PM – Potluck Dinner & Fellowship

6:30 PM – General Meeting

This is a meeting you won't want to miss! Together, we'll:

Celebrate our wins! Recognize our candidates, volunteers, and campaign teams.

- Nominate our next leaders! We'll accept nominations for the following, who will serve through December of 2028:
Chair
First Vice Chair
Second Vice Chair
Treasurer
Secretary

Elections will take place at our December meeting.

- Build our future! Share ideas, set goals, and explore how Brown County Dems can make a meaningful difference in our communities in 2027 and beyond.

- Grow our volunteer teams! Find your fit, share your talents, and help turn these great ideas into action.

- Recruit our next candidates! Begin identifying and supporting candidates for the April 6, 2027, spring election.

 - Submit names of outstanding volunteers to be recognized at our December 17th meeting.

Please come with ideas! 

Before the meeting, please take a few minutes to read the 2026 Democratic Party of Wisconsin Platform. Think about how we can put our values into action through community involvement, public service, and year-round organizing.  

https://wisdems.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/DPW-2026-Platform-Platform-Adopted-by-Convention-on-14-June-2026.pdf 

Important membership reminder: You must be a current party member to run for leadership or vote in December's leadership elections. Please renew or join before then!

 https://secure.actblue.com/donate/bcd-membership

We especially encourage sustaining memberships, with automatic monthly contributions, so your membership can stay current without annual renewal worries.

We're building more than an organization. We're building a community of people who care, show up, and get things done locally.

Bring a dish if you can, bring your ideas, and bring a friend! Everyone is welcome.

Note: We're meeting one week early because of Thanksgiving!

events.description:
oin Arizona Faith Network for Food at the Polls on Election Day!

Starting at 5:00 PM, we're bringing free food directly to communities across Arizona through pop-up food distributions for voters and community members.

Date: Tuesday, November 3, 2026
Time: 5:00 PM
Cost: Free and open to all

events.title: Brown County Dems December Meal & General Meeting at West High

location.venue: West High School Commons - park in the lot east of school

events.description:
Celebrate 2026! Elect Our Leaders! Build Our Future! 💙

Brown County Democrats December Meal, General Meeting & Year-End Celebration

What a year we've had! From knocking doors and making calls to organizing events, connecting with neighbors, supporting candidates, and building community, 2026 has been a year of extraordinary people doing extraordinary things!

Now it's time to celebrate—and choose the leaders who will guide us through the next two years!

6:00 PM – Community Potluck Dinner & Fellowship

6:30 PM – General Meeting, Officer Elections & Celebration

Here's what's happening:

Elect Our Party Leadership! We'll elect our Chair, First Vice Chair, Second Vice Chair, Treasurer, and Secretary for the next two years. Each candidate will have two minutes to introduce themselves before voting begins.

Celebrate Our People! Enjoy a photographic look back at 2026 as we recognize the committees, teams, and volunteers who made so much happen. From the spotlight to behind the scenes, every contribution matters!

Give Some Special Thanks! We'll recognize individuals whose dedication, creativity, generosity, and hard work helped make this year memorable.

Celebrate Our Community! Enjoy good food, friendship, and the company of people who have worked together toward a shared purpose.

Look Ahead to 2027! Meet our newly elected leadership team and look forward to another year of service, community engagement, and making a difference in Brown County.

IMPORTANT MEMBERSHIP REMINDER

To vote in our officer elections, you must be a current Democratic Party member. Please join or renew your membership in advance to help make check-in and voting run smoothly.

 https://secure.actblue.com/donate/bcd-membership

We encourage everyone to consider a sustaining membership, with convenient monthly contributions that help keep your membership evergreen while supporting our work year-round.

Come hungry, bring a dish if you can, and bring your enthusiasm! 

Whether you've volunteered hundreds of hours or are just getting involved, you're part of our Dems community, and we'd love to celebrate with you.

Together, we've accomplished so much. 
Just imagine what we can do next! 💙

Everyone is welcome! Current party membership is required to vote in officer elections, but membership is not required to attend this meeting.

We’ve knocked the doors, made the calls, and sent the postcards. Now let’s celebrate together!

Join Lauren and the team at Second Line Brewing in Mid-City on Tuesday, Nov. 3rd to watch the results come in live. Whether you’ve been with us since day one or are just getting involved, everyone who helped power this campaign is welcome.

Before you come: If you haven’t voted yet, make a plan to get to the polls before they close! And if you can, sign up for an Election Day shift. Every last voter contact counts.

It’s time to organize, unify, and build the movement that will carry us on Election Day, November 3, 2026.

During the block walk, volunteers will:

- Identify Democratic supporters

- Share information about our Democratic ticket

- Listen to voters about the issues impacting their families and communities

Every door knocked strengthens our grassroots efforts and brings us one step closer to winning up and down the ballot.

No experience necessary! We’ll provide training, materials, and turf at the start of each shift. 

Just bring comfortable shoes, a fully charged phone, water, and a friend.
**RSVP today and be part of the team building Democratic wins in Texas — one conversation at a time.**

events.title: Climate on the Ballot: 2026 Lead Locally Election Debrief
events.description:
2026 is looking to be a HUGE election for the climate movement. Join us to debrief the results with us the night after Election Day! 

You’ve probably heard about the race to flip the Senate. But this November 3rd, voters will also decide some of the most critical down ballot elections on climate, data center regulation, and affordability.

Lead Locally will bringing together our supporters, partners, and volunteers on Nov 4th, the day after the election, to debrief: 

-Did Democrats flip state legislatures in states like Arizona, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin and what does this mean for their work to lower bills by transitioning to clean energy?

-Did pro-climate Democrats win seats or majorities on statewide utility boards in Arizona and Georgia?

-How did climate ballot initiatives fare in Oregon and Colorado?

-What can we learn from these results as we head into elections in 2027 and 2028?

### Election Day is almost here!

 Join us Monday, November 2, for a final Zoom call to make sure everyone is ready to hit the ground running on Tuesday.

We'll go over everything you need to feel prepared and confident for Election Day, including:

- Assignments and locations: Make sure you know where you're supposed to be and when.

- Talking points: Review our key messages and what to say when talking with voters.

- Regional contacts: Connect with your regional Election Day leader and know who to reach out to with questions or issues.

We've spent months working toward this moment, and we're so grateful to have you on our team. Whether you've been volunteering since signature collection or are joining us for the first time, we want to make sure you have everything you need for a successful Election Day.

Join us on Zoom Monday night so we can finish strong on November 3!

events.title: Unhoused 101 - Panel Discussion

location.venue: Unitarian Universalist Church of Greater Lansing

events.description:
You've sensed and seen that there are more homeless people than ever in the Lansing area. You've heard about the horrific murders of homeless men on the River Trail. What do you need to know about all of this? What organizations have been working on housing security all along? What do they do? What challenges are they facing? What can we learn from homeless people themselves? How can we respond as a community in ways that keep us all safe, and also keep people sheltered? Knowledge is power.

Join us for a monumental panel discussion organized by the Lansing Interfaith Vision for Equity (LIVE). Get your questions answered by experts in the Q&A portion. You are guaranteed to leave knowing more than you did when you arrived. 

OUR PANEL:

Advent House - Susan Cancro

Mid-Michigan Tenant Resource Center & NAACP Housing Chair - Khadja Erickson

Punks With Lunch - Kelsea Hector

two individuals who are currently homeless

and more...

If you care about homelessness in our community, you do not want to miss this important event.

You are encouraged to BRING HATS, GLOVES AND/OR SOCKS for donations to Punks With Lunch to distribute to those in need.

events.title: Protest Against Mesa City Council & NTT Mesa PH10 Data Center Campus!
events.description:
### 🚨Protest NTT Mesa PH10 Data Center & the MCC! 🚨

Mesa Valley Indivisible officially teamed up with our sister group, [Indivisible Mesa](https://www.indivisiblemesa.org)—who has been leading the charge against Mesa’s 287(g) agreement and predatory data centers, like the planned 2.2 million sq ft [NTT Mesa PH10 Data Center](https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/no-mesa-ntt-global-ph10-data-center)—to make our voices heard at City Hall.

As public turnout surged, city officials escalated their efforts to quiet community opposition: 

- **On June 8th**, A local activist was physically removed from a council meeting simply for silently holding a small sign. 

- At the next Mesa City Council meeting **on July 17th**, after the indoor sign bans forced us outside, police arrested a peaceful protester for using a megaphone despite the fact that she complied with their demands. She was charged with bogus charges and forced to spend a night in jail...FOR USING A MEGAPHONE. The charges were dropped at her 9/28/2026 court date. k 

- **On August 7th** when Indivisible Mesa recently pressed the City Council coordinator for answers, the city shifted its story yet again! They claimed the councilmembers will not be voting on the data center at all and that NTT can proceed administratively, but only after grassroots pressure began mounting.

If they won't let us show our signs inside, we will make sure they are impossible to ignore on the steps of City Hall. Mesa Valley Indivisible is pivoting this event to an outdoor protest starting at 5:00pm (meeting starts at 5:45pm). We will make our voices heard loud and clear from the outside!

## 📢 Calls to Action:

**Whether or not you can attend, please do the following three things:**

1. [Submit a comment here](https://us.openforms.com/Form/44ff3314-58bb-418a-a122-46fe7725feef)! Feel free to choose one of the concerns listed below if you do not want to write your own comment. 

2. [Email the Mesa City Council members by](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1llwS0FcrAfxBdC1DwOL0hayMQ9SWK1WJkHFZlxXYdQ4/edit?usp=sharing).** Contact info, directions, and scripts/templates provided!

3. [Call the Mesa City Council members](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qedOvsbfPZ9mG1N6BKkc7QvL3XeamSdmvA_oVY7bu8w/edit?usp=sharing)** and use the script provided or your own! 


## 🚨 Important: 

- We do not care whether or not the data center is on the agenda. MVI and other local activists know it is VITAL we voice our disgust every single council meeting in order to make sure they actually listen to their constituents! 


#### 🔑 Key Concerns Driving the Protest:

- Massive Handouts, Tiny Returns: Similarly sized data centers receive over $100 million a year in tax subsidies. That is revenue stolen directly from our local community services and neighborhood improvements.

- Virtually No Job Creation: Despite taking up huge amounts of space, this massive facility will only create 40 to 60 permanent jobs paying $60,000 or less. Compared to advanced manufacturing or bioscience, data centers provide practically zero high-quality jobs per acre.

- We Pay Their Bills: The infrastructure improvements and utility upgrades required for this project will likely be passed on to everyday customers, not the multibillion-dollar company.

- Driving Up Local Costs: Developments like this artificially inflate land costs, making it harder for our local farmers, small businesses, and families looking for affordable housing to survive.

- A 2.2 million-square-foot facility requires an astronomical amount of energy and water to keep its servers cool. In our delicate desert environment, this level of resource consumption is completely unsustainable and directly threatens the capacity of our local utilities.

- This project threatens the safety and peace of our residential areas. The constant, 24/7 roar of massive cooling fans creates severe noise pollution, while the sprawling, windowless buildings will industrialize our local landscape and destroy our community's character.


## 🪧 Sign Ideas:

- We won't be silent!
- No more Mesa Data Centers!
- NO one wants Data Centers!
- Hate data centers = bipartisan 


## 📷 Pictures & Videos
- Make sure to always tag **Mesa Valley Indivisible** on our group [Facebook page](https://www.facebook.com/share/g/1CFYV1DSaT/), [Instagram page](https://www.instagram.com/mesavalleyindivisible/), [BlueSky](https://bsky.app/profile/mesavalleyindivisi.bsky.social), and [TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com/@mesa.valley.indiv)
- Please also include #MesaValleyIndivisible 
- Add all photos & videos to our [Google drive!](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1eV7iB0EtK3MIjyYBNc63tt6FFtljkW0I?usp=drive_link)

Let’s hang out and watch election night results for the Atlanta metro area and beyond! Join us at CreateATL from 8 PM-10 PM to watch those results roll in!

Yes! We will provide some light bites and refreshments.

events.title: Protest ICE Deportations the AROCC Detention Center at Mesa Gateway Airport

address_lines: East Southern Avenue & South Signal Butte Road

events.description:
## 🛫 ICE & AROCC: Stop ICE operations at Mesa Gateway Airport!

For eight months, [Mesa Valley Indivisible](https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/) members and a coalition of groups around the country have been working relentlessly to end Avelo Airlines’ involvement in the unlawful and inhumane deportation of primarily non‑violent immigrants via Mesa Gateway Airport. As a result, Avelo Airlines ended their contract with ICE in January 2026! 

Although Avelo Airlines has left our Mesa Gateway Airport, ICE deportation missions still happen every day and the Arizona Removal Operations Coordination Center (AROCC) continues to operate.

When local lawmakers recently conducted a surprise visit to the Arizona Removal Operations Coordination Center here at Mesa Gateway, they were sickened by what they found. Despite being a transit hub meant for 12-hour stays, people were being held for weeks, packed like sardines on bare concrete floors with no beds or showers. While the administration continues to claim these are short-term facilities, the reality has proven to be gut-wrenching medical neglect and overcrowding.

    
--------------------------------------

## 🔑 Key Concerns Driving the Protest:

- We have compiled public records, congressional oversight letters, and local reporting into one place. 
- Please read our complete [Mesa Valley Indivisible AROCC and ICE Air Deportations Fact Sheet](https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/ice-deportationsarocc) to understand the full scope of our key concerns and see how you can take action.

--------------------------------------
## 🚨 Important! 🚨

- To ensure you receive all necessary information for the upcoming event, please make sure you have officially registered via Mobilize.
- All vital updates—including parking instructions, logistical changes, and additional details—will be sent to the email address provided during registration. 
  - If you have not registered on the platform, we will be unable to send you these updates.
  - Keep an eye out for emails from Mesa Valley Indivisible and check your spam/junk folder if you do not see them!
  - [Mesa Valley Indivisible](https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/) prioritizes strategic visibility to ensure our message reaches the widest possible audience. To keep our movement growing, we protest at high-traffic areas where Mesa residents are most likely to see us and join the cause.

--------------------------------------------

##  ✨Protest Information:

- MVI's goal is to always to pack all 4 corners of the intersection. Please look for the empty spots and fill them!
- Make sure to stand side by side and not behind one another so every driver & the media can see how many attendees are present!
- Please share with friends, family, neighbors, EVERYONE!

--------------------------------------------

## 🪧 Sign Ideas:

Please create signs and graphics that are relevant to ICE deportations & the AROCC! Some ideas include:

- Abolish ICE
- ICE separates families
- AROCC is a humanitarian crisis
- Prison without due process is a concentration camp
- Illegal deportations without due process is human trafficking

--------------------------------------------

events.title: Tyranny Tuesday 11-3-2026: Election Day Call to Action: Ride the Big Blue Wave

location.venue: Bruce R. Thompson Courthouse and Federal Building

events.description:
📣 Tyranny Tuesday • November 3, 2026 • Indivisible Northern Nevada

✊ Election Day Call to Action: Ride the Big Blue Wave

⏰ New time! Tyranny Tuesday is moving from 10:00 to 12:00 because of the end of daylight saving time. 🕛 See you at the new time on November 3! 🗓️

🗳️ This Tyranny Tuesday, Our Protest Is a Ballot

Tuesday, November 3 is Election Day and our next Tyranny Tuesday. 📅 Every week we stand on the corner with our signs. This week, we turn every sign into a vote. 

✊We have marched, rallied, and called our representatives for months. 📢 But there is one place where tyranny has no answer to ordinary people: the ballot box. 🇺🇸 On November 3, we don't just protest power we replace it.

The world has been showing us how it's done. In the last seven months alone, voters in three countries walked into polling stations and walked out with their democracies back. 🌍

🌍 When Citizens Show Up, Strongmen Fall
Hungary: The "Illiberal State" Voted Out
For 16 years, Viktor Orbán was the model for would-be autocrats everywhere the man MAGA held up as a hero. 🏛️ He captured the courts, turned public media into a party mouthpiece, and gerrymandered the districts so the opposition needed roughly 5 points more than him just to win a majority.
It didn't matter. On April 12, Hungarians turned out at about 79%, the highest since the fall of Communism. 🔥 Péter Magyar's Tisza party won about 54% to Fidesz's 37% and a two-thirds majority in parliament. Orbán conceded.
Note this: Vice President JD Vance flew to Hungary the week before the vote to help push Orbán over the finish line. 🇺🇸➡️🇭🇺 Hungarian voters said no anyway. Magyar called the vote a choice between East and West, and between corruption and clean public life. Crowds in Budapest chanted "Russians out!" 🎉

Brazil: Turnout Turned a Loss into a Win
On October 4, Trump ally Flávio Bolsonaro, son of jailed former president Jair Bolsonaro, beat President Lula in the first round, 47% to 45%. 😬 About 33 million Brazilians stayed home, even though voting is compulsory there.
Three weeks later, on October 25, Lula's campaign went after exactly those missing voters in Brazil's biggest states. 🚪 He won the runoff - a comeback no Brazilian presidential candidate had pulled off in nearly four decades. Analysts credit higher turnout. 📈 The lesson: the people who stay home decide elections.

Serbia: Students Beat a Strongman — Just Days Ago
Aleksandar Vučić ruled Serbia for more than a decade. ✋ For nearly two years, students marched against his government. Then, on October 25, they turned their protest into a party list and their marches into votes. 🎓
Turnout jumped about 10 points to nearly 70% the highest since Yugoslavia broke up in 1992. 📊 The Student List won about 53% to Vučić's 40%, and Vučić conceded on election night as fireworks lit up Belgrade. 🎆

Sound familiar? Protest built the movement. Voting finished the job. 💪
Country	Election day	Turnout	Result
Hungary	April 12, 2026	~79% (record since 1989) Orbán out after 16 years
Brazil Oct 25, 2026 (runoff)Higher than round one. Lula comes from behind to beat Trump ally Bolsonaro

Serbia Oct 25, 2026	~69% (record since 1992) Vučić concedes to student movement.

🌊 Why We Need a Big Blue Wave
The Constitution gave Congress the tools to check a president: subpoenas, hearings, the power of the purse, and Senate confirmation. ⚖️ A rubber-stamp Congress has left those tools in the drawer. A Democratic Congress picks them back up on January 3. 🔨

🔍 Accountability for Corruption
With gavels in hand, Democrats can open investigations, put officials under oath, and follow the money. 💰 Every hearing room becomes a place where the public sees what was done in its name. No more "trust us." Show us. 📂

🤝 Rebuilding the Alliances That Made Us a Superpower
America didn't become a superpower alone. 🌐 We built it with allies NATO, our Pacific partners, our trading partners. Dwight Eisenhower, a Republican, was NATO's first Supreme Allied Commander because he knew alliances multiply American strength. 🎖️
This administration has treated those allies like enemies. 🚨 In January, Trump slapped tariffs on eight NATO allies Denmark, Norway, Sweden, France, Germany, the UK, the Netherlands, and Finland because they sent troops to defend Greenland, a NATO ally's territory. The Kremlin welcomed the move as evidence the Western alliance was collapsing. Even Republican Sen. Thom Tillis called the tariffs bad for America, its businesses, and its allies. Trump backed off within weeks but allies remember who threatened them. Every tariff on a friend is a tax on American families and a gift to our adversaries. 🎁

Siding With Putin Against Ukraine
In October, after a call with Vladimir Putin, Trump struck a deal on Russian diesel exports after pressing Ukraine to stop striking the Russian refineries that fuel Putin's war machine. ⛽ A Ukrainian official said Trump's envoys threatened to cut Ukraine off from U.S. support. Putin, meanwhile, would not even commit to restarting peace talks. 🚫
Now Putin is pitching a summit with Trump and China's Xi Jinping to decide Ukraine's fate with no seat for Ukraine. 🪑 Ukraine's foreign minister warned it would only encourage Putin to keep fighting. A Democratic Congress can protect aid to Ukraine, hold hearings on these deals, and remind the world which side America is on. 

🏦 Oversight of Billionaires and Corporations
Big money has bought access, favors, and silence. 💸 A new Congress can subpoena the records, expose the conflicts of interest, and write the laws that put voters not billionaires back in charge of our democracy. 🗽

✅ Your Mission: Vote — and Bring Five
Hungary, Brazil, and Serbia didn't win with one vote each. 🗳️ They won because people brought their neighbors. Brazil proved it: the voters who stayed home in round one decided round two. Midterm turnout is always lower than presidential turnout that gap is where this election will be won or lost. 📉➡️📈

•	☐ 🔎 Check your registration today with the Washoe County Registrar of Voters, the Nevada Secretary of State (nvsos.gov), or vote.gov. Confirm your ballot status and drop-off options there.
•	☐ 🗳️ Vote before you come to Tyranny Tuesday. Wear your "I Voted" sticker to the rally. 🏷️
•	☐ 📱 Text five people tonight — family, friends, neighbors, coworkers. Ask them one question: "What's your plan to vote?" 💬
•	☐ 🚗 Offer a ride to someone who might not make it on their own. 
•	☐ 📬 Mail ballot at home? Fill it out and return it don't let it sit on the counter. 🏠
•	☐ 📣 Share this newsletter in your group chats and on social media. 
💡 Talking tip: Don't lead with politics. Lead with what they care about prices, their kids, their Social Security, their son or daughter in uniform. Then ask: "Will you vote with me?" 🫶

See You on November 3
Hungarians did it.  Brazilians did it. Serbian students did it this very week. Now it's our turn. 🌊
Vote. Bring five. Then meet us at Tyranny Tuesday on Election Day and let's ride the Big Blue Wave together. 💙🗳️✊

📍 Tyranny Tuesday, November 3, 12:00 (new time!) ⏰

📚 Sources
•	AP via NY1: Orbán concedes defeat · European Movement Ireland: Hungarian election facts · AP via WOIO: Vance visit
•	Al Jazeera: Lula's historic win · AP via ITV: Lula's turnout path
•	France 24: Vučić concedes · Al Jazeera: Serbia turnout · 2026 Serbian parliamentary election

events.title: Kick Enterprise Presents: Every Vote Counts – Vote by Mail Phone Bank

sponsor.name: Dr. Letitia Plummer for Harris County Judge

events.description:
Join us Thursday evening for a targeted phone bank focused specifically on Harris County voters who are voting by mail.

With Election Day approaching, our goal is simple: reach vote-by-mail voters, make sure they have the information they need, answer basic questions, and help them understand the steps for successfully completing and returning their ballots.

Volunteers will contact Harris County voters who have requested or received a mail ballot and help connect them with accurate information about:
•	completing and returning their ballot;
•	important vote-by-mail deadlines;
•	tracking the status of their ballot;
•	what to do if they have questions or experience an issue with their ballot.
This is a focused ballot-chase effort designed to reach voters who may already have their ballot in hand but have not yet returned it.
No phone-banking experience is necessary. We’ll provide training, the call list, scripts, guidance, and everything you need to get started.

Joining Us In Person?
Bring your phone or laptop, headphones, and your energy. We’ll provide the training and materials you need to begin making calls.
Complimentary food, refreshments, and adult beverages will be available for volunteers.
Joining Virtually?
All you need is your phone or laptop, headphones, and an internet connection. Registered volunteers will receive instructions for accessing the phone bank remotely.

Whether you have volunteered before or this is your first phone bank, this is an opportunity to help Harris County vote-by-mail voters navigate the final days of the election and make sure they have clear, accurate information about returning their ballots.

Sign up today, choose whether you’ll participate in person or virtually, and help us reach Harris County vote-by-mail voters before Election Day.

This collaborative outreach effort is hosted by The KICK Enterprise Club in partnership with participating campaigns and community volunteers.

events.title: Win a Working Families Majority with Irreplaceable Action Fund!
events.description:
## Phonebank with Irreplaceable and Working Families Party

### Turn out big to check Big Tech and elect champions for working people.

On October 20, over a thousand people across the country walked out to demand real regulation of AI and accountability from Big Tech. From college campuses to communities across the country, people are standing up against billionaires making decisions about our jobs, our health, our privacy, and our future without our say.

**Now we have until Election Day, November 3, to turn that people power into political power.**

That's why Irreplaceable Action Fund is teaming up with Working Families Party and partners across the country to reach voters in must-win congressional and Senate races.

We're calling voters to help elect champions who will fight for working people, take on corporate power, and hold Big Tech accountable:

- Michigan: **Dr. Abdul El-Sayed** is running for U.S. Senate with a bold plan to regulate AI and protect working people. **Will Lawrence** is running for Congress in MI-7 with a proven record of standing up to Big Tech and fighting for stronger safeguards.

- Tennessee: **Justin J. Pearson** is running for Congress in TN-9 after taking on AI corporations whose operations threaten the air and water in his community. He's ready to bring that fight to Washington.

These races could decide who holds power in Congress and whether working people have a real voice in shaping our future.

We know that personal conversations with voters can make the difference in close elections. Every call is a chance to turn someone out to vote for leaders who answer to us, not billionaires and Silicon Valley executives.

We are just days away from flipping the seats we need to fight for candidates that know the stakes. We need real AI control and an affordable future for working people now! This fall, we're joining with organizations like Irreplaceable across the country to reach working-class voters in must-win congressional districts.

These battlegrounds will decide who controls Congress and the Senate. 

**We'll provide the training, script, and tools. You can join from home.**

Looking for other times? [Check out these public events with these candidates and partners!](https://www.mobilize.us/workingfamiliespartycoordinated/?event_type=2&org_ids=2425&org_ids=37218&org_ids=49546&org_ids=44737)

events.title: Public Hearing: Tell IDEM to Stop Giving U.S. Steel a Free Pass to Pollute Gary
events.description:
The Indiana Department of Environmental Management (IDEM) has published a draft air permit modification for the U.S. Steel Gary Works steel mill, adding more industrial pollution each year to a community that has already endured a legacy of it. 

Gary residents and regional neighbors deserve full public review, enforceable limits, and answers on health and cumulative pollution, not a rubber stamp on complex and polluting steel upgrades!

Join the virtual public hearing on November 4th to tell IDEM to protect our communities and airways from Gary Works' pollution.

Please sign and share our petition to send a quick comment on the permit: www.jtnwi.org/clean-air-gary.

And use our toolkit to develop your comments and learn more about the permit: www.jtnwi.org/gary-hearing-toolkit.

*The hearing begins at 6:00 PM CT and will conclude as soon as public comments are done, or no later than 9:00 PM CT.

events.title: Love as Action: Quaker Witness to Authoritarianism, Oppression, & War

address_lines: East College Avenue & South Allen Street

events.description:
# Love as Action: Quaker Witness to Authoritarianism, Oppression, & War

### Quakers have long stood in opposition to cruelty and inequality. In this time of rising authoritarianism and fascism, we are called to show this love in action again. 

Please join State College Friends Meeting and the American Friends Service Committee to bear witness and show resistance to the authoritarian actions of our country. 

On Saturdays, October 31 & November 14, 2026, at 1:00 p.m., we will gather at the Allen Street Gates for one hour of silent public worship.

Quaker worship is a communal time in reverent silence to listen inwardly for insight and guidance. Anyone who feels deeply led may share a brief message for the spiritual nurture of the group. Signs are welcome that, consistent with our values, highlight harms of authoritarianism or share love and support for communities who are suffering.

Together, we affirm: We will protect people and communities. We will resist authoritarian government. We will build a free, equal and just future. Shared witness reflects core Quaker principles: peace, equality, integrity, and community. And taking action publicly is a visible commitment to justice and compassion, in solidarity with communities facing harm and dehumanization. By standing together in silence, we affirm that every person has worth, that fear and violence must give way to love and fairness, and that our communities thrive when all are welcomed.

Our hope is that our presence will give hope to all who see us – to show that we can choose resistance - and remind everyone of our moral obligations to one another.

Join us! We gather monthly in communities across the country, showing love in action as a public witness of our Quaker values in times of rising injustice. To find our more about Love as Action nationally visit www.afsc.org/love-action

Supplies will be passed between shifts or dropped off prior to election day.

*****Petition Language Below*****
Petition to the Mayor and Holyoke City Council: Invest Cannabis Revenue in People, Not Policing

We, the undersigned residents of Holyoke, ask the Mayor and City Council to direct funds from the Marijuana Impact Fee Stabilization Fund (MIFSF), which is supported by taxes on cannabis sales, to social services and community programming, and not to surveillance technology or police overtime.

Specifically, we ask that these funds be used for:
    Establish an Office of Tenant Protection and Housing Remediation Programs
    Improve enforcement of building codes, without displacing tenants
    Mental health care and substance use support programs
    Youth programs, job training, paid work, and childcare
    Other community-based services and programs that address the conditions behind harm

We further ask that the Mayor and City Council publish a line-item accounting of how the MIFSF is allocated, what outcomes are expected, and who is accountable for evaluating results; and that residents have a public opportunity to comment before any allocation is finalized.
