events.title: No Country for Mothers: A Maryland Community Screening & Conversation
events.description:
**Mothers have long been expected to figure it out. Childcare. Work. Leave. School schedules. Aging parents. Healthcare. The endless logistics of keeping a family going.**

During National Family Caregivers Month, join journalist, author, and advocate Christine Michel Carter for a free Maryland screening of Moms First’s documentary *No Country for Mothers*, followed by a public conversation about what it actually takes to raise and care for a family in Maryland today.

So much of what makes caregiving difficult gets treated as part of the deal. Childcare falls through, leave runs out, a child gets sick, an aging parent needs help, and work keeps moving as if none of it happened. Families adjust. Mothers rearrange. Somehow, somebody makes it work.

But “making it work” can hide how much women are being asked to absorb.

*No Country for Mothers* looks at the systems behind those experiences, but it also asks why mothers have spent so much time fighting over one another’s choices.

Working mom or stay-at-home mom. Career or family. Tradwife or girlboss. Mothers are constantly asked to pick a side and defend how they are doing motherhood, while many are dealing with the same underlying problems: childcare they can’t afford or find, inadequate leave, workplaces that were not designed around caregiving, financial pressure, and too little support.

This night is not about deciding who is mothering the “right” way.

And you do not have to agree politically with every woman in the room.

Motherhood and caregiving cross those lines. Women can have different families, different careers, different politics, and different ideas about how they want to live while still recognizing something in one another’s experience.

After the film, we’ll bring that conversation home to Maryland.

Mothers and caregivers will share what is happening in their own lives alongside civic leaders, advocates, employers, community organizations, and public leaders. We’ll talk about what families have accepted as normal, where they are being asked to solve larger problems on their own, and where there may be common ground for making family life work better.

We’ll ask:

- What have we gotten too used to calling “normal”?
- What are mothers and caregivers absorbing that shouldn’t fall entirely on families?
- Where are families falling through the gaps?
- Where can people who may disagree politically still find common ground?
- What would meaningful progress look like for Maryland families?

And then comes the question that matters after the conversation ends:

**What do I want to do with what I heard?**

For one woman, that may mean asking her employer to reconsider a policy that doesn’t work in practice. Another may call an elected official, learn more about an issue affecting her family, share her story, join other mothers around something she cares about, or bring this same conversation into her own community.

For someone else, the first step may simply be sitting in a room with other women and realizing that something she has been struggling to manage quietly is happening in families all around her.

You do not need to arrive as an advocate.

Come because you’re tired of figuring everything out by yourself. Come because you want to say some of this out loud. Come because you want to hear what other women are carrying. Come because you may disagree about plenty of things and still wonder whether motherhood has to be this hard.

The goal is not to leave with every problem solved or everyone in agreement. It is to leave seeing your own experience more clearly, understanding how it connects to something larger, and knowing that your voice belongs in the conversations where decisions about families are made.

**We spend a lot of time asking mothers how they’re going to make it work. On this night, we’re asking what needs to work better for them.**

Free and open to the public. Registration required.

events.title: World Day of Remembrance for Traffic Violence Victims 2026
events.description:
Join Families for Safe Streets as we commemorate World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims in Central Park (exact location to be announced).

This year our ceremony will include an ancient tradition from Japan, folded paper cranes. The practice of folding a thousand paper cranes was originally an endeavor undertaken to with for a long life for oneself of a loved one.

Over time, the tradition has evolved to be associated with wishing for recovery from illness or injury, for happiness and good luck or for world peace. Members of Families for Safe Streets will create a thousand origami cranes to honor loved ones killed or injured by traffic violence and the people killed or injured this past year. We look forward to seeing you to mark this solemn, meaningful day with us.

After the ceremony, Families for Safe Streets members will gather for a meal together.

events.title: Election Night: Drinks, Democracy, and Blue Victories 🍹
events.description:
After months of organizing, phone banking, and waiting, the big night is finally here. The tension is real, but the optimism is higher! Let's channel that anxious energy into a night of fun with people who want to see a massive blue wave, and there is no way we are watching it alone on our couches!

We are gathering to watch the results roll in live, celebrate our hard work, and cheer on Democratic victories across the country.

• When: Tuesday, November 3, 2026, 7:00 - 9:00 PM
• Where: Pilot Project Brewing, Logan Square (2140 N Milwaukee St)
• The Setup: We've reserved a section of tables right in front of the big screens with full audio on.
• Food & Drink: The bar has a great menu, so come hungry and ready for a few celebratory toasts.

Let’s watch history happen together. 

Fingers crossed for a big night!

events.title: 93 County Tour: Town Hall with Dan Osborn in Kearney *Buffalo County*
events.description:
Independent U.S. Senate candidate Dan Osborn will be at The Nebraska Firefighters Museum & Education Center on Monday, November 2nd from 10:00 am - 11:00 am (CDT) for a town hall.

An industrial and service mechanic, Osborn is a veteran of the U.S. Navy and Nebraska National Guard. He is running to break the stranglehold that billionaires have on our economy and government. Osborn will unite Nebraskans around a common-sense platform that works for workers, small businesses, and family farms and ranches.

All are welcome to join, to ask questions, and share thoughts and insights. This campaign is about truly listening to ALL Nebraskans, not just the politically connected.

Questions or concerns can be directed to info@osbornforsenate.com. If you want to help us get the word out about this event please send us an email!

events.title: Salmonberry Trail Nature Walk: Opt Outside for Black Friday!
events.description:
Join us as we tour the Learning Mile of the Future Salmonberry Trail! It's a great opportunity to get outdoors and connect with fellow nature lovers over the holiday weekend. Led by Kira Taylor, a Master Naturalist and Chair of the Flora and Fauna Committee of the Salmonberry Trail, and Matt Streng, of OutdoorRX, they will guide us through a slow paced nature walk, show casing all the beautiful species we can see in our own backyard of Washington County and how nature makes us happy AND healthy!

This is an easy 1.8 mile hike perfect for the whole family! We will start out on NW Fisher Rd and Hwy 47 (the future Buxton Trailhead for the Salmonberry Trail) and hike to Williams Creek to hopefully see salmon spawning in the creek!

[Please read the volunteer waiver](https://salmonberrytrail.org/volunteer-waiver)

[You Can Make A Donation Here](https://salmonberrytrail.org/donate)

events.title: Salmonberry Trail Walk - Black Friday at Kilchis Point
events.description:
Join us in gratitude for a special Black Friday guided hike at the beautiful Kilchis Point Reserve in Bay City! 

This hike is ~2 miles and relatively flat. With 17 interpretive signs, it is a great learning opportunity of the local flora, fauna, and indigenous heritage. There are restrooms at the first parking area. We will meet/begin hiking from the second/rear parking area.

After the scenic hike, we'll meet for an all-ages Happy Hour at the Tillamook Creamery!

[Please read the volunteer waiver](https://salmonberrytrail.org/volunteer-waiver)

[You Can Make A Donation Here](https://salmonberrytrail.org/donate)

# From Your Doorsteps to the Ballot Box 🗳

### Free Rides. Good Vibes. Our Community, Our Voice.

The Equity Alliance is coming to **YOUR** community to pick you up and take you to vote! Ride with your neighbors, enjoy some music and community love, and make your voice heard.

## Don’t forget your photo ID! 
A Tennessee driver’s license, state photo ID, U.S. passport, or military ID works, even if it's expired. **Student IDs and library cards don’t count.**

Not sure if you’re registered? Check at GoVoteTN.gov or ask us when we pull up!

events.title: Cranksgiving-Maynard

location.venue: Mill Parking Lot (where the farmer market takes place)

events.description:
Join our pedal-powered community bicycle ride and food drive to purchase Thanksgiving-themed food to donate to Open Table.

We will ride at a very relaxed, family-friendly pace to 3 local supermarkets to pick up Thanksgiving-themed goods such as canned vegetables (ie-corn, yams), thanksgiving sides (cranberry sauce, bread mixes, stuffing boxes), and thanksgiving dessert ingredients (canned pumpkin, apple pie filling) that we will donate to Open Table. We will meet in the Mill parking lot near the corner of Sudbury st and Main St across from Ray and Sons Cycle and Ski.  

The ride will cover about 10 miles on rolling terrain (mostly paved roads). Turkey-themed costumes welcome. You should bring your bicycle (although rentals are available on the rail trail), a bicycle lock, a bag, and $15-25 to purchase food to donate. 

We will meet at 9:45 and leave at 10 am. Please be ready to go.  
Rain date will be Sunday, Nov 22.

events.title: A Doctor, A Nurse and a Biologist Walk into a Bar
events.description:
Take a look at this YouTube video of the inaugural show of what we hope will become a series. Click this link to see it:  
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KxSDZYKRhd0

The idea is to make a panel of 3-4 smart people, half of them politicians or officials who have the opportunity to move the needle of some of the social-political-economic issues we face, and put them in a bar with regular people who want to learn something or participate in solutions.

Then they talk, and listen, and learn and imagine what we might be able to do.  

Why a bar? 

Because it's always fun to think about unlikely people in a bar and what they might say. 

Because we can put politicians and candidates in a room where they don't do the canned political speech and we get to see what they know and what they think. 

Because we want to change up things where people sit on panels and have a formal, prepared conversation and the audience listens and then everyone goes home: We want to see if we can engage people on both sides of that table to know and trust each other and get real about making change. 

And, of course, this is great material to forward to everyone you know and acquaint them with candidates they can be proud of. Please do that, will you?

events.title: Phone Bank with One Colorado and Families, Not Politics [GJ Event]

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
# Call Voters with Families Not Politics: Defend Colorado Kids and Families

This November, Colorado voters will decide two ballot measures that sound simple but aren’t. Propositions 134 and 135 are sold as fairness and safety measures, but the fine print tells a different story. Voters deserve to hear it before they vote.

Proposition 134 is so vague it could subject any kid, in any sport, from kindergarten through college, to invasive verification just to prove they belong on the field. Proposition 135 takes medical decisions away from families and doctors and hands them to politicians. It could even block care for kids who aren’t transgender, including teens fighting cancer.

Here’s what our research tells us: many voters are still making up their minds, and when they hear the full picture, they move. Those are the voters we’re calling. These are real persuasion conversations, and they matter more right now than any other work we can do.

No experience needed. We’ll start with a training and team briefing so you feel ready to talk with voters, listen to where they’re coming from, and share what these measures actually do. Bring a laptop, a charged phone, and headphones if you have them.

Every conversation moves a voter. Every voter we move brings us closer to defeating these measures in November. Pick up the phone with us.

events.title: Unlocking Housing: A Community Listening Session
events.description:
We're launching our Housing Unlocked campaign and we want to hear from you. This listening session is a time for people impacted by incarceration and/or housing insecurity to come together, share our stories, and build a new campaign for housing justice. 

Dream.Org's Housing Unlocked campaign works with impacted communities to increase dignified housing for people impacted by incarceration, and fight back against the criminalization of homelessness in Pennsylvania, New York, Arizona, and Wisconsin. Our firm belief is that the people closest to the problem are most equipped to solve them. 

We want to work with you to build a world where people can access keys, not cages. Expanding access to quality housing is not only the humane thing to do, it is the common-sense solution to reduce recidivism, save taxpayer dollars, and keep communities safe.

People who have been incarcerated are up to 13 times more likely to experience homelessness, while unhoused people are often jailed simply for sleeping or standing outside. Housing insecurity is both a cause and effect of incarceration: the two operate in a vicious cycle, affecting tens of thousands of Americans every year. But it doesn't have to be that way.

Your voice is needed. It's time to unlock our blocks.

events.title: Philadelphia Día de los Muertos Day of Action - End the ICE Age
events.description:
# Día de los Muertos Vigil & Altar: Remembering Lives Lost at the Hands of ICE

This Día de los Muertos, join us in Philadelphia as we come together to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol, both inside and outside immigration detention, and demand an end to the violence.

On **Monday, November 2 at 6:30 PM**, the Shut Down Detention Campaign will gather outside the **ICE Field Office at 114 N. 8th Street** for a community vigil and altar to remember those we've lost.

Rooted in the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones, we'll gather to grieve publicly, remember the lives behind the headlines, and stand together for a future where all our communities can live with dignity, safety, and freedom.

This vigil is part of **End the ICE Age**, a national day of action taking place across the country from October 31 through November 2. Together, we're demanding that Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding toward what our communities actually need, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

Here in Pennsylvania, we continue that fight through our collective efforts to shut down the Moshannon Valley Processing Center and bring people home to their families and communities.

## Event Details

- **When:** Monday, November 2, 2026 | 6:30 PM
- **Where:** ICE Field Office, 114 N. 8th Street, Philadelphia, PA
- **What:** Community vigil and Día de los Muertos altar
- **Bring:** A white candle, if you can!

**Our loved ones deserve to be remembered. Our communities deserve to live free from ICE violence and detention.**

### Community Safety

This is a peaceful, nonviolent gathering. We ask all participants to act lawfully, help de-escalate any potential confrontations, and refrain from bringing weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted.

Join us in remembrance, solidarity, and collective action.

events.title: Canvass for Talarico with Ground Truth – West Garland Library
events.description:
## Join Swing Left to canvass for James Talarico! ##

Join us for one last canvass before Election Day! We'll be using Ground Truth, Swing Left's innovative approach to voter contact: real, in-depth conversations at the door that actually move voters, instead of rushing through a checklist.

No experience needed. Every shift starts with a training, so whether it's your first time canvassing or your fiftieth, you'll be ready.

**Here’s what to expect:**
- A training on the Ground Truth script and deep canvassing best practices
- Plenty of time at the doors having real conversations with voters
- Logging each conversation in the app
- A short debrief with an organizer to wrap up your shift

**What to bring:** A charged phone, comfortable shoes and clothes, and water.

Every conversation helps move voters toward voting for Talarico and allows us to connect with voters who are traditionally overlooked by campaigns.

Questions? Reach out to Sol Arellano 214-554-0000 marisol@swingleft.org

Want to go deeper? Sign up for an optional virtual training here: https://mobilize.us/s/NulnlI

People are FED UP with private health insurance companies denying us care while driving up costs and extracting enormous profits. And we’re saying enough is enough. Medicare for All has gained popularity and momentum all across the political spectrum this past year as people understand deeply that the system is broken.

People all across the country have turned out to vote for candidates that are fighting for universal health care and willing to stand up to big money and corporate interests. 

Join the Medicare for All National Coalition for this important post-election strategy call. We may have a historic opportunity to push Medicare for All forward in 2029, and the organizing starts now.
We need to grow our movement with thousands of volunteers and together we can win Medicare for All!

This call is sponsored by lead Medicare for All Table organizations: People's Action Institute, Healthcare-NOW, National Nurses United, Physicians for a National Health Program, Popular Democracy, and Progressive Democrats of America. events.description:
*United in Purpose, Strength & Hope — Let’s Watch History Unfold Together!*

---
After weeks of knocking on doors, making phone calls, and inspiring our communities across Texas, the moment is finally here!

BLD PWR, TOPS, BAJI Action, Doshi House, and Live Free cordially invite you to gather under one roof as we celebrate our hard work, track live results, and stand together in solidarity and hope. ---

- **Live Broadcast on Big Screens:** Follow election returns in real-time as results roll in from across the state and nation!
- **Power in Unity:** Connect with fellow volunteers, faith leaders, organizers, and neighbors who made this civic movement possible.
- **Delicious Refreshments:** Enjoy complimentary food, snacks, and an open bar while we cheer on our collective impact.
- **Debrief & Celebration:** Hear from community leaders, reflect on our journey, and celebrate the strength of our democracy.

---

Come as you are, bring your family, and bring a friend! Together, we demonstrate that when our community stands united, our power is undeniable.

Please confirm your attendance so we can ensure enough seating and food for everyone.

events.title: Tenant Power Summit: Know Your Rights. Demand Accountability. Build Community Power.
events.description:
### Tenant Summit: Know Your Rights. Demand Accountability. Build Community Power.

**Everyone deserves a safe, stable, and affordable place to call home. But too many tenants are facing rising rents, unfair housing practices, the threat of eviction, and landlords who are not being held accountable. It's time to change that.**

Join us for a community-driven **Tenant Summit** focused on empowering renters with the knowledge, resources, and collective power needed to protect their homes and fight for stronger tenant protections.

This summit will bring together renters, housing advocates, community organizers, and legal experts for honest conversations about the challenges tenants face and the solutions our communities deserve.

Together, we'll explore:

- Know Your Rights: Understand tenant protections, lease agreements, eviction processes, and your rights under Arizona law.
- Landlord Accountability:Learn how to document unsafe living conditions, address unfair treatment, and advocate for responsible property management.
- Housing Stability and Affordability: Discuss rising housing costs, displacement, and the policies needed to keep families in their homes.
- The Power of Tenant Organizing: Discover how renters can organize within their apartment complexes and neighborhoods to demand better living conditions and lasting change.
- From Conversation to Action: Connect with advocates, access community resources, and identify opportunities to shape housing policies that put people before profits.

This summit isn't just about understanding the challenges we're facing. It's about building the power to change them.

Whether you're a longtime renter, facing housing challenges for the first time, or passionate about housing justice, your voice belongs in this conversation.

Because housing is more than four walls and a roof. It's the foundation for our families, our health, our dignity, and our future.

Your home. Your rights. Our collective power. Join us and help build an Arizona where tenants are protected, landlords are accountable, and every family has the opportunity to thrive.

events.description:
On Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, Project HALO will be at Fair Oaks Recreation Center in Marietta to celebrate one of our most important shared American traditions with the voters who make it happen.

Swing by when you vote, or bring your family and neighbors. You'll find veterans, faith leaders, legal professionals, and community members creating a welcoming, nonpartisan presence outside the polls. It's about participation, not politics, and about our community showing up for each other.

Where: Fair Oaks Recreation Center, 1465 W Booth Rd Ext SW, Marietta, GA 30008
When: 12-7pm

Want to help? RSVP to volunteer for a shift. No experience is needed, and we'll cover the logistics when you arrive. As we mark the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, this is what Project HALO is about: neighbors showing up for one another. Learn more at halovote.org.

This event is nonpartisan and open to everyone. Any food, entertainment, or free items are available to voters and non-voters alike.

events.title: OUR FUTURE, OUR VOTE NC — COUNT EVERY VOTE!

sponsor.name: Camel City United Indivisible North Carolina

location.venue: Forsyth County Board of Election Government Center

events.description:
Our future. Our vote. Every vote counts.

Election Day may be November 3, but protecting our democracy doesn't end when the polls close.

On November 10, communities across North Carolina will gather at county boards of elections in more than 25 counties as part of the statewide Our Future OUR Vote NC election protection mobilization.

Join Camel City United Indivisible and our statewide coalition partners for a peaceful, nonpartisan gathering in downtown Winston-Salem.

We're coming together to:

Celebrate the voters who made their voices heard in this election.

Thank election officials and community volunteers for their hard work.

Stand together for free, fair, and transparent elections.

Remind our county Board of Elections that we are watching and expect every eligible vote to be counted and election results to be certified by the November 13 deadline.

We expect our election officials to do the right thing. We are gathering to support the democratic process and make clear that the people of Forsyth County expect their voices to be heard.

Our message is simple:

COUNT EVERY VOTE!

Bring your neighbors, your signs, and your commitment to protecting our democracy.

Tuesday, November 10 | 5:00–6:00 PM

Part of the statewide Our Future OUR Vote NC mobilization. Locally co-sponsored by Camel City United Indivisible.

This is a peaceful, nonpartisan gathering. Please respect election workers and keep sidewalks and building entrances accessible.

events.title: Love as Action: Austin
events.description:
# Love as Action: Resisting Authoritarianism

### Quaker public witness has stood in opposition to cruel and authoritarian actions in our country before. It is time for us to show this love in action again. 

Please join the American Friends Service Committee and Friends Meeting of Austin to bear witness and show resistance to the authoritarian actions in our country. 

On Election Day--Tuesday, November 3 at 12p we will gather at The Texas State Capitol for one hour of silent public worship. We will be on the grass, visible from the South Gate on 11th. 

Our hope is that our presence will give hope to all who see us – to show that we can choose resistance - and remind everyone of our moral obligations to one another.

We gather monthly in communities across the country, showing our communities love in action as a public witness of our Quaker values in a time of rising fascism.

Join us! 

To find our more about Love as Action nationally and get more resources visit us at [afsc.org/love-action](www.afsc.org/love-action)

events.title: Pack the Hearing for the FAAR Act!
events.description:
On Thursday, Nov. 5, we are asking DC residents to show up and pack the Judiciary & Public Safety Committee hearing to testify on the Full Accountability in Arrest Reporting (FAAR) Act and speak about the heightened National Guard and federal law enforcement presence in the District.

As the public, we have to demand that our elected officials and agencies DO NOT COOPERATE WITH THE OCCUPATION OF OUR CITY. We demand the National Guard off our streets, full accountability in arrest reporting, and bodycam transparency in use-of-force events.

We need you to testify before Council and pack the hearing room. Show up and take up space; the Wilson Building is the people's building, and we have a right to be there.

## You do not have to be a DC resident to testify!

events.title: Love as Action: Kennett Square, PA
events.description:
# Love as Action: Resisting Authoritarianism

### Quaker public witness has stood in opposition to cruel and authoritarian actions in our country before. It is time for us to show this love in action again. 

Please join the American Friends Service Committee and Kennett Friends Meeting to bear witness and show resistance to the authoritarian actions in our country. 

On Sunday, November 8 at 12 Noon we will gather at Kennett Friends Meeting for one hour of silent public worship.

Our hope is that our presence will give hope to all who see us – to show that we can choose resistance - and remind everyone of our moral obligations to one another.

We gather monthly in communities across the country, showing our communities love in action as a public witness of our Quaker values in a time of rising fascism.

Join us! 

To find our more about Love as Action nationally and get more resources visit us at [afsc.org/love-action](www.afsc.org/love-action)

events.title: Call Colorado voters to elect leaders who will stand up to Big AI
events.description:
Last week, over a thousand people walked out to demand a Freeze on AI. Now young people are taking that energy to the ballot box.

Irreplaceable Action Fund is teaming up with New Era Colorado Action to turn out young voters in two Denver-area House races.

**Colorado’s 8th** is one of the closest House races in the country. **Manny Rutinel** supports regulating AI. Incumbent Gabe Evans voted for massive tax giveaways to tech corporations and data centers, and he wants big AI companies to write their own rules. Young voters could decide who wins.

**Colorado’s 1st: Melat Kiros,** a community leader who joined last week’s walkout, is on track to become the first Gen Z woman in Congress. She’s been an unapologetic champion for regulating Big AI and giving people a say and a stake in how it’s built and used. A big youth turnout sends her to Washington with a mandate.

Personal conversations are one of the best ways to get people to vote in a close election. Every call could turn out a voter for leaders who answer to working people instead of Silicon Valley billionaires.

**With AI moving this fast, this could be one of our last chances to elect a Congress that will fight for working people on AI.**

Join us. No experience required. We’ll give you the training, script, and tools to get started! All you need is a device to call on that's connected to the internet (a smartphone, a computer, or tablet work great); a quiet-ish place; and a bit of your evening.

events.title: 2026 #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence
events.description:
2026 #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence

Beginning Wednesday, December 9, 2026 until the end of December, we will come together across the nation to host the #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence.

These local events will be anchored by the 14th Annual National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C.—held near the 14-year mark of the Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting tragedy, when a 20-year-old gunman armed with an AR-15 hunted and murdered 20 first graders and six educators.

Across the country, vigils (as simple as lighting candles) and gatherings will honor lives stolen by gun violence, uplift survivors, raise awareness, and demand urgent action from our leaders to finally end this epidemic. From schools and workplaces to houses of worship, neighborhoods, grocery stores, homes, nightclubs, streets, and even our democracy itself—gun violence impacts every aspect of American life.

The theme of this year’s campaign is #FreedomToLive—the simple, powerful idea that every person deserves to live free from the daily threat of gunfire. Together, survivors, families, advocates, and allies will raise our voices to ensure that FREEDOM means the right of every person to live, learn, work, worship, speak, vote, and gather without the daily fear of gun violence.

We stand in solidarity with over 1.4 million Americans who have been shot since Sandy Hook, with every community devastated by gun violence for decades. We will send a clear message to our local, state, and federal lawmakers, raise awareness, and help build the movement for common-sense solutions.

Let’s #HonorWithAction together. Let’s demand freedom from gun violence.

events.description:
We are hosting an information session for individuals who would like to learn more about bringing a school safety team to their neighborhood! 

There are two information sessions, please RSVP to only one - we are offering two opportunities to learn about the program.

School safety teams have three primary goals:

-Community walks within the radius of a school in the early morning hours, which include school arrival times, and afternoon hours, which includes dismissal.
-Share know-your-rights and NYC Schools policy on non-local law enforcement, making sure the school community is aware of updated protocols and their rights. 
-Engage with the schools, sharing information that will retain safety.

This program is a partnership with Hands Off NYC, Hands Off Families, and New York Immigration Coalition, and caring neighbors across the City.

Thank you for your interest in keeping our schools and communities safe!

events.title: Visibility Brigade Kane Election Night Watch Party, 11/3
events.description:
Election Night with the people you fought beside all year at Brother Chimp Brewing in St. Charles.

New here? Welcome to Visibility Brigade Kane (VBK)! We're a local grassroots crew in Kane County, Illinois, standing up for democracy and pushing back against fascism, nationalism, and authoritarianism. Our signature move? Gathering on bridges over rush-hour traffic with giant-letter messages, waving flags, and giving drivers a peaceful, joyful, impossible-to-miss reminder that they're not alone. We stood on bridges in the rain for this. We waved at rush hour for this. We danced, we honked, we held the line — for THIS. Now come watch it all pay off. Election Night with the people you fought beside all year. Brother Chimp Brewing, downtown St. Charles — 303 N 4th St, Suite A. Doors-ish 6:45 PM, polls close at 7, we stay till close (9 PM). Award-winning beer, cider, wine, seltzers, and spirits on tap. Grab a pint, grab a bite at the food truck's there. Bring your friends, your phone charger, and your lucky socks. Bring the person who said "my vote doesn't matter" — we'll fix that tonight. Wear blue if you've got it.

events.title: Rally at the Supreme Court: Protect Connecticut's Assault Weapons Ban

location.venue: Supreme Court of the United States

events.description:
Our Children's Lives Are on the Line. Show Up and Make Your Voice Heard!

Nearly 14 years after 20 children and six educators were hunted and murdered at Sandy Hook Elementary School by a 20-year-old gunman with an AR15 and high capacity magazines, the U.S. Supreme Court will hear oral arguments in cases challenging assault weapons bans in Connecticut and Cook County, Illinois.

These laws were enacted to protect our families and communities from weapons of war that are designed to efficiently and brutally kill as many people in the shortest time possible. Now, their constitutionality is before the nation's highest court, and the consequences could extend far beyond Connecticut and Illinois.

We cannot afford to be silent!

On December 2 at 9:30 AM ET, gun violence survivors, families, advocates, and concerned Americans will gather outside the Supreme Court to stand together for our children's freedom to live without the fear of gun violence.

We have seen the devastation these weapons cause in Sandy Hook, Parkland, Uvalde, Highland Park, Orlando, Las Vegas, Buffalo and communities across the country. We know what is at stake.

The Second Amendment should not mean that Americans must surrender their freedom to feel safe in classrooms, houses of worship, grocery stores, and public spaces.

Join us outside the Supreme Court on December 2 at 9:30 AM ET. Stand with survivors and communities impacted by shootings. Stand with families. Stand for the freedom to live.

Bring your signs, your friends, and your determination. Let's make sure the voices of those whose lives have been forever changed by gun violence are heard.

RSVP today and help us spread the word!

Organized by national gun control/gun violence prevention/gun safety groups. 

#ProtectKidsNotGuns #BanAssaultWeapons #BanWeaponsOfWar #FreedomFromGunViolence #HonorWithAction #EndGunViolence

events.title: Can't Fool Meck Poll Canvass - Election Day
events.description:
Join Carolina Federation-Mecklenburg for a poll canvass shift and talk with voters about the property tax amendments on this fall's ballot, its never to late to educate and get someone to know exactly what they are voting for.

The county tax rate is already set to drop in January 2027, amendment or not. What these amendments would do is let corporations like Duke Energy and the wealthiest property owners keep dodging what they owe, and move the final say on your property tax bill from the county commissioners you elect to politicians in Raleigh. Billions for CMS, CPCC, Atrium Health and CATS are on the line.

You'll work in pairs, outside the 50-foot buffer zone, with talking points and materials we provide. First time doing this? No problem. We'll walk you through what to say when you arrive. Bring water, comfortable shoes and a charged phone.

events.title: ELECTION DAY! LAST CHANCE TO ELECT JESSE HUSETH FOR HD97!
events.description:
Join TIRRC Votes PAC and other partners as we make our last push to elect Jesse Huseth for HD97 on election day! We've got a real chance to flip this seat, and we can't do it without you! Join us at Jesse's headquarters and we'll do a short training before sending you out to move election day voters. Were on the streets all day! Come join us!

HD97 is the most competitive State House race in Tennessee and the greatest pickup opportunity this election cycle. Join TIRRC Votes and the Jesse Huseth campaign in Memphis as we take action to bring Jesse to victory!

Jesse is a lifelong Memphian, small business owner, and former public school teacher who's spent his career serving this community and working families. In 2024, Jesse Huseth came within striking distance of winning, only being a few votes short from his opponent, marking arguably the closest election in the state of Tennessee. This November, we're going all in to close that gap and flip this seat!

Whether this is the first time you've knocked on doors or you're an experienced canvasser, we NEED you. If you have never canvassed before, we will have staff on-site to train and partner with you so you will never have to go alone. Let’s stand for Jesse Huseth and bring him to the finish line this year!

Paid for by TIRRC Votes PAC. Authorized by Friends of Jesse Huseth.

events.title: ELECTION DAY! LAST CHANCE TO ELECT ALLIE PHILLIPS FOR HD75!

HD75 is the most competitive State House race in Tennessee and the greatest pickup opportunity this election cycle. Join TIRRC Votes and the Allie Phillips campaign in Clarksville as we take action to bring Allie to victory!

HD75 is one of Tennessee's top pickup opportunities this cycle. Join TIRRC Votes and the Allie Phillips campaign as we take action in one of the most competitive state house races of 2026!

Allie is a working mom of two, a former small business owner who ran an in-home daycare, and a union member who's lived the same everyday pressures as the families she'd represent.

Allie Phillips came within striking distance in 2024, outperforming the top of the ticket in a district that leans Republican on paper. This is a turnout race. Real, sustained people power will decide it, and TIRRC Votes is showing up to help build it!

Whether this is the first time you've knocked on doors or you're an experienced canvasser, we NEED you. If you have never canvassed before, we will have staff on-site to train and partner with you so you will never have to go alone. Let’s stand for Allie Phillips and bring her to the finish line this year!

Paid for by TIRRC Votes PAC. Authorized by Allie Phillips for Change.

events.title: NY: Emergency Briefing to Stop the Dirty Energy & Water Bill
events.description:
**Join us for an emergency briefing about federal legislation that would gut key environmental laws, boost the approval of data centers, and unleash a buildout of fracked gas infrastructure, including the Constitution Pipeline.**

In early November, Congress is poised to consider the “Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026," so-called permitting reform legislation that is a wish list for Big Tech and the plastics and fossil fuel industry.

**New York Congressional leaders can play a key role in blocking this dirty energy and water bill.**

At the meeting, we'll discuss the policy and the politics, including ways to take action and get involved.

**SPECIAL GUEST: Congressman Jared Huffman, a leader from California fighting the bill.**

_Sponsors include: Food & Water Watch, Riverkeeper, Beyond Plastic, Third Act Upstate, Center for Organizing (list in formation)_

Ready, Set, Get Out the Vote!

Election Day is almost here, and we're gearing up for one final push to get voters to the polls!

Join us on Monday, November 2, for an evening of action, energy, and community as we work together to get out the vote across Hamilton County!

We'll be joined by Meeka Owens, candidate for Hamilton County Commissioner, and special guest Seth Walsh, candidate for Ohio State Treasurer, and other candidates on the Hamilton County Democratic slate!

Whether you're a seasoned volunteer or getting involved for the first time, there's a way for everyone to make a difference. Stop by to:

- Pick up a canvassing packet and knock on doors to remind voters to make their voices heard.
- Join our phone bank to connect with voters across Hamilton County.
- Help with literature drops to make sure voters have the information they need before Election Day.
- Meet candidates, connect with fellow volunteers, and build momentum for November 3!

WHEN: Monday, November 2, 2026 | 4:00–8:00 PM

WHERE: Cream + Sugar | 3546 Montgomery Road, Cincinnati, OH 45207

Every conversation matters. Every door knocked matters. Every vote matters.

With just hours until polls open, this is our opportunity to come together, mobilize our neighbors, and make sure Hamilton County is ready to show up on Election Day.

Sign up, bring a friend, and help us finish strong!

(Sign up for one shift,  or all of them!)

events.title: Allentown, PA: Planning Commission Meeting
events.description:
On November 10, the Allentown Planning Commission will meet once again to consider the proposed data center for 1024 N. Bradford St.

This was site was previously approved for a warehouse. But now the applicant, Tiger Den Partners VIII LLC, has submitted multiple proposals for various plans for the site, making it unclear what exactly they are asking to build in Allentown and what the intended use of this project would be.

Now they are requesting an extension on their application. Enough is enough — join us to pack the room to urge the Allentown Planning Commission to vote NO to this request. **Let's protect Allentown from data center developers!**

events.title: Home Is Here Community Call: The Fight for the Dream and Promise Act
events.description:
As Congress enters the lame-duck session following the midterm elections, the weeks before the end of the congressional term is a critical opportunity to advance legislation. 

With the future of DACA recipients, TPS & DED holders, and immigrant youth at stake – understanding this legislative window and building pressure on our elected officials to advance the Dream & Promise Act is more important than ever! 

**Join Home is Here with our partners for an urgent community conversation on Wednesday, Nov. 18  @7pm ET about the fight to pass the Dream & Promise Act, and securing a pathway to citizenship for 4.4+ million people during the lame-duck session.** 

**During our community conversation, together we’ll:**

- 🟡 Break down what the lame-duck session means & explore the path towards passage of the Dream & Promise Act. 

- 🟡 Discuss what it will take to build the support needed to move the legislation forward. 

- 🟡 Hear from directly impacted folks, learn how to turn your stories into powerful advocacy while making space to processing the emotional toll of organizing around our own immigration status. 

- 🟡 Review practical tools to contact your representatives, share stories, mobilize our families and urge Congress to act. 

**Our goal is to turn urgency into collective action.** Every call, story and conversation can help build the pressure needed to move the Dream & Promise Act forward.

### RSVP TODAY & invite your circle to join us!

events.title: Can't Fool Meck Poll Canvass - Election Day
events.description:
Join Carolina Federation-Mecklenburg for a poll canvass shift and talk with voters about the property tax amendments on this fall's ballot, its never to late to educate and get someone to know exactly what they are voting for.

The county tax rate is already set to drop in January 2027, amendment or not. What these amendments would do is let corporations like Duke Energy and the wealthiest property owners keep dodging what they owe, and move the final say on your property tax bill from the county commissioners you elect to politicians in Raleigh. Billions for CMS, CPCC, Atrium Health and CATS are on the line.

You'll work in pairs, outside the 50-foot buffer zone, with talking points and materials we provide. First time doing this? No problem. We'll walk you through what to say when you arrive. Bring water, comfortable shoes and a charged phone.

Safe, affordable housing
Strong public schools
ICE out of our communities
Accountability from the people we elect
Utica's members, neighbors, faith leaders, union members, and community advocates are coming together to build the people power we need for the fights ahead. Bring your family, bring your neighbors, bring your voice.

This is what democracy looks like. Save our democracy. Join the fight. Build to win!

events.description:
# **LET’S PARTY AT THE POLLS!** 🗳️

*Celebrate our community. Cast your vote.*

We’re turning the ballot box into a block party! Come for the community, stay for the fun, and let’s make our voices heard together. It’s time to celebrate our power and show up for the neighborhood we love.

Join American Indians in Texas at the Spanish Colonial Missions (AITSCM) alongside our good friend Jesse Borrego, a San Antonio native, actor known for Blood In Blood Out, Mi Vida Loca, and Fame, and longtime community advocate, for an afternoon of good food, conversation, and community spirit as we kick off Native American Heritage Month!

**THE VIBE:**

We’re bringing the energy to the ballot box! Whether you’re voting early or on Election Day, come hang out, meet your neighbors, and celebrate democracy in action.

**WHERE & WHEN:**

📍AITSCM-  1616 E Commerce St

📅 November 3, 2026, 12:30-3:00 PM 

**FEATURING:**
✊ Meets & Treats- Come together with your Eastside neighbors and our good friend Jesse Borrego for good conversation, laughter, and connection. 

🍦Good Eats & Sweets - Enjoy a delicious lunch, ice cream floats, and a little something sweet!

🎲 Games and Activities - Bring friends and Family for light-hearted fun, games, and activities for all ages! 

🎨 Community Mural and Music- Enjoy good music, get creative, and leave your mark on a collaborative mural celebrating the people and voices that make our community special.

🗳️ VOTING RESOURCES & COMMUNITY SUPPORT
Have questions about voting? We've got friendly faces, helpful resources, and information to help you feel prepared and confident at the polls!

📍 ELECTION DAY REMINDER! 🗳️
Did you know Bexar County voters can cast their ballots at any Election Day Vote Center across the county?

At 3 PM, we'll head out together to the Claude Black Community Center at 2805 E. Commerce St. to cast our ballots! Prefer another location? We'll have resources to help you find a Vote Center that works best for you.

Find your voting location: https://maps.bexar.org/VoterRegSearch/

**LET’S VOTE TOGETHER!** 

Bring a friend, meet the community, and let’s make it count.

**Any food, entertainment, buttons, stickers, or any other free items at this event are available to voters and non-voters alike. This is a nonpartisan event.**

events.description:

Oklahoma applied to be a host and is one of five finalists.  At our September meeting we learned basic information about nuclear energy and discussed issues worth tracking. Our November meeting will be devoted to a discussion of nuclear waste disposal.

While the meeting is in-person, the speakers will be joining us via Zoom. Attendees will be able to see and hear them on a TV screen but the speakers will only see and hear the person operating the computer. As a result, all questions must be submitted so they can be read to the speakers. Those submitted online will be answered first. Attendees will have the opportunity to text or write and submit a question and it will be answered if time allows.

Signing up is requested but not required but those signing up will have the opportunity to submit a question online.

events.title: Southern Made Post Election Debrief
events.description:
Join Southern Made WFP for a post-election debrief as we unpack the 2026 midterm elections, celebrate our shared work, and talk about what comes next for working people across the South.

From Georgia to Tennessee, North Carolina to Florida, and across the region, organizers, candidates, volunteers, and everyday people have knocked doors, made calls, built relationships, and fought for a South where working families can thrive.

Now it's time to come together, take stock, and chart our path forward.

We'll talk about:
- What happened: Election results, key races, victories, setbacks, and what they tell us about the political landscape across the South.
- What we built: The organizing, relationships, and people-powered infrastructure that will outlast any single election.
- What's next: How we turn this election season's energy into lasting political power for working people across our region.

Whether you knocked doors, made calls, supported a candidate, or simply showed up to vote, you're part of this movement. And we want you in the conversation.

Because the South isn't just a battleground every two years. It's our home. And it's worth investing in every single day.

Come ready to reflect, connect, and imagine what's possible when we keep building together.

RSVP today to receive the Zoom link.

_Much like the American Revolution and the Founders themselves, our Constitution has been wrapped in mythology—often making it harder to understand its impact on our nation today. What forces shaped its creation, and how does that founding document continue to shape our shared life?_

Together, we’ll investigate the forces that drove the Constitutional Convention, the principles embedded in the Constitution, and how those foundations continue to influence our institutions, politics, and lives today.

_Join NWSOFA on Zoom Thursday, November 5, at 7 p.m. CST / 8 p.m. EST for this timely conversation with Joel Edward Goza, moderated by Marilyn._

Location: Grass Valley (provided upon registration)

events.title: Let's Go Spook Some Republicans

location.venue: Texas's 21st Congressional District and Texas House District 122

events.description:
Democratic Pop Up Campaign Office in North Central neighborhood 

DROP IN ANYTIME 9am-8pm SATURDAY THROUGH TUESDAY.

We'll give you a turf map for Democrats who haven't voted that you can walk in a couple of hours. We also have literature for the statewide candidates plus lit for Kristin Hook and Shelly Nickels--we're in their district.

We know a lot of the elections will be close--those nail biters that turn on a few percentage points. So we turn out everyone we can--big numbers are turning out so far, so time to squeeze out that last bit. Let's go find those voters who can bring home that win.

There's only one way to do it: We know what Dems haven't voted, so we show up on their door steps and tell them we know they haven't voted. That's a little spooky. But then a treat: we'll tell them how to be heroes by going to the polls.

We'll run an operating base Saturday through Election Day (Tuesday) from a North Central neighborhood to extend our reach out to CD21 and TX House 122. 10 A.M. on Saturday is the kickoff but we'll be going all weekend and on to Tuesday. It ain't over till it's over.

events.title: Post-Election Briefing: Where Are We Now and What's Next?

Georgia voters showed up in record numbers this election season. We casted ballots, monitored the polls, supported our fellow voters, and made our voices heard. And now, we're looking towards our collective future.

events.title: Defend the Pacific Islands Heritage Marine National Monument from Industrial Fishing
events.description:
The Trump Administration is attempting to illegally rollback protections for the Pacific Islands Heritage Marine National Monument (PIHMNM) – threatening to open up **408,000 square miles of protected ocean to harmful industrial fishing.**

In April 2025, President Trump issued a proclamation seeking to allow commercial fishing in the waters 50 to 200 nautical miles around Jarvis Island, Johnston Atoll, and Wake Island. When the National Marine Fisheries Service attempted to immediately allow commercial fishing without going through the legally required rulemaking process, a federal court struck down that action.

Now, these protections are under threat again. In March 2026, a federal fishing council voted to reopen these protected waters to commercial fishing, and the National Marine Fisheries Service may be moving forward to take action. Any attempt to open these waters must comply with procedural requirements under federal law, including providing robust and meaningful opportunities for public participation. 

The Pacific Islands Heritage Marine National Monument protects **one of the last wild and healthy ocean ecosystems on Earth.** These islands, atolls, reefs, and waters hold profound cultural significance for Indigenous Pacific Islanders with ancestral, historical, and cultural ties to the region and are part of a cross-cultural Indigenous Pacific voyaging legacy. 

The monument is also a refuge for extraordinary marine life, including whales, sharks, rays, sea turtles, millions of seabirds, ancient coral systems, and deep-sea species found nowhere else on Earth.

**Industrial fishing puts this irreplaceable ecosystem at risk.** Large-scale fishing operations can catch and entangle endangered and threatened wildlife, including whales, dolphins, sea turtles, sharks, and seabirds, while removing fish and top predators that are essential to healthy ocean food webs and harming fragile corals.

For nearly two decades, the Pacific Islands Heritage Marine National Monument has represented a bipartisan conservation commitment. More than one million people, including cultural practitioners, scientists, and organizations across the Pacific and around the world, have stood up for the protection of this extraordinary place.

**Take action today to demand that existing protections remain in place.**

**Tell the Trump Administration and the National Marine Fisheries Service: Keep industrial fishing out of the Pacific Islands Heritage Marine National Monument and maintain existing protections.** Any action affecting these culturally and ecologically irreplaceable waters must follow requirements under federal law, honor Indigenous voices, use the best available science, and provide meaningful opportunities for public participation.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.description:
Baby Doe: Film Screening with If/When/How: BSL Chapter
Special Film Screening and Guided Discussion with IF/When/How: BSL Chapter 

November 6, 2026
6:30 p.m.
The Majorie Barrick Museum of Art Auditorium
4505 S. Maryland Pkwy, Las Vegas, NV 89154

Thirty years ago, Gail Ritchey, a young woman from a conservative Christian community in rural Ohio, gave birth alone and left her newborn in the woods. Now a devoted mother of three, her quiet suburban life shatters when DNA evidence links her to the infamous cold case of “Geauga’s Child.” Arrested for murder and vilified in the media, authorities dismiss her claim that the baby was stillborn. Facing a possible life sentence, Gail and her family must confront religious stigma, community judgment, and long-buried shame in the fight for her freedom.

Directed by Jessica Earnshaw (JACINTA), BABY DOE looks beyond the headlines to reveal the human complexity of Gail’s case, exploring how women’s health, justice, and powerful outside forces shape stories like hers. Watch the trailer here.

A guided discussion led by If/When/How: BSL Chapter will accompany the film screening. As well as tabling of local organizations for reproductive and women's rights.

events.description:
Join Blue Turn Indivisible and a large coalition of allies in San Jose after the election to reaffirm our commitment to ensuring that every vote is counted, and duly elected officials are certified and seated.

We've worked hard to make our voices heard at the ballot box. We showed up, organized, and voted for our values. Let's come together to celebrate what we've accomplished and show our resolve to defend democracy.

events.title: Court Watch
events.description:
Court Watch: Community Accountability in Action

Join CALEB for Court Watch and help bring transparency and accountability to Hamilton County’s legal system. Court Watchers observe General Sessions Court, where community members make their first appearance before a judge, to document proceedings and bear witness to how justice is administered.

Volunteers will be supported by an experienced Court Watch leader and do not need legal experience. Your presence in the courtroom helps challenge harmful practices, protect due process, and build collective power for meaningful criminal legal reform.

We'll share a 20 minute training virtually after you sign up to help prepare you for court watch.

**Please know that you are welcome to join us at anytime during the indicated timeframe. You do not need to arrive at 8:15 am or stay until 12:30 pm. Show up as you can! ** We'll text everyone who signs up so they have a direct contact to an organizer.

Sign up to attend one of our upcoming Court Watch dates and stand in solidarity with our neighbors.

events.title: Special Listening Circle: Election 2026
events.description:
This event is for (dis)abled and others who for whatever reason cannot do in-person events but are interested in participating in building healthier communities. It will involve an open check in or dialogue regarding thoughts, questions, and concerns about the election results and counting process. If necessary, we will plan for a virtual rapid response event. The zoom space will open at 7pm ET and ending time will depend on the need. 

As before, our leaders are located in Virginia and our focus is on SWVA, but we have people from many parts of Virginia, and as far away as CA. So, feel free to join us.

While we don’t have to worry about physical violations of our non-violent commitment in virtual events, we do have to demand and will monitor conversation that is divisive, rude, unconstructive to the promotion of democracy, mean, racist, or demeaning. We are non-partisan and focus mainly on issues of immigration/criminal justice and (dis)abilities; however, we definitely work to elect candidates who are progressive and align more closely with our issues. This will be enforced by removal of those who violate our non-violent speech commitment.
events.accessibility_notes: Please let us know if you have special interpretation needs. If we cannot meet your need in this event, we will try to make those arrangements for future events.

We've set early voting records this midterms, and we expect to see record turnout on November 3rd but we're not in the home stretch!  Between now and January 3rd, we are keeping a watchful eye.

events.title: Broward Election Day Get Out the Vote Lit Drop
events.description: Broward! Join us first thing on Election Day for a GOTV lit drop. No knocking, no script, no conversations. Pick up a walk list and door hangers, walk your turf, and check back in. Most turfs take about two hours. Why it matters: polls open at 7:00 AM. The voters on our list haven't cast a ballot yet — and the people who vote before work are the people who see our literature on the way out the door. This election decides what we pay for rent, groceries, and healthcare, whether our neighbors are safe here, and whether we keep the power to change any of it. Today it's decided. Never volunteered before? Perfect place to start. Everything's ready when you arrive, plus breakfast and coffee. Wear comfortable shoes and layers — it's colder at 6:00 AM than you think. Bring a charged phone and a power bank, and bring a friend. Turf goes twice as fast in pairs. Two hours before your day even starts. Today you get one vote. This morning you get a whole block. Come walk with us.

events.title: Statewide Election Day Get Out the Vote Phone Bank
events.description: Join us on Election Day for the last calls of the cycle. We'll be on the phones from mid-morning until the polls close, reaching voters who still haven't cast a ballot. Polls close at 7:00 PM. Every call before then can turn a non-voter into a voter — a ride arranged, a polling place confirmed, a reminder that there's still time. This election decides what we pay for rent, groceries, and healthcare, whether our neighbors are safe here, and whether we keep the power to change any of it. There is no shift after this one. No experience necessary. Come for an hour or stay for the day — every seat filled means more calls made. From home, you'll need a phone, a charged laptop or tablet, a quiet space, and headphones.  In person, bring a charged phone and charger, plus earbuds. We'll send the link and details beforehand. Food all day. Bring a friend — calls go faster, and it's a lot more fun. Sign up below for the block that works for you.

events.title: Broward Election Day Get Out the Vote Canvass

location.venue: Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Community Center

events.description: Broward! Join us for the final canvass of the election. We'll go door to door to reach voters who haven't made it to the polls yet — answer their questions, sort out how they're getting there, and get them out before polls close. Polls close at 7:00 PM. This is the last window we have. Voters still home at 3:00 PM are exactly who this shift exists for. This election decides what we pay for rent, groceries, and healthcare, whether our neighbors are safe here, and whether we keep the power to change any of it. Every last voter, right up to the final hour. No experience necessary. We'll train you on site and get you everything you need before you head out. Wear comfortable shoes and weather-appropriate clothes. Bring a charged phone and a power bank, and bring a friend — turf goes twice as fast in pairs. Food and refreshments are on us. Sign up below. A few hours, and then it's done. Today you get one vote. This afternoon you get a whole block. Come walk with us.

Electing Democrats up and down the ballot is how we continue delivering results for Massachusetts. We need all hands on deck.

MI-10 is the ONLY open, toss-up seat in Michigan, and one of just three open, toss-up seats in the entire country. Every voter we meet on the doors could make the difference in this race. 

We'll do a quick training before anyone goes out, you'll be paired with a team or a partner if you prefer to canvass in pairs, and there will be snacks to fuel your time on the doors!


Come out and meet the team and get out into the community!

Join Bend the Arc on November 10th — one week post-election — to celebrate, learn from the results, and plan for how we build momentum for the 2028 presidential election. 

On this call we will:

-  Discuss key learnings from the Michigan Senate race and how we fought back against AIPAC

-  Learn how Jews both impacted and were impacted by this election cycle, and how we move forward

-  Celebrate our movement's work to protect elections, in the most at-risk jurisdictions

-  Learn what’s next in our collective fight against authoritarianism, including protecting future elections

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Every election, thousands of mail ballots get flagged for easily fixable issues. In Nevada, voters have a short window to fix it, and many never hear about it in time. That’s where we come in.

Join us for the launch of our ballot curing canvass. We’ll start with a quick training (no experience needed), then head out in teams to reach voters whose ballots need attention and walk them through the simple steps to get their vote counted.

Never canvassed before? Perfect. Join our Cure Team.

Ballot curing sounds technical, but it’s really just a friendly conversation: letting a voter know their ballot has been flagged and helping them fix it so it can be counted. We’ll teach you exactly what to do.

events.title: Duval Election Day Get Out the Vote Lit Drop
events.description: Duval! Join us first thing on Election Day for a GOTV lit drop. No knocking, no script, no conversations. Pick up a walk list and door hangers, walk your turf, and check back in. Most turfs take about two hours. Why it matters: polls open at 7:00 AM. The voters on our list haven't cast a ballot yet — and the people who vote before work are the people who see our literature on the way out the door. This election decides what we pay for rent, groceries, and healthcare, whether our neighbors are safe here, and whether we keep the power to change any of it. Today it's decided. Never volunteered before? Perfect place to start. Everything's ready when you arrive, plus breakfast and coffee. Wear comfortable shoes and layers — it's colder at 6:00 AM than you think. Bring a charged phone and a power bank, and bring a friend. Turf goes twice as fast in pairs. Two hours before your day even starts. Today you get one vote. This morning you get a whole block. Come walk with us.

events.title: Duval Election Day Get Out the Vote Canvass
events.description: Duval! Join us for the final canvass of the election. We'll go door to door to reach voters who haven't made it to the polls yet — answer their questions, sort out how they're getting there, and get them out before polls close. Polls close at 7:00 PM. This is the last window we have. Voters still home at 3:00 PM are exactly who this shift exists for. This election decides what we pay for rent, groceries, and healthcare, whether our neighbors are safe here, and whether we keep the power to change any of it. Every last voter, right up to the final hour. No experience necessary. We'll train you on site and get you everything you need before you head out. Wear comfortable shoes and weather-appropriate clothes. Bring a charged phone and a power bank, and bring a friend — turf goes twice as fast in pairs. Food and refreshments are on us. Sign up below. A few hours, and then it's done. Today you get one vote. This afternoon you get a whole block. Come walk with us.

events.title: Statewide Election Day Get Out the Vote Phone Bank
events.description: Join us on Election Day for the last calls of the cycle. We'll be on the phones from mid-morning until the polls close, reaching voters who still haven't cast a ballot. Polls close at 7:00 PM. Every call before then can turn a non-voter into a voter — a ride arranged, a polling place confirmed, a reminder that there's still time. This election decides what we pay for rent, groceries, and healthcare, whether our neighbors are safe here, and whether we keep the power to change any of it. There is no shift after this one. No experience necessary. Come for an hour or stay for the day — every seat filled means more calls made. From home, you'll need a phone, a charged laptop or tablet, a quiet space, and headphones.  In person, bring a charged phone and charger, plus earbuds. We'll send the link and details beforehand. Food all day. Bring a friend — calls go faster, and it's a lot more fun. Sign up below for the block that works for you.

events.description:

Eye-to-eye conversations are crucial. We're working hard before in-person early voting begins on 10/15 and heading out into NC-01 in force to knock on doors, listen to what's really on voters minds this year, and to earn their support for Congressman Don Davis.

Why it matters:
This district has shifted again: what was once rated R+3 has been redrawn to R+5. That's a real challenge, but it also means this race is winnable, and it will come down to one thing: who shows up and has the best conversations at the door.

This moment is a turning point. It's the moment voters start paying closer attention, making their plans, and deciding whether this election is worth their time. We want NC-01 to hear from us first.

events.title: Day After Debrief with Jessica Craven and Robert Hubbell!
events.description:
The day after the 2026 midterms will be a day of anxiety and anticipation for members of Grassroots organizations everywhere. With the large nationwide early voting campaigns, more results will be in than in prior elections but there will still be counting going on. We are beyond honored and excited to host Robert Hubbell author of Today's Edition Newsletter and Jessica Craven author of Chop Wood, Carry Water--both on Substack. We will review where we are in the election results, discuss seats still undecided, talk about any incidents of voter interference and what is being done about it, and outline next steps to protect and ensure every vote is counted. 

In addition, we will share our best memories of this election work we have all been engaged in. And, so important to this treasured event, we will hear straight from the hearts of these two patriot guest speakers what they are thinking about the current condition on November 4th. Don't miss this incredible, and what will be a memorable event!

events.title: Take Back The House Ballot Cure Phonebank
events.description:
Join campaigns across the country to help cure mail ballots in races vital to securing a strong House majority! 

We'll be calling into districts to help voters fix errors with their mail ballots to ensure they can be counted before the state's counting and certification deadlines. We're fighting to protect every one of these voters, and every ballot we cure is one more that will help build a stronger country for all of us! 

We'll begin each session with an overview of the states and districts we'll be calling into, training on how to cure a ballot using that states rules, and an orientation to the tools and processes we use to make this effort effective. 

**PLEASE NOTE:**

**Please be on time as training is required. All times listed here are given in Eastern.** Anyone who arrives after training has started will be unable to participate. Once you sign up for a shift please add to it to your own calendar.

**Comfort with tech is required**-- specifically, the ability to use multiple tabs on your computer screen is necessary to make these calls. No dialers are used; you will be using your personal phone.

Additional shifts may be added! Check back for more.

events.title: Join Team Bernie and Get-Out-the-Vote for Peggy Flanagan/Keith Ellison in Coon Rapids

sponsor.name: Organizing to Fight Oligarchy / We The Fighters

events.description:
Join Team Bernie and Get-Out-the-Vote for Peggy Flanagan/Keith Ellison in Coon Rapids this coming Nov 2, 2026 at 5:30pm -7:00pm. 

Organize and Win Minnesota is our program to elect Peggy Flanagan to the United States Senate on November 3rd. We are building a powerful grassroots organizing program in communities across the state.

Senator Sanders says it best:

Friends,

Over ten years ago, we set out to create a political revolution in this country. You showed up because you believed in a simple principle that we must build a government that represents all Americans, not just the wealthy few.

Right now, our movement is winning. Why?

Whether it is a corrupt campaign finance system, unprecedented income and wealth inequality, a broken and wildly expensive healthcare system, the enormous threats posed by AI or an immoral and destructive foreign policy, progressives are talking about the real issues facing working families. And we are providing real solutions while establishment Democrats continue to tinker around the edges.

We now have candidates in New York, Ohio, Maine, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Montana, Minnesota, Florida, Michigan, California, Colorado, Arizona, and New Jersey who are winning by running campaigns to change the broken political and economic system. And they have the guts to stand up to the billionaires and corporations who only want more political power and money.

But this isn't going to be easy. Right now the billionaire class, Donald Trump, and the Republican Party Establishment are spending millions of dollars to defeat our progressive movement. Why? Because they believe that their money can stop our people-powered movement.

We know that organized people can beat organized money, but organized people need to show up.

So what can you do? I am asking you to show up, organize events, and get out the vote for our progressive candidates before November 3rd. This movement has never been about me. It’s about us.

Let’s get to work.

In solidarity,

Senator Bernie Sanders

events.title: Join Origin Stories pt3 Constitution: How America's Founding Shapes Today's Chaos: Thurs 11/5@7CT
events.description:
#### Join “Origin Stories pt3, How America's Founding Shapes Today's Chaos” “Constitution” Thurs 11/5@7CT -ZOOM

_Much like the American Revolution and the Founders themselves, our Constitution has been wrapped in mythology—often making it harder to understand its impact on our nation today. What forces shaped its creation, and how does that founding document continue to shape our shared life?_

#### let us know you will be attending - CLICK HERE TO  RSVP -> https://mobilize.us/s/2Bcdg2

Author Joel Edward Goza returns for Chapter Three of Origin Stories: How America’s Founding Shapes Today’s Chaos, presented by NWSOFA Indivisible. This session, “The Mission of the Constitution,” takes a closer look at the ideas and interests behind our nation’s governing framework.

Together, we’ll investigate the forces that drove the Constitutional Convention, the principles embedded in the Constitution, and how those foundations continue to influence our institutions, politics, and lives today.

_Join NWSOFA on Zoom Thursday, November 5, at 7 p.m. CST / 8 p.m. EST for this timely conversation with Joel Edward Goza, moderated by Marilyn._

Joel Edward Goza is the author of America’s Unholy Ghosts: The Racist Roots of Our Faith and Politics and Rebirth of a Nation: Reparations and Remaking America. 

#### ZOOM link - Click Here at 6:55 pm to attend the NWSOFA–Indivisible “Origin Stories pt3, How America's Founding Shapes Today's Chaos” “the Constitution” Thursday November 5th @7pm CT - ZOOM -> https://bit.ly/NWSOFA-Zoom

events.title: Southampton Village Election Day Morning Canvass with SwingLeft!
events.description:
Join Young Democrats of Eastern Long Island and other Swing Left volunteers to talk face-to-face with potential voters or volunteers! We'll be going into Southampton Village to talk to potential voters and hand out campaign literature!

We’re taking action because winning back power for Democrats starts with face-to-face conversations. Especially in a media environment plagued by polarization and misinformation, talking to voters – and in turn encouraging them to engage their own networks – is a critical way to increase our impact. Our high-traffic canvass program is designed to build a sustained relationship with individual voters, and give them an easy on-ramp to connect with people in their lives who might be less likely to vote.  

Swing Left is a grassroots organization that helps people make an impact in the elections that determine the national balance of power in the country. Our goal is simple: elect Democrats to help strengthen our democracy.

events.title: 2026 #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence

location.venue: First United Church of Oak Park

events.description:
2026 #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence

Beginning Wednesday, December 9, 2026 until the end of December, we will come together across the nation to host the #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence.

These local events will be anchored by the 14th Annual National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C.—held near the 14-year mark of the Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting tragedy, when a 20-year-old gunman armed with an AR-15 hunted and murdered 20 first graders and six educators.

Across the country, vigils (as simple as lighting candles) and gatherings will honor lives stolen by gun violence, uplift survivors, raise awareness, and demand urgent action from our leaders to finally end this epidemic. From schools and workplaces to houses of worship, neighborhoods, grocery stores, homes, nightclubs, streets, and even our democracy itself—gun violence impacts every aspect of American life.

The theme of this year’s campaign is #FreedomToLive—the simple, powerful idea that every person deserves to live free from the daily threat of gunfire. Together, survivors, families, advocates, and allies will raise our voices to ensure that FREEDOM means the right of every person to live, learn, work, worship, speak, vote, and gather without the daily fear of gun violence.

We stand in solidarity with over 1.4 million Americans who have been shot since Sandy Hook, with every community devastated by gun violence for decades. We will send a clear message to our local, state, and federal lawmakers, raise awareness, and help build the movement for common-sense solutions.

Let’s #HonorWithAction together. Let’s demand freedom from gun violence.
